title: Tre'von Moehrig Misses Top 32 Rank, Panthers Should Trade for Safety Who Made It
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers signed star safety Tre'von Moehrig to a three-year, $51 million deal ahead of the 2025 season. It was one of many moves that helped spur a league-worst defense to mediocrity.
Moehrig has been as advertised , excelling in the run game and giving Ejiro Evero a chess piece to work with. He's been hailed as one of the league's most versatile players .
That said, he did not rank within the top 32 on PFF's list of the best safeties. He ranked pretty low in that metric, actually around 50th-best. While PFF grades are not perfect, it is a little troubling to be ranked so low.
Fortunately, there is a top-32 safety who made the cut and could be available via trade, and the Panthers ought to jump on that.
Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker did not request a trade, but let's examine his situation for a moment. The Cardinals are pretty bad and they play in an absolutely loaded division. They need assets, and Baker is both aging and expensive.
Plus, with two years of team control left, the safety would likely fetch a pretty decent trade return for the Cardinals. Now, for the Panthers: they need safety help, and Baker would give them a solid duo to play over the top.
Moehrig is a run-defending safety who struggles badly in coverage, allowing nearly 80% of passes to be completed while in coverage. Lathan Ransom, Zakee Wheatley, and Nick Scott are somewhat decent options next to Moehrig, but they're no Baker, at least not yet.
Baker just made the cut for PFF's top 32, ranking 32nd. Bradley Locker wrote, "An eight-time Pro Bowler, Baker is a well-respected player — but one whose advanced statistics paint a more cloudy picture. Baker has sat below a 65.0 overall PFF grade in two of the past three seasons."
Unfortunately, Baker's coverage has dipped in recent years, but he's still a much better and more proven commodity than any of the three options the Panthers are currently working with. Ransom and Wheatley are young, and Scott just isn't that good.
Baker is obviously on the decline, but that just means he can play until Ransom or Wheatley is ready to start full-time, mentoring them and providing improved safety play in the interim. It's a win-win for everyone involved, including the asset-needy rebuilding Cardinals.
And despite Locker's harsh description, Baker did make the top 32, and Moehrig didn't.

title: Panthers’ Bryce Young, Mike Jackson Might Both Be Headed For Career Years
full_text:
Training camp is in full swing as the 2026 season rapidly approaches. With training camps, tension and scuffles always come up, whether it's within teams or in joint practices.
That remains true for the Carolina Panthers , who have been in training camp longer than any other team in the league. Carolina started camp back on July 23rd since they had to prep for the HOF game .
With even more time in camp before the season, it gives more opportunity for scuffles and dust-ups in practice, and this week has been the apex of that thus far.
On Monday, the biggest fight of camp broke out. RB Jonathon Brooks was rushing the ball and was reportedly hit hard by one of the safeties, either Nick Scott or Lathan Ransom; both had been reported to be the one to hit Brooks.
Big fight here. Started when Lathan Ransom tried to hit Jonathon Brooks on a run. Bryce Young took offense. He and Mike Jackson were jawing. An offensive lineman stepped in. Someone got hit in the head.
That’s not the important piece, though, since Brooks is okay. What came after the hit was Panthers star cornerback Mike Jackson getting into it with offensive lineman Luke Fortner, and also heavily jawing with Carolina’s most important player.
Young and Jackson were seen jawing heavily at each other after that play and throughout practice on Monday. The arguments escalated to the point that Jackson and Young had to have a long conversation after practice, along with Scott.
Scott commented on the matter and said the conversation revolved around keeping the team safe while maintaining an appropriate level of physicality. The best quote from Scott on the matter was “If practice was all kumbaya, I’d be worried. But it’s not.”
Later Scott said: “If practice was all kumbaya, I’d be worried. But it’s not.” https://t.co/9FKNRykj5R
Scott’s on the money here. This is competition at the end of the day, and the best way for Carolina to prepare for the season is to compete at the highest level possible at camp.
This situation mirrors another notorious training camp scuffle in Panthers history, one involving the same position groups.
Back in 2015, QB Cam Newton and CB Josh Norman got into a huge scuffle at training camp, which had to be separated by basically the entire team.
To the damn date! The prophecy has begun https://t.co/lIYobYGjkU pic.twitter.com/9juTlz0XUu
Maybe it’s a correlation, maybe it’s not, but the Panthers finished the regular season 15-1 and made the Super Bowl that year. Cam Newton won NFL MVP, and Josh Norman was first-team All-Pro.
Now, over 10 years later, Young and Jackson keep the tradition of QB-Corner animosity going, and if anything, it’s a good sign for the Panthers.
Competitive spirit is higher than ever in Carolina, and that will only help the Panthers going forward. Young and Jackson are focal points on both sides of the ball and could be in for huge years in 2026.

title: Drake Maye & Matthew Stafford Fall Short of Bryce Young in This Epic QB Stat
full_text:
Former first-overall pick Bryce Young is about to enter his fourth season in the NFL, and he has shown flashes of being the dynamic, franchise-defining starter under center that the Carolina Panthers hoped he would be when they drafted him three years ago.
One of the areas in which Young has shown to be exceptional is throwing the deep ball. He regularly ranks among the NFL's best at pushing the ball down the field, which was a driving force behind his career year in 2025.
Many may not realize just how good Young was at throwing the ball deep last season, but PFF recently put out a post on X that shows just how exceptional the Carolina quarterback was in this area compared to some of the NFL's best gunslingers.
Highest DEEP BALL (20+ yard) passing grade last season (min 40 attempts) Bryce Young               99.7 Matthew Stafford     98.9 Drake Maye                 97.4 pic.twitter.com/3Jwf56KH5X
According to PFF, Young had the highest deep ball passing grade in the entire NFL last season at 99.7, a mark that surpassed both league MVP Matthew Stafford (98.9) and MVP runner-up Drake Maye (97.4).
Anytime a quarterback can put themselves in the same conversation as Stafford, they're probably doing something right, but the fact that Young bests him in the area many consider to be his biggest strength shows just how special the Panthers' signal-caller truly is when it comes to throwing it long.
Maye is also widely considered to be the next big thing at the quarterback position, so the fact that Young also beats him out as well is another massive feather in his cap.
Anyone who has watched Young over the course of his early career in the NFL has always known that he has a knack for hitting his receivers in the deep part of the field . This has been a massive strength of his, even going back to his college days at Alabama.
The next step in Young's development will be figuring out how to translate his proficiency on deep passes to the shorter and intermediate areas of the passing game. These are the areas he has to improve in if he wants to reach his full potential.
If Young can figure out how to unlock those other pieces of his game, then Carolina might have the franchise quarterback they were looking for when they drafted him at the top of the draft three years back.
He'll have to prove he can take that next step soon, though, as the deadline for any potential long-term extension is rapidbly approaching.

title: The Biggest Reason For Pessimism in Carolina Panthers' NFC South Defense
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers took a massive step forward in 2025 under second-year head coach Dave Canales, finishing 8-9 in the regular season and winning the NFC South for the first time since their legendary Super Bowl run in 2015.
Now, Canales and the Panthers will be looking to defend that division crown in what is arguably the most wide-open division in the NFL, and while there are a lot of reasons to like Carolina's chances to repeat, there are also some serious areas of concern that could end up impeding them in that quest.
Pro Football Focus analyst Gordon McGuinness recently broke down what fans can expect to see from the Panthers in 2026, and he listed a couple of areas of concern as the biggest sources of pessimism when it comes to defending their NFC South Crown.
The most glaring red flag that Carolina will be dealing with heading into the new campaign, per McGuinness, will be the health of their offensive line, and, more specifically, the current injury concerns plaguing both the right and left tackle positions.
"The Panthers are currently without both starting offensive tackles," McGuinness writes. "Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon in the wild-card loss to the Rams, while right tackle Taylor Morton is sidelined with blood clots. It remains unclear when either will return in 2026, but both appear likely to miss at least the start of the season."
The Panthers also dealt with injury issues up front on offense in 2025, but the tackle spots were a rare bright spot and played a massive role in Bryce Young's career year. As such, potentially missing both Ekwonu and Morton for extended periods would be a massive blow for Carolina's offense, especially early on in the season.
After a rough first 2 seasons under center in Carolina, 2023 first-overall pick Bryce Young finally had somewhat of a breakthrough in year three, posting career-bests in passing yards (3,011), touchdowns (23), and completion percentage (63.6).
2025 represented a major step in the right direction for Young, but the former Heisman winner was far from perfect under center. It seemed like every week it was feast or famine for Young, putting together a phenomenal performance one game, only to follow it up with an absolute dud the next.
Now on the verge of a potential contract extension, Young has yet to prove he can be the franchise QB the Panthers hope he will be on a consistent basis, a reality that McGuinness mentions as another potential pitfall for the team in 2026.
"There is also the question of how far Bryce Young can take this team," McGuinness writes. "The 2023 No. 1 overall pick is coming off his second consecutive season with a PFF grade above 70.0, but he has shown the potential to become a top-tier quarterback only in flashes."
He continues, "His 4.5% big-time throw rate in 2025 ranked tied for 19th among the 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks. That level of production is manageable while Young remains on his rookie contract, but the Panthers will likely need to see more before committing to him beyond his fifth-year option in 2027."
If both Panthers and Young want to become consistent division contenders, then there simply has to be more consistency from the latter from week to week throughout the season. If he is unable to do so, then there could be some uncomfortable questions that need to be asked next offseason.

title: Zakee Wheatley Might’ve Played His Way Into Panthers Plans After HOF Game
full_text:
There certainly has been a lot of good news coming out of Carolina Panthers’ training camp these days. Second-year pass-rusher Nic Scourton and rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell II will miss the 2026 season, and right tackle Taylor Moton’s status remains a question as well (blood clots). Even quarterback Haynes King, who scored the game-winning touchdown last Thursday night against the Arizona Cardinals, has been bitten by the injury bug.
Of course, there were some positives coming out of the team’s 33-30 victory. One of those was the play of one of general manager Dan Morgan’s seven draft choices back in April.
The Panthers wound up with a pair of fifth-round selections this year. With the first, Morgan addressed the offensive line by picking Kansas State University center Sam Hecht with the 144th overall pick. Seven selections later (151), he opted for Penn State safety Zakee Wheatley. The back end of Carolina’s defense has been an issue in recent seasons and the team has been looking to upgrade the position. It’s just one preseason game, but the former Nittany Lion had a very productive outing vs. the Cards.
Panthers Rookie safety Zakee Wheatley cut up from the Hall of fame game #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/eYhlJAaf4g
Wheatley earned the start at safety opposite second-year pro Lathan Ransom, and played a total of 35 defensive snaps. He led Carolina with eight tackles, and also forced a fumble. The 6’3 1/8”, 203-pound rookie earned a lot of praise from Pro Football Focus . He was the highest-graded player on Dave Canales’s club (88.0) and was solid vs. both the run and the pass.
All told, Wheatley was graded on 18 running plays and 17 on pass coverage. He earned a team-high 84.7 mark against the run, and was second on the club vs. the pass (73.7) behind linebacker Isaiah Simmons (82.4). Perhaps the most impressive grade was given for his tackling with a team-best 87.4. It’s one game and a preseason contest at that, but it was certainly a very encouraging outing for the 24-year-old rookie.
ZAKEE WHEATLEY PICK!!! WHAT A START pic.twitter.com/9OdIAvewm9
In his final four seasons at Penn State, Wheatley played in 54 games. He totaled a half-dozen interceptions, six passes defensed, two forced fumbles, and three fumble recoveries. Those nine takeaways are somewhat notable and that’s the kind of plays that the Panthers didn’t get from Veteran Nick Scott ( who they re-signed this offseason ) in 2025.
The seven-year pro started all 17 games and finished second on the team with 109 defensive stops, but managed only one interception and a fumble recovery.
Could the Carolina starting secondary have a new face come Week 1 when Canales’s team hosts the Chicago Bears? The situations bears a closer watch.

title: Carolina Panthers May Have No Choice But to Extend Mike Jackson
full_text:
Following a horrific showing by their defense in 2024, Carolina Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan was determined to fix Ejiro Evero’s unit last offseason. Up front, there were the additions of free-agent defensive linemen Tershawn Wharton and Bobby Brown III, edge rusher Patrick Jones II, and strong safety Tre’von Moehrig.
Via the draft, Morgan added pass-rushers Nic Scourton and Princely Umanmielen, safety Lathan Ransom, and massive defensive tackle Cam Jackson.
There was certainly some improvement, and a healthy Derrick Brown was a huge factor after he missed the final 16 games of 2024. However, there’s still a long way to go.
Meanwhile, a pair of components in the secondary that were already in place prior to Morgan’s offseason work were cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. The former was the team’s first-round pick in 2021, while the latter came via trade from the Seattle Seahawks in 2024. Jackson’s first season with the club saw the Panthers allow an NFL-high 35 touchdown passes.
However, the former Miami Hurricane and a fifth-round pick in 2019 by the Dallas Cowboys was a 17-game starter in his first season with Dave Canales’s squad. He finished fourth on the club with 76 tackles, picked off two passes, and led Carolina with 17 passes defensed.
Matthew Stafford gets picked off by Mike Jackson who takes it back for the pick 6. What’s going on Stafford? 😬 pic.twitter.com/NQkFkj8p2P
This past season, Jackson enjoyed a career year that saw him earn Second Team All-Pro honors from Pro Football Focus . Once again, he was a 17-game starter. In 2025, he was fifth on the team with 68 tackles, and finished second on the team behind Horn (5) with four interceptions.
That included a pick-six of eventual NFL MVP Matthew Stafford in the Panthers’ 31-28 regular-season win over the Rams. Also, Jackson once again led Carolina with 19 passes defensed.
Mike Jackson had a PickSix against Stafford in the regular season pic.twitter.com/6gqAeAKqHX
Of course, Jackson was also in the starting lineup vs. Sean McVay’s club in what proved to be a heart-breaking 34-31 home loss in the wild card playoffs. He finished the game with three tackles, intercepted Stafford once again, and led Carolina with four passes defensed. Hence, it’s little wonder that PFF has the seven-year pro as its No. 10 cornerback entering the 2026 season.
“In a matter of just two seasons,” explained Dalton Wasserman, “Jackson has gone from an afterthought in Seattle to being arguably the Panthers’ best defensive player. Last season, he earned an 85.8 PFF coverage grade that led all cornerback who played at least 300 coverage snaps…”
Now comes the tricky part. Jackson is in the final year of a two-year, $10.5 million contract he signed in 2025. He’s proven to be quite the bargain for a player who has started every game for the Panthers since his arrival.
Some have suggested that the team use a first-round pick in 2027 to find his replacement should they allow him to test free agency. On the other hand, Carolina Panthers On SI’s Zach Roberts feels that a three-year, $54 million deal would be good for both Jackson and the team.
Keep in mind that Morgan wound up dealing 2024 seventh-round linebacker Michael Barrett to Seattle for Jackson. The former has yet to see any action in an NFL game. It’s turned out to be quite the steal for the Panthers’ GM and the organization as well.

title: Panthers Urged to Put Player on Trade Block They Simply Can't Afford to Lose
full_text:
It’s been a rough few months for Dave Canales’s club. And it actually started well before the team’s recent rash of season-ending injuries to edge rusher Nic Scourton and rookie wideout Chris Brazzell II, as well as the medical issues for reliable right tackle Taylor Moton.
Back in May, veteran defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton underwent neck surgery. A year ago, the two-time Super Bowl champion inked a three-year, $45.05 million deal with the Carolina Panthers. The former Chiefs’ defender missed four of the club’s first six contests, as well as Carolina’s final five regular-season games, however he did return for the playoff clash with the Los Angeles Rams.
The six-year veteran finished with 36 stops, a pair of sacks, and three quarterback hits. Wharton played 50 snaps in the 34-31 loss to Sean McVay’s club in the wild card round, finishing with two tackles (1 for loss), and a pair of QB hits. The 28-year-old defender is still on the mend and it remains to be seen when he will return to the field.
And that’s why the notion of trading away an experience interior defender doesn’t seem to make much sense at this time. Longtime NFL writer Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report came up with one player from each NFL team that he feels should be available via trade. When it comes to the defending NFC South champions, his choice was also a 2025 free-agent addition like Wharton.
Every snap Panthers Rookie DT Lee Hunter played in the Hall of Fame game #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/jrRRlHf7pH
Last offseason, Morgan also signed Bobby Brown III away from the Rams to the tune of three years and $21 million. It has not proven to be a wise investment to date. “Brown appeared in all 17 games last season,” explained Knox, “finishing with 31 tackles and a half-sack. However, he only made five starts and was graded 80th overall among defensive linemen by Pro Football Focus . His long-term future became uncertain after the Panthers used a second-round pick on Lee Hunter, who is well suited for the nose tackle role."
To be fair, Knox does mention Wharton’s issues as his “ongoing recovery from spring neck surgery clouds the defensive-line rotation a bit.” Still, he feels that if Hunter proves his worth this summer, dealing Brown would be a good move which would also open up some cap space for the team.
Along with Hunter, there’s also another young player to consider here. That’s second-year defensive tackle Cam Jackson— a fifth-round draft choice in 2025. He wound up playing in only nine regular-season games with zero starts. He finished with a mere nine tackles, but did block a field goal in the Week 18 loss at Tampa Bay. The massive 6’6”, 328-pound former Florida Gator appeared in the playoffs vs. the Rams but recorded no tackles.
At the moment, parting ways with Brown is probably not advisable (unless there’s an offer Morgan simply can’t refuse). However, there’s a lot of time between now and September 13.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Monday's Panthers Training Camp: Another Fight
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers wrapped up another day of training camp, this time coming off last week's victory in the Hall of Fame Game . Like all practices, there were good things, including Kenny Pickett, of all players. There were also some bad things, like another fight that got pretty intense.
Big fight here. Started when Lathan Ransom tried to hit Jonathon Brooks on a run. Bryce Young took offense. He and Mike Jackson were jawing. An offensive lineman stepped in. Someone got hit in the head.
There have been multiple skirmishes at Panthers camp, with none of them boiling over into anything serious. That's good. These players have walked the line pretty well, but they're also not wavering in their intensity. That matters as they ramp up for a really intense season.
Bryce Young, Mike Jackson and Nick Scott having a long conversation after practice.
The aforementioned skirmish included Jonathon Brooks getting hit hard by Lathan Ransom, and Bryce Young took exception to it. He probably doesn't need to get in the middle of those things, and it's also not a great look that Nick Scott and Mike Jackson seemed to talk to him after practice like he's not the undisputed leader of the team.
Corey Thornton leaps to knock down a deep Kenny Pickett pass that was intended for Trevor Etienne in team.
Lost in the shuffle of the fight was the fact that the Panthers had several defenders make good plays on the ball. Devin Lloyd forced a fumble. Cam Miller broke up a pass. So did Mike Jackson (after his dust-up with Bryce Young), Bam Martin-Scott, and Corey Thornton. It was a solid day for the defense.
Canales: Open competition between Wallace and Cherelus for LB2.
We always assumed that Trevin Wallace would end up starting because there just wasn't anyone behind him that could challenge for that second ILB spot. Well, Claudin Cherilus is officially up for the spot, and that speaks volumes about where Trevin Wallace is at entering his third year in the NFL.
All the talk surrounding the Panthers has been that Haynes King deserves to take the QB2 role from Kenny Pickett. After the Hall of Fame Game, it's impossible not to see the vision. But Pickett responded while King recovers from his injury, delivering a great practice session.
Jimmy Horn vs. Tre’von Moehrig. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/EdRInFGXgj
Jimmy Horn Jr. beat Tre'von Moehrig to the end zone and made a nice catch in individual drills. Jaycee Horn was beat by Jalen Coker, who took in a Bryce Young sideline throw. This was the theme: cornerbacks and safeties getting beat by wide receivers when matched up. It's both good and not so good.

title: There's One Big Reason For Optimism Ahead of Carolina Panthers 2026 Season
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are hard to read heading into the 2026 season. On one hand, the defense should take a step forward after adding star talent like Jaelan Phillips and Devin Lloyd .
On the other hand, there are questions in the backfield, and major injuries are already occurring throughout both sides of the roster.
On offense in particular, there are huge question marks on who the RB1 will end up being. It is also uncertain whether Bryce Young can deliver under immense pressure this season, and if the offensive line can protect Young well enough after being revamped and starting a rookie at right tackle.
All of those potential doubts are warranted, but there is one player whom fans can blindly trust.
If there's one player that Panthers fans don't need to stress about, it's McMillan. The now second-year receiver out of Arizona was a bright spot in Carolina's offense last season and has already solidified himself as a true No. 1 wideout in the NFL.
PFF released its season preview for the Carolina Panthers , and correctly highlighted McMillan as a reason to be optimistic heading into the upcoming season. Among rookie receivers in 2025, McMillan graded the highest, finishing the year with a 79.2 PFF grade.
The high grade was warranted. For context, McMillan earned that grade after posting 70 catches, for 1014 receiving yards, and 7 touchdowns. A season that culminated in winning the Offensive Rookie of the Year award.
One other stat that PFF pointed out really shows how important McMillan has been and will be going forward. Carolina's WR1 finished 2025 with 126 targets, double the amount as any other receiver on the team.
That trend has to continue in 2026, and with rookie receiver Chris Brazzell II out for the season, there's no other option than to keep McMillan busy.
If Bryce Young and the offense as a whole are to take a step forward, the catalyst is No. 4. McMillan will likely see snaps on the outside and the slot, and will need to be the safety blanket in the middle of the field just as much as he is the home run hitter.
Tetairoa McMillan beats Mike Jackson in the endzone #Panthers pic.twitter.com/3BC6q1vODY
As far as stats go, a sizeable but achievable improvement would look like 80-85 catches, for 1200-1300 yards, and 10+ touchdowns. Right now, Tetairoa McMillan is widely perceived as a top-20 receiver in the NFL. A year-two leap where he breaks into the consensus top 10 could be vital for Carolina's NFC South repeat.

title: Why Panthers Legend Steve Smith Sr. Really Deserves HOF Berth in 2027
full_text:
The headcount now reads 387. The Pro Football Hall of Fame welcomed Carolina Panthers’ linebacker Luke Kuechly, quarterback Drew Brees, running back Roger Craig, wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald, and placekicker Adam Vinatieri to Canton, Ohio, this past weekend to receive their busts. It’s always a special time.
Of course, there’s always time to look ahead. Last week, Grant Gordon of NFL.com made his selections for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027 in terms of modern-era selections. His five choices included a pair of first-time eligibles in tight end Rob Gronkowski and running back Adrian Peterson.
Mentioned among the other modern-era candidates was a 16-year pro who last took the field in 2016 and has been eligible the past five years. And perhaps it’s time that wide receiver Steve Smith Sr., a finalist back in 2025 , received his bust after an outstanding career.
A third-round pick from the University of Utah in 2001 by the Carolina Panthers, the 5’9. 195-pound performer was a Pro Bowler as well as a First Team All-Pro selection based on his special teams’ prowess. He returned 34 punts for 364 yards and one score, and totaled 1,431 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 56 kickoff returns. Meanwhile, he touched the football just 14 times (for 197 yards) in 15 games as a rookie, catching just 10 passes.
Obviously, that would soon change. In a total of 16 NFL campaigns, 13 with the Panthers and the final three with the Baltimore Ravens, Smith finished his career with 1,031 receptions. It adds up 14,731 yards and 81 touchdowns.
He’s Carolina’s all-time leader with 836 catches, 12,197 yards, and 67 TD grabs. He was named to a total of five Pro Bowls with the Panthers and also earned First Team All-Pro honors in 2025. His 75 total touchdowns with Carolina (67 receiving, 2 rushing, 6 returns) is yet another franchise record.
All told, Smith’s 1,031 career receptions ranks 14th in NFL annals, and only seven players have totaled more receiving yards. In 219 regular-season outings, he’s amassed 19,180 total combined yards and 89 touchdowns.
Jake Delhomme connects with Steve Smith for a 69-yard touchdown on the first play of the second OT to give the Panthers a 29-23 win over the Rams in the Divisional Round in St. Louis (2004) pic.twitter.com/pRH4Ek2lHI
But wait, there’s more. Smith has appeared in a total of 11 postseason contests (9 with Carolina, 2 with Baltimore), including Super Bowl XXXVIII with the Panthers. That adds up to 1,160 total combined yards and 11 more trips to the end zone (9 receiving, 1 rushing, 1 punt return) for the explosive playmaker.
Who could forget his 69-yard catch and run for the game-winning touchdown in the Panthers’ 29-23 double overtime victory over the then-St. Louis Rams in the 2003 NFC Divisional Playoffs?
Yes, changes in the voting procedure have made it much more difficult to earn a spot in Canton. There have been a total of nine enshrinees the past two years. Still, Smith’s impressive career resume screams Pro Football Hall of Famer. Perhaps some of the voters will listen a little more carefully when it comes down to deciding the Class of 2027.

title: Coby Bryant's Injury Will Put Ryan Poles' Defensive Line Plan to the Test
full_text:
It seemed like the Chicago Bears were dodging bullet after bullet on the training camp injury front. Luther Burden III had a few scares, but the team reportedly feels good about his chances of being ready for the season opener. Cam Lewis was back on the practice field yesterday after some misfortune of his own. Ozzy Trapilo is somehow well on his way back to the field after rupturing his Achilles in January.
We even thought Ben Johnson's comments about Coby Bryant's reported 8-10 week timeline were a good sign for his future. However, it turns out we were all duped in that regard. Those comments were interpreted incorrectly, as Johnson announced that Bryant would instead be on the shelf for the next 4-6 months earlier today.
It's a true worst-case scenario for a Bears defense already down one key starter in nickelback Kyler Gordon. The injury will not only strain the secondary, but it'll also put a lot more pressure on the defensive line.
Virtually everyone expected the team to make a deeper nvestment in the defensive line this offseason. It was widely considered one of their most glaring weaknesses entering the offseason after failing to get consistent pressure on opposing QBs and often getting gouged in the running game last season.
However, the fact that they already have the league's fifth-most expensive defensive line limited how much they could justify improving the room in free agency. They instead opted for bargain-bin free agent additions and the sixth-round selection of Georgia Tech's Jordan van den Berg. It was always a bold strategy.
Fortunately, it was a bold strategy that appears to be off to a brilliant start. It's still far too early to have the rookie's gold jacket fitted for Canton, but there's no denying the fact that he's made serious waves at training camp . That's a good thing, too, because they desperately need some juice in the pass-rush department with Grady Jarrett not getting any younger and hope increasingly fading in Gervon Dexter getting any better in his fourth season.
Montez Sweat and Austin Booker's hopeful progression at least instills some hope on the edges, and they might be able to unlock last year's biggest free agent disappointment , Dayo Odeyingbo, on the interior. However, Sweat is the only sure thing in that regard, as well.
The fact that the Bears signed Xavier Woods shortly after Bryant went down makes a lot more sense after Johnson's comments today. The veteran safety has 121 career starts under his belt, and he will at least provide some stability opposite rookie Dillon Thieneman.
Growing pains were always expected for Chicago's first-round selection, and that will especially be the case with Bryant out of action. While Woods has always been solid in coverage, Bryant is much more comfortable against the run than the veteran has been. That might be an area where they rely more on the rookie now, which could limit his upside and, in turn, remove the alignment flexibility that Dennis Allen was clearly vying for with the team's new safety duo.
It's also fair to question how well the new-look secondary will gel after losing one of their best players until (at least) December. The importance of getting Kyler Gordon back in the lineup has never been more paramount. Unfortunately, his health has always been far from reliable .
The loss the secondary suffered today cannot be understated, and it's going to have a wide-ranging impact on the entire defense.

title: 4 Chicago Bears Who Need a Strong Debut in Preseason Week 1 vs Browns
full_text:
The 2026 NFL preseason slate of games is finally upon us, and the Chicago Bears are set to host the Cleveland Browns at Soldier Field on Saturday. We don't know yet how much time the starters will get in this game, if any at all, but we're sure to get a long look at the backups and rookies. Roster cutdown day is fast approaching, and the coaches will have some tough decisions to make at that point. No doubt they're hoping to gain some clarity on these decisions during this preseason Week 1 game against the Browns .
This extended look at players who are fighting for roster spots is what makes these preseason games so intriguing. No final decisions will be made just yet, but this is one of the players' last best chances to convince the coaches that they've earned a spot on the team. With that in mind, here are four players who need an especially strong showing on Saturday.
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said at the start of training camp that Tyrique Stevenson needs to show more consistency, along with the rest of the defense, but we haven't got much of that from the fourth-year cornerback. According to Bears reporter Herb Howard, who spoke with FOX Chicago's Devan Kaney during Week 2 of training camp , Stevenson's good plays have consistently been followed by some pretty bad ones.
Stevenson's case for a roster spot has been largely bolstered by a rash of injuries over the past week, especially in the secondary, but if he wants to make an emphatic case for himself, he'll need to show up in a big way on Saturday during however many snaps he gets.
We finally got some proof-of-life from Hyppolite on Day 10 of Bears training camp , but one good practice is hardly enough to guarantee a spot on the 53-man roster. Hyppolite was a healthy scratch more often than not last year, and when he did play he was almost a complete non-factor, even in the preseason. It's not his fault that he was drafted far above where he was expected to go, but Hyppolite has utterly failed to even come close to validating Ryan Poles' trust.
Making matters worse, the Bears' linebacker room is surprisingly stacked. TJ Edwards returns for his fourth season in Chicago, where he'll be starting alongside free agency acquisition and former first-round pick Devin Bush. Behind them you have D'Marco Jackson, who re-signed with the Bears on a two-year deal , fan-favorite Jack Sanborn, and rookie Keyshaun Elliott, who the Bears are very excited about.
For Hyppolite to beat out any one of these guys for a roster spot, he's going to need a monster preseason performance, and that starts on Saturday.
The early hype around rookie Jordan van den Beg has ebbed and waned throughout the summer, but he still looms large as a potential draft gem on this needy Bears' defensive line. After a rough performance during spring OTAs, van den Berg's training camp surge has caught everyone's attention and is taking his hype to new levels. He's even been getting some reps with the starters on defense.
Of course, training camp hype is one thing. Performing in a game, even a preseason game, is something else. Van den Berg doesn't need to dominate Cleveland's offensive line on Saturday, but a solid showing would serve as proof of concept for the kid from South Africa.
The Bears' highly regarded first-round rookie has quietly had a disastrous training camp. I don't say that to alarm Bears fans, but it's simply the truth. Almost every day in practice, Thieneman has been getting burned for touchdowns or big plays. However, in fairness to the rookie, he's playing a very tough position to learn at the NFL level and is going up against such dynamic playmakers like Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. This is what they call a 'baptism by fire'
Again, I don't say this to alarm Bears fans, and they shouldn't be alarmed anyway. It's totally normal for rookie safeties who are immediately thrust into starting roles to struggle in August. And remember, this Bears offense is supposed to be very, very good. However, it would probably be good for the nerves of Bears fans, as well as his own confidence, for Thieneman to come out on Saturday and make a splashy play or two against the Browns.

title: Bears Hit With Worst-Case Scenario in Latest Coby Bryant Injury Update
full_text:
Just hours after news broke that Ozzy Trapilo could return from injury far sooner than expected , the Chicago Bears got hit with a devastating injury update for another player. Free agent acquisition Coby Bryant, who was carted off from training camp practice early last week, underwent knee surgery and will now miss four to six months as he recovers, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune .
It's hard to overstate just how bad this is for the Bears. Contrary to how most teams build their defense, general manager Ryan Poles opted to build his unit from the outside-in, meaning he focused on the secondary first and foremost while the defensive line remains questionable.
At first, this looked like a strategy that could work. Adding former Seattle Seahawks safety Coby Bryant on a $40 million agreement in free agency was a smart move, and the return of a healthy Jaylon Johnson would keep at least half of the field as a no-fly zone.
Now, one of the planned centerpieces of this defense will miss almost the entire season, even in a best-case scenario. And that creates a worst-case scenario for Dennis Allen's defense. His other planned starting safety is a rookie who has been getting cooked in coverage during training camp so far. Cam Lewis could play safety, but the Bears had wanted him to play slot cornerback in place of Kyler Gordon, who started training camp on the PUP list and has not practiced since then.
They still have to prove it on the field, but Chicago's offense is looking like a championship caliber offense. The plan was always that they would be able to score enough points to carry a defense loaded with question marks. Now, that defense will be even less reliable than anyone would have expected.
The pass rush situation is already built on hopes and wishes. The linebacker group has plenty of potential, but remains unproven. The secondary that was supposed to be a strength is now riddled with injuries, and they've just lost their best playmaker and safety for almost the entire season.
It turned out to be a good thing that the Bears signed two more defensive backs over the weekend. They're going to need those players to step up in a big way, and to play for far longer than anyone hoped.

title: Bears' Ozzy Trapilo Could Return From Injury Far Sooner Than Expected
full_text:
Modern medicine continues to work miracles, especially in the world of football. Back in January, Ozzy Trapilo ruptured his patellar tendon, an injury that was expected to sideline him for most of the 2026 season. But according to Adam Hoge and Adam Jahns of the Hoge and Jahns podcast , general manager Ryan Poles confirmed to them that Trapilo could "potentially" be back before the end of training camp, blowing away even the most optimistic interpretation of Trapilo's latest injury update from Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated.
Hoge and Jahns have not yet released their full conversation with Poles; that episode drops tomorrow. But in the clip shared to social media on the official Hoge and Jahns X account, Poles mentioned the necessity of participating in padded practices for players to prepare for games. "We've looked at that on a calendar and want to map that out for him so he feels confident coming back," Poles said.
When asked by Hoge whether training camp was still on the table, Poles replied with one word: potentially. That word can mean many different things to different people, but even acknowledging such a possibility is incredible news for the Bears. Instead of going almost the entire year without their starting left tackle, the Bears could very well have him back in the lineup in September.
Again, there's still a wide range of outcomes for Trapilo here. As Poles said, padded practices are vital for NFL players to be ready to go in for the regular season, so even if Trapilo does in fact return before the end of training camp, he's going to need a ramp up period. How long that takes will be up to head coach Ben Johnson, his coaches, and the athletic staff.
Trapilo only started six games in 2025 during the latter part of the season, but he once he got that starting job, he never gave it up. He looked like the best left tackle Chicago had seen in years; watching him limp to the sideline on the Bears' final offensive drive of their Wild Card matchup in January devastated Bears fans. Adding insult to injury, the initial reveal of a ruptured patellar tendon was even worse than we thought .
To be fair to his teammates, the Bears likely would have been okay if they had to turn to a replacement for half the season. The left tackle position battle in training camp has had a few twists and turns, but Braxton Jones was the top dog and would have likely been fine as a starter. He may still get to start early in the season, if Poles' projection proves overly rosy.
But as good as he is, Jones is no Trapilo. Plus, the rest of the offensive line already has good chemistry with Trapilo that they may not have with Jones, who hasn't played a football game since last September. Once Trapilo gets back into the lineup, whether that's September or November, we should see the Bears' offensive line return to being one of the best in the league.

title: The Easiest Decision Ben Johnson Must Make for Bears Preseason Opener
full_text:
The week of the first preseason game has arrived and Bears coach Ben Johnson faces one big decision. It's the same one every coach must make for every preseason game and one fans seem to get all up in arms about every year.
How much playing time will he give the first-team offense , and quarterback Caleb Williams in particular?
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken has already said he'll at least begin the game with starters on the field and is hoping to look at both quarterbacks vying for the starting role, Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson.
Johnson hasn't indicated anything yet about which players will start, but the smart money says they don't play starters. The smart decision is also that Johnson doesn't play starters.
There are a few reasons this is the way the Bears need to go.
, @DavidHaugh and @RuthiePolinsky thought the praise Matt LaFleur had for his QB Jordan Love was a bit crazy. That brought up the discussion...which NFC North QB is the most indispensable? "I would take Caleb Williams over any QB in the NFC North," says Haugh. pic.twitter.com/JcmHh3DKU4
Johnson didn't use his starters in the preseason opener last year.  It didn't matter that the Dolphins came into that preseason game and decided to use Tua Tagovailoa and starters. Johnson stuck with his own plan. He should do the same here. Who cares what Monken is doing?
To Johnson, the key is how the Bears practice this week and not how they'll play Saturday at Soldier Field when nothing matters. Tyson Bagent and the backup offense should be starting just like last year's preseason opener, and the same is true with the backup defense.
ZAVION THOMAS INJURY SITUATION NOT SERIOUS FOR MORE THAN ONE REASON
If Johnson wouldn't use his starters last year when the team was still in a formative situation in 2025 preseason, they certainly wouldn't want to do it now. Last year they really did need any practice rep they could get because they were having problems in practices even geting plays run, but he still wouldn't give starters the playing time.
Bears have released their first unofficial depth chart for 2026 Nothing too crazy. I expect rookie DT Jordan van den Berg to be higher by end of preseason. pic.twitter.com/aIEsU6VehS
They've been in the offense and defense a year now and are much more advanced. There's no urgent need for extra play reps. So there's no reason to expect he would buck last year's trend while facing a different situation with his own team.
Unlike the Browns, the Bears are already well positioned at quarterback and the coach and his passer know what to expect of each other. There is no need to get a feel for this in game conditions.
“If you take this insane level physical specimen talent who has bought into Ben Johnson’s coaching and you take elite talent with elite coaching, the ceiling is limitless and I expect Caleb Williams to be consistently competing for Super Bowls and MVPs.” @DannyParkins explains: pic.twitter.com/Xf1KU2ybTK
These happen every year in training camps and decisions can be made entirely based on this, but with an injury affecting left tackle Braxton Jones and considering they didn't use veteran standout guard Joe Thuney all of preseason last year, it would mean putting Williams out there behind a makeshift line in a meaningless game. There's absolutely no reason to attempt this.
Williams won't even have receiver Luther Burden available, and possibly even rookie Zavion Thomas, as a result of injuries so there really is no point to using the starting QB and starting offense.
As for the defense, almost all of the starters look like they're hurt anyway. Linebackers T.J. Edwards and D'Marco Jackson sat out the last practice. Safety/CB Cam Lewis went out Saturday and missed Sunday's practice. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is still on PUP.  Starting safety Coby Bryant won't be back until mid-October.
The health situation indicates there really is no decision to make here. It's obvious.
On a scale of 1-10, how concerned are you about the Bears' training camp injuries? (10 being the most concerned) Vote on today's SportsClick poll to let us know! Sponsored by The Joint Relief Institute https://t.co/fK3ohvgtIS
About the only thing there is to see for coaches is special teams coordinator Richard Hightower could sort out things between young players in pecking order for coverage and blocking one his units for punts and kickoffs. They don't get enough full-contact work in practices and can use it in games.
This is the only thing coaches really need to see.
Training camp and preseason are about the bottom of the roster, anyway. There's nothing so pressing that the starters need to be out there and the backups and bottom feeders of the roster need the time to try and win one of the very few spots that will be open to new players beyond their 2026 draft picks.
On defense, it should be all about Jack Sanborn leading a group of substitutes.
On offense, it's Tyson Bagent's time of year.  In the last three preseasons, he is 83 of 123 for 874 yards with seven TDs, two interceptions for a 100.12 passer ratting. He should be adding more passes to that total, and they're not meaningless. You can never tell when a backup QB will need to play and they need to have their timing down, as well.
Chicago Bears Injuries: #Bears pic.twitter.com/IsAdp9IUSp

title: The Good and Not So Good From Day 11 of Chicago Bears Training Camp
full_text:
The Chicago Bears held their "Varsity Bears" event on Monday and also had their 11th practice of training camp during it.
But the Bears didn't hold a full practice and instead just had a walk-through before they hold a scrimmage on Tuesday that will feature full pads and hitting , head coach Ben Johnson said.
Because it was just a walkthrough, there wasn't a ton to glean off the session. Here's the most notable things to come out of the practice based on beat writer observations.
Despite leaving a recent practice on a cart, Lewis was taking part in the walk-through on Monday, according to CHGO Bears' Adam Hoge .
While we still don't know how much, if any time he's going to miss, the fact that Lewis was active in the walk-through suggests he doesn't have a serious injury.
Lewis was competing for the slot cornerback job earlier in camp but has now been switched to safety full time in the wake of the injury to Coby Bryant.
Adam Hoge also reported that Zavion Thomas, who left Sunday's practice early with an injury , "doesn't appear to have much of a limp at all," which is a strong sign he doesn't have a significant injury. Thomas did not take part in the walk-through, though.
In other news, Luther Burden, who is reportedly expected to miss the entire preseason but should be ready for Week 1 , didn't seem to be walking with any limp based on the following video. Like Thomas, Burden didn't take part in the walk-through.
No limp for Luther. - cream pic.twitter.com/vXiah6l6UU
ESPN's Courtney Cronin reported earlier in the day that Thomas is not expected to miss much time and is day-to-day with soreness.
According to Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune , the list of absent players included Coby Bryant, Jaylon Jones, D'Marco Jackson and Luke Newman.
While we knew Bryant, Jones and Jackson were all injured, the fact that they weren't even present for the walk-through isn't a great sign, as even the players on the PUP list and others who have suffered injuries were at least present.
In addition to that, if Newman's absence was injury-related, he is a new member of the walking wounded at Bears training camp.

title: Why I'm Buying the Early Chicago Bears Hype Around Jordan van den Berg
full_text:
You would have to be living under a rock to avoid the hype surrounding Jordan van den Berg over the first two weeks of training camp. His teammates have raved about him at every opportunity , and he's already receiving first-team reps in practice.
Grady Jarrett on Jordan Van Den Berg: “I think that guy is super athletic, he has a super bright future. He’s still learning a lot and he’s hungry to learn. We’re excited to have him and I think he would be a huge addition to the room and we would continue to have someone who… pic.twitter.com/DYhTzwxALi
However, it can often be difficult to know what to trust at this stage of training camp. We've seen countless players look like phenoms in early August only to disappear when the regular season begins.
If the hype proves to be legit, then the sixth-round selection has probably already locked up his roster spot . Investing a heavy amount of belief in a late-round pick usually seems like a dangerous proposition, but there are a few reasons why the excitement seems justified in this instance.
The Georgia Tech product has a near-perfect Relative Athletic Score. He blew every drill out of the water at his Pro Day, and that type of athleticism is tough to find.
Jordan Van den Berg was drafted in round 6 with pick 213 in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 10.00 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 2 out of 2278 DT from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/iW4K4xO8ZS pic.twitter.com/jestNjaHJp
The only reason he was available as late as he was is that he is raw, but his physical traits could give him a baseline that sees him contributing while still learning on the fly. We might be seeing that happen in real time.
It'll probably take some time before he develops into an early-down threat. However, the team can rotate him in on passing downs to make the most of his traits right out of the gate. It wouldn't be surprising to see him finish the year with a couple of sacks if that comes to fruition.
Players hype up their teammates all the time. While the sheer amount of praise Jordan van den Berg has received is definitely promising, it's far from out of the ordinary.
Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen giving his flowers to a sixth-round selection, and then reinforcing that praise via first-team reps in practice can appropriately be classified as "out of the ordinary", though. He always speaks his mind, and he also gave the rookie a glowing review last week.
"He's really taken to the coaching, and he plays with great pad level," Allen said. "He can get in a good stance and come off and strike at the line of scrimmage, and he's got some really good football instincts. He plays extremely hard. A lot of the things we saw on the tape at Georgia Tech, we're seeing a lot of those same athletic qualities show up."
#Bears DC Dennis Allen on Jordan van den Berg pic.twitter.com/Sv2KGGR7Wg
Allen's thoughts were shared by former All-Pro offensive lineman Terron Armstead, who went to practice last week after working with the team's offensive line this offseason. He might not know van den Berg's name, but he thinks it could soon become a household one.
"They got a young guy, [number] 96 (van den Berg), I believe he's a rookie, he's impressive," Armstead said. "Pad level. He's twitchy. He's relentless. He has a motor. Still has things to learn of course, he's super young, but there's a lot of upside there. I apologize I don't have the name, but he'll make you learn his name soon."
The local media (and Armstead) also has nothing to gain from reporting inaccurate information in July and August, when fans are pining for virtually any news from camp. Training camp performances can be deceiving, but yellow journalism isn't exactly prevalent at this time of the year. Everyone is excited for the season, and bad reviews get just as many clicks as good ones.
With that said, it's also notable that virtually everyone is impressed with what they've seen from the sixth-round pick so far. We have to take the local media's word as bond when it comes to JVDB's performance, and he's received nothing but glowing reviews so far.
He'll have to flash in the preseason games (unless he doesn't play much in them, which would be telling) to sustain the momentum, but he still seems like a relative lock to make the roster at this point. The hype seems as real as it possibly could at this stage.

title: Chicago Bears Finally Get Some Positive Injury News in the Secondary
full_text:
It has been a rough training camp for the Chicago Bears when it comes to injuries , and that has been especially true in the secondary.
At the outset of training camp, both Kyler Gordon and Elijah Hicks were placed on the PUP list, and then it only took one padded practice before the Bears lost Coby Bryant for what could be around eight to 10 weeks, per reports.
Dallis Flowers and Gervarrius Owens have landed on injured reserve, and Jaylon Jones, Cam Lewis and Terell Smith have gotten injured at practice and missed time.
However, believe it or not, the Bears actually received some good injury news on Monday, as Lewis was taking part in the team's walkthrough.
"Good sign: Cam Lewis is out here participating in today’s walk-thru at Stevenson HS. He left practice on Saturday and did not practice yesterday," CHGO Bears' Adam Hoge reported.
That is obviously great news for the Bears after Lewis needed to be carted off the sideline following his injury . It also gives hope Lewis won't be sidelined for long.
A free-agent acquisition of the Bears during the offseason, Lewis was expected to provide depth at safety and nickel cornerback when he signed in March.
But now Lewis has an opportunity for a significant role right away, and he might have a few avenues to get it.
Lewis was competing against Jaylon Jones and Malik Muhammad for the slot cornerback role with Gordon sidelined, but the Bears moved him over to safety after Bryant's injury.
Lewis played the majority of his snaps at safety during his six years with the Buffalo Bills, but he also had nearly 500 snaps played in the slot in that span.
We're already beginning to see why Lewis was an attractive addition for the Bears, as his versatility could come in handy during the 2026 campaign.

title: Chicago Bears Position Battle Updates After Week 2 of Training Camp
full_text:
The Chicago Bears caught the NFL by surprise last year, winning an NFC North championship and pulling off a miraculous Wild Card win over the Green Bay Packers . But this is a new season, and head coach Ben Johnson months ago made it clear that nothing the team accomplished in 2025 will have any bearing on 2026. Everyone has to start at 0-0 and prove they deserve a playoff spot.
After the usual roster turnover this offseason, the Bears entered training camp with a few starting positions up for grabs, primarily at left tackle, center, and cornerback. Have they gained any clarity on these position battles after two weeks of practice? Let's take a look.
As Ozzy Trapilo continues to recover from his season-ending ruptured patellar tendon, the Bears are once again in need of a starting left tackle for Week 1. Braxton Jones entered training camp as the favorite to win the starting job and has kept his challengers at bay through two weeks of practice. Bears reporter Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune confirmed on SiriusXM NFL radio on Monday that Jones has been reliably consistent in camp thus far.
Jones did leave training camp practice with an injury last week, but Ben Johnson told Bears reporters Adam Hoge and Adam Jahns on Saturday that it's not a serious injury. I would say that as long as Jones recovers sometime before the Bears' final preseason game, he's a lock to be the Week 1 starter.
Additionally, the latest Ozzy Trapilo injury update is terrific news for the Bears, as Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported on Monday that Trapilo could be back earlier than expected.
When the Bears drafted Logan Jones with a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft , I expected there to be a fierce training camp battle between the rookie and veteran Garrett Bradbury for the starting center spot. Instead, Bradbury has taken all the reps with the starters while Jones as worked with the backups.
Barring a significant injury to Bradbury, it looks like the Bears' center competition has already been decided .
With Kyler Gordon starting training camp on the PUP list (Physically Unable to Perform) and no end in sight, the Bears found themselves in need of not one but two starting cornerbacks, one to play slot and the other to play on the boundary opposite of Jaylon Johnson. Unfortunately for the Bears, neither position battle is anywhere close to settled.
Injuries are the main culprit in these starting roles remaining in flux. After Coby Bryant was carted off from practice with a leg injury , Cam Lewis, who had been taking reps in the slot, was moved into Bryant's place. Lewis himself was then injured, though it sounds like he's going to be okay after a short recovery. Rookie Malik Muhammad got some first-team reps at the slot, but that's a tough position for a rookie to play.
As for the boundary, Tyrique Stevenson was expected to be one of the top candidates for this role at the start of camp, but he continues to struggle with consistency, the No. 1 thing that Dennis Allen wants from his defense in training camp . Muhammad was another contender for the job, but, as aforementioned, he is a rookie and may need more time to develop.
At the end of the day, I can't say for certain that there's any clarity on the slot and boundary cornerback position battles, even after two weeks of practice. Hopefully, these minor injuries stop occurring and Dennis Allen will at least be able to work with the same unit consistently rather than cycling through multiple players.

title: Bears Go From Top Regression Candidate to an Elite Power Ranking
full_text:
As preseason gets set to open for the rest of the NFL besides the first Bears regular-season opponent, Carolina, and the Arizona Cardinals, the words of coach Ben Johnson stood out even more.
Earlier in camp he had what seemed to be a cloaked war of words with Jaguars coach Liam Coen and actually took a shot at the offseason media forecasts for the Bears as well.
"Well, we're the No. 1 regression candidate ," Johnson retorted after Coen had been complaining about how much media coverage Caleb Williams gets and the prime-time dates the Bears have as opposed to his team and QB Trevor Lawrence.
True enough, the offseason has been full of the Bears named as regression candidates. Whether it was CBS Sports, Sports Illustrated, ESPN, NFL.com or any number of other outlets, the Bears are always named among top regression candidates and it's usually based on their toughest NFL schedule and how they won so many close games while winning the takeaway battle, as well. Then there are the Caleb Williams doubters who don't see him as capable of raising his completion percentage. That's an entirely different level of anti-Bears rhetoric.
Bears regression in 2026-27 is going to hit like a truck🤯 • 11 wins, but only a +26 point differential • Expected record was just 9.1–7.9 • NFL-best +22 turnover margin, even if they remain good at taking the ball away and get like a +10 thats still 12 less possessions… pic.twitter.com/LprPTILEsZ
What's important is how most of the predictions call for the Bears to decline, even though Vegas hasn't seen this as a likely path.
With preseason, various power rankings come out or come into sharper focus and few are calling the Bears a top team. That is, except for one. USA Today's Nate Davis is a veteran at putting out their power rankings and has never been particularly soft on the Bears. Davis has the Bears ranked a startling fifth overall. They're ahead of the San Francisco 49ers, Houston Texans and both Detroit (10th) and Green Bay (14th).
USA Today power ranked the Bears at No. 5 in the NFL entering the new season. @DavidHaugh envisions that as a "best-case scenario. He thinks it's more likely the Bears are a tier below that because of a "spotty" defense. pic.twitter.com/bDyLqnyuo3
Only the Rams (1), Seattle (2), Denver (3) and Buffalo (4) rate higher than the Bears in his power rankings.
Davis acknowledges all of their training camp secondary injuries, "But if an offense with so many young players at the skill positions can take a dramatic leap in Year 2 under Ben Johnson, then a team that reached the divisional round last season could well take the next step … maybe even two."
The next step would be the NFC Championship Game and two would be the, gasp, Super Bowl.
Last year camp was very similar to this year. The intensity was very high and players got banged up. Dialing down the intensity is only going to allow complacency come the regular season! In a season where the #Bears have expectations and the regression police on our tail, Ben…
While this has to tickle Bears fans, even the most staunch supporters have to admit this is a reach to put them fifth. This is a team with pass rush and run defense as its biggest weakness last year. and the only thing they did to improve it was add backup help at tackle and get back an edge in Dayo Odeyingbo who hadn't done anything before suffering a Achilles tear. He looks remarkably healthy now considering it's only nine-plus months later but his production was the issue last year for half a season.
There's one very good reason to think such a high ranking is possible and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen touched on it Sunday at his press conference prior to practice. He had just come back from Canton, Ohio and the Hall of Fame induction for Drew Brees. Allen doesn't necessarily like comparing coaches but couldn't help but see the similarities between Johnson and his former Saints boss, current Broncos coach Sean Payton.
“I mean, I think I see a lot of the same qualities in terms of how the attacking mindset and not just how we practice offensively, but how we practice in general," Allen said. "The physicality and the effort level that's required is very similar to what we did in those years under Sean in New Orleans.
"So, you know, there's a lot of similarities as to how they coach and philosophically how they see the game.”
“I see a lot of the same qualities…there’s a lot of similarities in how they coach and philosophically how they see the game.” Dennis Allen on Ben Johnson & Sean Payton: pic.twitter.com/GWowXRVlr3
If Johnson rates up there already with Payton, a coach who has his team in the top three of these rankings, then perhaps this No. 5 rating isn't so wild after all. Someone with this type of resume can keep a team in Super Bowl consideration for long periods.
However, it's still a shock to the system to see such respect after so many predictions of collapse. And it also makes Johnson's retort to Coen a little less valid.

title: Ja’Marr Chase Names 3 Bengals Who Are Standing Out at Training Camp
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase knows what it takes for a receiver to stand out in the NFL.
He's done it himself — and now he says he's seeing it in two newcomers who have caught the 26-year-old superstar's attention. When Kay Adams recently asked Chase which teammates had impressed him at training camp, the All-Pro wideout named Colbie Young and former CFL standout Dohnte Meyers.
“Colbie’s been making big plays,” Chase told Adams. “Dohnte’s been making plays with the ones.”
The two receivers are taking different routes through a crowded WR room. Young is a fourth-round draft pick expected to develop behind Cincinnati's established stars, Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers is trying to turn a strong summer into a spot on the 53-man roster or the practice squad. Earning recognition from Chase is a promising sign for both.
Young, picked No. 140 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, gives the Bengals another big-bodied target behind Higgins. The six-foot-three, 215-pound Georgia product has used his size to make several contested catches during his first NFL training camp.
Meanwhile, Meyers has been given fewer opportunities on offense, but Chase has noticed how productive he's been when those chances arise.
“He gets in with the ones every couple — maybe he has like three or four plays out of the whole day with the ones — and he makes plays with the ones,” Chase said. “So that’s a big step.”
The 26-year-old Meyers spent the past two seasons with the Saskatchewan Roughriders before signing with the Bengals in January. He recorded 89 receptions for 1,405 yards and nine touchdowns in the CFL. He also has experience returning both kickoffs and punts, which could help his case in a roster battle.
Chase singled out DJ Turner II on the opposing side. The two have regularly competed against each other in practice, giving Chase a close look at the 2023 second-round pick's development.
“DJ’s been playing pretty good in camp. He’s been playing a little different,” Chase said. “I told him about himself earlier.”
Chase declined to disclose what he told Turner privately but said his teammate appears to be playing with more confidence and embracing his style. Turner is coming off a breakout season in which he recorded 18 pass deflections, one of the NFL's highest totals in just 16 starts.
Turner already has a starting role and is trying to build on a career year. Young and Mayers still have much more to prove. Their next opportunities will come in the preseason, when both receivers can show that the plays drawing Chase's attention in practice will translate to games.

title: Jordan Battle's Interception of Joe Burrow Adds Juice to Bengals D in Final Tune-up Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
Tuesday’s Cincinnati Bengals practice was light on participation, tight on space and slight on activity.
Numerous players dealing with tightness and tweaks took the day off for the final practice before Thursday night’s preseason opener against the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium.
It also was the second practice in five days forced inside due to weather, as storm clouds and rain rolled in about 30 minutes into the session.
Once inside the indoor facility, the Bengals only ran one period of 11-on-11. The first drive by the first-team offense ended with the defensive highlight of the day, with Jordan Battle ranging over from his single-high alignment to intercept a Joe Burrow deep ball intended for Ja’Marr Chase.
Jordan Battle reads the deep ball from Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase perfectly and makes the pick. pic.twitter.com/6yhIpCUTK0
It was the second time in Battle’s four-year career that he has intercepted Burrow in a training camp practice, with the first coming last year, also during an indoor session.
“Very rare,” Battle said. “I was more of a robber last year. This time I was out in the middle of the field.”
“It's all about knowing where Uno (Chase) is on the field," Battle said. "When you're playing middle of the field, you've just got to know certain things, see the quarterback's shoulder -- if it's high, it it's low -- so you can go from breaking down to breaking high.
“I was just reading his eyes and seeing the release of Uno,” he continued. “I saw him going deep, and just breaking before the throw allows you to make plays. I was happy he threw it because I knew I had a chance to make a play, and I did.”
Battle recorded a career-high four interceptions last year after snaring just one in each of his first two seasons in the league.
His four last year were tied for the fourth most in the league among safeties. They also are tied for the fourth most by a safety in Bengals history behind Reggie Nelson (eight, 2015), Kevin Kaseviharn (six, 2006) and Shawn Williams (five, 2018).
While practice picks don’t mean much in the overall picture, Battle said they do have value.
“They keep the energy up and gets us started,” he said. “After that, they fumbled a snap and we had a couple (tackles for loss). It’s just a spark for the defense. Obviously you don’t have momentum in practice, so we create momentum for ourselves.
“I feel like we’ve been doing a good job of that all training camp.”
Battling it out. pic.twitter.com/eNPiP8yIlh
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed the starters will play some Thursday against the Lions, although Battle's running mate at safety, Bryan Cook, will not be one of them. Nor will cornerback Dax Hill as both defensive backs deal with soft tissue tweaks.
Battle said he’s happy about Taylor's decision.
Obviously, you don’t want the first regular-season game to be the first time you’re tackling somebody. That can lead to bad things,” he said. “So I love the idea of playing in preseason games, being able to go out there and work on those things now so I don’t have to worry about them in Week 1.
“I’m ready to put my pads on and hit somebody else and take them to the ground,” he added. “It’s a long offseason. It feels like the time is finally here. I’m excited for this defense. I’m excited for myself. I’m excited to see what we do as a team. It’s been looking good. Let’s hope we continue on that path.”
Burrow, as he’s wont to do, got revenge on the defense on the next drive, marching the offense to the 2-yard line after hitting Andrei Iosivas on a slant to set up first and goal.
Burrow’s pass for Chase at the front pylon was broken up by Josh Newton. But Burrow went back to the same spot, only this time with Tee Higgins as the target, and the receiver made a one-handed snag and somehow tapped both feet as he was flying out of bounds at the pylon.

title: Joe Burrow Feeling 'Winning-Level Football' From Bengals Additions as Opening Preseason Game Approaches
full_text:
Joe Burrow seemingly can't stop gushing about the importance of Dexter Lawrence and all of the new additions for Cincinnati this offseason.
The Bengals' top star sat down with Kay Adams on Up & Adams this week, and he dove into all of the pieces fitting together in a championship puzzle.
"Yeah, of course, of course he's part of that," Burow noted on the show about Lawrence's championship impact. "But also, a lot of the guys that we've added this off-season: Boye (Mafe), Jonathan (Allen), Bryan Cook, getting DJ Turner back, Dax Hill back, Jalen Davis on the inside. We've got a lot of guys that we feel confident in that can go out and produce and play winning-level football."
Burrow is slated to suit up in the preseason opener on Thursday night for his first game action since closing the 2025 season in January.
Lawrence is firing out of the gates and playing alongside him as plenty of Bengals' starters get a taste of live ball against Detroit. The big fella has had fun prodding his new offensive leader in the early days of training camp.
On Day 1, Lawrence came at "the king" a little bit on and off the field. He's disrupting plenty of passing reps and had a little something to declare before that impact even started.
"I wanna see it today, Mr. Burrow," Dan Hoard noted Lawrence said on Day 1 before practice started.
"You can see it every day, brother," Burrow responded.
It's all in good fun as the chemistry and on-field execution grows throughout the rest of this month and beyond.
"Somebody has to challenge the King of the Jungle, as they say," said Lawrence after that practice. "Somebody has to keep him on edge for him to get better and grow. That competitive spirit won't stop. And with a guy like that, I know he's going to bring it. It's going to be fun."

title: Chase Brown Showers Bengals' Defense with Praise During Training Camp Interview
full_text:
There are plenty of storylines for Cincinnati Bengals fans to focus on as the team prepares for their first preseason game against the Detroit Lions on Thursday .
For example, there are many talents on the offensive side of the ball that have earned headline praise, which includes running back Chase Brown.
During a recent interview with the NFL Network, the Bengals' running back discussed his goals for the 2026 season as well as giving some high praise to the defensive side of the ball.
"They've been doing a really good job during this training camp," Brown said when asked about the team's defense. "I feel comfortable saying this, that's a top ten, top five defense."
That is some high praise for a unit that was one of the worst in the NFL just a season ago. Last year, the Bengals allowed the second most yards per game at 380.9. When it came to yards allowed on the ground, the Bengals allowed the most per game with 147.1.
Revamping this defense was a must, and the front office delivered. The Bengals' defensive line is going to look completely different this season, and the team even added some veteran secondary help.
The newest additions to this defense making the biggest impacts are defensive linemen Dexter  Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, edge rusher Boye Mafe, and safety Bryan Cook.
It's been clear very early on in camp that this isn't the defense that Bengals fans are used to seeing. In a recent practice , Lawrence got a little too close for comfort to quarterback Joe Burrow. That has been one of the most talked about moments online with fans, but the play is a great example of what this defense needs to be.
No one wants to see Burrow hurt before a game is even played, but that wasn't Lawrence's intention. This defense is sending a message that if you don't want them to get to your quarterback, then you better stop them. Iron sharpens iron, and for the Bengals, each practice is making both units better.
The preparations are being made for a memorable season. Check out the full interview below:

title: Zac Taylor Details Starter Playing Time, Latest Bengals Injury Update Ahead of 2026 Preseason Opener
full_text:
Zac Taylor held his latest press conference on Tuesday morning after an indoor Bengals practice during training camp.
The biggest topic of the day is injury updates on a bevy of players across the defense . Names like Dax Hill and B.J. Hill got updates as both try to work back into practice.
Hill is still on the physically unable to perform list, but has increased his workload on the rehab field in recent days. Meanwhile, Dax Hill has missed three consecutive practices to go with no Tuesday action for Bryan Cook, Cashius Howell, Tacario Davis.
Taylor dropped updates for all of those players below. Tacario Davis and Cashius Howell: "I think that's why I'm a little limited right now, just on some guys that we're kind of limiting day to day and making decisions for on Thursday, so I'm not quick enough right now to say who's gonna be full go yet because there's just some guys that I just really want to manage through this week and we'll make some decisions if they're playing tomorrow or not. "But those guys, there's nothing long-term on them. It's just we kind of get out there some days, decide for that day if we're gonna put them out there." Dax Hill and Bryan Cook: "They will not play in this game, so we'll get them through the week and then see where that lands going into next week." B.J. Hill and Shemar Stewart: "We won't put a timeline on them, but they're both progressing as we would hope that they would."
It's a lighter workweek of practice for Cincinnati. Tuesday is the only weekday practice session on the schedule, with Thursday's preseason opener on the docket against Detroit.
Taylor is eager to see what this expanded Bengals roster looks like in live game action. That includes the starters, who Taylor reaffirmed will play.
"The starters will play, but I'm not there yet on everybody," Taylor said. "Joe (Burrow) will play. Ja'Marr (Chase) and Tee (Higgins as well). Will kind of announce everything for tomorrow at some point.
"Limited series, so it won't be a ton of time ... (Fans are) going to see Joe and Ja'Marr and Tee. They're going to see Dexter (Lawrence). So they'll get a chance to enjoy some of our players there. But how long they keep them out there remains to be seen."
Cincinnati takes on the Lions at 7 p.m. ET on Thursday in Paycor Stadium.
