title: Bengals Veteran Defensive End is Being Overlooked in Latest Preseason Rankings
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are seemingly putting all their chips into the 2026 season. Sure, one could say that every team does that every season. However, not every team has the talent the Bengals do coming into the new season.
After a few disappointing runs that resulted in the Bengals missing the playoffs, it feels like the pressure is on this campaign. It also seems from those who are getting the chance to watch the team during training camp that this is arguably the most talented team head coach Zac Taylor has had in Cincinnati .
There are stars on both sides of the ball coming into this season.
Pro Football Focus recently ranked the top 32 edge defenders in the NFL. Bengals pass rusher Boye Mafe made the list at number 24.
"Mafe’s performance dropped a bit in his fourth season in the league, but he did still earn a PFF grade above 70.0 for the third straight season. In 2023, he set career highs with 58 pressures and a 77.8 PFF pass-rush grade, while his best season as a run defender came in 2024, also coming in at 77.8," wrote Gordon McGuinness . "If Mafe can combine those highs in a single season, then he can become a force on a Bengals defensive line that lost Trey Hendrickson to free agency this year."
Losing Hendrickson was a blow to this defense. But the potential is there for Mafe to rise on a defensive front that's going to look completely different this season.
Two of the biggest additions to the Bengals' roster this season have been defensive tackles Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Lawrence and Allen bring a veteran presence, as well as elite talent that will be focused on by opposing offenses.
Having multiple Pro Bowlers to clog up the middle is going to give the edges an incredible opportunity to make noise this season.
It appears that many do not believe Mafe can be an even top 20 talent on the edge for the Bengals this season. The only thing left for Mafe to do is make everyone eat their words.

title: Bengals Talent Projected to Make NFL All-Rookie Team Ahead of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Bengals may have a dark horse All-Rookie candidate on their defense.
NFL.com's Gennaro Filice released his full All-Rookie team projections for the 2026 season, and Cashius Howell was one of his first-team edge rusher picks.
The second-round pick is going to get some more rep exposure than normal over the foreseeable future with Shemar Stewart on the mend. He was the only Bengal to make this All-Rookie projection .
"I guess I really don't care about arm length," Filice said about Howell's historically short arms. "Howell's measurement was even shorter than Rueben Bain Jr.'s at 30 1/4 inches, which helps explain why the reigning SEC Defensive Player of the Year fell into Round 2. The undersized defensive end could be a liability on early downs, but Cincinnati didn't draft the 6-3, 255-pounder to stop the run. With Trey Hendrickson now playing for the rival Ravens, the Bengals need guys to heat opposing quarterbacks.
"Last year's first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, proved to be as raw as many feared, so Cincy went back to the Texas A&M edge factory for a different model. As a speed ball with a deep bag of tricks, Howell has the kind of refined skill set that can provide immediate returns in a DPR (designated pass rusher) role. For comparison's sake, Howell had more sacks last October (5.5) than Stewart had in his three-season college career (4.5). So, yes, I expect Howell to blow past Stewart's rookie sack total of one."
Howell is hungry to prove his doubters wrong this coming season, and performing well enough to make an All-Rookie team would do just that.
He spoke about the noise with FOX 19's Gabi Sorrentino after the first day of Bengals training camp.
"What I'm looking forward to the most is just going out there and proving myself. Just, just really showcasing what I could do," Howell told Sorrentino. "I know there's been a lot of doubts, you know, within my game. Just, just really going out there and showcasing that my game does actually translate to the next level, and that I'm here to stay."
Howell was a monster AP first-team All-American performer last season, and it vaulted him to SEC Defensive Player of the Year status. The edge rusher tied for seventh in the FBS with 11.5 sacks and started all 13 games.

title: Duke Tobin Sees Confidence in Bengals Roster, Believes in Young Players
full_text:
Duke Tobin sees the confidence continuing to grow to new heights with the Bengals' current roster during training camp. Tobin appeared on The Tony And Mo Football Show on ESPN 1530 during the team's training camp practice inside Paycor Stadium and spoke about the confidence he has seen from the roster.
"I see confidence in our guys, one thing that I always look for is early confidence in what we're doing, how we're doing it, and belief in the group as a whole," Tobin said. "I see that out there on both sides of the ball, whether the ones are in there, the twos are in there, or the threes are in there, you can see a real attention to detail and motivation out of it."
Tobin also confirmed that the volume of versatility used for players such as Kyle Dugger and Dexter Lawrence has not resulted in any miscues on either side of the ball.
"My head spins when I sit in some meetings about the volume thats there, but the execution of the volume has been so good and it hasn't been sloppy in any way," Tobin said of the teams positional versatility volume. "We haven't had a bunch of false starts, misalignments, open gaps, drop coverages. With the volume we have in that'll play well over the season."
When the Bengals added players like Bryan Cook, Jonathan Allen, and Dexter Lawrence, it was clear they targeted players capable of leading a young locker room on defense.
Tobin emphasized the approach of adding talent that loves football enough and is capable of leading a team.
"You gotta get the guys about the right things, they have to love ball. Whether they're at the top of the league or just coming into the league, they have to love ball," Tobin said on the values he looks for in players. "If they don't, they can get complacent and one guy can turn into two guys can turn into 10 guys that get complacent, right now the leaders on this team are anything but complacent."
Tobin doubled down on his faith in linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. improving across the second-year of their respective careers.
"There is a huge jump between year one and year two, and when you bring two guys in and you throw them right into the fire, you're going to have some growing pains," Tobin spoke on the struggles at linebacker.
"Those two guys are much more comfortable in what we're doing, they're much more willing and able to direct. As those guys have progressed, they have really gained confidence in what they're doing and now their ability can show."
Tobin also shares the sentiment that the team's rookie class must make an impact immediately this season.
"We need our young guys to come on, it's just the way the NFL is now. You've gotta have your young guys come on and find roles early in their career and then take bigger roles the second year or third year," Tobin stated of his expectations for the teams rookies.
"It used to be where you could red-shirt guys and it's just not the way the NFL is anymore, you need those young guys to find real roles."
Tobin and the rest of the Bengals front office did a stellar job of adding talent to the Bengals roster this offseason. Now the expectations are for Zac Taylor and the coaching staff to continue getting the best out of the current roster and compete for a Super Bowl this season.

title: Bengals Cornerback DJ Ivey Proving He's Worthy of a Bigger Role - Just Ask Tee Higgins
full_text:
Walking into the locker room after Sunday’s long, physical practice, Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins was lamenting the heat and humidity he and his teammates endured for the longest session of training camp.
But Higgins also pointed the temperature wasn’t the only thing taking a toll on him.
Asked about his touchdown reception from quarterback Joe Burrow, in which he high pointed the ball against DJ Ivey, Higgins was quick to praise how challenging it has been going against the 2023 seventh-round pick, especially over the last few practices since starting cornerback Dax Hill has been out with leg tightness.
Tee-D pic.twitter.com/ym7Py1Ma2S
“He’s gotten me better,” Higgins said. “He’s really pushed me.”
Told of Higgins’ praise, Ivey said it meant a lot.
“It feels good,” he said. “I mean, I’ve been battling him for the last few practices. And that’s gotten me better. So it feels good to hear that from a top five receiver in the league.”
Ivey looked defeated after Higgins’ touchdown, as if he was muttering to himself “what in the heck am I supposed to do to stop that.”
Burrow and Higgins have been connecting on those sort of passes for seven seasons.
Ivey has six career pass defenses on just 195 snaps.
“I knew it was a high possibility that he was gonna get the ball,” he said of Higgins. “I thought he was gonna do a stutter go, or maybe just a fade. I knew it was coming to him.
“It’s hard to tell what I could have done differently,” Ivey said. ““Obviously Tee’s a big target and Joe is putting the ball in a spot where only Tee could make the play,” Ivey added. “He’s one of the best five receivers in the league. I just have to try to make the play.”
The tape doesn’t lie, and neither do the reps. That means Ivey is a lock to make the 53-man roster for the fourth consecutive season.
“DJ Ivey is as consistent as ever,” defensive coordinator Al Golden said.
Ivey said that’s because even four seasons into his career, he still has the seventh-round chip on his shoulder after being the 246th player drafted out of 259 in 2023.
“Every camp I go into, I, go in as if I'm at the bottom of the barrel and just got to work my way up,” he said. “All my life I've, I've been working. So there's no difference in what I'm doing here. I’ve just got to keep putting in the work to stay here.
While he hasn’t seen the field much on defense, Ivey has been a strong special teams player for coordinator Darrin Simmons.
What’s made Ivey’s performance this summer even more impressive is that the team is not adjusting his special teams snaps in correlation to the increase in defensive reps he’s been getting.
Ivey’s 273 special teams snaps in 2025 were the third most of the team behind Oren Burks (385) and Tycen Anderson (382).
Anderson signed with the Broncos this offseason, so Ivey could be in line for an even bigger role on special teams.
“It’s been tiring at times in camp, but in the end it’ll be good,” Ivey said. “No, in the end it will be great. So I can’t think about it in the moment. Just have to keep working.
“I want to be the best gunner in the league,” he added. “I want to make the Pro Bowl and be a special teams leader for us.”
The Bengals listed Ivey as the backup nickel corner to Jalen Davis on their first depth chart of the season Sunday.
He hasn’t played there much in camp as those reps have mostly gone to Davis, Ja’Sir Taylor and Bralyn Lux.
But Ivey is carving out a role not only as the first outside corner off the bench, but as a specialist in covering tight ends.
He is certain to have a role in 2026. It’s just a question of how big it will be.

title: New Star Defensive Tackle Contract Adds Even More Value to Dexter Lawrence Contract Amidst 2026 Training Camp
full_text:
Dexter Lawrence just keeps becoming a bigger and bigger bargain for the Bengals.
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that the Cowboys inked Quinnen Williams to a new three-year extension to end his contract demands.
"Sources: The Cowboys and star DL Quinnen Williams have agreed to terms on a three-year, $105.9M extension to make him one of the highest-paid DLs. The deal, done by Nicole Lynn of Klutch Sports, is the largest third-contract ever for a DL and secures Williams’ future in Dallas."
It just makes the deal Cincinnati gave to Lawrence even more of a value after Jalen Carter also resigned this offseason to reset the market.
According to Spotrac , Lawrence is on an average yearly salary of $28 million with Cincinnati and was the fourth-highest-paid interior defensive lineman entering the day, but now he is No. 5 behind Carter ($38 million), Quinnen Williams ($35.3 million average on his new deal), Jeffery Simmons ($35.27 million), and Chris Jones ($31.75 million).
Lawrence is slated to take up just 4.8% of the 2026 salary cap (maxes at 8.7% in 2028, 7.4% next year). Cincinnati is getting a bigger steal by the day for a player wrecking training camp so far.
Defensive coordinator Al Golden discussed his early impact last week.
"Dex is everything you would imagine that he is," Golden declared. "He came back in great shape, and I think that's a testament to him and his work ethic and his energy, renewed energy and his focus. So he's powerful. We're going to continue to work to get him to beat blocks. His middle push is significant, so he's doing a great job of buying in and being a leader for us.
"Again, upstairs did a tremendous job, giving us depth and versatility. And I think I said back to the first day or before the first day, we're trying to find out what we do best too, and our guys are putting on film every day what we do best, and we're making little adaptations daily to make sure that we are using them the way they should be."
The roster build in 2026 just keeps looking better and better from the Bengals front office.
Something to keep in mind with Dexter Lawrence who is from the same 2019 draft class as Quinnen Williams. title: 5 Cleveland Browns Players Who Need a Big Preseason and Why
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have finished their installations and are beginning to seriously prepare for their preseason games.
On Saturday, the Browns will travel to Chicago to face the Bears. They’ll return to Cleveland for a joint practice with the Buffalo Bills before hosting them at Huntington Bank Field in preseason Week 2. After that, the Browns round out their preseason with a dress rehearsal against the AFC Championship winning New England Patriots.
Browns coach Todd Monken has alluded to starters participating in the preseason, even though there isn’t any clarity yet on which players will play and when.
Regardless of that, let’s take a look at a handful of Browns players who need to have a big preseason.
As has been the case all training camp, Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will have all the attention during the preseason. Unless Monken changes his mind, each quarterback will have an opportunity to start a preseason game.
Recently, the Browns have given more starting reps to Watson, illustrating that he could potentially be the leader of this competition . If he starts against the Bears, he needs to be sharp. Throughout the team’s 11 training camp sessions, the quarterbacks have combined for 17 interceptions. So a strong showing from either quarterback would be a welcomed sight for the Browns.
The Browns have already handled Jamari Thrash, who will miss the entire season with an injury. That leaves Tillman as the lone Berry draft pick fighting for a roster spot in the wide receiver room.
Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and Isaiah Bond should be treated as locks to make this roster. If the Browns keep six wideouts, that leaves just two spots for free agent Tylan Wallace, who will be a core special teamer and Tillman, who is entering his fourth pro season.
Tillman will be competing against Malachi Corley and former preseason standouts Gage Larvadain, Luke Floriea for the final receiver spot, if the Browns decide to keep six.
Harold Fannin Jr. is the unquestioned starter at tight end after leading the Browns in receiving yards last year. But the room behind him? It’s unclear.
The Browns signed Stoll in free agency before adding tight ends Joe Royer and Carsen Ryan on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft. Royer has missed all of training camp with a personal matter.
That sets up Stoll to have plenty of opportunities in the preseason, especially if Fannin doesn’t play, as the 22-year-old has been banged up since the end of last season.
On Monday, Monken promoted No. 9 overall pick Spencer Fano to the starting offensive line at training camp. The rookie had been alternating for Dawand Jones, who should have an opportunity to prove to the Browns that he’s healthy and in shape ahead of Week 1.
Jones has an opportunity to be Cleveland’s backup swing tackle, as long as Fano and veteran right tackle Tytus Howard are both ready to go Week 1. A strong preseason from Jones would give Monken and offensive line coach George Warhop the confidence to keep him ready while continuing to develop rookie Austin Barber and transitioning KT Leveston to guard depth.

title: 3 Reasons Browns May be Forced to Start Deshaun Watson Week 1
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns remain in a quarterback battle that feels never-ending. Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been competing for months , with no one named the winner as August rolls along.
It's clear at this point that neither of the two have done anything to seize the job.
Yet this reality leads to several reasons why the job may ultimately go to Watson.
Todd Monken is a first-time head coach and wants to win . He knows he could be one-and-done if the team struggles and if he feels there is no clear winner in the competition, Watson does have the track record of someone with prior NFL success.
Browns fans would argue his success was a lifetime ago in Houston. That still does give him more of a resume than Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, who struggled in 2025 as rookies.
#Browns Deshaun Watson’s 9th pick in 12 practices: pic.twitter.com/dJ3kK793Qf
Watson winning by default would be a frustrating outcome for all involved. It may also point toward another one of the reasons why the Browns have to start him Week 1.
Watson is taking home $46 million in cash this year on the final season of his $230 million contract. Naming him the backup to start the year may have him and his agent asking for an immediate trade, or to be sent home to prepare for 2027.
The veteran needs to start and play well this season to have a shot at a decent contract in 2027 and beyond. If he is named the backup, he could argue the Browns were a terrible destination for him and ask to be sent home. Doing so would prevent him from putting any play on tape in 2026, using his past hype for next offseason.
Thus, the Browns may need to at least have Watson start the season to avoid blowing up the quarterback room right before the season begins.
Jimmy Haslam is a wealthy billionaire who can afford to waste $230 million from time to time. Yet it does make some sense to start Watson, at least to begin the season, because he is making $46 million this year. He is finally healthy and the team may just want to see what they have and try to extract any value out of him.
That could mean starting him, hoping he plays well, and trading him during the season to fully move on and start anew in 2027.
Sanders was a fifth-round pick, so starting him Week 1, especially if he can't separate himself in the competition, is much different than benching Watson and potentially having him demand to be out for the full season.

title: Browns Hopeful To Get Defensive Starter Back From Injury Ahead of Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are just a few days away from their first preseason game and are still hopeful for a few players to return to practice in order to see some in-game action over the next couple of weeks.
Among those players they hope will return soon is defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr., who is still working back from an injury plagued summer. Hall hasn’t practiced since August 3rd, but Cleveland’s coaching staff seems to think he’ll be back soon.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday regarding Hall Jr. and had some positive comments on his progress to get back on the field before their Saturday matchup against the Bears.
Here’s what Monken had to say, and what a return for Hall Jr. means for the Browns moving forward.
Having Hall Jr. back on the field will be great for the Browns heading into the preseason, but there really is no rush to get him back on the field right away based on his recent injuries this summer.
Monken commented on a return for Hall Jr., saying he’s hopeful to get him back at practice soon. “He got off to such a great start”, Monken said, and a return will really help the Browns plan for their 53-man roster with defensive tackle Maliek Collins still on the PUP list .
No date has been given for Collins to make his return to the team, but it will likely be closer to the regular season if not a few weeks into the season. This matters a lot when it comes to Hall, as he’ll likely be the starter alongside Mason Graham for a few weeks.
There’s no reason to get Hall Jr. back on the field as soon as possible, especially if they will need him to fill in starting time. Knowing that he was off to a good start before this recent injury is a positive sign for the coaching staff, which also plays into why they shouldn’t rush him back.
Through two seasons with the Browns, Hall Jr. has worked his way up to being one of their contending starters on a defense that has exceeded expectations in recent years and becoming one of the better units in the NFL.
While Hall Jr. has yet to play a full season for the Browns , he is still a serviceable player when he’s on the field. In his two seasons, Hall Jr. has 25 total tackles, 12 solo tackles, and 2.5 sacks as a rotational player.
Having a veteran like Maliek Collins on the defensive line helps the Browns feel more comfortable not relying a whole lot on Hall Jr. to produce. In his increasing role, he can surely learn from having one of the better defensive tackles in the room.
Hall Jr. will surely have a larger role on defense this season, even when Collins returns to the field. Being in a new defensive scheme under Mike Rutenberg should help him fight for more reps as well.
With Graham as their unanimous starter, Hall Jr. will have a good time playing alongside their first round pick from last year. Both should benefit from having Jared Verse on the outside, and if Alex Wright can take a step forward, the pressure applied should be similar to recent years.

title: Latest Reports From Browns Training Camp Proves QB Battle Remains a Mess
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have still not named a Week 1 starting quarterback. New head coach Todd Monken continues to insist both Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will get a shot to start their own preseason game before he comes to a decision.
Reports out of camp Monday may show why Monken is taking so long.
Beat reporter Ashley Bastock shared the ugly details from the end of Monday's practice.
End of #Browns practice.  One minute end of half situation.  Sanders up first and the drive ends with two false starts on the line.  Watson next and after two completions, a sack, an illegal formation and a false start.  Monken ended practice and looked like he threw something.
The offense was in an end-of-half situation and both Sanders and Watson got a shot to show off their clutch abilities. The former kept seeing his linemen jump and the latter had a solid start, followed by a sack and several penalties.
Mary Kay Cabot confirmed the scene shared by her colleague out of Berea.
A sloppy finish for the #Browns ' offense. Shedeur Sanders' 2-min drill ended with 3 straight procedural penalties, including a false start by Spencer Fano on the final snap; Deshaun Watson's 2-min ends with a sack and 2 procedurals.
Browns fans were ready to run Kevin Stefanski out of town for all the penalties in recent seasons, especially those by his offense. The Browns offense, under both Sanders and Watson, is now having trouble avoiding penalties in practice . That is the definition of a "total mess."
It is important to point out the offense will struggle in general because the defense is so talented. But it's inexcusable to have multiple pre-snap penalties in this type of drill in August. Such a thing happening in high school summer practice would lead to players running laps for it.
Monken was reportedly so mad he was throwing things, per Bastock. That is not quite where he wanted his offense to be to start the week of the first preseason game. Fans, meanwhile, may not be so surprised.
Monken has already gone away from his stated plans over the weekend, when Sanders saw reduced reps with the first-team offense. That seemingly meant Watson was the favorite, only for the veteran to struggle to even get snaps off on Monday.
This is a nightmare situation and one that will hopefully resolve itself when the preseason games actually begin. Even then, Week 1 will tell the true tale.
The fact a competition is taking place this late in training camp does indicate the team is still set on looking for a quarterback in the 2027 Draft . That is, the front office is viewing the plan that way. Monken and his coaches are doing their best to will the players to success, even if it may ultimately be a futile effort.

title: Browns Quarterback Decision Already Impacting Todd Monken’s First Season
full_text:
Cleveland Browns’ head coach Todd Monken created some turmoil on Saturday when he tore up the rotation of starter reps among quarterbacks to keep Deshaun Watson with the first team .
One simple last-minute action, as he characterized it, has now created unwanted distraction at Browns’ camp, while pitting fans -- and possibly players -- favoring Shedeur Sanders against him.
Monken doubled-down on Monday, stating to reporters at camp that “I sure as hell wasn’t thinking on coming back down to tell you guys that I was gonna change my mind. I really don’t have to, so that’s just the way, being the head coach, I can kinda do that.”
Todd Monken explains what happened with the QB rep changes. pic.twitter.com/919LhJDSeC
On Saturday, Sanders led walkthroughs with the first team just to be demoted once the team hit the practice field, with Watson getting all starter reps.
While Monken announced that Sanders would work with the starters on Monday -- “unless on the way out I change my mind,” he joked -- the sudden switch raised some questions.
Monken justified the switch saying he was told “Shedeur has been getting a few more reps with the ones,” which led him to decide “Yeah, sure, we’ll flip it and next week we’ll go the other way.”
This statement seems pretty innocuous -- an attempt to level out the reps out between Watson and Sanders. However, Monken said back in March that reps wouldn’t be divided evenly and, until now, the Browns seemed to stay on schedule alternating between Watson and Sanders. If dividing reps equally wasn't important and there’s still time to make up for a difference, why the sudden change on Saturday?
Despite Monken saying “As long as we’re still sharing reps, it’s a competition”, the way in which said reps are shared says a lot, too.
Whether it was solely Monken, or general manager Andrew Berry and/or team owner Jimmy Haslam’s voice had any influence, we might not know for sure, but the Browns pulling Watson’s career out of the grave was certainly a remarkable turn of events during the offseason.
In a vacuum, it makes perfect sense for a team like the Browns -- who’ve been without a franchise quarterback since last century -- to open up the competition for the best passer available, but Cleveland isn’t operating in a vacuum.
According to almost anyone who has witnessed any portion of the competition in Cleveland, Watson hasn’t shown anything to suggest he should be the winner up to this point. Think about that. A 30-year old veteran who’s supposed to be in his prime, cost the team three first-round selections, a third-rounder and two fourths, and was handed a still NFL-record $230 million fully guaranteed five-year deal the moment he walked through the door can’t separate himself on a practice field from a second-year fifth rounder who’s in his very first training camp getting reps with the ones.
Given how the Browns have been managing Sanders for a year and a half, it's likely that had Watson showed any tangible evidence that could hint at viability as the team’s starter, he would have been named QB1 already. Remember, Monken wanted the competition wrapped up by minicamp.
As we said before, an open battle in Cleveland sounds like a good idea, in a vacuum. But the Browns’ chosen contender to fight it out against Sanders, who ended last year on a high note and almost universally praised in the locker room was less than ideal, to put it mildly.
Had the Browns chosen to put Sanders up against a high-to-mid round rookie, we might be witnessing a better battle. Or, maybe the Browns should have just trusted Sanders all along, as many of his teammates clearly do, tabbing Watson for a mentor-type role in the last year of his toxic deal. But the current competition doesn’t feel genuine.
Fans shouldn't determine who starts at quarterback for an NFL franchise, but having them boo your hand-picked contender at training camp can’t be good, especially when you want to sell all those PSLs for your new stadium, set to open within a few years.
Either way, Monken’s first array into the NFL head coaching business doesn’t seem to be firing on all cylinders at the most important position in the game -- ironically, his field of expertise. And his handling of the quarterback competion has opened the doors for everyone to second-guess hi, in Cleveland.

title: Quinshon Judkins Shares Great News on How He’s Feeling After Devastating Leg Injury
full_text:
Quinshon Judkins' rookie season didn't go exactly the way he thought it would.
While it was full of a handful of ups and downs, Judkins' first year in the NFL came to an end when he suffered a dislocated right ankle and fractured fibula in Week 16 against the Buffalo Bills, abruptly ending his rookie campaign.
But after making a full recovery from those injuries and preparing for his second year in the league, Judkins appears to be ready to go – and possibly even feeling better than he did a year ago.
"Definitely fortunate. Super grateful to our staff," Judkins said Monday. "I feel good. I feel the same, if not better. I had an offseason to prepare a long time for. And even just making it through rehab, I think that was his own journey."
#Browns RB Quinshon Judkins on how he's feeling this summer following an offseason of rehabbing his leg injury: "I feel good. I feel the same, if not better. I had an offseason to prepare a long time for. And even just making it through rehab, I think that was his own journey." pic.twitter.com/K3tM8iCkb0
Before suffering his season-ending injury, Judkins had 230 carries for 827 yards and nine touchdowns while adding 26 catches for 171 yards in 14 games. Despite missing three games, the 2025 second-round pick finished third in rushing yards among rookies, behind only Ashton Jeanty (266 carries for 975 rushing yards and five touchdowns in 17 games) and fellow Ohio State Buckeye TreVeyon Henderson (180 carries for 911 rushing yards and nine scores in 17 games).
It was a rookie campaign that was filled with plenty of ups and downs for Judkins. He had more than 20 carries in five games and amassed at least 80 rushing yards in four games. In four of his first five NFL games, he had at least 80 yards on the ground. Judkins' two best games were when he notched 23 carries for 110 yards in Week 5 against the Minnesota Vikings, and 25 carries for 84 yards and three touchdowns in a Week 7 win over the Miami Dolphins, one of the Browns' five wins last season.
As a rookie, Judkins led the Browns in touches (256), first downs (50) and was tied with Harold Fannin for the most touchdowns (seven) on the team.
But Judkins totaled just 34 carries for 69 yards in his last three games before he suffered the season-ending injury. It was a three-game stretch when he averaged only 2.0 yards per carry and didn't score a touchdown.
In 2026, Judkins will be tasked with working behind a new-look offensive line for the Browns, one that will feature five new starters.
"I think we have a great group of guys up front, Judkins said. "All of my belief is in them and my coaches. Just going out there, I know physicality, I'll be able to do everything I've always done, that's not a question for me. But just the mindset, the mentality we have as a team, I think that's what is going to carry us over the top."
Even with so many new faces up front, first-year head coach Todd Monken has relied on his rushing attack in previous years. With Derrick Henry being the bellcow in Baltimore, the Ravens' rushing offense finished No. 1 or No. 2 in rushing yards in two of the last three seasons while Monken was the offensive coordinator between 2023-25.
“(He’s) got his confidence back, his explosion," Monken said of Judkins in June .
It's clear that Monken loves to lean on his running back(s) to carry his offense, while also using multiple tight end sets to put his rushing attack at an advantage. Judkins will be the lead back, with fellow second-year running back Dylan Sampson expected to play a third-down role.
And now, with a full NFL offseason under his belt, Judkins appears to be more ready – and feeling even better – than he ever has to carry that load.

title: Joe Thomas Shares Why Browns Already Looking Ahead to 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
Joe Thomas spent his entire 11-year career with the Cleveland Browns, a tenure that perfectly encapsulated the franchise’s instability. The Hall of Fame left tackle experienced as many winning seasons (one) as 0-16 campaigns, all while protecting the blind side for 22 different starting quarterbacks.
If anyone understands the Browns’ struggles and long search for a franchise quarterback, it’s Thomas.
And in his view, Cleveland’s answer at the position likely isn’t on the current roster.
Thomas has been back in Berea at times this preseason, working with and helping develop the Browns’ offensive line after declining a full-time role on Todd Monken’s staff . While he hasn’t officially joined the coaching staff, his perspective still carries weight — and his latest comments suggest Cleveland’s long-term focus may already be shifting toward the 2027 NFL draft.
“The Browns, they’re never going to come out and say it, but you trade the greatest defensive player in history of football at his peak, you are not thinking about this year," Thomas told The Land on Demand's Tony Grossi . "We don’t have an answer yet at quarterback. Maybe one of these two guys turns into that guy, but I wouldn’t bet the farm on it, so to speak. It’s pretty obvious that they want to set themselves up as well as possible for the probability of drafting a rookie quarterback."
The moment the Browns traded Myles Garrett, the team admitted that 2026 would be yet another rebuilding season. Was the trade a good one for Cleveland given the current state of the team? Absolutely. But trading one of the best players in franchise history wouldn't happen during a competitive window, no matter the return in the deal.
That makes the 2027 draft even more important. Cleveland didn’t trade Garrett simply to become mediocre in the future. The Browns are betting that the assets acquired in the deal can help them build the next version of the franchise. But this time, the hope is that it will include a franchise quarterback, likely one that's not named Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders.
Watson and Sanders are currently competing to be Cleveland’s QB1 heading into the season. But realistically, the quarterback who leads the Browns in 2027 may still be playing college football.
Watson hasn’t thrown for 1,200 yards in a season since 2020 with the Houston Texans. After missing all of 2021, he has totaled just 3,365 passing yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions across 17 games in three seasons with Cleveland. Even setting aside his off-field issues, his production hasn’t matched that of a long-term franchise quarterback.
Sanders, meanwhile, showed flashes during his rookie season in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions while completing 56.6% of his passes in eight games (seven starts). But the inconsistency was evident.
There’s a reason he was a fifth-round pick, and reports of concerns from multiple coaching staffs about his command of the huddle and pre-snap operation suggest he remains a developmental project. The problem is that the NFL’s most important position rarely affords that kind of patience.
Oddsmakers aren’t optimistic about Cleveland in 2026, either. The Browns’ win total is set at 5.5, according to DraftKings. Unless something unexpected happens, Cleveland could once again find itself near the top of the draft order, along with an additional first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams that will likely fall late in the opening round. Those multiple first-rounders could be necessary to move up the board to get their guy that the front office has identified as next franchise quarterback for the Browns.
That combination may finally give the Browns the flexibility to answer the question that has lingered since 1999: Has Cleveland *finally* found its franchise quarterback?
For Monken, that answer could define his tenure. Entering his first season as a head coach, the urgency is clear. In today's NFL, few factors determine a coach’s longevity more than stability at quarterback.
That’s why Thomas’ perspective is so telling. While Watson and Sanders dominate preseason headlines, the more important evaluation may be happening on Saturdays rather than Sundays this fall.
College quarterbacks like Texas’ Arch Manning, Oregon’s Dante Moore, Ohio State’s Julian Sayin, Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, and Ole Miss’ Trinidad Chambliss could ultimately prove more relevant to Cleveland’s future than anyone currently in its quarterback room.
And that's what makes the upcoming college football season so important for Cleveland. The Browns don't necessarily need one particular quarterback to emerge as the obvious No. 1 pick. They need multiple quarterbacks to establish themselves as legitimate first-round prospects, giving Cleveland options when the time comes. It would allow the Browns to then trust their evaluations to draft their guy, and the QB1 they believe will finally be the answer in Cleveland.
That's the uncomfortable reality for the Browns. Cleveland's next franchise quarterback is more likely to be found on a college field this season than on their own sideline.
And if Thomas is right, the Browns already know that.

title: Cleveland Browns Promote Two Rookies to Starting Offense During Training Camp
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are ready to kick off their preseason this week and have made some noteworthy decisions during training camp that will show up during their first game.
Amongst those decisions was one that fans were hoping to hear, that being the promotion of rookies Denzel Boston and Spencer Fano to the starting offense where they’ll be getting regular first team reps.
This is a positive move for Cleveland, as both players have been impressing the coaching staff over the course of the summer up through this week. Both players have also made highlight worthy reels in the past couple of days, which had to have made the decision easier.
With Fano and Boston now a part of the starting offense, this points to their direction over the next few weeks leading into the regular season. If both players can continue to show that they belong, they’ll surely be ready to roll come September.
Here’s what it means for the Browns in moving Fano and Boston to the starting offense.
The preseason always reveals which players on each team have the best chances to make the final 53-man roster, but this decision by the Browns reveals they may already have their minds made up on Fano and Boston.
Cleveland made a smart decision by investing heavy resources into their offensive line this offseason, which included them drafting Fano No. 9 overall in April. Then, they followed that up with another great draft selection by taking two promising receivers, one being Denzel Boston.
Denzel Boston is about to put the NFL on watch. #DawgPound “He’s probably been the best and most consistent player on the offense.” - @NickPedone12 https://t.co/0qwxycxpUC pic.twitter.com/zkarOxtpmI
Fano could have easily been the first offensive lineman off the board but fell to the right spot with Cleveland. The case is the same for Boston, who should have been a first round pick. Either way, that’s the most glaring reason they could start right away.
Aside from that, their training camps respectfully have been impressive, as both have made great plays and shown off their immense football knowledge. Fano has been showing he can hold his own at left tackle, and Boston continues to use his height and strength to make plays over any Browns defender; Denzel Ward included.
If each rookie can continue to show that they belong with the starters, that makes for a major sign of relief knowing you have two starting caliber players in their first year and have them under control for three more.
With both Fano and Boston playing with the starters in training camp, this could already indicate that Cleveland had another stellar draft class. Of course, two out of the ten rookies drafted doesn’t mean it was an instant success, but if it’s two out of their top three, that’s really impressive.
Browns general manager Andrew Berry was praised for his successful draft class in 2025 , as every pick from last year ended up starting on offense or defense throughout the regular season. If he comes away with another draft class filled with starting caliber players, then he’ll receive further praise.
Having two positions as important as tackle and receiver being filled by rookies under their own will, not because of lack of depth, is as good as it gets, especially for their positions.
Cleveland has had a bad track record with drafting at both positions in recent years, so the hope is that they finally got it right. Both have continued to earn their keep with the Browns throughout training camp; the question is whether it’s too early to say they had another stellar draft.
Either way, both players will be heavily featured this season in one capacity or another. They’ll get their first taste of NFL action during the preseason, in which the Browns face off against the Chicago Bears this Saturday. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. from Soldier Field.

title: Ranking 7 Things at Browns Training Camp More Interesting Than Quarterback Battle
full_text:
All eyes are on Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders in the 2026 Cleveland Browns training camp.
A decision on which player will be the starting quarterback looms over each practice. Neither player is inspiring a ton of hope for the upcoming season .
So here are seven things at Browns training camp that are more interesting than the quarterback battle:
The rookie class. Reports say that receiver Denzel Boston has been dazzling in training camp with contested catches. At 6’4 inches, he stands out amongst his fellow receivers. KC Concepcion has shown his elusiveness and him returning kicks should be an interesting story line in camp as the Browns have not had a steady returner in recent years. Tackle Spencer Fano matching up against defensive end Jared Verse is a great battle to watch to get a first evaluation if he can anchor down the left side of the offensive line.
The defensive line. Injuries have rattled the defensive line so far in training camp. Maliek Collins, Kalia Davis, Mason Graham, Sam Kamara and Mike Hall Jr. have all missed time this training camp. The Browns defensive line making it through camp and getting healthy for week one will be something to watch. Should the Browns have a fan prize to play defensive line for training camp? Of course not, but winning a chance to be offensive coordinator for the Akron Zips would be fun.
Todd Monken’s press conferences. Monken’s press conferences have been entertaining this training camp. He is loud, he is raspy, and he will say what is on his mind. Monken even pulled a switcheroo after he told the media that Sanders would get the first-team reps last Saturday, but instead it was Watson under center. This week’s press conferences should be a fun listen as he explains the decision making.
The kickers. In training camp, the kickers are usually on their own end of the field. The roster is so large in training camp that it can be hard to see the offense and defense practice. The kickers are typically easier to watch and focus on. Plus it is fun to watch them kick the ball through the narrowed goal post and still hearing fans say “you have one job” when one misses.
The “how do I get those seats” clubs. Browns training camp is very hot. The metal seats become heating pads for the keister and provide little shade. There are always groups that are sectioned off with shade, fans, cold drinks, and some food that are reserved, which prompts the question “how do I get those seats?”.
The players that stay late to sign autographs. It is nice to watch the kind players that take the time to sign the kids’ jerseys and footballs. Also funny to watch the parents looking up an end-of-the-roster player’s number on their phone to get their name.
The puppies! The Puppy Pound is at Browns training camp. The adorable fur balls are for adoption and are always worth stopping by for a good ear scratch. Naming a puppy a pun with a player’s name is a good way to go. Barker Brailsford?
The Browns quarterback battle is still the most important for this training camp, but this year’s training camp can offer so much more.

title: Todd Monken Shares Why Deshaun Watson Took Reps From Shedeur Sanders at Browns Camp
full_text:
Todd Monken has finally spoken about what happened with the Browns quarterback competition on the afternoon of Saturday, August 8.
On Saturday afternoon, Browns head coach Todd Monken stated during his normal pre-practice media availability that it would be Shedeur Sanders’ turn to take reps with the first-team offense. That, however, was not what happened.
Day 10 of Browns training camp is over. On a day when Shedeur Sanders was  scheduled to practice with the starting offense, Deshaun Watson took every rep with the No. 1 unit. Sanders split the remaining reps with Dillon Gabriel.
Despite what Monken told the media , Deshaun Watson, the Browns' $230 million quarterback, took all of the first-team reps, looking solid while doing so.
When finally speaking to the Browns media before a rainy, indoor practice at the Browns training facility, Monken was asked why Deshaun Watson took all of the first-team reps during Saturday's practice when it was supposed to be Shedeur Sanders' turn.
Monken said at the pre-practice presser on Monday, “When I walked out, guys grabbed me and said, 'Hey, the last couple days we’ve been looking at it, and Shedeur has gotten a few more reps with the ones,’ that’s all it was.”
#Browns Todd Monken explains why he said Shedeur Sanders would get the 1st team reps Sat and then didn’t: pic.twitter.com/CVQWb67v7Y
Monken continued to give insight later on in the same presser that the quarterback competition is just that, still a competition. The Browns head coach stated, “As long as we’re sharing reps, it’s going to be a competition,” while also adding, “They’re each going to start a game.”
#Browns Todd Monken on how both Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders can still win the job and where things stand: pic.twitter.com/gvFPtPXv7e
So it seems, despite the online reaction, that it is business as usual, with no clear decision for the Browns regarding their quarterback competition. Monken also shared the nugget that there has yet to be a decision on who will start the Browns' preseason game against the Bears this Saturday, August 15.
Both Sanders and Watson still have a shot to win the starting quarterback job.
While Watson getting a double dose of first-team reps over the weekend troubled many Browns fans, it is important to remember we do not get to see everything the Browns do in terms of practice. There are walkthroughs, film studies, and scripts that not even the most keyed-in members of the media get to see.
If Todd Monken, who has been as transparent as he can be since assuming the role of Browns head coach, says it just happened so they can even out the reps and keep the competition fair, then so be it. If Todd Monken continues to say one thing and do another, then the media storm around the team will continue to spiral as it has in years past.
The hope is that the quarterback competition remains fair and the team continues to be transparent about it. With the first preseason game being just days away, more answers as to what is next for the Browns are just on the horizon.

title: Quinnen Williams Extension Puts Finishing Touches on Cowboys' Micah Parsons Trade
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys signed defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to a massive three-year, $105.9 million contract extension on Monday, locking him in for the foreseeable future.
And in the process, the Cowboys put what could be viewed as the finishing touches on the blockbuster Micah Parsons trade that shook the NFL world last August. The New York Jets then got involved with pieces of the trade after sending Williams to the Cowboys before last season's deadline.
With the trade being a potential franchise-altering move for both Dallas and the Green Bay Packers, it's worth revisiting each part of the deal, including how things worked out for the Jets.
Let's look at the Cowboys-Packers Parsons trade as if it were a three-team deal with the Jets.
- DT Quinnen Williams - DT Kenny Clark - 2026 first-round pick (Dallas then traded this pick to move down and select Malachi Lawrence)
- DT Mazi Smith - 2027 first-round pick (from Green Bay via Dallas) - 2026 second-round pick (traded to Detroit)
The answer to that question remains up in the air. After all, the Jets could use their new 2027 first-round pick to select a franchise-altering player that brings multiple Super Bowls back to the franchise.
But until that unlikely scenario plays out, the clear winner so far is Dallas.
The Cowboys have one of the NFL's best interior duos on the defensive line with Clark and Williams. With seven combined Pro Bowl appearances and 79.5 career sacks between them, Dallas has the core of its defense in place for the next handful of years.
And with Parsons still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in November, it's unclear if he will ever get back to the form he was at during his first 14 games with Green Bay last year. The Packers may not end up getting the franchise-altering results out of Parsons that they anticipated when they traded for him.
One could argue that Clark, 30, will hit a wall soon and won't be as productive. That's a reasonable stance for most players, but Clark has missed just one game over the past five seasons and doesn't look to be slowing down anytime soon.
While Parsons will look to reprove himself coming off of injury, expect Clark and Williams to be the catalysts behind Dallas' defensive turnaround this upcoming season.

title: Dallas Cowboys Joint Practice Takeaways as Defense Dominates Rams
full_text:
Tuesday brought some welcome change for the Dallas Cowboys as they were able to take the field against a different team for the first time this offseason. Dallas headed to Woodland Hills to take on the Los Angeles Rams at their facility in a joint practice.
These joint practices have become very popular with NFL head coaches and players saying they get more from these sessions than they do any preseason game. That's why head coach Brian Schottenheimer hardly plays starters in the preseason, instead giving them their practice reps in controlled atmospheres such as the one they were in against L.A.
Cameras weren't allowed, so information was limited, but beat reporters on site were able to give us plenty of insight to the day's events. With their help, here's a roundup of the biggest takeaways from the day.
One thing that stood out to Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News was how much better the defense looked. While the starting offense had its issues, Hoyt said the defense held their own. He stated the Cowboys looked "shellshocked" by the Rams' offense in 2025 and despite giving up one big play to Puka Nacua, he said they " held up very well ."
He added that while Nacua beat Shavon Revel for a decent gain, the Dallas defensive back also made a great stop by catching up to Nacua on a deep route and forcing an incompletion. That's a huge win for new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is being tasked with fixing one of the league's worst defenses from a year ago.
Parker's solid work continued with the reserves taking over as the Dallas defense had multiple turnovers, stuffs in the run game, and pass deflections. Overall, it was a huge win for Parker and a momentum builder for the defense.
After moving from linebacker to EDGE this offseason, Marist Liufau is beginning to make some noise at his new position. His ascension continued on Tuesday as Liufau recorded an early sack while working with the backups.
He wasn't alone, however, with Isaiah Land also recording a sack while stuffing a run for no gain as well. Land was an undrafted free agent addition in 2023 but left in 2024 to join the Indianapolis Colts. He re-signed this offseason and while he's a longshot to make the roster, he's making sure he doesn't go down without a fight.
Dee Winters has been a forgotten man in Dallas with rookie Jaishawn Barham stealing all of the attention. Winters made sure to remind everyone he could play during the joint practice which included a great stop against Blake Corum in the run game. According to Patrik Walker, Winters showed excellent speed and recognition to shut down the play for a short loss.
Another linebacker who has been overlooked is Justin Barron, an UDFA from Syracuse in 2025. A converted safety, Barron showed off his coverage skills against Los Angeles while recording three interceptions . He was also active against the run, picking up a couple of stops.
Second-year running back Jaydon Blue has been turning heads throughout camp and seemingly had the inside track on the RB2 job. He might have hurt his chances against Los Angeles, however, as Blue had an early fumble. It's not the end of the world, but with Phil Mafah playing as well as he has, Blue has very limited room for error, making this a noticeable mistake.

title: Dallas Cowboys Defense Shows Out With Amazing Performance vs Rams in Joint Practice
full_text:
It's no secret that the Dallas Cowboys entered the offseason needing to make massive changes on  defense.
On the bright side, things can't get much worse on that end in 2026 after some historical lows last season, but early indications during training camp continue to show that new defensive coordinator Christian Parker might be ahead of schedule when it comes to turning the defense around.
The Cowboys' defense got a chance to show what it's capable of during Tuesday's joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams, and all signs are positive about what the unit was able to do against Sean McVay's offense.
The Dallas defense was the clear winner of the day, according to reports from Patrik Walker of DallasCowboys.com.
"It wasn't close at all," Walker wrote on X.
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford "really struggled" against Parker's defensive looks, per Walker.
It's important to note that both teams likely didn't have complete game plans for the scrimmage portion of the joint practice. Perhaps things would've been different for Stafford and the Rams offense, but for now, the edge goes to the Dallas defense.
Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua also left practice early due to an unknown injury, a notable absence for the Los Angeles offense.
Of course, it's still only training camp. The Dallas defense will need to prove itself once the season begins and the bullets actually start flying. But after the year the defense had in 2025, this is the kind of news that Cowboys fans have desperately been waiting for.
Talk about staking your claim for a roster spot.
Cowboys linebacker Justin Barron had three interceptions against the Rams on Tuesday, the team confirmed on X.
Here's a look at one of the picks against Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett:
3️⃣ INTs Have yourself a day, @justinbarron22 👏 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/Dfv4SLCtmK
Barron could end up giving the Cowboys no choice but to put him on the 53-man roster once training camp and preseason are complete.
This now puts pressure on the other Dallas linebackers to step it up moving forward, as the position is one that still holds some concern from fans entering the season.
All in all, the Cowboys couldn't have asked for a better day during their joint practice with the Rams.

title: Dallas Cowboys Salary Cap Implications From Quinnen Williams Contract Extension
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have wrapped up a key defensive player for the long haul after agreeing to a massive contract extension with Quinnen Williams — and we now have an idea of how that new contract could impact Dallas' cap space situation.
According to reports, Williams' new pact with the Cowboys is a three-year, $105.9 million contract that makes him one of the highest-paid defensive linemen in the NFL.
Now, Cowboys fans want to know how this impacts the salary cap, and while we don't have exact numbers until the official details are released, we do have an idea.
Patrik Walker of DallasCowboys.com says the deal could save the Cowboys close to $35 million in total over the next two years "depending on the contract structure."
That is broken down into roughly $15.5 million this season and $19.2 million next season.
According to Over The Cap , the Cowboys are sitting with about $5.4 million in cap space currently, so they could have nearly $20 million to work with after Williams' extension.
As far as next season is concerned, the Cowboys are projected to be $15.5 million over the cap, so Williams' extension could put them back in the black all by itself.
With that anticipated injection of cap space, the Cowboys are well-positioned to make at least another significant move.
And we know the Cowboys are open to doing so after both Jerry and Stephen Jones have made that quite clear in recent weeks.
"I'd give up the future to substitute where we are today," Jerry said to the media at the outset of training camp. "As to a player, to give you an idea about what I'd invest, something substantive, to get the right kind of deal and improve us for Opening Day? I would.
"Stephen Jones was talking on the Cowboys broadcast about tinkering with the roster and said that they are still actively talking to other NFL teams about options as well as veteran free agents," Blogging The Boys' RJ Ochoa relayed. "He said if he was a betting man the 90 man roster would look different in a couple of weeks."
Stephen noted that he was focused in on the linebacker and cornerback battles in training camp, so that may indicate which positions the Cowboys are thinking about adding at.
The first player who immediately comes to mind there is Bobby Wagner , who is still a free agent and would no doubt shore up Dallas' promising but uncertain linebacker spot.
When it comes to possible trades, we'd love to see Dallas make a play for either Maxx Crosby or Josh Sweat, although Crosby feels likely begin the season in Las Vegas after re-committing there following the nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens.
That said, a deadline deal remains possible if things go south for the Raiders once again in 2026.
Sweat was reportedly unhappy in Arizona earlier this offseason, so there's a legitimate chance he hits the trade block before Week 1.
If that happens, the Cowboys absolutely should make a play for him to bolster their edge rushers room, which, like the linebacker position, has some question marks.
Whether it's adding Crosby, Sweat, Wagner or a cornerback or another position, the Cowboys are in great shape to bolster the roster ahead of the season thanks to Williams' extension.

title: 6 Dallas Cowboys Who Need a Strong Preseason Debut vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys aren't expected to play their starters much, if at all, during the upcoming preseason. This should come as no surprise to anyone who watched the team a year ago as head coach Brian Schottenheimer was reluctant to expose any of their key players to unnecessary hits in the preseason.
That doesn't mean these games aren't important. They are still incredibly vital for players who are fighting for a spot on the roster and want to prove themselves in game situations.
Here we look at six such players who need to perform well in the Cowboys' preseason debut this Saturday against the Seattle Seahawks.
As an undrafted free agent a year ago, Traeshon Holden made a name for himself with a strong training camp. His performance wasn't enough to earn a spot on the 53-man roster as Holden spent the year on the practice squad.
Entering year two, Holden has been even better and is said to be higher on the depth chart than expected . Still, Dallas has had several players step up recently, including Camden Brown, which is putting plenty of pressure on Holden. That's why he needs to step up in the preseason to ensure no one surpasses him.
Cornerback was a weakness heading into camp but the competition has heated up. Shavon Revel and Cobie Durant have been excellent and are battling for the starting spot opposite DaRon Bland.
Behind them, Caelen Carson has also been playing well, but needs to fend off Devin Moore, Derion Kendrick, Reddy Steward, and Josh Butler. It's a tight race and Carson needs to do something to separate himself from the pack.
Earlier this offseason, Brian Schottenheimer said Nate Thomas would compete for the starting left tackle spot. That no longer appears to be the case as Thomas has been working with the second team at right tackle during camp. He's suddenly in danger of losing the swing tackle spot to rookie Drew Shelton and can use the preseason to remind the coaching staff why they liked him so much entering the offseason.
One of the changes Christian Parker made this offseason was moving Marist Liufau from linebacker to EDGE . It's a brand new position for Liufau, who has the physical tools to get the job done. He's also been stepping up his performance in practice lately, sending him into the preseason with rising stock . Liufau is firmly on the bubble but can lock up a spot with a strong preseason, which begins on Saturday.
Added in a trade with the New England Patriots last year, Joe Milton was the QB2 throughout the season for Dallas. When he was first added, there was plenty of excitement for the rocket-armed quarterback, but he had issues with consistency throughout the preseason. That's been the case again this year, as Milton is falling behind Sam Howell in the battle for the backup spot. Milton enters the preseason on the roster bubble and can't afford any lackluster performances.
Just as Milton can't afford to slip up, Sam Howell can't surrender any ground. He's been the more consistent signal-caller during camp but a poor performance against Seattle can erase a lot of the goodwill he's built up. On the other hand, if he comes out and impresses, he might be able to lock up his spot in a hurry.

title: Quinnen Williams' Agent Nicole Lynn Celebrates Blockbuster Cowboys Extension
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' defensive overhaul was in full swing during the offseason, with defensive coordinator Christian Parker bringing in a new batch of players to fit into his versatile scheme .
But even before Parker got his hands on the defense, the Cowboys were rebuilding the defense and culture, acquiring Quinnen Williams at the NFL trade deadline .
Williams brought All-Pro credentials to Dallas' defensive front, and now he is here long term.
On Monday, the Cowboys and Williams agreed to a blockbuster three-year, $105.9 million contract extension, with $101 million in guaranteed cash. Right before his deal was announced, Williams' agent, Nicole Lynn of Klutch Sports, foreshadowed and celebrated the deal.
In his seven games with the Cowboys last season, Williams recorded 20 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 33 quarterback pressures, and two tackles for a loss. It was clear that he was going to be the anchor for the Cowboys' defense, and he was rewarded.
Williams' agent, Nicole Lynn, celebrated the deal by shouting out Brinks.
Anyone have a Brinks truck? 👀
Not only does Williams' $105.9 million deal include $101 million guaranteed, but Williams also receives $63.35 million at signing. His $35.3 million annual average ranks second among defensive tackles across the league.
When speaking about Williams, Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones made it clear that Williams was a leader in the locker room, and someone the team values moving into the future.
"One, let's talk about what he does on the practice field," Jones said, via ESPN. "I mean he's a great player and he's one of the hardest practicing guys out there. Anytime he lines up, you feel him. He doesn't take anything for granted, doesn't say, 'Hey, I got this.' [It's,] 'Let my play do the talking when we play a game.' You see it. He's the best player on the field whenever he's out there. And so that was a big piece of it. And then the other thing is just what a man he is. He's a leader. We didn't have a lot of leadership on defense for the last couple of years. Now to have him and Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary, I think has really picked it up over there in terms of culture and the leadership ."
With an impressive offseason and high hopes for the defense, it was crucial to sign Williams to a big deal, and now the team can look to the future with an All-Pro talent in the center of its defense.

title: Cowboys Defense Has Been a Nightmare in Training Camp, But in a Good Way
full_text:
It's obviously hard to gauge exactly how good the Dallas Cowboys' defense is going to be this season given the fact that the team has a new defensive coordinator and several new players .
However, we can at least make an educated guess based on how the unit has looked in training camp through two-plus weeks . If an assistant coach's assessment of how things have gone is any indication, Dallas is moving in the right direction.
Joseph Hoty of the Dallas Morning News shared a quote from Steve Shimko, the assistant quarterbacks coach, on Monday in which he admits Dallas' defense has been giving its offense fits during training camp.
“This defense has given us nightmares right now," Shmko stated. "I can’t wait to watch them play. If we can keep up our standard, then we’re going to do a lot of great things.”
We normally might take this with a grain of salt considering it's just one view from one man, but we've heard something similar from players this offseason.
Take CeeDee Lamb, for example, who noted how difficult it was to play against Christian Parker's unit during OTAs.
"It's annoying. It's been annoying to prepare against, but obviously just seeing it practice every day... it's kind of unique, just seeing different guys communicate and being able to understand and take what they learn from the meeting room and being able to easily translate it on the field. It's good to go against, it's very tricky," Lamb said.
Again, nobody is claiming this defense is fixed off a few quotes, but they are good signs nonetheless and help to continue building hope that things really are different for Dallas' defense in 2026.
We also have practice observations to go by and it seems like the Cowboys' defense is, at the very least, putting up a great fight against Dallas' offense on a daily basis. We've also seen the defense win convincingly on some days.
Not something to throw a party over for sure, but the Cowboys do have an elite offense and the defense not succumbing to the talent on that side of the ball is yet another great sign.
Bear in mind, with how good their offense is, the Cowboys do not have to be elite on defense to make the playoffs.
But if the Cowboys want to accomplish winning a Super Bowl, a top-10 defense may be required, as only two Super Bowl winners since 2013 haven't sported a top-10 unit.
But, like the Cowboys are set to sport in 2026, those teams, the Kansas City Chiefs (2022) and Los Angeles Rams (2021), sported elite offenses, so there's that.

title: Stephen Jones Seems to Take Shot at Micah Parsons After Quinnen Williams Extension
full_text:
Last offseason, the Dallas Cowboys had a lot of eyes on them as they were negotiating a long-term extension with star pass rusher Micah Parsons. Those talks broke down, eventually leading to a blockbuster trade with Parsons going to the Green Bay Packers in exchange for defensive tackle Kenny Clark and two first-round draft picks.
Dallas used one of those picks as part of a package to bring in Quinnen Williams, who had been a star defensive tackle with the New York Jets. On Monday, the Cowboys agreed to an extension with Williams, adding three years and $105.9 million to his current deal. Williams now has a five-year contract worth a total of $153.15 million .
The Cowboys clearly see Williams as a building block for their defense, which is why they locked him up as early as they did. Doing so also raises questions about their lack of desire to work with Parsons in 2025. One of those questions was whether Dallas ever saw Parsons as a true leader and building block.
There's no debate he is an elite talent, but recent comments from Stephen Jones suggest he wasn't much of a leader. While praising Williams, Jones said he gives them the type of leadership that their defense has been missing for a couple of years.
"He's a great player and one of the hardest practicing guys out there. Every time he lines up, you feel him. He doesn't take anything for granted. He doesn't say, 'Hey, I got this. I'll let my play do the talking.' You see it," Jones said via Jon Machota of The Athletic .
"He's the best player on the field whenever he's out there. The other thing is just what a man he is. He's a leader. We didn't have a lot of leadership on defense for the last couple of years. To have him and Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary. I think they really picked it up over there in terms of the culture and the leadership."
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has been adamant about getting strong leaders throughout the roster. He prioritized that in the 2025 draft class, targeting players such as Tyler Booker and Donovan Ezeiruaku who were team captains and leaders of their respective teams.
Parsons, on the other hand, had his role as a leader on defense questioned. That included being called out by former teammate DeMarcus Lawrence for being overly focused on social media. He was also criticized by current Cowboy Malik Hooker for hosting a podcast instead of working on his game.
At one point, Schottenheimer tried to encourage Parsons by moving his locker next to Dak Prescott's in an attempt to help him grow as a leader. It appears that didn't do much to change the perception of Parsons, at least not with the front office.
As for Williams, he has been praised as a strong leader dating back to his time with the Crimson Tide. He will now be given the opportunity to prove he's the right building block for defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is trying to turn around a defense that was among the worst in the league last year.

title: Cowboys Make George Pickens Contract Goal Clear After Quinnen Williams Extension
full_text:
Over the weekend, we wrote that Nicole Lynn, the agent for Quinnen Williams, was spotted at Dallas Cowboys training camp. That led to speculation that Williams could be in line for an extension and on Monday, that's exactly what happened.
Williams and the Cowboys agreed to a three-year, $105.9M extension . Added to the two years remaining on his current deal, Williams is now locked up for five years at $153.15 million. He will earn $101 million total guaranteed with $63.35 million as a signing bonus.
With that contract done, it might seem difficult for the Cowboys to come to terms with wideout George Pickens, who is playing on the franchise tag in 2026. Executive vice president Stephen Jones doesn't see this as an issue, though. When asked about locking up Pickens, Jones said that was the plan .
"That's the ultimate goal," Jones said via Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com.. "So it's just a lot of moving parts that we've got to obviously keep playing option quarterback and we'll see where it takes us."
Pickens was added ahead of the 2025 season in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He exploded with 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, leading the team in each category.
Pickens, who will earn $27.3 million on the tag, can't negotiate a new deal until the offseason. That gives him another year to improve his value, which is currently at an all-time high.
It also will afford him time to shut down the narrative that he has character concerns. While Pickens wore out his welcome in Pittsburgh, he was well received in Dallas. He's even become great friends with CeeDee Lamb, who recently said Pickens is "a good dude," who doesn't have character concerns.
"He's not a crash (out) until he has a reason," Lamb said on 105.3 The Fan . "I swear, he's a good dude. He's literally funny all the time, bro. He's funny all the time until he feels like 'all right, somebody's trying to play with me,' and then that's when you get the NFL young boy."
Lamb added that he's a great talent and wants to see Pickens get "get every dollar in which he deserves." The big question will be if Pickens attempts to cash in at current market value , which could exceed the $34 million annual average that Lamb currently makes. If so, that creates its own concerns, but that's a problem for another day.

title: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb Sets Record Straight on George Pickens' Character Concerns
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have arguably the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, and they are certainly no strangers to making headlines.
CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens give the Cowboys one of the potent one-two punches at receiver in franchise history, but they also might be the most interesting.
Both possess unique and charismatic personalties, though for Pickens, this has led to somewhat of a "troublemaker" label dating back to his time with the Pittsburgh Steelers when he got hit with multiple fines from the NFL for various reasons.
Lamb recently cleared the air about who Pickens is as a person as the two have built a friendship in Dallas. It seems Pickens' time with the Cowboys has helped shed some of the negative labels that likely should've never been there in the first place.
In an interview with 105.3 The Fan, Lamb spoke at length about his impressions of Pickens, emphasizing his good-natured personality.
That said, Lamb made it clear that Pickens won't hesitate to figuratively "fight back" if given a reason to.
"He's not a crash (out) until he has a reason," Lamb said. "I swear, he's a good dude. He's literally funny all the time, bro. He's funny all the time until he feels like 'all right, somebody's trying to play with me,' and then that's when you get the NFL young boy."
Lamb also added that though he doesn't watch Pickens' interviews, he's given him advice on how to handle all of the media attention the right way.
"As far as in the media, I feel like he does a good job. I don't really watch any of his interviews, but I do I do understand that the position that he's in, he don't need any like backlash. He don't need anything that's gonna really negate what his worth essentially, and that's all I'm in his ear above."
Pickens will play on the franchise tag this upcoming season but his future with the Cowboys remains uncertain. Regardless of what happens, Lamb has Pickens' back as he seeks a new contract, whether that's in Dallas or elsewhere.
"I want him to get every dollar in which he deserves because he's a great talent," Lamb said. "He's amazing. He's one of the best receivers that I've played with."
