title: Bo Nix Extension Timeline: Greg Penner Makes Broncos' Stance Clear
full_text:
Bo Nix is back on the field, which makes everything happening at Denver Broncos HQ right now feel right as rain.
Two weeks into training camp, Nix has looked very, very good. His mobility is not in question, seven months after fracturing his right ankle in the playoffs. He seems to be unencumbered by the ankle, and fully back to his pre-injury form.
As a passer, Nix's throwing motion looks even more polished , like he spent time working on it during the offseason. And as Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said on Day 8 of camp, Nix's deep-ball accuracy has been " off the charts ."
With an upgraded arsenal around him, there's every reason to hope for a big year-three leap from Nix, just as offensive coordinator Davis Webb forecasted earlier this summer . Sean Payton has insisted that this year's squad is just as fierce a Super Bowl contender as he predicted the 2025 Broncos would be.
After 2026, though, the Broncos have a big decision to make because Nix will be eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. With the rapidity of the quarterback market's growth each year — heck, each month — the Broncos are incentivized to get a Nix extension done as soon as possible.
The question is, have the Broncos begun to look at Nix's future contract? Co-owner and CEO Greg Penner was asked that very question on Tuesday.
“Not much at this point," Penner said. "Obviously, we want Bo here long-term, but we’re really focused on getting ready for this season, putting a competitive team on the field."
The Broncos would be forgiven for not having already locked in a detailed plan, as they're about the business of preparing for the 2026 season, and, frankly, the team can't take action on a Nix extension until the NFL's next new league year opens in March of 2027.
At some point, the Nix conversations will be had, and Penner will leave those initial explorations of the topic to GM George Paton and head coach Sean Payton.
"I’ll leave that to George [Paton] and Sean [Payton], [they] will have conversations about it, but I’ll leave that up to them to lead," Penner said.
The Broncos extended both Paton and Payton during this past offseason. Both men's fingerprints are on the Broncos' 24 wins over the past two years, but without Nix, as we learned in January, the music stops.
They say a franchise quarterback is the tide that raises all ships. If we hold Nix to that standard, does he measure up?
The answer is a resounding yes. Nix deserves a ton of credit for his influence on the Broncos' remarkable turnaround over the past two years. This team went from being an AFC doormat for most of the preceding eight years to immediately making the playoffs with Nix as a rookie.
In Year 2, Nix led the Broncos to a 14-3 record — tying the franchise's single-season wins record — dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West, and earned the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. From there, all of Denver's Super Bowl aspirations were on the table, but Nix would have to out-duel Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills as the first order of business.
Nix did just that, but suffered that heartbreaking ankle fracture on the third-to-last play of overtime. Wil Lutz's game-winning field goal gave Denver the 33-30 win, but it echoed hollowly in retrospect, as soon as Payton announced Nix's injury and that he was done for the season.
Payton and the Broncos put on a brave face, pushing Jarrett Stidham to the fore as the Broncos had no choice but to march ahead to host the New England Patriots in the AFC championship game. But without Nix, the Broncos were dead in the water.
Payton is an excellent coach, but overcoming the loss of a young franchise quarterback on the doorstep of the Super Bowl was a bridge too far for almost any team in NFL history. If nothing else, though, the AFC title game clearly illustrated just how important Nix is to the Broncos.
The Broncos will only go as far as Nix can lead them. And there's every reason to believe the third-year quarterback can rally the Broncos once again, make another postseason run, and perhaps get over the Super Bowl hump.
After the 2026 season, though, the Broncos will want to jump on getting Nix extended. Right now, the going rate for a proven franchise quarterback is somewhere between $44 million and $65 million per year.
The Broncos probably won't even start trying to crack that nut until the 2026 season is in the books. But the sooner they can get Nix re-signed, the better it'll be for the bottom line, because the mind-boggling cost of a franchise quarterback will continue to grow between now and March of 2027, especially if Nix fulfills expectations, and leads the Broncos back to the playoffs.

title: The Biggest Mistake Broncos Can't Afford to Make This Training Camp
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' front office has assembled a strong roster that should keep them among the favorites in the AFC.
Two weeks into training camp, the Broncos are shaping up well. The early signs are more than encouraging, but there are a couple of things I'm concerned about.
As camp marches on, there's one big mistake the Broncos can't afford to make. Let's talk about it.
The Broncos should play the trade market, but in a very specific way. Despite calls on social media for them to trade away a wide receiver or cornerback, they can’t afford to.
That being said, the Broncos would also be remiss if they ignored the opportunity to trade for a tight end. This would keep the team's strengths strong, while bolstering a clear weakness, depending on the tight end Denver traded for.
The reason the Broncos need another tight end really boils down to how weak the position is. Evan Engram built some early hype in camp, and while he and the Broncos are striving to involve him more in the run game as a blocker , it's certainly not his strong suit.
Meanwhile, there has been very little positive about the tight end room as a whole. Tight end has been a roster weakness for three years in a row ; the Broncos need to take greater measures to strengthen it.
Fifth-rounder Justin Joly is displaying his rawness as a rookie; rookie seventh-rounder Dallen Bentley is at the bottom of the depth chart; Nate Adkins has already dealt with a camp injury , and Adam Trautman is yet to make one of our camp notebooks for any reason through two weeks.
Lucas Krull has made a positive play or two as a receiver , but they're few and far between. Caleb Lohner has yet to practice after undergoing a "routine" clean-up procedure in June that wasn't supposed to cost him any days in camp.
It isn’t clear which tight ends might be currently available for a trade, but there isn’t anyone left in free agency who could make enough impact to change the direction of the position in Denver. The Broncos can’t accept just rolling it back with what they have, and no, the solution isn’t Taysom Hill either.
As for why it would be unwise to trade a player away, there are two very different reasons at wide receiver and cornerback. At wide receiver, it's about the medicals, and at cornerback, it's about the depth.
At wide receiver, Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr. are both banged up, and Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin both dealt with injuries last year. This is an offense looking for more explosive plays and a more consistent passing attack throughout the season, so they'll need as many of their weapons in the arsenal as they can get.
Run it back at wide receiver this season, especially with the Broncos' clear Super Bowl aspirations, and then re-evaluate after in 2027 based on who steps up and, of course, contract situations. The Broncos shouldn’t look to disrupt the room right now, and potentially their passing game, which has shown some encouraging signs of taking flight already despite facing a tough defense in practice every day.
As for cornerback, Jahdae Barron has been unable to force his way into the starting lineup. Riley Moss has been on fire, and the Broncos just gave Ja'Quan McMillian a one-year raise on a restricted free-agent tender, so it's not as if Barron has had it easy, despite being a 2025 first-round pick.
However, Barron seems to be behind Kris Abrams-Draine in the boundary cornerback competition. Moss is the starting boundary corner opposite Patrick Surtain II, and he looks like he's made a leap with his play. Trading Moss away would make the room significantly weaker.
If Barron had stepped up by now, this could be a different discussion, but he seems to be falling behind and is trending in the wrong direction. The Broncos can’t afford to make the mistake of trading Moss and putting too much trust in Barron at this point.
It isn’t just one misstep the Broncos can’t afford to make, but three mistakes that are all closely related. This is a good roster, and the Broncos don’t want to disrupt it too much, but they have to see the glaring weakness at tight end and address it.

title: Broncos Camp Day 10: Broncos Thin at Center | Takeaways | Winners and Losers
full_text:
Denver Broncos training camp marches on, with the team back at it on Tuesday.
Day 10 of Broncos camp featured a 2:10-minute practice in the weltering Colorado heat. The players were in pads once again, slugging it out at Broncos Park.
The hope was that a day would pass without a player injury, but alas, it wasn't meant to be. Since the pads went on eight days ago, the Broncos haven't completed a practice without at least one injury.
With that said, let's get to the unfortunate injury that occured on Day 10, as well as the takeaways, and winners and losers.
The Broncos are suddenly extremely thin at center. Deiter went down during a 9-on-7 team drill and had to be carted off by trainers .
With Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth already sidelined by injuries, Deiter had been running with the first-team. The Broncos' center depth is being tested, but head coach Sean Payton dismissed it as a concern moving forward.
“We’ll work through it," Payton said after practice. "We have guys that are flexible. We’ll be fine."
Following Deiter's injury, Calvin Throckmorton took over as the first-team center, a young veteran who's been with the Broncos organization for a couple of years. Undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega saw a bump-up, too, running with the second-team offense, per The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson .
The Broncos still list All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz as a guard/center on their roster, and on cue, he was seen practicing his snapping skills on Tuesday, though not during any team drills. After practice, Meinerz said that he tries to stay sharp at snapping, just in case of emergency.
With the first preseason game coming up on Friday on the road against the Atlanta Falcons, that emergency may be at hand, despite Payton's remarks.
Not in pads on Tuesday were Forsyth, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, outside linebacker Dasan McCullough, wide receiver Michael Bandy, and tight end Caleb Lohner. Meanwhile, running back J.K. Dobbins, wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr., and Wattenberg were in pads but didn't fully participate, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel .
That's a step in the right direction for Dobbins ( injured on Monday ), Mims, and Wattenberg. The Broncos have really struggled to avoid the injury bug in this camp.
It is football, after all, so there's no avoiding injuries completely, but this camp has to be the most eventful injury-wise since Payton took over as head coach in 2023. Again, it's been every single day.
I do wonder whether the Broncos' strong emphasis on the run game in this camp has anything to do with the injuries, especially to the centers and front-seven players on defense. It'll build that callus, to be sure, but it's coming at a cost.
Dobbins was in pads, but he also participated in individual drills ( Tomasson ). Dobbins had fun with the media, conveying that he's doing just fine, as captured by CBS Colorado 's Romi Bean.
J.K. Dobbins running hard and letting everyone know he is good and healthy 👍😏 pic.twitter.com/D9O9O4VEav
Dobbins had to let everyone know he's good after the " pinky promise " he delivered early in camp, vowing to the media and fans that he'd stay healthy for all 17 games. He has a long injury history since entering the league as a Baltimore Ravens second-round pick in 2020, and missed the final seven regular-season games and the playoffs in his first year with the Broncos.
Despite the injury, the Broncos re-signed Dobbins on a two-year, $16 million deal in March, which amounted to a 4x raise. The Broncos believe they can keep him on the field, and not only view him as one of the NFL's premier running backs, but also as a "force multiplier" in terms of the many ways he makes the team better.
It's good to see Dobbins at least practicing individual drills.
"Patty Ice" continued his breakout camp performance on Day 10, catching multiple touchdown passes. He's been a force to be reckoned with, especially in the red zone.
Throckmorton is a big winner on Day 10 because he got to run with the first-team offense. He may be the fourth center option, but it's a great opportunity to showcase his versatility and value to the Broncos, especially with how much depth the team now has on the interior offensive line.
Moss and Bryant are the two biggest standouts of camp thus far. Moss once again had multiple pass break-ups on Day 10, including a deep Bo Nix pass to Courtland Sutton, per KOA 's Ryan Edwards .
Coleman may be a rookie, but he doesn't look or talk like one. He's already displayed his prowess as a between-the-tackles rusher in camp and his receiving skills out of the backfield, but on Day 10, he had a couple of impressive reps in pass protection, too, per Denver7 's Troy Renck . Coleman is a complete back.
Toward the end of practice, when the Broncos were running their situational drills — like two-minute and red-zone — Katsis made an impressive catch in the back of the end zone, skying up to catch a 25-yard Sam Ehlinger "dime" on 4th-&-10, per 9NEWS ' Mike Klis . Katsis has had a great camp thus far, and as an undrafted rookie, he also brings returner ability to the table, which I'm sure fans will get to see in the preseason games.
Krull caught a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jarrett Stidham to end practice ( Klis ). It was another nice red-zone play made by the veteran tight end, who's feeling the pressure with the Broncos' two rookie tight ends, both of whom were draft picks (Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley), pushing from the bottom of the depth chart.
Deiter makes this list simply because of his unfortunate injury. Otherwise, though, he's been solid and reliable this summer as the Broncos' third center behind Wattenberg and Forsyth. Fingers crossed for the seventh-year Deiter.
Sutton makes this list simply because he's yet to really shine since returning to practice late last week following three straight veteran rest days . On Day 10, Nix looked Sutton's way a couple of times during team period, but couldn't connect; both were broken up by Moss.
With Bryant making plays left and right, it would be good for Sutton to remind everyone of his Pro Bowl pedigree in practice, but the absence of big plays of late is far from an indictment on his status and place with the Broncos. When the regular season rolls around, odds are, Sutton will continue to be Nix's first look and security blanket.
It's worth mentioning, though, how Bryant has capitalized on the time missed by veterans like Sutton and Waddle. Nix has been looking Bryant's way first in practice; how much that has to do with the absences of Sutton and Waddle is unclear, but at the very least, it's safe to say that "Patty Ice" has established some strong chemistry and trust with his quarterback.

title: Ramifications of Backup C Michael Deiter Being Carted Off at Broncos Camp
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were already stretched at the center position. They ended Tuesday even thinner.
That's because backup C Michael Deiter was carted off during training camp practice with an apparent injury suffered in 9-on-7 drills. He did not return to practice and was replaced by veteran lineman Calvin Throckmorton.
Head coach Sean Payton failed to provide an update on Deiter's immediate status, suggesting he's undergoing an evaluation to determine the severity.
A former Dolphins third-round pick, Deiter is entering his second season with the Broncos after joining the club's practice squad in January and subsequently inking a reserve/future deal. The 30-year-old (in September) arrived to Denver following stops in Miami, Houston, and Washington.
Deiter had been assuming primary center responsibilities with starter Luke Wattenberg and direct backup Alex Forsyth both battling injuries and working off to the side amid Tuesday's session.
Deiter is the latest in a long line of Broncos players to go down since camp opened. The list also includes the aforementioned Wattenberg and Forsyth, wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims, and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen, who suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon last week.
"I don’t think it’s heat-related as much as you always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration, obviously. It’s incumbent on the player," Payton said of the injury epidemic on Monday. "It’s hard for anyone to know your soft tissue. So I’m always looking at, all right, what did we do leading up to maybe a period where someone had a strain? We had a warm-down after practice, and we’ll continue to focus on it, though."
As mentioned, Deiter was Denver's third option at center with Wattenberg and Forsyth unavailable. Throckmorton, a more natural guard by trade, was forced into the pivot for the remainder of Tuesday. The latter will likely continue operating as such on Wednesday.
Other in-house options include undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega, who sailed an errant snap on Monday, and perennial All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz, who holds some previous center experience (some last preseason) — and would be up to filling in temporarily if called upon.
"I gotta have it in the back pocket," Meinerz told reporters. "I know that it's important I add that value to the offensive line room, in an emergency situation."

title: Vance Joseph Says Bo Nix Has Taken a Big Step in One Crucial Area
full_text:
It's been a heated training camp thus far at Denver Broncos HQ.
Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph called it "very competitive" after Day 8's scrimmage. Emotions are high, tempers have flared , and each side of the ball wants oh so badly to win the day.
Within that setting we have third-year quarterback Bo Nix returning from the ankle injury that sidelined him for the AFC championship game. Nix's mobility has not been limited at camp, that's for sure, but there are other aspects of his game that seem to have taken a leap forward.
Nix's supposedly subpar deep-ball accuracy was one of the common tropes we heard from the national media types during the offseason. The ubiquitous lists and quarterback rankings that serve as offseason fodder often featured a blurb about Nix's deep ball as part of the justification for placing him as, say, the 17th-best quarterback in the NFL.
Suffice it to say, Nix's deep ball has been on full display in Broncos camp, and the results he's getting have impressed his veteran defensive coordinator.
"Bo’s played well. He’s been accurate. He’s moving very well," Joseph said on Saturday. "That’s a great sign, but his deep-ball touch has been really off the charts this training camp."
The Broncos' offense lacked an abundance of explosive plays last season. Nix and company made do and found their way, relying on their fourth-quarter poise to often come out on top, and he nearly passed for 4,000 yards.
Head coach Sean Payton wants more down-the-field passing and explosive plays, though, so the Broncos acquired Jaylen Waddle via trade in March. With new offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays, this camp certainly feels like it has featured more downfield passing , and Nix has been capitalizing on those opportunities with accurate throws.
"I know Sean wants to make more big plays this year, and it’s there. It’s happened in training camp," Joseph said. "It’s been two a day. I don’t like it for our defense, but I get it."
Nix has hit all of his receivers down the field, including Waddle, before he went down with a soft-tissue injury on Day 5 of camp. Tight end Evan Engram has been one of the early beneficiaries of Nix's downfield push.
Joseph loves the implications for the Broncos, even though these big camp plays come at the expense of his unit. Still, Joseph can still hold his head up high, as the Broncos' defense continues to win day after day of pracitce.
"Big-picture-wise, it’s so good for our team to watch him be so explosive with Waddle and Evan and those guys," Joseph said of Nix. "It’s been competitive. It’s been a great camp on both sides, and both are playing well."
The defense has been outstanding in camp, which is what you expect. Joseph's unit has been one of the NFL's best over the past two years, and the format of training camp tends to favor defense, especially early on amid offensive installs and new personnel change-over.
But the Broncos' offense hasn't backed down. There's been a heavy emphasis on the ground game, which will help build the callus Payton and Joseph are looking for, while putting in the physical work to unlock the rushing attack come September and beyond.
Nix's deep-ball touch has been great. The volume of deep passes has been higher in this camp. And Nix's throwing motion even looks a bit more polished; it's clearly something he worked on during the offseason.
Nix has relished the opportunity to go against Joseph's defense in his third training camp. The young quarterback has an 'iron sharpens iron' philosophy on the topic, even if the Broncos' defense leaves him frustrated at times.
"It’s been great," Nix said on Monday. "When you get these reps, we’re seeing every defensive structure imaginable — safeties going everywhere, blitzes coming from everywhere, fronts from everywhere.
"That helps you as a quarterback get your eyes up and slows the game down when you get into a game setting. For me, it’s been irreplaceable to go against V.J., not only his defense, but also being able to ask him questions and understand the why behind certain things. It’s helped me as a quarterback in our system to see things and find different answers within what we do."
When it comes to the possibility of Nix taking a third-year leap , all the markers are there thus far. The success he's having as a down-the-field passer has been impressive, and the arsenal around him looks much improved, not just because of the new faces but also because the young receivers have shown tremendous growth this summer.
The experience Nix and the offense are getting by going into the teeth of Joseph's unit will toughen and wisen them up. It's football resistance training of the highest order.
Now, if the Broncos can get to the bottom of all these soft-tissue injuries that have plagued them since the pads went on, this team's valuable training-camp reps would only become that much more valuable.

title: Why I'm Buying the Early Broncos Hype Around Pat Bryant
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were believed to have reached big time when they selected Illinois wide receiver Pat Bryant in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft.
Many draft analysts viewed Bryant as a late fourth- or fifth-round pick, and the Broncos took him with the No. 74 overall pick, roughly 75 spots higher than where many had him ranked.
Bryant had a slow start to his rookie season, as he hardly saw the field over the first few weeks with only 31 total snaps. However, he started to get more snaps, showcasing what he brings to the table, and he would’ve had the second-most snaps at wide receiver over the final eight weeks of the season if it weren’t for injuries.
If there's a concern about Bryant, it's the injuries he suffered as a rookie. A couple of them were scary, including one hospitalization .
He dealt with two concussions in close succession late in the season and again in the divisional round of the playoffs, and then a hamstring injury in the AFC championship game that caused him to miss time as well.
Those injuries lead to concerns for this season, especially the concussions, but hopefully Bryant wears a Guardian Cap, which has been proven to help cut down on head injuries.
Through the first two weeks of training camp this summer, Bryant has been one of the top standouts and one of the most consistent. It's still early in training camp, and the Broncos' preseason games haven’t started yet, but Bryant has made a clear leap , which is leading to some hype.
At this stage, whatever stock there is to buy on Bryant, get some. You'll be glad you did.
When Courtland Sutton missed three straight practices last week for "load management," Bryant stepped in and balled out. There hasn’t been a single training camp practice where Bryant hasn’t stood out, and that level of consistency is noteworthy and more meaningful than the individual big plays he's made.
One of the pros of Bryant pre-draft was the level of consistency in every element of his game. He wasn’t the most explosive or athletic receiver, though his tape showed that he's a better athlete than his testing suggested. He was consistent and reliable with his routes and hands, something the Broncos have struggled to find in their receivers over the past few years.
Bryant is poised to be the Broncos' No. 3 receiver, not only in snap counts but also on the stat sheet. If Bryant keeps rising, it could call Sutton's future with the Broncos beyond 2026 into question, with Bryant able to step in and replace him.
The hype around Bryant is at an all-time high, and it wouldn’t be surprising to see it grow even more. There isn’t a single player on the Broncos' roster who has made more of their opportunities and chances in practice than Bryant thus far.
With the consistency, reliability, and play-making he's shown, I'm absolutely buying the hype around Bryant. He's emerged as the Broncos' top breakout candidate for 2026.

title: Bo Nix Weighs In on Broncos' Davis Webb Booth-vs.-Sideline Decision
full_text:
One big decision new Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb has been mulling over is whether he'll call plays from the sideline or from the booth.
This will be the first time in Webb's coaching career that he'll be a primary play-caller, but it's only been four years or so since he was playing quarterback in the NFL. He went from starting the season finale at quarterback for the New York Giants to joining Sean Payton in Denver as the Broncos' quarterbacks coach in a matter of weeks in January of 2023.
Webb's rise as an NFL coach has been meteoric, and it's thanks, in large part, to Payton's competence as a head coach and to how he has transformed the Broncos from being a cellar-dweller the preceding eight years into a bona fide Super Bowl contender.
Bo Nix has also had a lot to do with the Broncos' turnaround and Webb's rapid rise through the coaching ranks . On Saturday, Webb said after practice that, while it hasn't been officially decided, his preference will be to call plays from the sideline, and on Monday, Payton echoed that.
How does Nix feel about it, though?
“I’ve always loved it from a quarterback to a play-caller when they’re on the sideline with me," Nix said after Day 9's training camp practice . "I feel like they get the feel of the game a little bit differently."
To each his own, but it's much harder to feel the energy and momentum of a game from a booth up in the sky. The more remote a coach is from the action, the harder it is to pick up the vibes of a game, and all the communication with the field has to be over the phone.
Vic Fangio has always preferred to call plays from the booth as a defensive coordinator, but when the Broncos hired him as head coach in 2019 , he wanted to still call his defense, which meant he had to get comfortable doing it from the sideline because that's where the head coach has to be to manage the game and interact with the officials.
That was a work in progress for Fangio, but he eventually got used to calling plays from field level. As soon as he went back to being a coordinator, though, he returned to the booth.
Wade Phillips, another former Broncos head coach and the team's defensive coordinator in Super Bowl 50, was a sideline play-caller. Both coaches are among the most highly revered and influential defensive minds of their era, but they each have a different feel for play-calling.
"It’s obviously seeing the game from a different vantage point, but I think they get to feel the emotions on the sideline," Nix said. "They get to feel the comments from us coming off the sideline, what we’re seeing and all that kind of stuff."
Many of the best play-callers in the NFL are former quarterbacks, including Payton. Webb is the latest in a long line of quarterbacks-turned-play-callers whose entire football perspective has always been at the field level. Why try to fiddle with the touch-and-feel aspect of being on the sideline now?
"From his point of view and playing quarterback his whole career, I think that’s just where he feels comfortable," Nix said of Webb. "A lot of former quarterbacks like to call it from the sideline."
As a pro, Nix has always had a direct line to his play-caller on the sideline. After a series, he could approach Payton and have a face-to-face discussion about a given play or some trend or tell he's seeing in the defense.
The same will hold true with Webb, who's also always been on the sideline with Nix, as both his quarterbacks coach and as the Broncos' pass game coordinator last year.
"I like when the play caller is there with me, and I can come off and have the eye-to-eye conversation," Nix said. "We can sit down and look at the pictures and go through them together and really get to hear from him and not have to call up to the office or get on a headset. I think the eye-to-eye communication is really important, so I’m excited that he’s going to be down there with us.”
The plan is likely for Webb to call the plays from the sideline. The Broncos could always use the preseason games to test the difference, with Webb on the sideline in one game and up in the booth in another, but if he, Payton, and Nix already have a strong preference, then the young offensive coordinator would be better off utilizing these exhibition games as an opportunity to really start honing his craft as a play-caller and finding his groove.
Again, Webb said he's leaning toward the sideline, but he also wanted Payton's take on it before making a final decision. Hearing from Payton on the subject two days later, it sounds like the decision has been made.
“Well, it’s not like we’re splitting the atom," Payton said. "That’s probably where he’ll be with his communication and the QBs. It’s an area where I felt comfortable, and I think you get the plays in so quickly either from up or down, but I have that same vision.”
Webb has expressed his excitement for Nix's third year, pointing to the parallels he saw as Josh Allen's backup in Buffalo when the Bills acquired Stefon Diggs via trade ahead of the quarterback's third season. The idea being that Jaylen Waddle's arrival could serve as a similar Year-3 catalyst for Nix.
That could well be the case, but also having Webb as his play-caller might be a springboard in its own right for Nix. It's going to be fun to see how these two young men continue to grow together as player and coach.

title: Broncos Camp Day 9: More Injured Starters | Takeaways | Winners and Losers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were back at it on Monday for Day 9 of training camp.
The Broncos took Sunday off again, which will be a common thread of what remains of camp and the preseason. After the high volume of soft-tissue injuries that have beset the Broncos since they donned the pads a week ago, taking Sundays off in August, as a rule, is wise.
Head coach Sean Payton was back at practice after missing most of Friday and all of Saturday's session as he traveled to Canton, OH, to serve as Drew Brees's presenter to the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
I wish I could report that the Broncos had a day without an injury, but alas, that's not how Monday played out. That's where we'll start.
The Broncos' No. 1 running back left practice accompanied by trainers on Monday. Considering Dobbins's injury history, that's the last thing Broncos fans want to hear after he was re-signed to a two-year, $16 million deal in March.
After practice, Payton didn't sound worried about Dobbins.
“Yeah, soft tissue," Payton said of Dobbins. "I think he’s gonna be fine. We’re just being smart with it."
Time will tell how much practice Dobbins will miss, but considering his experience as a seventh-year veteran, he can afford the missed reps. This may be a reality check to remind the Broncos to go easy with Dobbins this summer, especially after he "pinky promised" media and fans as camp began that he'd stay healthy for the full 17 games this season.
Outside of defensive lineman Matt Henningsen's season-ending Achilles tear , most of the injuries the Broncos have sustained since camp started have been of the soft-tissue variety — muscle strains. Sounding a bit frustrated and perplexed, Payton plans to figure out why it's happening so frequently this summer.
"We've got to get a handle on some of the soft tissues," he said. "We've had a couple either strains, hamstring, or groins. We'll continue to fight through that."
The Broncos will examine their pre-practice routines to see if any trends can be identified relative to when certain players suffered a soft-tissue injury, but Payton doesn't believe the heat has anything to do with it. He also made it clear that the players need to be conscious of their bodies, meaning they need to speak up if something doesn't feel right.
"I don't think it's heat-related as much as you're always trying to look at your pre-practice routine—your hydration, obviously," Payton said. "It's incumbent on the player—it's hard for anyone to know your soft tissue... I'm always looking at what we did leading up to maybe a period where someone had a strain, so we had a warm-down during practice. We'll continue to focus on it."
The Broncos did a warm-down after practice, with some additional stretching and conditioning. This is an issue that Payton needs to get ahold of fast.
It's unclear why, but Surtain practiced on the side field with the other injured and rehabbing players, per 9NEWS ' Mike Klis . Likely another soft-tissue situation, Surtain is the fifth starter to get bitten with a strain since the pads went on a week ago.
Fans shouldn't worry about Surtain, though I understand any anxiety surrounding Dobbins. Fortunately, both appear to be minor injuries. If the Broncos were in-season, they might be limited in practice or even miss a session or two, but they'd likely be playing on gameday.
Wide receiver Michael Bandy also exited practice early, per The Denver Post 's Parker Gabriel . Hopefully, it's just another soft-tissue thing that won't keep him out long.
Once again on the side field today were center Luke Wattenberg, wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr., safety Devon Key, offensive guard Nick Gargiulo (PUP list), cornerback Sam Fresch Jr., and outside linebacker Dasan McCullough.
After exiting Day 8's practice early , defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike returned to practice on Monday, as did tight end Nate Adkins.
Second-team center Alex Forysth was not seen at Day 9's practice. It's unclear what's going on with him, but with Wattenberg also out, Michael Dieter ran with the first team ( Gabriel ). Rookie Gavin Ortega continued to get a lot of work as the only other backup center.
Broncos Owners Greg Penner, Carrie Walton Penner & Rob Walton catching up with HC Sean Payton & GM George Paton at today’s #BroncosCamp practice. pic.twitter.com/NtT6SljcMB
Owners Rob Walton, Carrie Walton Penner, and Greg Penner were in attendance at Broncos Park, observing practice. Penner, also the team's CEO, is heavily involved in the day-to-day operation of the team, but his wife, Carrie, and father-in-law, Rob, were out there with him.
The Walton-Penner group has done a tremendous job of turning the Broncos around. Hiring Payton as head coach in 2023 and choosing to keep GM George Paton at his post has paid dividends.
Beyond purchasing the Broncos, the ownership group has also invested greatly in upgrading Empower Field at Mile High — installing a massive new scoreboard and prioritizing the upkeep of the playing surface — not to mention the $175 million new training facility and office building at Dove Valley. They're also far along on the site for the new stadium at Burnham Yard, recently unveiling the new " master plan " for the planned project.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos haven't wanted for much since the Walton-Penners purchased the team.
The ground attack continues to be a focus for the Broncos as training camp marches on. Day 9 saw the coaches linger on the run game, going deep into team period before the first Bo Nix pass was thrown.
Whether that's a new leaf Payton is trying to turn over or an emphasis that offensive coordinator Davis Webb has brought to the proceedings, the run game has taken center stage this training camp. The tight ends are being asked to stay in and block more, including Evan Engram, which not only hints at a commitment to the ground attack, but also the possibility for some big play-action passing in this offense.
In Nix's opinion, it's all part of forming the championship-caliber callus.
"Well, run periods, I think they help practice flow a little bit differently. I think when you start with run period, when you do a couple run periods, it makes practice extremely physical, and to be a great team and to win down the stretch, to win Super Bowls, you have to be able to run the ball," Nix said after Monday's practice.
"So, to be able to practice that, and especially bring the physicality early at practice, when the defense knows it's run period, when the offense knows it's run period, and you've got to block things up and get good runs off, I think that's when teams become tough. I think that's when teams develop that physicality that's needed throughout the season, especially in the postseason, to win tough games. I think it just sets a standard for practice, that it's going to be a tough, physical practice."
Engram started off camp with some big plays down the field . That vertical aspect has cooled as camp has marched on, but the most intriguing aspect of Engram's summer has been his inclusion in these bare-knuckle run periods.
Engram isn't leaving the field as he did so often on early downs last season. Engram is staying in to block, along with Adam Trautman.
Payton talked about Engram being more comfortable in the scheme this time around, with a year under his belt. But Engram's inclusion in the run game this summer, as Nix explained after practice, is all by design.
"I think his ability—strengths in the run game—are what's showing right now. He's a willing blocker," Nix said of Engram. "I think last year, we used him a little bit more as a vertical pass threat, but I think him getting in the box and blocking is going to open some more things up. And that's a game-plan thing. That's a coaching thing, to put him in that position.
"But I also think he's willing and able, and I think that's part of his game that he's going really to be able to show off this year and not be on and off the field. He'll just be able to play. He and…

title: Potential Impact of Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins' Soft-Tissue Injury
full_text:
Denver Broncos starting running back J.K. Dobbins exited Monday's training camp practice with an apparent injury and did not return.
After practice, head coach Sean Payton confirmed Dobbins is dealing with a soft-tissue issue and expects him to be OK going forward.
“Yeah, soft tissue, I think he’s gonna be fine. We’re just being smart with it," Payton told reporters.
This has always been the rap on Dobbins, who signed a two-year extension with the organization earlier this year. He's a fantastic back when on the field (as evidenced by his 2025 production). The problem is, he's rarely on the field for long (as evidenced by his 2025 season-ending foot malady).
The narrative reached such a critical juncture that last month Dobbins made a " pinky promise " to be available for all 17 regular-season games this year — something he's yet to accomplish since entering the NFL in 2020.
"I've had three major injuries, all on my left leg—the knee, the Achilles, and the foot," Dobbins said. "That's three. It's over. Whoever's got the voodoo doll for my left leg is done with it now."
Dobbins is the latest Bronco to suffer a soft-tissue injury through roughly two weeks of camp; it's also claimed wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims, among others.
“Gotta get a handle on some of the soft tissues. We’ve had either strains, hamstrings, or groins. [We'll] continue to fight through that,” Payton said.
Similar to Waddle, even if the injury is minor in nature, it's possible (if not probable) that Dobbins is held out or at least limited in the run-up to Friday's preseason opener against the Atlanta Falcons.
That being the case, the Broncos will likely put a bit more on the plate of fourth-round rookie RB Jonah Coleman, who's presumably the next man up on the depth chart with RJ Harvey largely functioning as a pass-catcher in camp.
An extended look at Coleman wouldn't be the worst thing considering he's been among the summer's standouts , and could be the future of the position when Dobbins no longer calls Denver home.
"I think the young runner, you don’t feel a rookie with Jonah," Payton said on Aug. 5. "He’s playing. It’s been harder with some of the linemen because we haven’t been in pads in fairness to them. Then a couple of these young linebackers, we’re getting to see them move around, make the calls. There’s a lot to that position, a lot of it is key and diagnose. That’s been good.”

title: Broncos' LB Competition Gets a New Wrinkle With Return of Jordan Turner
full_text:
The Denver Broncos opened training camp by placing Turner on the Active/Non-Football Injury list and offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo on the Action/Physically Unable to Perform list. Both men have counted against the Broncos' 90-man offseason roster.
On Monday, Day 9 of Broncos camp, the team announced that Turner has been activated off the NFI list. The second-year linebacker was out there in pads, practicing with his teammates.
Turner, 6-foot-1 and 231 pounds, joined the Broncos last season as an undrafted rookie out of Michigan State. He impressed the team enough during training camp and the preseason to earn a spot on the practice squad.
Through gameday elevations, Turner was heavily involved in special teams as a rookie. The Broncos utilized him as a depth option at linebacker when Dre Greenlaw was suspended in Week 8.
Ahead of the Broncos' Week 15 home game against the Green Bay Packers, the Broncos officially promoted Turner to the 53-man roster . He was off the practice squad. It also happened on his birthday (December 13).
Turner appeared in seven regular-season games as a rookie, plus both playoff games. He finished the 2025 season with seven tackles and a quarterback hit.
The Broncos like Turner a lot. He's a quintessential 'stack' linebacker, and the only such player among the Broncos' depth players.
All this being said, Turner has to make up for lost time, as several depth linebackers have shined through the first eight practices of training camp. Behind the starters — Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad — the Broncos have two linebacker spots up for grabs on the 53-man roster this year.
Since camp began, all four of the active depth linebackers have had their moments, including Karene Reid , Levelle Bailey, Red Murdock, and Taurean York. Reid beat out Turner and Bailey for a roster spot out of camp last year, though Denver kept the latter two around on the practice squad.
During Saturday's scrimmage (Day 8), Bailey garnered an extended look with the first-team defense while Singleton enjoyed a rest day. Bailey has looked good so far in his third training camp with the Broncos.
"We have two college free agent linebackers that we like, Levelle Bailey, who got a little taste, and then Jordan [Turner], who was really good on special teams," head coach Sean Payton said during his end-of-season press conference this past January.
As for the rookies, Murdock — a seventh-round draft pick — was a bit quiet over the first week of camp, but he's begun to pick up a head of steam over the past two practices. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph felt like Murdock was in his head a little bit early on, "overprocessing things."
"Red has had his best two days the last couple of days," Joseph said after Day 8's scrimmage. "Red, from Day 1, has made every call cleanly, but he was kind of overprocessing things. Now he’s playing fast again. He’s punching the ball out, like yesterday’s practice."
The Broncos are asking Murdock to make the calls on third-team defense, which gives fans an inkling of how the team values him, and that differs from York's responsibilities. Murdock has had to process more cerebral information as the play-caller.
York has been consistently impressive, making plays all over the field, but he has a mountain of obstacles to contend with on top of his lack of draft pedigree, especially his 5-foot-10, 220-pound size.
Turner now enters the competition. The Broncos clearly value him, but it's a true open competition for the No. 3 and No. 4 linebacker spots on the 53-man roster.
As good as Turner is against the run, he could really help his roster outlook by showing some progress in coverage this summer. Coverage may never be his strong suit, but he's strong at the point of attack and good at stacking and shedding blockers to get to the ball-carrier.
The Broncos' first preseason game is this week, as they'll travel to take on the Atlanta Falcons on Friday, August 14 .

title: Winners and Losers From Day 11 of 2026 Detroit Lions Training Camp
full_text:
The Detroit Lions held a shortened, non-contact practice Tuesday ahead of their preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals.
Coach Dan Campbell doesn't plan to play many of the team's starters in Thursday's game, and with Wednesday being a travel day the Lions used Tuesday to get some reps for players not playing in the exhibition game.
The head coach expressed his excitement for the preseason opener, particularly for the young players who will have a chance to show off their development in terms of technique after being coached for the first three weeks.
"I think always with these is, as a coach, you want to see some of these guys, you've been coaching them on technique, fundamentals," Campbell said. "The scheme is not as big of an issue right now, I'm not concerned with that because with what we're giving them they're gonna be able to play fast, but how do they handle competition? Cincinnati, I think (Bengals coach) Zac (Taylor) is gonna play those guys a couple of drives, their starters. So it'll be a great look for our guys."
Here are winners and losers, as well as what we're learning from day 11 of Lions training camp, with some insights provided by the team website .
Avonte Maddox returned after missing practice Monday. With the latest update on Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch being that they're expected to return after the start of the season, Maddox is believed to be part of the team's starting safety tandem for the start of the regular season along with Chuck Clark.
Derrick Moore (groin), Malcolm Rodriguez (ankle) and Sione Vaki (eye/broken nose) were all getting work in with trainers. Running back Jabari Small, cornerback Khalil Dorsey and offensive lineman Devin Cochran were all out for undisclosed reasons.
The Lions remain without center Cade Mays (wrist), linebacker Jimmy Rolder (hamstring), offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (undsiclosed soft-tissue), Isiah Pacheco (MCL) and defensive end Payton Turner (back). Campbell noted that Kerby Joseph is away dealing with a personal issue.
After a slight lull in productivity over the recent stretch of practices, cornerback Ennis Rakestraw appeared to bounce back for a strong day on Tuesday. He was matched up with Jameson Williams three separate times in one-on-one drills, and Rakestraw had a good showing.
On the first rep, Rakestraw was in phase from the snap against Williams and forced an overthrow. He was also in good coverage on a throw in the end zone to force an incompletion. The third rep went to Williams, who brought in a slant route that Rakestraw initially deflected.
Another defensive back that had a bounce back day is Roger McCreary, who reportedly won two of his three reps against Greg Dortch.
Sam LaPorta has been somewhat quiet to start camp, but reviews indicate he is rounding into season shape. When the Lions began a team rep, the Iowa product showed up in a big way.
LaPorta had two big catches with the first team offense, beating a linebacker for a big gain on an out-and-up. Then, he burnt Thomas Harper for a touchdown grab in the red-zone.
After missing the last seven games of the year with a herniated disk in his back, LaPorta continues to incrementally improve as he gets reacclimated. This is a positive development, as his absence was felt heavily throughout the offense after his injury.
Additional Lions Insight: Analyzing First Unofficial Depth Chart
With the Lions not playing quarterback Jared Goff in the preseason opener, Josh Dobbs could be thrust into action shortly into his tenure with the team. Dobbs took team reps for the first time on Tuesday, running one drive.
He started strong, firing a completion to Cedrick Wilson between a linebacker and a safety to move inside the 10-yard line.
A penalty derailed the drive, as Miles Frazier jumped early. Dobbs wouldn't finish the drive, as he was relieved by Luke Altmyer before third-down. According to reports, Dobbs stated he came out because he is still learning the team's red-zone plays after arriving Sunday.
Altmyer was unable to lead the offense into the end zone, as his pass to Greg Dortch was stopped short to force a field goal.
The Lions finished practice with a situation for the offense. They were down 10 with all three timeouts with under four yards to go. After an early completion, the offense took a step back as Aidan Hutchinson sacked Goff after he beat Blake Miller.
Detroit's offense got the yardage back after a defensive holding, then ultimately couldn't move the chains as Goff overthrew Brock Wright. They were in range for a field goal, so they were able to get within a score.
After notching the needed stop to get the ball back to the ofense, who took over at their own 20-yard line with 1:38 left. It ended poorly, as a sack by Avonte Maddox set the offense back. The Lions got yardage back with short completions from Goff to Gibbs and St. Brown, but a last-ditch attempt from Goff to Williams was ruled incomplete as he came down with the ball out of bounds.
Coaches overruled the incompletion, instead opting to get the offense some extra work. Yet, their fortunes stayed the same as Goff was intercepted by Thomas Harper to end practice.
1.) Cornerback Keith Abney had a tough day, getting beat by Dominic Lovett on a slant and also being whistled for penalties working against Tom Kennedy and Wilson. Kennedy also got the best of him near the goal line, making a leaping catch on a fade route.
2.) Nick Whiteside had an interception for the third straight day, picking off a pass working against Isaac TeSlaa during one-on-ones.
3.) Offensive tackle Blake Miller had a big block during team drills, taking care of Avonte Maddox on a screen pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown.

title: Analyzing Detroit Lions First 2026 Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their first unofficial depth chart ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
Detroit has its first preseason game on Thursday, so the unofficial depth chart adds some clarity to how the organization may be thinking heading into the opener. However, this depth chart is compiled by the communication staff and as a result may not be entirely indicative of how the coaching staff is thinking at this stage of training camp.
Here are four takeaways from the team's first released depth chart of the 2026 season.
Detroit Lions first unofficial depth chart @DetroitPodcast @CBooher_ pic.twitter.com/QUjirKWf4Q
The Lions currently have three position battles going on for spots along their offensive line. They entered camp with competitions for right tackle and left guard, and another wrench was thrown into their plans with the injury to center Cade Mays .
Currently, the Lions have veteran Larry Borom listed ahead of rookie Blake Miller at right tackle. Miller has taken his fair share of first team reps at the position, and is being viewed with a very realistic chance at starting the opener at the position after the team drafted him 17th overall.
At left guard, Juice Scruggs is currently listed ahead of Christian Mahogany. However, Mahogany has drawn strong reviews for his performance early in camp and is right in the mix to win the position.
Additionally, Scruggs is expected to get reps at center when he returns from a soft tissue injury, and as a result Mahogany may still be the favorite to win his job back and start at left guard.
When Scruggs returns, the Lions will have him competing to start at center with Seth McLaughlin and Michael Niese. The depth chart lists Niese ahead of McLaughlin, but it was McLaughlin taking first team reps at the position in Monday's practice.
The Lions have an established top four at the wide receiver position, but there is plenty of competition for the fifth spot. Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Greg Dortch are all roster locks, but there are several players in the mix for the final one or two roster spots at the position.
The starters are St. Brown, Williams and TeSlaa. With this pairing, which would be 11 personnel, it would likely be St. Brown in the slot with Williams and TeSlaa out wide. Dortch, meanwhile, is behind St. Brown which checks out with him being expected to be a slot-exclusive presence.
Dominic Lovett is listed as the backup behind Williams, while Tom Kennedy is the third-string in the slot. Those two players are expected to be competing for the fifth spot, so the Lions could make the choice dpending on which player offers more versatility.
Cedrick Wilson Jr. is the backup behind TeSlaa. Another wide receiver with a big physical profile, Wilson has flashed with several strong moments in camp.
The Lions' depth chart lists two linebackers and a nickel cornerback, which could be an indication of coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's intent to play more nickel defense as opposed to base in 2026. The Lions have had different players playing the position throughout camp, with Roger McCreary currently holding top billing on the depth chart.
McCreary's performance throughout camp has been up and down , with the consensus being that he has work to do to become a starter within the unit. Head coach Dan Campbell stated that Christian Izien would also get some work at the spot, and Izien is currently listed second behind McCreary.
At linebacker, the Lions currently have Devin White and Malcolm Rodriguez listed as the top two backups behind starters Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes. White, a former All-Pro, seems to have the leg up in the competition to be the top option in Detroit's three-linebacker packages.
Several standouts have emerged amidst the Lions' roster through the first 10 days of training camp. Among them are defensive linemen Ahmed Hassanein and Tyler Lacy, who have both been showing up in a big way throughout camp.
Detroit has deployed a big end traditionally in their defense, and both Lacy and Hassanein have played well in this role throughout camp. On the first depth chart, they are listed second and third, respectively, behind presumed veteran starter D.J. Wonnum opposite of Aidan Hutchinson.
Another development on the defensive line is the fact that undrafted free agent Anthony Lucas has been listed ahead of veteran Payton Turner. A former first-round pick who has had his career interrupted by injuries, Turner has been absent from practice since completing the first day and could be in danger of not making the roster if he remains sidelined.
Another rising defender is cornerback Nick Whiteside. Viewed as a potential afterthought not long ago in Detroit's secondary, Whiteside has generated a ton of positive momentum behind a strong camp.
On the first depth chart, Whiteside is listed as the backup behind D.J. Reed. This puts him ahead of Khalil Dorsey and rookie Keith Abney, which would be a very positive development for his hopes of making the roster.
Both Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are listed as starters on this depth chart, but neither is currently expected to play in Week 1. Instead, their backups are listed as Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox, and that pairing is anticipated to be the starting duo against the New Orleans Saints.

title: Detroit Lions Will First Wear 'Rivalries' Uniform Against Division Rival
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will wear their "rivalry" uniform for the very first time against the Minnesota Vikings on November 1, 2026 at Ford Field.
While the design has yet to be released publicly, retiring team president Rod Wood expressed at the owners meeting he believes fans will be impressed.
“The NFL is home to some of the biggest football rivalries, and today marks a historical moment for the NFL as we share Rivalries with the world," Chief NFL Revenue Officer Renie Anderson said back in 2025. “Together with Nike, we are harnessing the power of rivalry matchups to bring fan excitement and community pride to the next level. Through specially designed player uniforms and limited-edition fan gear, we will embark on a journey that inspires competitive spirit and reveals the winner in all of us.
"Teams from the AFC South and NFC North will debut their Rivalries uniforms in 2026, followed by NFC East and AFC West teams in 2027, and teams from the AFC North and NFC South in 2028."
It is believed the official design of the uniform will be revealed on August 25, 2026.

title: Lions Kerby Joseph Health Update, Is Away Dealing With 'Personal Issue'
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided an update on All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph ahead of Tuesday’s training camp practice.
Joseph has been sidelined due to a nagging knee injury that held him out of the final 11 games of the 2025 season. He has yet to participate in practice in training camp, but has been observed putting in work with trainers on the side at points throughout camp.
On Tuesday, Campbell said that Joseph is dealing with a personal matter, and noted that he remains on roughly the same trajectory to return to action as fellow safety Brian Branch. Branch is currently out while rehabbing a torn Achilles suffered in December.
“Kerby right now, first of all, he’s dealing with a personal issue right now. But his rehab is coming along very well,” Campbell said. “That is still, I still see him on the Branch plan if that makes sense. And Branch is doing well too. Those guys, we’re talking about on down the road, the season’s already begun. But I like where Kerby’s at.”
At the start of training camp, Campbell stated that getting Joseph back for the regular season opener against the New Orleans Saints would be a "bonus."
Joseph was coming off an All-Pro season after leading the NFL in interceptions in 2024. He signed a four-year contract extension prior to last year, but began dealing with swelling in his knee during training camp.
He initially tried to play through the injury through the start of the regular season, and recorded three interceptions in his first five games. However, the pain became too much in Week 6 against the Kansas City Chiefs, and that would be the final game he played in last season.
The specific details of Joseph’s injury remain relatively uncertain, with speculation being that it could be a chronic injury dealing with cartilage in his knee.
When healthy, Joseph and Branch have formed one of the NFL's top safety duos. Joseph has earned a reputation as a ballhawk, with 20 career interceptions in his first four seasons. He spoke to the media earlier in training camp, and stated that he's confident he'll be able to contribute at some point in 2026.

title: Detroit Lions Do Not Seem Impressed With CB Ennis Rakestraw
full_text:
Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw has had an up and down start to training camp. Unfortunately for the third-year defensive back, teammate Nick Whiteside has made many more plays and has earned more reps on the outside with the first-team defense.
Lately, the former second-round pick has been working more with the second-team defense.
Head coach recently Dan Campbell recently addressed why the team brought in former Dallas Cowboys cornerback Trevon Diggs and if adding more high-level competition to that group was reflective of his comfort level with the cornerback room.
His comments raised many eyebrows, as it appears the coaching staff is developing more trust in other players.
While the team did not sign Diggs, it appears the coaching is keeping their options open regarding who will start opposite of D.J. Reed.
"Rakestraw, look, he's had some ups and downs. He needs to string a few days together here of some good stuff, but he can do that and he's gifted. Now that being said, look, we're always looking to upgrade the competition," said Campbell. "Is there a way to bring in somebody that we feel like can push the other guys or has a chance to help us? So, that's why we brought him in.
"Look, Brad (Holmes) is always looking that way. How can we bring in somebody that we feel like maybe has a chance here or can upgrade us or upgrade the position ? So, that's an ongoing process.”
Additional Detroit Lions Insider Analysis: Week 2 Rookie Training Camp Report
Throughout the spring and summer, the coaching staff has praised the secondary, offering optimism the group has the right mix of veterans and youth.
Terrion Arnold not working out is a major setback, but the team is hopeful Rakestraw can keep developing while Whiteside and Rock Ya-Sin continue to also compete for playing time.
“I do like those guys. It's a good group. Obviously (D.J.) Reed’s down right now, but I don't feel like that's a significant injury. It's a soft tissue. He'll be back. So, that's a good thing," said Campbell. "And I feel like Rock (Ya-Sin) is having a good camp. I feel like Nick (Whiteside) has had a very good camp. Roger (McCreary) can cover. He's had some ups and downs, but he can cover. We got (Khalil Dorsey) Dorse, (Keith) Abney. I mean, I like the group."

title: Everything Jared Goff Said During Day 10 Lions Training Camp Interview
full_text:
Here is everything Detroit Lions said to local reporters following Day 10 of training camp.
Thoughout about working with Lions C Seth McLaughlin: “Yeah, he did a good job. He stepped in there nicely and didn't miss much of a beat, mentally. Obviously he did a good job. And I don't know, I haven't seen the film. I wouldn't call myself an evaluator of talent at the O-line, but they'll be able to better tell, but I though he did a good job.”
How the communication went between him and center Seth McLaughlin: “Yeah it was really good.”
Dan Campbell recently talked about him improving year over year: “That’s good, yeah. I think it’s just human nature, you start realizing where things can slip and you don’t want to allow that to happen and the older I get, the more I'm learning and try to stay on that type of stuff. But yeah, that's good that it's noticeable. It's not necessarily something I'm conscious of every day, but I think it maybe just overall a little bit more of that mindset this year.”
What his comfort level is working alongside Drew Petzing: “Really good. I think the last four or five practices, it's really started to come together nicely where we're running stuff that looks the same but is different and able to mess with the defense in certain looks and do a little bit more than just call the play on the paper. So, it's been great.”
What growth has he seen from Jameson Williams year over year: “ Yeah shoot. I mean, he's the best example of that. He just continues to get better. And the stuff that he's doing now that's nuanced, that you can't really teach, you can feel coverage and he can change his stem of his route, that little stuff has been so cool to see him start to adopt that and understand coverage and understand space. And that's the next level for him and he's done a great job of it.”
How fatherhood has changed training camp: “Yeah, makes it fun when it's over. I get to see her and yeah, it's really fun. It's really cool. Something you've always dreamed about as a player, having your child here and her being able to enjoy it. I know she probably won't remember these days, but I know I will.”
Additional Detroit Lions Insider Analysis: 2026 Preseason Opener
The importance of having tight end Sam LaPorta back at practice: “Yeah, he's a stud. He had a good play down the field today on third down and he's a stud. He's the same guy every day and continues to get better like they all do and got to find ways to give him the ball.”
What his initial reaction was to learning center Cade Mays is going to miss time: “Yeah, it sucks. He's done such a good job up to this point. It was kind of a freak deal that happened to him and yeah, it just stinks, but I know he'll work his way back here and be ready to go at some point.”
What him and Cade Mays will work on off the field to make sure the transition will be seamless when he does return: “Other than watching tape, no. I mean, he'll be fine. He just continues to stay on top of it and he'll be just fine.”
What he is focused on to get on the same page as Drew Petzing: “Honestly, just constant communication. Telling him what I like, what I don't like, him telling me what he wants to do and what he doesn't want and constantly talking, constantly giving him suggestions, some of them are good, some of them aren't. And that blend, it eventually blends into this thing that we both love and we're working towards that and we're doing a good job.”
What he has seen from the Lions' defense: “Yeah, it's been good. Today they got after us a little bit. I think they do a good job of creating chaos and creating hard looks. And obviously the front seven gets the notoriety right now with all the big-time players, but the backend's doing a good job too with the veteran guys. I thought (Lions S) Chuck (Clark) made a great play on me today and almost had another one on me. (Lions DB) Avonte (Maddox)'s doing a great job, (Lions CB) D.J. (Reed), when he's out there is doing a great job. They're competing, it's fun and it's competitive.”
How he defines the defense creating chaos: “A variety of pressures and looks up front, creates a lot of communication for us and creates that chaos.”
What ways Lions rookie OT Blake Miller has grown during camp: “Yeah, he just continues to not make the same mistake twice, I think. And his mistakes go down and down every day and I think that's what you're looking for. You're here as a rookie, he's going to make mistakes, it's going to happen, certainly in camp. But every day seems like it's getting less and less and he's starting to settle in. “
What are his impressions of Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers: “Gosh, big question. Aaron's one of the all-time greats and I loved competing against him when he was in Green Bay. Got to play him once last year, but it was always fun to compete against him as a guy I grew up watching, a guy I grew up a fan of, and getting a chance to play against him and to win and try to compete against somebody at that level, it was always great. And he's been great to me and I wish him the best.”
Thoughts on Aaron Rodgers still playing at age 42: “Yeah pretty good, something to look forward to for me.”
Would he would want to play that long in the NFL: “I don’t know, we’ll see.”
On building the relationship with a backup center and ramping it up now that Cade Mays will miss time: “Yeah, certainly ramp it up now. Seth (McLaughlin) and I, I don't know if we had a rep together until today. But yeah, he did a good job, man, he really did. He stepped in there, he was good authority with his calls, he was sharp. He was decisive, I think that's all you can ask for. You're going to make mistakes, things are going to happen, but he was decisive and he was quick and commanded the huddle well, it was good.”
What is his relationship like with Lions OL Juice Scruggs: “Yeah, same thing. I got more reps with him in OTAs and even some in camp, I believe at some point. But yeah, whenever he gets back, he’ll be in the mix as well.”
Reaction to Dan Campbell saying that he is going to push Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs: “I don’t know, I guess we’ll see. I’m sure we’ll give him the ball a few times a game and see what he can do.”
Reaction to Teddy Bridgewater’s retirement and what he remembers from working alongside Josh Dobbs: “Yeah man, Teddy, I'll miss him, man. He was great to me, he was great to the guys around the locker room, great to have in the room. Sad deal the way it happened, but it is what it is and I wish him the best. I hope he's happy, I know he's happy and hope everything goes well for him. With Josh, Josh and I met in high school at the Elite 11, 15 years ago or so. And so I've known Josh for a long time, competed against him. He was here for, what was it, 10 days or something? He was great to have in the room then, and I'm excited to have him back.”
Does he have thoughts about how much longer he wants to play in the NFL: “ No, I’m right in the middle of it. No, I haven't. I think I said this other day, until I don't feel like I can help a team win a championship. And I think that's going to be a long time.”

title: Is Trevon Diggs Right Addition for Detroit Lions?
full_text:
Two weeks into training camp, it's become increasingly apparent that the Lions need help in the secondary, particularly at cornerback .
Notably, Detroit is looking to fill the void opposite starting outside cornerback D.J. Reed, a hole which was created by the release of former first-round pick Terrion Arnold in June.
Rock Ya-Sin is presently the favorite to capture the job, though third-year pro Ennis Rakestraw Jr. has also received first-team reps on the boundary so far in camp.
Offseason acquisition Roger McCreary could also be in the mix, although he has struggled and is more likely to earn the starting gig at nickel corner.
Consequently, it wouldn’t hurt Lions general manager Brad Holmes to attempt to strengthen the team’s defensive backfield prior to the start of the regular season.
Enter veteran corner Trevon Diggs, who earned a tryout with Dan Campbell’s squad on Sunday. It doesn’t guarantee the Lions will add him to the roster, yet there is merit behind doing just that.
At his very best, Diggs is one of the NFL’s most prolific ballhawks , most notably intercepting 11 passes during his career-best 2021 campaign. Throughout his career, he has also showcased the ability to consistently make plays on the football and provide top-notch coverage against the league’s best receivers.
Yet, there are valid concerns with Diggs, too.
The former Dallas Cowboys cornerback has dealt with multiple injuries in recent seasons, and his overall production has taken a hit as a result. In fact, he’s earned Pro Football Focus overall grades of just 56.6 (2024) and 59.8 (2025) the past two seasons.
However, I believe the former Crimson Tide DB has a chance to get back on track heading into his age-28 season. And undoubtedly, a healthy Diggs – who would be a game-changing presence on the boundary – would significantly fortify Detroit's secondary.
The Lions have a clear-cut void at cornerback, and Diggs has the potential to make that weakness a strength.
The risk is undeniable, but so is the upside. Subsequently, I believe it'd be worthwhile for Holmes & Co. to seriously look into adding Diggs at some point during training camp.

title: Winners and Losers From Day 10 of 2026 Detroit Lions Training Camp
full_text:
The Detroit Lions returned to the practice field with another padded session on Monday.
Detroit is making its preparations for its first preseason game of the 2026 slate, as they will take on the Cincinnati Bengals in the opener. While many starters aren't expected to play, the Lions are going to get first-round pick Blake Miller some action in the matchup.
With that in mind, the Lions conducted a contact practice Monday that had officials present.
"We're back in pads today. We've got the officials out there," coach Dan Campbell said. "It'll be good. It'll be competitive, get these guys going again and try to get better today."
Here are winners and losers, as well as what we're learning, from day 10 of Detroit Lions training camp with insights provided by the team website.
The big news of the day came before practice, when Campbell announced that the Lions would be without center Cade Mays for a significant amount of time due to a wrist injury. With Juice Scruggs also sidelined due to a soft-tissue injury, Seth McLaughlin handled the Lions' first team center duties.
Additionally, Campbell noted that Isiah Pacheco has an MCL sprain. Pacheco is expected to be ready for the preseason, but with he and Sione Vaki both sidelined there are opportunities available for players like Jabari Small and Jacob Saylors.
The Lions were reportedly still without D.J. Reed (groin), Sione Vaki (eye/broken nose), Payton Turner (back), Jimmy Rolder (hamstring), Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee). Wide rceeiver Greg Dortch and linebacker Damone Clark also didn't practice for undisclosed reasons.
Defensive end Derrick Moore and defensive tackle Aidan Keanaaina were both out, and Keanaaina was placed on injured reserve following practice. Also out was safety Avonte Maddox. With Joseph and Branch both on PUP, Maddox's absence left the Lions further depleted at safety.
On a brighter note, the Lions did get wide receiver Cederick Wilson Jr. and defensive tackle Mekhi Wingo back into action.
It was mostly McLaughlin's show as the center for the Lions' offense on Monday. He handled the first team duties, while veteran Michael Niese was with the second team. McLaughlin reportedly handled the duties well, minimizing hiccups and going about his business at a high level.
Time will tell how long of an opportunity McLaughlin gets, as Scruggs is expected to compete for the job once he returns from injury. However, McLaughlin does come with some acclaim as the Rimington Award winner in 2024, and could prove himself worthy of a job with a strong showing in practices and preseason games.
With the second team offense, Niese had a mishap that led to a fumbled snap by Luke Altmyer. Niese has some experience on the Lions' active roster, and has the interior versatility that could make him an asset.
The Lions have to be pleasantly surprised with the emergence of Ahmed Hassanein. The Boise State product has produced day in and day out, seemingly making big plays every day. He's also ratcheted up the performance since padded practices began, which is exactly what the Lions have wanted to see.
On Monday, Hassanein had a sack and a tackle for loss during a team period. He also threw up in the end zone at the conclusion of another drill, according to reports, then let out what is becoming one of his trademark screams after fans reacted in support of him.
It was a sloppy effort at times for the Lions' offense, as they were turnover prone throughout.
Both Jared Goff and Luke Altmyer had bouts of turnovers. Goff tried to extend a play that likely would've been a sack, and paid for it as his pass was deflected and picked off by Chuck Clark. Meanwhile, another safety had a tone-setting play as Dan Jackson secured an interception off of Altmyer.
Christian Izien would add to his tally of takeaways later in practice with a pick off of Altmyer, while Nick Whiteside continues to pop on a daily basis. Whiteside got the best of Goff, hauling in an interception off a deflection.
The opportunities in Detroit's backfield are available for the taking , and Small and Saylors appear to be taking advantage. With Pacheco, Vaki and Jahmyr Gibbs all sidelined for portions of camp, practices have been a showcase of the team's depth at times.
Now that Gibbs is back after getting his contract signed, there are less first team opportunities but still plenty of action to go around for Detroit's running backs.
Campbell discussed both Small and Saylors' performance throughout camp during his media session Monday, and had positive reviews for both players. Both players have shown special teams value, which could be of huge value for their chances of making the roster.
Roger McCreary has had a tough time standing out in a positive way throughout camp, as the free agent has struggled. However, reports indicate that Monday was a better day for the veteran.
Among his highlight moments were a nice coverage rep against Amon-Ra St. Brown and forcing Gibbs to the sideline with a good pursuit angle on a run play.
The offense and defense traded blows during the red-zone period. There were some big plays on both sides, with linebacker Erick Hunter reportedly delivering one of the biggest hits of the day on tight end Jackson Meeks.
Hunter continues to make his case for a roster spot. Meanwhile, the Lions' offense had some strong moments as Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Brock Wright all had touchdown catches. Jacob Saylors had a rushing touchdown, while Altmyer also reached the end zone on a read-option.
To close out practice, the Lions put their offense in a situational drill designed to test their ability to kill the clock.
However, instead of simply running out the clock, the Lions ended up putting a bow on their day offensively with a big play. Goff went play-action, and hit Jameson Williams for a huge gain to end the day. Williams simply outran veteran Rock Ya-Sin, and went down at the 1-yard line to keep the clock moving.
This catch set up the offense taking a knee to finish the day.
1.) Newly signed quarterback Josh Dobbs was mostly limited in Monday's practice. He was observed throwing in early drills, but didn't take any team reps. It remains to be seen whether he'll have a role, and if so how significant, in their preseason opener on Thursday.
2.) Christian Mahogany continues to dominate the rep count at left guard with Scruggs out. Ben Bartch has also been limited throughout camp, and as a result Mahogany seems to be trending up early in camp.
3.) Former Michigan State linebacker Joe Bachie showed up with some productive plays. He had a deflection at the line of scrimmage on a blitz, and almost logged an interception on a swing pass.
4.) Jake Bates went 6-of-8 on field goal attempts. He had a long of 54 yards, but missed wide right from 51 and wide left from 47 yards out.
