title: Good and Not So Good From Day 10 of Jaguars Training Camp: Injuries Keep Stacking
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars held their last official practice before they hit the road to New Orleans on Tuesday, and it featured plenty of ups and downs.
Day 10 of Jaguars training camp saw one side of the ball particularly stand out, but what exactly was The Good and The Not So Good from Tuesday's practice at the Miller Electric Center? We break it all down below.
The Jaguars' front seven simply beat up on the Jaguars' offensive line on Tuesday. There is the required context of injuries on the offensive line impacting the first-, second-, and third-team units, but Tuesday was as dominant a day as Anthony Campanile's defensive front has had in training camp to date. Now, it will be up to them to keep it up from here.
"I thought the defense came out with more energy and better mindset and mentality. I thought the offensive skill players, obviously, and some of the pass game stuff was good. But they kind of took the fight to us, to the offense in the run game today," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said following practice.
It is hard to pinpoint any singular dominant performances, though Coen said he was impressed by Albert Regis and Arik Armstead. It instead seemed more like a completely team effort by the defensive line and linebackers to swarm to the ball and totally deny the Jaguars any momentum on the ground. That is the way Campanile had them playing against the run last season, and it has carried over into this year's training camp.
It has been awhile since we had a 53-man roster projection without Jabbar Muhammad on it. The second-year cornerback has been one of the most quickly-ascending players in the building ever since his stellar offseason program in the spring, and he has continued to carry it over into training camp. In fact, Muhammad has been the clear No. 5 cornerback for the Jaguars during camp, which would earn him an active game day jersey during the regular-season.
"I’d say Jabbar, you go back to the spring, he's probably one of the most improved players on the team. He's doing a heck of a job playing obviously corner and nickel. I’m excited," Coen said after practice.
Muhammad will have to prove himself on the practice field in New Orleans and on the game field this Saturday, but he has all of the traits and confidence to do so. He once again made some big plays in coverage on Tuesday, including a near-interception of Nick Mullens. He is carrying a considerable amount of momentum with him into the rest of the week against the Saints, and he has a chance to really solidify a role and roster spot in the weeks ahead as a result of that momentum and what he has put on the practice field.
When it comes to the Jaguars' pass-catchers, it seems like the always-reliable Jakobi Meyers is sometimes forgotten about. Parker Washington is a breakout star who has arguably been the MVP of training camp to this point; Brian Thomas Jr. is a first-round pick who has been a star in his own right; and Travis Hunter is a former No. 2 pick who is one of the most recognizable athletes in sports. That sometimes leads to Meyers not getting as much talk as the rest of the room, but it has no impact on the clear value he brings the Jaguars.
Meyers had a slow-ish start to camp but turned it on around the time the Jaguars got the pads on, and he hasn't turned it off since. He has been the most sure-handed receiver in the room, including a diving third-down catch from Trevor Lawrence on Tuesday that was one of the best plays the Jaguars made on offense all day. We already know just how important Meyers is to the Jaguars after the way he changed their passing game a year ago, but days like Tuesday are a good reminder that even with the noise of the receiver room's talent, his consistency will still show up.
The Jaguars have slowly seen injuries stack up over the last week. After entering camp with minimal injuries, the Jaguars had a number of players either sit out of practice completely (Cole Van Lanen, Walker Little, Zach Durfee) or be limited to only reps in individual drills (Emmanuel Pregnon, Ezra Cleveland). Other players like Jourdan Lewis were undressed and to the side. There is a long way to go before a real game kicks off, but the injury list is getting a bit long.
"I think that you’ve got a couple of guys, I mean, we’ve got an ankle. We’ve got a couple—not a ton of injuries that would maybe pop up from hitting," Coen said. "More so the general soft tissue hammy stuff, right, and groins and things like that that you guys see popping up all over the NFL right now. Thankfully we haven't had a ton of big, big ones, right? Knock on wood. It's just these are the times of the year it happens, it occurs."
We talked about the defense dominating the Jaguars' running game, and it would be hard to not draw the conclusion that injuries were a significant reason. The Jaguars had multiple projected Week 1 starters (Patrick Mekari, Walker Little, Ezra Cleveland) miss practice, which led to the Jaguars having a first-team offensive line of Anton Harrison-Jonah Monheim-Robert Hainsey-Wyatt Milum-Chuma Edoga.
As a result, the Jaguars' first-team offensive line looked a good bit like their second-team line. Then the second-team looked like the third-team, and so on and so forth until the Jaguars simply could not get any positive yardage in team drills. The unit was clearly overpowered on Tuesday, and it is easy to say injuries were the biggest reason why this was the case.
From a dropped snap from Trevor Lawrence in team drills to multiple defensive pass interference calls on the secondary, the Jaguars have had sharper days. Outside of injuries and these self-inflicted mistakes, there weren't many things to truly nitpick, but the Jaguars have to once again prove that they can stay out of their own way when the real games start a month from now.

title: Everything I Saw at Day 10 of Jaguars Training Camp: Defense Gives Liam Coen a Hurdle
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Well, that was certainly a practice.
The Jacksonville Jaguars held Day 10 of training camp at the Miller Electric Center on Tuesday, and the suddenly banged-up Jaguars did not have the most productive day on offense. In fact, head coach Liam Coen was clearly upset with the unit's performance post-practice, and it is easy to see why.
So, what did we see on Day 10? We break it all down below.
It started in the first team period of the day, and it continued for the rest of the practice. The Jaguars' defense simpy bonked the Jaguars' offense over the head with a club repeatedly on Tuesday, and it got to the point that Coen said after practice that he actually cut the day short as a result. Things were not going to change with another period of work, and he opted to let the defense have the day that they definitively won.
A big part of it had to do with the Jaguars' injuries up front, which have been a problem for a few days now. The Jaguars' front seven took the Jaguars' running game down with mostly ease though, with it being the first day in pads that the Jaguars did not seem to get much traction on the ground. The pass-rush was also relentless, with Travon Walker, B.J. Green, and Dennis Gardeck all record would-be sacks during team drills.
There are going to be days in training camp where one side has the edge, but this day will go down as one of the most lopsided practices of camp thus far. Coen told us exactly that with the way he concluded practice and then evaluated it afterward.
The Jaguars still have 30+ days before they kickoff against the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, but the offensive line is at a concerning point right now. Injuries have taken a toll on the line, with Patrick Mekari and Cole Van Lanen still not getting team reps, and with Walker Little missing another practice after his injury in last week's scrimmage. Add in some limited work from Ezra Cleveland and Emmanuel Pregnon and it was ... well, Liam Coen used the word "thin" several times. That sums it up.
The Jaguars' starting line for most of the day was (left from right) Anton Harrison-Jonah Monheim-Robert Hainsey-Wyatt Milum-Chuma Edoga. There is no reason to think this is going to be the Week 1 offensive line at this point, but it could create some significant challenges for the Jaguars when they share the practice field with the Saints later this week.
As things stand today, though, the Jaguars need to get healthy quickly. Anton Harrison seems secured at left tackle and we know Robert Hainsey is at center. What will the other three spots look like throughout the rest of training camp?
Even on days where the defense easily has the edge, Parker Washington is still impressing. It has become a daily occurrence during training camp this season as Washington has separated himself as Trevor Lawrence's favorite target in one of the NFL's best wide receiver rooms, and this was again the case during an otherwise lackluster offensive day on Tuesday.
Washington had the play of the day (more on that later) in team drills, but once again ultimately showed that he is a true seperator at each level of the field. It feels like the Jaguars know they can break the glass in case of emergecy and dial up a conpletion to Washington whenever they really feel like they need to. The fact it has become so easy for him even against a much-improved secondary speaks volumes about where he is at.
With the offensive line and defensive line tucked on the end of the practice field and with the receivers and defensive backs working on 3-on-3 concepts, we went to take a look at the 1-on-1s between the running backs/tight ends and linebackers/safeties, with the focus being on pass-protection and blitzing. Here are a few of the stand out reps that we saw during that period.
The best play of the day once again came from Parker Washington. Washington does not get many reps against Travis Hunter in coverage, but he was able to be one of the few receivers to beat Hunter on a downfield rep on Tuesday when he hauled in the longest completion of the day down the left sideline. It was as impressive of a win as Washington has had against any cornerback so far in camp, and it another sign of his stellar chemistry with Trevor Lawrence.

title: 3 Jaguars Trending Toward the Roster Bubble Through 2 Weeks of Training Camp
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are set to enter the third week of Jacksonville Jaguars training camp with Tuesday's practice at the Miller Electric Center, and we are starting to get into the thick of things.
This week, the Jaguars will travel to New Orleans for joint practices with the Saints before kicking off their first preseason game on Saturday, setting up one of the most important weeks of training camp.
With that importance comes a few Jaguars who will need to make up some ground as camp sees them drift closer to the roster bubble. Here are three such players, broken down below.
I came out of the Jaguars' scrimmage last week thinking Jalen McLeod did a good job of setting himself apart in the backup strong side linebacker battle between him to Yasir Abdullah, though Abdullah himself has also flashed at times. But this is a niche role on the defense and there are only so many spots on the Jaguars' 53-man roster for strong side linebackers, which means it feels more likely the Jaguars only keep one of these two behind Dennis Gardeck on the depth chart.
Abdullah has been a core special teamer for the Jaguars, but the Jaguars are looking for as much pass-rush upside as they can find. McLeod offers that for the Jaguars and Anthony Campanile has already thrown his support behind the second-year defender. Abdullah has done nothing to lose a spot, but this is more so due to numbers.
The Jaguars have been slowly easing in cornerback Christian Braswell over the course of the first half of camp, with Braswell's snaps in practice mostly coming during individual drills to this point. The Jaguars know what he can do on both special teams and defense, so there is not a lot of mystery in terms of what he offers or has to prove.
But Braswell has been out, the Jaguars have seen some backup cornerbacks impress with Jabbar Muhammad and Devon Marshall, who are both players who can line up inside and outside like Braswell can. If he can't get to 100% soon, he may be a stash candidate as the Jaguars promote the young guys.
I came into the spring and summer believing the Jaguars' newfound interest in multiple tight end sets would lead to them carrying four tight ends on the roster, with Quintin Morris as the favorite to be the fourth tight end behind Brenton Strange and rookie tight ends Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol. Now that we are a few weeks into camp, though, I may lean toward the Jaguars carrying just three tight ends.
The Jaguars have simply not featured the position enough beyond the first three tight ends to warrant carrying a fourth unless that player has shown enough to mark himself safe on the roster independent from the Jaguars' plans. Morris has not been that type of performer in camp thus far, and he also sustained an injury in last Friday's scrimmage. It remains to be seen how long that injury could impact Morris, but it feels like any missed time could hurt his chances.

title: No Member of Jaguars Has More to Gain vs. Saints than Grant Udinski
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There are not many things at stake when it comes to the preseason.
Some players are fighting for jobs and roster spots of course, but the games do not count, starters play sparingly , and nothing is really taken too seriously until Week 1 rolls around a month from now.
So when the Jaguars enter the first week of the preseason this weekend against the New Orleans Saints, there will not exactly be many high stakes attached for much of the Jaguars' organization. That is unless you count offensive coordinator Grant Udinski, of course.
With Udinski already getting several head coach interviews during the 2026 coaching cycle, it seems like a foregone conclusion that he will once again be at the top of some wish lists entering next year's cycle. The Jaguars have to do their part and win enough games for Udinski and the offense to get that kind of attention, but that feels like it is due.
For Udinski, it feels like there is little else he can do to raise his stock between Week 1 and the offseason beside help guide the Jaguars and their offense to another year of success. That is why the preseason in general is a massive oppurtunity for him.
Just like he did in the preseason finale a year ago, Udinski is set to call plays for the offense against the Saints on Saturday and then throughout the rest of the preseason after that. It will be one of the few chances he has to call plays for a team that is led by one of the NFL's top offensive minds in Liam Coen, which is why it is such an important stage.
"Looking forward to it and part of it is because I have that group of guys to call plays for that are guys that are, so focused on their craft and have been so diligent with the way they study, which makes it nice for me because a lot of times in preseason you're going out there and just trying to get kind of the basic plays snapped and executed and see if guys can go out there and communicate," Udinski said after Sunday's training camp practice.
"Now there will still absolutely be an element of that where we want to be able to find out what we have with those guys. So, I understand going into it that we always go out and compete every single time we're going out there to play, whether it's a seven-on-seven or a preseason game. But we know that there are other things we want to accomplish to set ourselves up and set each player up for success going into the season, so we'll put together a call sheet and a game plan accordingly so that way we can see what these guys can do and let them go out there and hopefully compete and have some fun.”
Is it calling plays in the regular season? Of course not. But it is a chance for Udinski to show other NFL franchises what kind of instincts he has as a play-caller, a chance that he otherwise would not get before the next hiring cycle.
No team is going to make Udinski their next head coach because of how the Jaguars' offense performs in the preseason against the Saints. But with a strong outing this weekend and in the two games to follow, it could be another feather in the cap of one of the NFL's fastest-rising assistants.

title: Why One Jaguars Position Battle Isn't Nearly as Close as Fans Think
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There is one under-the-radar position battle that might surprise some Jacksonville Jaguars fans.
Everyone knows about the battle between Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs, the battle between Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr., and the eventual battle at right guard between Patrick Mekari and Wyatt Milum.
But outside of the starting units, there are a number of other interesting position battles that have brought on quite the change thus far -- with one involving a rookie draft pick.
When the Jaguars had linebacker Jack Kiser go down with an injury on the first day of training camp, the immediate expectation was that it would mean more reps to go around for seventh-round linebacker Parker Hughes. Hughes entered the summer on the bubble as far as the 53-man roster goes due to the other pieces the Jaguars have at linebacker, but Kiser's injury could have presented Hughes a chance to make his mark and earn a spot somewhere on the depth chart and on special teams.
But fast forward a week, and it looks like Hughes is still on the bubble following the addition of veteran linebacker Jahlani Tavai. That is not to say it is overly unusual for a seventh-round pick to not make the roster, but it would be for this Jaguars' regime.
The Jaguars did not cut a single one of their nine draft picks a year ago, and all nine members of the 2025 class are still on the roster in camp this year. As for the first nine picks of the Jaguars' 2026 class, they look fairly safe as well. That is simply how the Jaguars' new regime aims to operate. But Hughes could be the lone exception.
Last week, the Jaguars added a veteran lineback in Tavai who could push Hughes for the potential final linebacker spot on the depth chart. Even though Tavai's first day on the roster was a few days ago, he was already getting more prominent reps with the No. 2 defense on Sunday than Hughes was despite Hughes being in the defense since April.
Tavai seemingly already getting promoted over Hughes on the depth chart could be due solely to the fact that he has years of experience and is not a late Day 3 pick with under 10 training camp practices under his belt. Or it could be a sign that the Jaguars believe they can't simply rely on Hughes to be ready in a linebacker room that has taken some hits over the last few weeks.
“Obviously, we've had some injuries in camp, but I've seen Jahlani play over the years and some guys who I know really well have coached him, been around him, so there's definitely a familiarity with him and the way he plays," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said over the weekend. "He's been in a system that has a lot of the same tenets as ours. When he was in Detroit and in New England, we played very similarly in Miami when I was there. So, there's a lot of carryover, even just the verbiage to everything. It's an easier transition for him."
If Hughes becomes the first draft pick this new regime cuts, then this recently-ignited position battle will seemingly be the reason why.

title: 5 Things We Have Learned About the Jaguars at Training Camp So Far
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have wrapped up two weeks and nine practices of training camp, and there have been plenty of lessons learned.
So, what have we really learned about the 2026 Jaguars over the course of training camp so far? From the offense to the defense, we break it all down below.
The Jaguars entered training camp with one of the best pass-catching rooms in the entire NFL between wide receivers Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, and Travis Hunter and tight end Brenton Strange. So far, that group has been just as good as the Jaguars hoped they would be, with each player having different standout days and moments through the first nine practices thus far. But one player still has to emerge on top as the potential alpha male of the passing game, and that player has been Washington.
Washington has consistently diced up the Jaguars' cornerbacks in coverage, getting open on all three levels of the field and making some of the biggest plays of camp. I have come away from the first two weeks of camp believing Washington will lead the Jaguars' wideouts in routes and snaps this year, and I think he is the target who will often stay on the field when the Jaguars go to two- and one-wide receiver sets in 12 and 13 formations.
Washington doesn't have a deal done yet, but he simply looks too important to the Jaguars for them to not keep around for the long-term. This was already the case before training camp started, but his performance so far has only reinforced it.
All offseason, the debate about the Jaguars' running back room centered on whether it would be led by Bhayshul Tuten or Chris Rodriguez Jr. Through two weeks, though, the only real answer we have gotten from the Jaguars' running back room is that both Tuten and Rodriguez will play quite a bit. So too will second-year running back LeQuint Allen, who is the runaway favorite to be the Jaguars' third-down back this season.
“Yeah, just great hands, good route runner. He's going to be in there because he's such a good protector, so I think the more we can do with him and getting him out on routes and concepts, the better for our offense. I know that he's capable," Trevor Lawrence said on Sunday about Allen.
"I remember watching his highlights and when we drafted him out of college and some of the crazy catches he had in college. So, we've seen him out here. He's making plays. He had a good catch down in the red zone today. If he can be a threat for us, it's real because he's going to be in on a lot of passing situations.”
Tuten and Rodriguez are getting near-equal reps, while Allen has been the Jaguars' top option on all passing downs in camp. That sounds more like a room that is about to spread the wealth than a room that is set to lean on just one face.
Travis Hunter's exact snap split between cornerback and wide receiver will not be known until the Jaguars actually kick off the season in Week 1 against the Cleveland Browns. What has been clear through the first two weeks of camp, however, is that the Jaguars are prepared for Hunter to play a significant role on both sides of the ball. This has always been their messaging, but they have put their money where their mouth is.
Hunter has played both wide receiver and cornerback with the starting offense and starting defense in every single training camp practice to date. Last year, he would focus on one spot for the majority of a practice before switching positions at a later practice. Now, the Jaguars are making it clear where they see Hunter fitting in.
The Jaguars' pass-rush depth was, well, questionable entering training camp. It still is a bit questionable until the Jaguars' defensive depth chart proves it on the field in Week 1 and beyond of course, but the early returns suggest the Jaguars might be better off up front than they were largely being given credit for ahead of camp, especially on the edge.
B.J. Green has been the breakout star of camp thus far, rookie Zach Durfee has provided consistent pressure, Danny Striggow has been as reliable as ever, and new defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro brings some serious juice as an interior pass-rusher. For a unit facing plenty of questions, this group has aced each test thus far.
Everything we have seen from the Jaguars' offensive line in recent weeks suggests to me that we are going to see Anton Harrison start the first game of his career at left tackle in Week 1. Harrison has been a right tackle-only for the Jaguars since he was drafted in 2023, but he has now spent the majority of time this training camp at left tackle. Walker Little spent the first few days at left tackle, but Harrison has been there since before the Jaguars even put on pads a week ago.
So, why do I think that means Harrison will play left tackle? Simply put, I do not think the Jaguars would spend the time and resources to have Harrison take reps at left tackle this consistently if they expected Cole Van Lanen to be available in Week 1. If the Jaguars thought Van Lanen was a sure thing for Week 1, they could have kept Harrison on the right side and had Little and Chuma Edoga take snaps at left tackle. Instead, they moved their best offensive lineman to right tackle.
Add in Little's recent injury and the Jaguars' hand might be forced when it comes to Harrison. One way or another, he seems due for a start at left tackle once the regular season rolls around.

title: Where Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence's Focus Is Ahead of Saints Week
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The preseason is going to look a bit different for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars this week.
Last year, Lawrence and the starting offense got playing time in the first two preseason games before sitting out the finale after one joint practice with the Miami Dolphins. Now, there is a real chance Lawrence doesn't play in the preseason at all as the Jaguars prepare for their first week of joint practices with the New Orleans Saints this week.
So, where is Lawrence's focus ahead of Saints week, and why are the Jaguars making the shift?
Entering a week where the bulk of Lawrence's reps will come on the practice field instead of on Saturday against the Saints, Lawrence is not considering the change in his preseason routine. Instead, he is placing his focus on being where his feet are, and ensuring the Jaguars have a smooth day of practice against the Saints before the two teams kick off the preseason over the weekend.
“Not really. It's never something I focus on too much. Obviously, if you do play, you want to play well, so you put everything into it so you can go out there and play good, clean football," Lawrence said after Sunday's practice.
"And it's good practice for us, but to me, it's just taking it one day at a time. Like we got practice still on Tuesday here, and then we're going to go do joint practice and just trying to treat all those like game reps and get all these valuable reps that are good opportunities for us to learn and grow. And then when the game comes, if I play, then I'll go and do my best there too. But I try not to focus on it too much. It's not something that takes up too much space in my brain.”
In short, Lawrence is not making too big of a deal out of what a new preseason will look like. Lawerence has gotten preseason reps in every other season of his career, but the Jaguars are switching things up this year in hopes of avoiding any serious preseason injuries. That might mean less true live reps for Lawrence, but it does not mean the Jaguars' offense can't grow this week against the Saints.
Lawrence will still get the lion's share of reps when the Jaguars and Saints hold their joint practice later this week, giving the Jaguars a chance to see how their offense and passing game stack up against an opposing defense that their offense does not practice against every single day of camp. It will be a different atmosphere than the preseason, but it will be a valuable perspective after the way the Jaguars' own defense has attacked the Jaguars' offense.
"Our defense honestly has given us some really good looks. They've added some stuff since last year that they're playing coverage a little bit differently, and then they're showing some things and then they're bluffing out. And so, they're challenging us, which is really good for us," Lawrence said.

title: Good and Not So Good From Day 9 of Jaguars Training Camp: Travis Hunter Shows Off
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Another day of training camp down, another day where several players flashed the kind of talent that could take the Jacksonville Jaguars a long way.
A host of players had productive days on Day 9 of Jaguars training camp on Sunday, but what were the ups and the downs from the latest day of work at the Miller Electric Center? We break it down below.
Hunter's ball skills at wide receiver have been shown off time and time again in training camp, and Sunday was no exception. The best example of Hunter being a quarterback-friendly target who can go up and get any pass in his zip code came during a 1-on-one period where he lined up against Jabbar Muhammad, who has otherwise been a tough matchup for the Jaguars' wide receiver group.
Another one @TravisHunterJr | @Dream_Finders pic.twitter.com/ZQr9xBxd5M
Hunter's ability to go up and win the ball in the air makes him a natural candidate to play more of an outside role for the Jaguars moving forward. He spent more snaps in the slot and making plays closer to the line of scrimmage a year ago, and that is one area the Jaguars should look to expand his game moving forward.
Hunter continued to play on both sides of the ball for the Jaguars in practice, and once again it was a day where he was able to make plays on both sides of the ball. One such play was his second interception in camp, with the natural ball skills and ability to make a defensive impact as clear as ever. Hunter has looked the part and then some at cornerback, and his ability to take the ball away could take the Jaguars' secondary to another level.
YOINK ‼️ @TravisHunterJr | @Dream_Finders pic.twitter.com/Bg5NkCzIGe
How much time Hunter actually spends at cornerback (and receiver) remains to be seen. The early trend in training camp suggests that he will at least have a much larger role on defense compared to a year ago, however, and adding him more to the mix with Montaric Brown, Jarrian Jones, and Jourdan Lewis should only make the Jaguars more formidable moving forward.
If it feels like we are saying the Jaguars' running backs are standing out quite a bit lately, it is because the position group simply keeps making plays. Sunday was no different, with multiple players in the room standing out over the course of practice. This was a room we were bullish on this offseason in terms of overall improvement and effectiveness, and they have yet to disappoint since the pads have come on.
Bhayshul Tuten had several impressive runs in team drills, LeQuint Allen had a long catch-and-run, Ameer Abdullah made one of the days biggest plays with a carry that saw him cut across the field for a massive chunk gain, and then there was Chris Rodriguez Jr. Even withoutfull pads on, Rodriguez is consistently getting yards after contact in camp on seemingly each carry.
"You saw it here in the mock game and ever since we put the pads on, some of these runs that don't look as great when we're tagging off, you see it when we're thudding and you're like, there's no way that guy's going to tackle him before five yards," Trevor Lawrence said after Sunday's practice.
"He's running over people. He runs downhill, he's a big guy. He's hard to get your arms around. His legs are moving. So, I think he's going to be great for us because he can get those and find those dirty yards and he also has the capability to make people miss. So, I think he's really well-rounded and he has been doing a good job for us.”
Jabbar Muhammad continues to standout in the Jaguars' secondary, and it is becoming tougher and tougher to picture this secondary without him. He made several plays for the Jaguars on Sunday, but his best came in the red-zone against Tanner Koziol. Despite Koziol having the size advantage, Muhammad made a play on the ball and knocked it away for an impressive pass break-up.
Muhammad's ball-skills have been on display ever since his breakout performance in the spring's offseason program, and they have continued to pop up throughout Jaguars' camp. Making plays with the football in the air is how corners are able to carve out a role and stick around, and Muhammad has done exactly that.
The Jaguars' offensive line is a bit on the mend right now, and Sunday's practice was yet another example. The Jaguars have been without Cole Van Lanen all training camp, while Patrick Mekari has not taken a rep in team drills since training camp began. Then on Sunday, they were joined as sidelined players by Walker Little and rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon.
Jacksonville had to make a roster move on Saturday as a result of the offensive line injuries, and this is a unit that could be entering next week in New Orleans with a fair amount of questions, at least in the short-term.
The Jaguars' starting secondary continues to have a strong camp, and there are some backups in the secondary like Jalen Huskey, Caleb Ransaw, Jabbar Muhammad, and Devon Marshall who have made some plays in camp as well. But with that in mind, the Jaguars' backup defense had several deep passes go over their heads on Sunday, a day that felt like the best day of camp for the Jaguars' deep passing game on offense.
Between two deep Austin Trammell touchdowns and deep passes to Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr., there were a few too many deep shots allowed by the Jaguars' depth in the secondary on Sunday. There is always the chance they will need some of those players to step up, so some consistency will be a goal moving forward.
The Jaguars had a few different turnovers on Sunday, which came after the Jaguars had two such turnovers in Friday's scrimmage. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception to Eric Murray in the red-zone, with Murray having a particularly interception-heavy training camp. The second turnover came when Rayuan Lane forced a fumble on J'Mari Taylor that he then recovered.
DISRUPTOR 😤 @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/xik7WNfHA9
Turnovers in training camp are always two-fold. On one hand, the last thing any offense wants to happen is for a drive to end with a turnover. On the other hand, the Jaguars' defense forcing turnovers is, actually, good for Jacksonville. Tough line to balance, I know, but the Jaguars have still been a bit sloppier with the ball in recent days.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: What Are Fair Expectations for Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Cyrus Allen in 2026?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' first preseason game is just around the corner, and there are only six training camp practices remaining in St. Joseph, Missouri . Before the team gets more information from Saturday's preseason kickoff against the Los Angeles Rams , what do you want to know about where the team stands now?
Jordan Foote and I ( Joshua Brisco ) are here for this week's edition of the Chiefs On SI mailbag, fielding your questions from the KC Sports Network Twitter/X accounts or @jbbrisco.com on BlueSky . Let's get into it.
"Does FAU become a useful rotational player? Is the contract year still undefeated?" -@jettyrat_RB
Former first-round defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah is one of the more interesting stories of the Chiefs' offseason. His first two seasons had a couple of highlights here and there, but he never approached the production you'd want from a first-round selection. Then, he missed all of 2025 due to a preseason hamstring injury. However, even after declining his fifth-year option , the Chiefs appear to expect some legitimate production out of Anudike-Uzomah in his fourth season.
Even after the Chiefs reportedly signed veteran EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah , Anudike-Uzomah still has plenty of opportunity ahead of him. I see Ogbah's signing as a larger indictment on KC's questions about their internal candidates for the No. 5 or 6 defensive end positions.
As things stand now, Anudike-Uzomah (and Chiefs fans) should forget his original draft slot and focus on what he could be as a role player in 2026. He's clearly behind George Karlaftis, Ashton Gillotte and R Mason Thomas, but if he can be an NFL-caliber rotational piece, he can certainly extend his NFL career, perhaps even by remaining in Kansas City. — Brisco
"In order, who do you currently have as players 49-58?" -@krichardson.bsky.social
Ranking end-of-roster players in order before preseason game No. 1 would keep us here for quite a while, but I do have some top bubble candidates to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks.
On the offensive side of the ball, the perceived battle between Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun immediately jumps out. There's ample incentive for KC to keep a third quarterback this year, and why not roll with the one the club used 2026 NFL Draft capital to acquire ? At wide receiver, I'm not quite there with Jalen Royals being a cut candidate, but Andrew Armstrong delivering a quality camp thus far does have me thinking.
In the trenches, both the offense and defense are worth keeping an eye on. The Kahlil Benson hype train isn't slowing down even a bit, which might just push someone like Ethan Driskell to the practice squad. At defensive end, the Chiefs' reported pickup of Ogbah doesn't bode well for the likes of Vincent Anthony, Tyreke Smith or Anthony Dunn.
Finally, the secondary picture is quietly intriguing. Assuming health for everyone else, former first-round pick Kaiir Elam seems to be squarely on the outside looking in at cornerback. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa was one of the first men out in our first roster projection but continues to make a case to be included in edition 2.0.
The Chiefs have some calculus to do, but their three preseason games should provide clarity. — Foote
"Obviously Cyrus Allen is coming off an injury, but should we read anything into his days in pads having a lot less highlights?" -@EthanCo67716681 "According to Matt Verderame, Chiefs staff is high on Cyrus the Virus. Will we see more or less of him in preseason because of that?" -@Dusty_Roads_BBQ
Two questions for the price (free) of one! These are getting at different elements of the Cyrus Allen excitement, but they both help us look ahead to the preseason.
This often makes me feel like a party pooper during this time of year, but I generally try to read very little into training camp highlights in general. For what it's worth, Allen's pre-pads highlights also didn't particularly move me. However, I do take note from tweets like this one from Pete Sweeney out at camp :
"Patrick Mahomes' first two completions during the early team blitz period? Cyrus Allen."
Anything that indicates the building of trust and chemistry between Mahomes and one of his receivers matters to me, at least when it happens consistently. Either by choice or by injury-impacted necessity, it does still seem like Mahomes has given Allen lots of training camp attention; I don't really care if the highlights are spectacular until they come in an NFL stadium.
So, on that note, I do wonder how Allen will be used in the preseason. With Mahomes not expected to play in at least the first preseason game , I'd be a bit surprised to see Rashee Rice (knee) or Xavier Worthy (shoulder) take the field on Saturday while they continue their respective recoveries. I'm not sure that Tyquan Thornton needs many reps with Justin Fields, but you also probably don't want to start Fields with Royals, Armstrong, and Nikko Remigio as his starting receivers. That leads us back to Allen.
If the Chiefs are completely in love with Allen, they could sneak him through the preseason without showing the NFL what they have in mind for him when the season arrives. Still, I think Allen starts as the Chiefs' No. 4 receiver (already an accomplishment for a fifth-round rookie) and that it would be reasonable to give him a decent workload in the preseason so he can run his first NFL routes before the lights get brighter.
The last wrinkle worth noting is that Allen briefly exited practice on Tuesday and hasn't been back on the practice field for very long; perhaps he's entirely held out on Saturday, delaying this conversation by another week. — Brisco
"Which 1-on-1 would you dominate Jordan at, and vice versa?" - @bradbatchelder
This is the question we needed. After giving it some thought, I think I'm winning on both sides of the trenches. I'm betting on myself having a power advantage if I can show off some vaguely passable footwork. I'm definitely disrupting the pocket and probably dying a slow-enough death in pass protection. Heck, I think I could win my fair share of reps as a pass-catcher too. ...But I'm not covering Jordan unless the quarterback is having a terrible, terrible day. — Brisco
Even as someone who has a size advantage, I'd be a tad worried about the trenches. The individual drills up front tend to be defense-slanted, so I'm in agreement and think life as a pass rusher would be easier than as a pass protector. The bad news is I play with too high of a pad level to be consistent snap-to-snap.
I'm all over anything that puts me in coverage, whether I'm running a route to beat it or putting on a prime Darrelle Revis (Chiefs legend) performance in the defensive backfield. I'm getting physical at the line of scrimmage and setting the tone for the rep. Josh knows that, as there's video proof to back up my claim. — Foote

title: Chiefs OT Jaylon Moore Is Welcoming the Challenge From Rising Rookie Kahlil Benson
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' offensive line is almost completely set, but there is still a lingering battle between Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore for the starting right tackle job. The undrafted rookie out of Indiana has emerged as a starting candidate , taking first-team reps on the right side for over a week ahead of the veteran.
Moore, who is in the final season of a two-year, $30 million deal he signed last offseason, spent four years with the San Francisco 49ers as a swing tackle before signing with K.C.
He was expected to be the blindside protector of Patrick Mahomes until Josh Simmons fell to the Chiefs in the first round of last year's draft. As a result, he only started six games after beginning the year as a backup and eventually dealing with a knee injury of his own. Now that Simmons is healthy and in the best shape of his life , the only starting spot available to Moore is on the right side. Although he's predominantly played left tackle throughout his NFL career — including over 90% of his combined snaps in San Francisco — Moore is more than willing to adjust to a new spot on the offensive line.
"Honestly for me, throughout my career, I've been back and forth," Moore said. "It's good to get the reps on either side because at any point, anything can happen. And it's good to make sure that every one of our guys are able to play multiple different positions and be able to play wherever your number is called."
The last handful of days at training camp have featured Moore and Benson starting alongside each other with the first team, as projected right guard Trey Smith continues to deal with a hip injury . Moore says that working next to Benson rather than competing against him for a spot has gone a long way in building their relationship. "It's been really good for both of us," Moore continued. "Obviously, him transitioning to [guard] during this camp, he's been working in and out of both spots. So, it's been good for me as well, just being able to get camaraderie and being able to play with whoever."
Naturally, one would think there's some animosity between a six-year veteran and a bright-eyed rookie who's never even taken an NFL snap competing for a starting spot. However, Moore is a true professional who doesn't let competition get in the way of the team's goals.
Even in a contract year, Moore made it clear that while there certainly is a position battle, the two players are working in harmony and pushing each other to become the best they can be. "Honestly, we're all pushing each other to get better every single day, regardless of what the depth chart looks like," Moore promised. "It's good for him, it's good for me as well. We're all pushing each other in that room."

title: Rashee Rice Reflects on Jail Time, Goals for Contract Year With Chiefs
full_text:
For the first time since the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice spoke to the media and provided updates on a multitude of fronts.
The fourth-year man had one of the NFL's more unorthodox offseasons, undergoing knee surgery but spending part of that recovery time in jail after violating his probation order from a prior incident. Rice got released in time to make it to the start of Chiefs training camp , where he's been monitored closely and had his workload managed over the past few weeks.
Rice, who described his jail stint as a "learning experience" and a "reality check" on Tuesday, said he wants the world to know he's focused on being the best player and teammate possible this season.
"I'm 100% locked in on what's going on now with the team," Rice said. "I'm ready to go out there and dominate, and I've got a good group of brotherhood behind me."
The former second-round pick believes his positivity will shine through after the first half of his year was overshadowed by a dark cloud.
"I would say I'm a positive guy," Rice said. "I'm a great person to feed off as far as energy [is concerned]. A smiling guy mostly, at all times — unless it's time for work, then I'm serious. And then I'm a father, so I take the most responsibility in being a good father to my boys."
As far as the knee is concerned, Rice took a significant step last week when he participated in 11-on-11 work for the first time at camp. He's since been heavily involved in the team's practice plans, which could be a good sign for his Week 1 availability. All eyes are on him getting the green light to make impactful plays right out of the gate in the regular season.
He said he thought he merely had some nagging knee swelling earlier in the process, but the stars aligned for a clean-up procedure to occur during the offseason. Now working his way back to 100%, Rice wants to improve on plays where the ball isn't going to him in the final year of his rookie contract.
Speaking of which, a complete season may go a long way for Rice in the financial department. Being able to produce at volume for the entirety of a campaign while also staying out of trouble might just allow him to recoup some of the value he's presumably lost in the last two years.
He'd be lying if he said the opportunity to deliver in a pressure-packed environment didn't add to his drive.
"I mean, it's motivating," Rice said. "Honestly, just being able to be back on the field with my brothers is motivating. That's in the future [but] right now, I'm just focused on what's going on right now, and that's getting better for the team."
After recording career highs in targets (102), receptions (79), receiving yards (938) and touchdowns (seven) as a rookie, Rice has appeared in just 12 games across 2024 and 2025. In eight contests a year ago, his numbers would've extrapolated to roughly 113 catches, 1,213 yards and just under 11 scores over the course of 17 outings. Now, the onus is on him to string everything together and realize that potential.
Set to become a free agent next March, Rice has maintained "the right group of guys" in his circle and seeks a constant "positive attitude" moving forward. Only time will tell if he's able to put a checkered past behind him in the biggest season of his football life.

title: Report: Chiefs Reuniting With Former Super Bowl Champion DE Emmanuel Ogbah
full_text:
Dating back to early in the offseason, the Kansas City Chiefs have had a questionable collection of talent in the defensive end room. Just days before the club opens its preseason slate against the Los Angeles Rams, general manager Brett Veach is making a move to help add some depth.
Per a Tuesday morning report from Adam Schefter of ESPN , the Chiefs are reuniting with old friend Emmanuel Ogbah. It's a one-year deal for the veteran, who spent the 2019-20 campaign in Kansas City and was a member of the Super Bowl LIV-winning team.
Free-agent defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah is signing a one-year deal with the Chiefs; per source.  It’s a reunion. Ogbah won a Super Bowl with them in 2020. pic.twitter.com/hZp0zQePeh
Ogbah sat out the team's last six regular-season games and the entirety of the ensuing postseason run during the aforementioned year due to injury, then moved on to the Miami Dolphins. He spent five seasons in Miami, racking up 29.5 sacks and 28 tackles for loss in 73 outings.
The former second-round pick played 13 regular-season games with the Jacksonville Jaguars a year ago, although he mustered just half a sack on 323 defensive snaps. His 45.9 Pro Football Focus overall grade ranked 111th out of 115 qualified edge rushers, accompanied by 16 total pressures and 12 hurries in 181 pass-rushing opportunities.
Standing 6-foot-4 with 35-inch arms and a sturdy frame, Ogbah fits the more traditional mold of a Steve Spagnuolo defensive end. His background in the system is a plus, but he does turn 33 in November, so it's worth monitoring exactly how much he has left in the tank.
In the aftermath of the Ogbah signing, Joshua Brisco of Chiefs On SI outlined what this pickup could mean for the rest of the defensive end rotation in KC.
"After months of questioning the Chiefs' defensive end depth, a move like this always made sense for Kansas City," Brisco said. "Even with optimism for second-year third-round pick Ashton Gillotte or fourth-year first-rounder Felix Anudike-Uzomah, the room has been shallow all offseason (after being a weakness throughout 2025).
"Ogbah, in his age-33 season, shouldn't be expected to take on a tremendous workload, but he has a clear path to playing time. George Karlaftis is still the room's lone surefire starter, while rookie R Mason Thomas will be the most important unknown for '26 and beyond, but Ogbah should be able to play passable snaps while helping set the floor of KC's rotation of edge defenders.
"The timing is interesting for a few reasons. The Chiefs could've connected with Ogbah before training camp to get him into Spagnuolo's defense weeks earlier, but it's reasonable to assume that the Chiefs wanted to give their in-house options the first crack at a potential No. 5 defensive end position.
"Instead, after Gillotte's hamstring injury held him out of practice for more than a week, KC made the move to bring in Ogbah. Between Gillotte's injury scare and a quiet week for the team's developmental EDGE hopefuls, Ogbah's return makes for a logical bolstering of KC's pass rush with a steady veteran."

title: Brett Veach Shares Reassuring Injury Assessment About Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane
full_text:
As the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, expectations are sky-high for Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane . He is expected to immediately become the leader of a young Kansas City secondary.
While Delane has been present during the Chiefs' training camp, he has donned a yellow non-contact jersey throughout the entirety of it. He only recently began to put on pads and has still not been cleared for contact.
With Kristian Fulton and L'Jarius Sneed nursing their own respective injuries , this news has created a lot of uncertainty around an already inexperienced Kansas City defensive backfield. However, general manager Brett Veach provided Chiefs fans with some much-needed clarity on Monday.
Veach joined SiriusXM Radio and talked about the severity of Delane's injury. He noted that it first appeared during Chiefs OTAs, but that he is gradually progressing in his recovery. "Starting first with Mansoor, he had a shoulder blade right toward the end of OTAs," Veach said. "And so we don’t think it’s going to be long-term or anything, but that has to just completely heal."
Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo explained last week that Delane's ailment was in fact a shoulder blade injury , not just a typical shoulder. It's evidently been going on for quite some time now, as OTAs wrapped up in early June, but he appears to be getting closer to full health.
Although there is still a bit of concern with his injury, it shouldn't be long before he's near 100% and taking hits. It is mostly a good thing that he's been practicing in the non-contact jersey so he doesn't fall too far behind with the scheme as a rookie.
Even if he does fall behind a bit in practice, Veach doesn't expect Delane's return to speed to take very long. "There’s nothing limiting him out there. He's been taking all the 7-on-7 reps and just not the team periods and the contact stuff," he continued. "We want to leave him out of that right now, but I would say in the next 7-8 days, he'll probably get the green light to do everything. So, we're excited about him."
Delane will be one of the X-factors on K.C.'s defense this season alongside likely CB2 Nohl Williams. His development and growth should play a major factor in determining how effective the pass defense is.

title: Chiefs Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times and TV Channels
full_text:
With training camp past the halfway mark , preseason NFL action has arrived. For the Kansas City Chiefs, their three-game August slate kicks off on Saturday night.
Head coach Andy Reid's team faces a pair of its 2026-27 regular-season opponents from the NFC West over the next few weeks, with a bout against a third playoff-caliber NFC foe sandwiched in between. This serves as a great first look at the team, also providing Reid's staff and the front office with opportunities to evaluate depth ahead of roster cuts on August 30.
Here's everything you need to know about the Chiefs' preseason schedule.
To begin their preseason gauntlet, the Chiefs host the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday afternoon. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford isn't tracking to suit up, nor is K.C. superstar Patrick Mahomes . Expect some starters to get work, albeit not a ton.
By this point, Chiefs training camp will have already wrapped up. With the team out of dorms at Missouri Western State University, it travels to Tampa to play the Buccaneers. Coming off a letdown of a season, the Bucs have every incentive to put the past behind them and deliver a rejuvenated effort in 2026.
Reid didn't seem very optimistic that Mahomes would play at all in the preseason, but that storyline is worth monitoring.
Preseason outcomes may not roll over to the regular season, but this specific game remains critical. It's just two days before rosters must be trimmed down to a final group of 53, meaning dozens of players will be under immense pressure to put quality performances on tape.
Anticipate a heavy dose of backups, with everyone from journeyman veterans to undrafted rookie free agents putting the finishing touches on their cases to stick with the organization.

title: Andy Reid, Chiefs Welcoming Eric Bieniemy Back: 'Everybody Was Glad to See Him'
full_text:
After a two-week absence from Kansas City Chiefs training camp , offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy made his return to the team to kick off a new week of practice.
Head coach Andy Reid's right-hand man briefly left the club in late July after his wife, Mia, was shot multiple times in the family's Virginia home. With Mia now on the mend and making progress in her recovery , her husband is back at the Missouri Western State University facility ahead of the Chiefs' preseason opener on Saturday.
Reid can already feel Bieniemy's presence, citing it as something that boosts the offense.
"Good to have EB back," Reid said. "He's back in the fold, and I don't think he missed a step, man. He was out there getting after it, so that's a positive for the offensive side."
Bieniemy's famous fire and competitive drive were out in full force on Monday in the form of him giving pointers to running backs during pass protection drills and much more. Reid believes he's picked up right where he left off.
"It was great to have him back out there," Reid said. "Everybody was glad to see him. I think once you start going, then you're going. It's a little bit like a game — once you're in the game, you're in the game. He always brings great energy."
While Bieniemy was out, Kansas City leaned on pass game coordinator Joe Bleymaier and offensive line coach Andy Heck to step up to the plate. That duo, as well as assistants such as wide receivers coach Chad O'Shea, kept everything rolling to kick off the month of August. Bieniemy's return to St. Joseph, Missouri comes just five days before the team faces the Los Angeles Rams in preseason outing No. 1.
With plenty left to figure out on offense regarding roster construction, positional rotations and playing time, having Bieniemy in the mix again certainly makes Reid's life easier. It might make things a tad more difficult for the players, but that's precisely the point of Bieniemy coming back to the organization earlier this year.
It came down to ideal timing, which Reid was in conversations with Bieniemy about on a daily basis. Now, it's all systems go.
"Listen, I was talking to him several times a day," Reid said. "So I knew he was coming back if everything worked out the way it had been. The primary thing is that Mia's stable and in good hands and that she's doing well. That was the primary thing with it, and that's where we're set with it."

title: Eric Bieniemy, Xavier Worthy, Ashton Gillotte Return to Chiefs Camp – Others Remain Sidelined
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs brought three good pieces of news with them to Monday's training camp practice in St. Joseph, Missouri .
Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy returned to practice for the first time since leaving the team in late July to be with his family after his wife, Mia, was shot on July 26 .
Happy to have EB back ❤️ pic.twitter.com/5B8EDbeJZn
Meanwhile, two important Chiefs players returned to practice after noteworthy absences.
Wide receiver Xavier Worthy suffered a shoulder sprain on August 1, before the Chiefs' first padded practices began. On Monday, Worthy returned for his first padded practice of the 2026 season.
With Worthy back on the field, the Chiefs' wide receiver room is nearing full strength for the first time this camp. Rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen returned from his shin bruise on August 7 , while veteran receiver Rashee Rice has been ramping up his workload following an offseason knee surgery .
According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star , Worthy is participating in a limited capacity as he works his way back to 100%.
"Xavier Worthy participated in work with Mahomes and the offense," McDowell wrote. "As the Chiefs move to a team drill, Worthy jogged to the tent, presumably part of today’s plan in his first day back."
Second-year defensive end Ashton Gillotte, who entered training camp as the likely favorite to be one of the team's starting edge defenders, suffered a hamstring strain on July 31 and had also missed all of the team's padded practices so far. On Monday, Gillotte returned for his first practice of the month.
Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) and DE Ashton Gillotte (hamstring) are back at practice Monday. pic.twitter.com/Yp4k7KiBBH
Gillotte's absence provided even more opportunity for former first-round pick Felix Anudike-Uzomah and rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas , but the team will need multiple players to fill out the defensive end rotation in addition to surefire starter George Karlaftis.
Rashee Rice and Cyrus Allen both in 11-on-11s today. First time both have done that on the same day, IIRC. Ashton Gillotte has headed to the training tent and is rehabbing on the side.
As reported by Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , the Chiefs still had several key players not participating in Monday's practice: right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee), linebacker Drue Tranquill (back) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (PUP, knee).
Of this group of sidelined players, Smith's management is currently the most concerning. On August 7, Smith missed his first practice due to a hip issue, but head coach Andy Reid downplayed the ailment after practice.
"Trey, his hip was bothering him, [we] sent him to a specialist just to have it checked out, precautionary, he's gonna be OK."
Tranquill has managed lower back issues in the past, Sneed is having persistent knee concerns managed regularly, and Norman-Lott is still working back from last season's torn ACL.

title: This Chiefs Rookie WR Stunningly Made One of the Best Catches of Training Camp
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are carrying 13 wide receivers in their 90-man training camp lineup , but only about half of those players will actively be with the team by the time Week 1 rolls around. There are two or three spots up for grabs, aside from the Chiefs' obvious core of wideouts. One rookie under the radar among Chiefs fans is quietly putting together a strong camp. No, we're not talking about rookie receiver and training camp sweetheart Cyrus Allen , but rather California graduate Jacob De Jesus.
During Saturday's practice, De Jesus completed one of the filthiest routes we've seen from a Chiefs receiver in all of camp, and he topped it off with an incredible two-handed diving grab on a ball thrown by Chris Oladokun.
#Chiefs catch of the day might belong to the smallest player on the field: 5'7" WR Jacob De Jesus #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/dPEgibMjGW
Standing at 5-foot-7 and 170 pounds, what De Jesus lacks in size he makes up for with his gritty play style. He is a slot wideout who finished his senior year at Cal with 108 catches for 1,030 yards.
De Jesus' undersized nature will make it difficult for him to carve out a role in the offense, but he does have extensive special teams experience. ST coordinator Dave Toub praised De Jesus in his presser yesterday afternoon. "De Jesus is solid, great catcher," Toub said. "Just not a real big guy, but he's going to be exciting in the preseason games, for sure."
Across his three years of Division I ball, De Jesus returned 63 punts and 59 kickoffs. With the Chiefs' return job still a question mark, that is one way he can get on the field for KC.
De Jesus may be a long shot to make the final 53-man roster , but he's going to do his best to prove himself as a special teams asset. At the very least, he is someone who should generate exciting plays in each of the Chiefs' three preseason contests.

title: Three Chiefs Players With the Most to Lose in Preseason Opener vs Rams
full_text:
Time has flown by in the offseason, as the Kansas City Chiefs are just a week away from their preseason opener at Arrowhead Stadium. Fans will finally get to witness what all the hype is about from training camp and see which players will be able to carve out a role for the regular season. While the mandatory roster cuts aren't for a few weeks, the first preseason game will play a major role in determining who makes the final 53-man cut, especially for a select few players.
Which Chiefs have the most to lose (or potentially gain) this Saturday against the Rams? Here are three players who will have a lot on the line in that matchup.
With Patrick Mahomes likely sitting out the entire preseason , a door has opened for seventh-round draft selection Garrett Nussmeier to receive more playing time this weekend. The LSU product should be the second quarterback fans watch in preseason after second-stringer Justin Fields' day is over.
Now that he has an extended opportunity, Nussmeier's performance could have massive implications for his chances of securing the QB3 job. It will be his first real opportunity to play with the rest of the squad, and it's possible that he receives snaps with some of the first-team starters as well.
While it's highly unlikely that Chris Oladokun jumps him up the depth chart, K.C. is in a tricky situation with Nussmeier. If he plays poorly in the preseason, the Chiefs could decide to run with two quarterbacks on the active 53-man roster to open the campaign and leave Oladokun on the practice squad. Nussmeier cannot simply be placed on the practice squad like Oladokun as a drafted rookie , as he would first have to clear the NFL waiver wire. Ultimately, Nussmeier has three weeks to make or break his spot on the roster, starting against Los Angeles.
The coaching staff is expected to play it safe with defensive end Ashton Gillotte's latest hamstring injury, making him questionable for the first few preseason games. An absence would allow fourth-year defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah to continue receiving first-team reps opposite George Karlaftis on the edge. Coming off a 2025 season where he did not play any games due to a hamstring surgery , this could be Anudike-Uzomah's near-final chance to earn a permanent starting role on the D-line. Gillotte's injury is giving him an opportunity to work his way up the depth chart.
Anudike-Uzomah is running out of chances to live up to his first-round draft pick billing after being taken 31st overall three years ago. All Chiefs fans will be rooting for him to succeed, but there's no doubt that he has quite a lot to lose this weekend if he doesn't have a strong showing.
After practicing with the first team for all but one day of training camp, the undrafted rookie out of Indiana has a real chance to start at right tackle over Jaylon Moore in Preseason Week 1. It will be a huge opportunity for Benson, who could make a major statement in his first preseason action. Young offensive linemen can easily get overwhelmed in situations like this and make costly mistakes. Benson will need to stay level-headed, trust his technique, and avoid letting the moment get too big when he takes the field.
Whether he starts or not remains to be seen, but he's going to get at least a quarter or two worth of playing time this weekend. How he performs compared to Moore will be a massive factor in determining whether he makes the 53-man roster or potentially starts the regular-season opener against Denver.

title: 1 Quote and a National Spotlight at Chargers Training Camp Hint at Big Things in 2026
full_text:
It didn’t take long for Los Angeles Chargers fans to see all the positives of the Mike McDaniel hiring, which paired him with head coach Jim Harbaugh and elite quarterback Justin Herbert.
Free from the likes of Greg Roman and a long, long, exhausting list of other coaching names to roll through Los Angeles over the years, watching Herbert finally get a modern offensive mind like McDaniel sort of felt like an offseason Super Bowl.
Now that preseason games are almost here, the national side has started to catch up with these ideas a bit. That’s especially the case when seeing how things have worked out on the field, plus more quotes from McDaniel and Harbaugh , too.
The result? Even more hype for Chargers fans, too.
Offseason moves hinted that the Chargers gave McDaniel pretty much free rein over what he wants to do with the offense.
McDaniel's moves included adding fullback Alec Ingold, tight ends Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, running back Keaton Mitchell, an entirely new interior offensive line and even drafting wideout Brenen Thompson.
So, every layer of the depth chart while revamping the scheme and fits.
Oh, and McDaniel forced Herbert to rework his footwork and approach in certain packages while installing an entirely new offense.
Fast forward to camp, the results look good and for some, like Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer , the quotes kick things into overdrive. That’s especially true when McDaniel talks about the freedom he’s been given by Harbaugh.
“And he really fosters the maximum out of me because he gives me responsibility and doesn’t micromanage things I earned, in his opinion, that he’s comfortable with me taking ownership of,” McDaniel said. “ He’s just an elite leader that way. … Our relationship couldn’t be stronger.”
Look no further than the running back room. McDaniel just told onlookers that he’s going to ride the hot hand regardless of whether it’s Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell or Kimani Vidal.
The modernized unpredictability of it all might fluster fantasy football managers, but from a national perspective, the Chargers feel more dangerous than ever.
Good thing McDaniel gets the all-clear from Harbaugh, too: This might be his only year with the Chargers. If they match the hype, there’s little doubt he will instantly become one of the top names on the head-coach hiring cycle again.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: Genesis Smith, a Rookie Ball Hawk Who Can Make Big Plays
full_text:
Genesis Smith, born on November 5, 2004, in Chandler, Arizona, played his high school ball at Hamilton High School, where he had 16 interceptions during his football career with the program, earning three-star recruiting status, according to 247Sports .
Smith decided to stay close to home, committing to the University of Arizona, where he would instantly see the field in 2023 as a true freshman. He recorded an interception and 24 tackles during this season.
Going into his sophomore season, he had his breakout season with 63 tackles (3.5 for loss), three interceptions, six pass deflections and two forced fumbles. After this successful year, Smith looked to transfer away from Arizona, but eventually found himself back with the program for his third and final year with the Wildcats.
This final season saw Smith help the Wildcats to the seventh-best passing defense across college football, becoming a stalwart roaming safety striking fear into opposing Big 12 offenses.
This elite season, coupled with his first attempt to have draft eligibility, led Smith to decide to enter the 2026 NFL Draft, with NFL Scout Lance Zierlein describing him as a player who: "...offers ballhawking coverage qualities but has alarming issues as an open-field tackler. He’s instinctive, with the eyes to digest route development while reading the quarterback like a poker player looking for tells. He has average top-end speed but good route recognition and premium ball skills. Smith is a low-impact run defender and open-field tackler, though...His run defense won’t appeal to some teams, but his ability to read the field and make plays on the football will entice other squads looking for a safety on Day 3."
The Los Angeles Chargers selected Genesis Smith in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft , with hopes of him improving his tackling while continuing his dominance as a free-ranging safety who can create turnovers in a defense that is now under new leadership.

If Smith can clean up his tackling woes, he could very well turn into an elite safety in the NFL. If he does not, he may be buried on the depth chart for his first NFL season.

title: Chargers Underdog Story: Branson Taylor's Rise and Jim Harbaugh's Culture Shift
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are starting their third week of fall 2026 training camp. One of the most anticipated position battles at the left guard spot along the offensive line is heating up with at least three players battling for the job heading into the first preseason game.
One of the biggest surprises in the position battle is second-year player Branson Taylor. Taylor has received praise from nearly every corner of the team for the improvements he has made from year one until present day.
Taylor was a sixth-round pick out of Pitt in the 2025 draft. The coaching staff experimented with him throughout training camp in different roles last season but he ultimately failed to make the 53-man roster out of training camp. He spent the entirety of the 2025 season on the practice squad before being elevated to face the division champion Denver Broncos and start in place of starters who were resting heading into the playoffs.
Entering the 2026 offseason, Taylor was largely written off with the additions in free agency and the 2026 draft that the Chargers had brought on to the roster with the new scheme from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. I did not have him on the initial 53-man roster in my first post-OTAs prediction.
What has changed? How do we explain how Taylor is firmly a contender to take the starting left guard job and also showing tackle flexibility? The short answer is simple: he worked his tail off.
Jim Harbaugh was asked about Branson Taylor getting reps with the first team at his pre-practice press conference before Saturday's padded practice and the growth he has seen from year heading into Year 2. "This offseason, just been a really incredible offseason," Harbaugh said in reference to Taylor's growth, "In the training environment, saw it there first and then on the field in OTAs and in minicamp."
Harbaugh also specifically mentioned the reports he was getting from the training staff and executive director of player performance Ben Herbert regarding Taylor's work in the offseason. "I mean, the reports coming back from Ben Herbert and staff were like, Branson, wow! Leveling up."
Quarterback Justin Hebert was also asked about Taylor getting work with the first team in his post-practice press conference after Monday's walkthrough. Herbert's response to the question was indicative of how much Taylor has changed from last season. "Branson's put in a lot of great work this offseason, he showed up a different man," Herbert said, "It's been fun to see and it's been cool for him to get the opportunities to run with the ones."
A sixth-round pick spending a year on the practice squad and one year later possibly pushing for a starting role, if not at least a roster spot, is a great story. The fact that Taylor is in a true battle for the job is a testament to the work that he put in this offseason and his dedication to becoming a professional.
Taylor's current resurgence is also a testament to the culture Jim Harbaugh has brought the Chargers, now in his third year with the franchise. Taylor's hard work got him the opportunity, but the coaching staff, starting with Ben Herbert noticed and rewarded that hard work.
Just before Justin Herbert, Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said at his press conference, "I really want the starter to earn it. I think the player will tell us. I think his teammates will tell us by the collective group execution," McDaniel said. "The best player for that position will be helping the whole group operate with great communication and decisiveness and style of play."
The collective mindset and culture from every corner of the Chargers' staff and roster appears to be something that Harbaugh has brought to Los Angeles.

title: What Recent Chargers Training Camp Practices Mean for Week 1
full_text:
Day 11 of Los Angeles Chargers training camp is in the books. While Monday's practice wasn't anything special, due to it being a walkthrough day, it still gave us another look at the direction the team is heading.
The first preseason game against the Houston Texans is less than a week away and the Chargers are getting a clearer picture of what they will possibly look like when the season starts.
Even with it being a slow practice, there are a few developments that Chargers fans should pay attention to.
During the first padded practice of the year, Rashawn Slater went to the medical tent on 11-on-11 drills. He returned briefly and was seen after practice doing routine activities, but he has now missed three consecutive practices.
The Chargers haven't disclosed what exactly went wrong, however you have to think how serious it could have been. Slater missed all of the 2025 season with a torn left patellar tendon, which hurt the Chargers offensive line immensely.
It seems like they are taking precautionary measures as of recent, making sure no further damage is done. Trying to ease the Pro Bowl tackle back into action. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh mentioned to reporters that Slater was taking a rest day on Saturday, but have not been told what the reason for the last two days is.
The Chargers have plenty to figure out when it comes to the left guard position with the first game of the season lurking around the corner. As of Monday's practice, the position is still wide open for anybody to take.
Second-year Branson Taylor and former Detroit Lion Kayode Awosika appear to be the frontrunners of the competition. Splitting the first-team reps almost every practice, these two have impressed the coaching staff early on. Despite neither being viewed as the obvious favorite when the competition began, these guys have really shown what they are capable of in 2026.
Honorable mentions in the race for the starting position are Jake Slaughter, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins, who have also impressed at times during camp, and are still in the race for that number one spot at left guard.
On Monday courtesy of Chargers.com , the Bolts' offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel stated, "No one's eliminated themselves from the tournament". To me, it's their position to lose or win. Meaning, making no mistakes and being as sharp as possible on a regular basis
At this point in preseason, the Chargers will have to start making decisions in all aspects of the team. As each day passes, new situations occur that can affect the whole season, starting with Week 1.
