title: Rashawn Slater Setback, Chargers' Fantasy Dilemmas and Joe Alt Shines to Start Week 3
full_text:
Week 3 of 2026 training camp has started for the Los Angeles Chargers with their first game on the horizon. The Chargers will face the Houston Texans at 5 p.m. on Thursday night to kick off the preseason games.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh said about 15 of the veterans will warm up with the team but will not play in the first game. None of the regular starters are expected to play in the first preseason matchup.
The Chargers released their first unofficial depth chart following their Sunday practice to wrap up week two which had a few interesting takeaways but overall serves as what to expect for Thursday night's lineup and position rotations.
Los Angeles started their third week of camp with a light walkthrough after a weekend of padded practices. Since it was a walkthrough on Monday, there are no significant highlights from the practice. Let's take a look at noteworthy news from the Mike McDaniel's press conference as well as some lineup questions from practice plus a pair of roster moves to start the week.
Chargers left tackle Rashawn Slater is returning from a devastating ruptured patellar tendon which he suffered just days into his return to the field in training camp of 2025. The timing of his return was always subject to some management by the coaching and training staff.
Slater gave everyone a scare last week during the first padded practice of training camp. He left practice and headed to the injury tent and the NFL world breathed a sigh of relief when he was spotted back on the sidelines and participating in conditioning drills.
Slater participated is practice in the days following the scare but has now missed three practices in a row. Slater did not participate in padded practices over the weekend and he did not participate in walk-throughs on Monday. The team will stay tight-lipped about his health but it is clear that he is experiencing something that is causing to to take a step back at let it rest.
At the moment, Slater's absence can simply be chalked up to soreness in his surgically repaired knee which missing two padded practices makes sense including the start of game week for walk-throughs in a game there is not way he will play in. It is obvious Slater suffered some sort of setback that is being managed and the situation is worth monitoring going forward. At the very least, this gives the Chargers a chance to rotate through multiple options at left tackle to be better prepared if Slater has to miss any time or even if he is not ready to start the season.
Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel took the podium after practice today and gave massive praise to right tackle Joe Alt for successfully setting up and blocking Khalil Mack on a screen play. Mack apparently has been making it impossible for the offense to run a screen to his side so far in camp.
McDaniel also faced a question regarding the running backs and how the roles will be handled. He jokingly responded that he felt the question was rooted in fantasy football.
" Bad news, fantasy owners. Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level," McDaniel said, "Bad news is I can’t tell you which games those are.” He went on to say, "I'll use all three of those guys probably every game. The relative ratio, that will be based on opponent."
Omarion Hampton is widely considered a fantasy breakout in waiting and has been going very high in redraft leagues. Figuring out where to draft Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal will be much more difficult to value.
The Chargers have made a roster move to start the week.
we've signed OLB andre carter + waived WR mante’ morrow pic.twitter.com/HvP5FBOdEl
The Chargers released wide receiver Mante Morrow, who was signed as an undrafted free agent after a rookie minicamp tryout but has been unable to practice. In his place, Los Angeles signed former Army star edge rusher Andre Carter. Carter was a highly productive player at West Point who was once considered a potential early-round draft pick but ultimately went undrafted after a poor pre-draft process.
Carter has had several years in the NFL bouncing around practice squads but also plenty of time to build up his size and strength. He had a stint with Mike McDaniel and the Miami Dolphins last season and is likely depth to bolster the edge room for preseason.

title: Some Almost Shocking Chargers Coach Comments Repaints Final Cuts Outlook at Key Spot
full_text:
Every team has to make tough calls at final cuts after training camp, but it feels especially critical and difficult for the Los Angeles Chargers this summer.
These Chargers, after all, enter Year 3 of the Jim Harbaugh era and have once again undergone a serious roster churn as he remakes the program.
Amplifying that is the arrival of two new coordinators who want to put their own stamps on both sides of the ball: Mike McDaniel for the offense and Chris O’Leary for the defense.
All this means Chargers recent draft picks, signings and longstanding veterans aren’t guaranteed anything as the program gets reshaped once again.
Some key comments dropped recently certainly hint at this well enough.
The comments in question come from O’Leary and the defensive side of the ball.
There’s supposed to be a theme of continuity for the defense, given that O’Leary worked under Jesse Minter before going to the college level for a year. Harbaugh brought him back to keep things going when Minter left this offseason to coach Baltimore.
But that doesn't guarantee anything, especially at the edge-rushing spot.
Speaking with reporters around a training camp practice this week, O’Leary had nothing but praise for undrafted free agent Nadame Tucker, saying the rookie has “done a really good job.”
More telling might be O’Leary’s comments on Kyle Kennard: "Consistently getting better...the effort has improved."
That comment about “effort” sure seems to stick out. Fans and the Chargers had pretty big expectations for Kennard when he arrived via the fourth round in 2025. But he simply hasn’t been able to break into the rotation often.
This, in part, led to the trade for Odafe Oweh last season. Once he got away in free agency, the Chargers used a first-round pick on Akheem Mesidor and Tucker followed O’Leary from college as a college free agent.
Hope that the super-productive Tucker would be an undrafted success story after reuniting with O’Leary seemed to be more of a fan dream than what would be guaranteed to play out in camp. But he’s having a superb summer so far and indeed appears to have an inside track on a final 53 spot.
Right now, that could have the edge rushing depth chart looking like this on the final 53:
If Kennard doesn’t keep ascending, though, veteran Bud Dupree is still right there as a veteran option. Or, if there’s a roster crunch, the Chargers could always choose to keep four with reserves on the practice squad.
Regardless, it’s seemingly a telling comment from O’Leary about what might’ve gone wrong in the past, some public motivation for players and a sign of what’s to come as the summer continues.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: Tony Jefferson, Everyone's Favorite "Unc"
full_text:
Tony Jefferson, born on January 27, 1992, in San Diego, California, played his high school ball at Eastlake High School, where he led Eastlake to a San Diego Division 1 CIF championship during his senior year. As a four-star recruit, according to 247Sports , Jefferson committed to the Oklahoma Sooners.
The 2010 freshman season for Jefferson was an instant impact year, with him winning the 2010 Freshman All-American by multiple outlets and the Big 12 Conference co-Defensive Freshman of the Year (along with OSU Cowboys linebacker Shaun Lewis). 2011, saw Jefferson improve upon his award-winning freshman season, earning double the amount of interceptions (4) and sacks (4.5) from his previous season.
2012 was Jefferson's final year with the Sooners, where he had 119 tackles as a defensive back...just putting a cherry on top of all the other accolades he earned during his college tenure.
Somehow, Jefferson went undrafted ( some reports say that WalterFootball.com leaked character concerns that affected his draft stock...even though said concerns were quickly and later refuted by actual sources). The San Diego native landed in Arizona with the Cardinals, where he had a role from day 1, collecting 24 tackles during his rookie season.
Jefferson became the team's starter from 2014-2016, quickly becoming one of the league's most reliable starting safeties. He would move on to Baltimore, where he would find himself as a mainstay starter from 2017-2019, helping John Harbaugh and his defense.
After a torn ACL in 2019, Jefferson found himself out of the league in 2020, seeing his career now in jeopardy. He was now a 29-year-old safety who had not played for two years previously and was coming off an injury. Jefferson went to play for the 49ers and Ravens for a total of six games during the 2021 season, likely marking the end of what was a strong NFL career.
Jefferson had seemingly one last opportunity in 2022, when he would play for the New York Giants, seeing nine games of action for 23 tackles. Jefferson would retire in 2023 and go back to Baltimore to become a scouting intern under then-Ravens Director of Player Personnel Joe Hortiz and company.
Jefferson's playing career seemed over, but with Hortiz moving onto the Los Angeles Chargers in 2024 as the team's General Manager, he called up Jefferson and asked if he was willing to try out for the team during the offseason.
Jefferson did just that and became a crucial piece of the Bolts' defense for their 2024 season. He was technically a practice-squad guy who saw himself elevated up and down the roster for the entire season, giving the Bolts roster flexibility while also giving them Pro Bowl-level Safety play when called upon. This season yielded a few votes for the Comeback Player of the Year award for Jefferson.
Going into 2025, fans were excited about the San Diego native, but were concerned about how a 33-year-old Safety would hold up for an entire NFL season. Jefferson once again did the up-and-down practice-squad roster movement , but had much more playing time and much more impact plays than the year prior.
13 Games (8 Starts) 4 Interceptions (!) 7 Pass Deflections 57 Tackles (One for Loss)
"Tony Jefferson signed a 1 year, $1,500,000 contract with the Los Angeles Chargers, including $100,000 signing bonus, $1,400,000 guaranteed, and an average annual salary of $1,500,000. In 2026, Jefferson will earn a base salary of $1,300,000, a signing bonus of $100,000 and a roster bonus of $100,000, while carrying a cap hit of $1,750,000 and a dead cap value of $1,400,000." - Spotrac
Tony Jefferson's 2026 season will be an intriguing one . I will not argue against the same guy who has beaten all odds multiple times (being undrafted, injuries, retirement, etc), but it is an important note that he will be 34 years old for the 2026 season.
However, it is reasonable to believe that Jefferson should still be a strong downhill safety who will help the defense with his play recognition and leadership.

title: Biggest Takeaways from the Los Angeles Chargers' First Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have wrapped up their second week of training camp. The team has released its first unofficial depth chart leading into their first preseason game against the Houston Texans on Thursday night, August 13th.
NFL coaching staffs will argue that the unofficial depth chart is simply something put together by the  PR team heading into the preseason because the league requires it. However, the depth chart serves a general purpose as it helps structure the expectations heading into the game for fans and the flow of substitutions throughout the game.
Additionally, the unofficial depth charts can also serve as an indicator for position battles and where certain players stand in their position groups. The PR staff may make the depth chart and have no actual input on the roster but they are also generally plugged in to the team, who is getting practice reps, favor within the organization and the circumstances around the team.
Lets dive into the biggest takeaways from the Chargers first 2026 unofficial depth chart.
The Chargers opted to let a battle play out amongst five different players for the vacant starting left guard job. Offensive line expert and evaluator Brandon Thorn said in a social media thread that letting the competition play out was the right move given the lack of track record amongst the five possible players.
Over the past week, pads have been introduced, a major point of emphasis from the coaching staff in terms of evaluating offensive linemen . Of the five players who were contenders for the starting role to start fall camp, three have appeared to stand out and risen to the top of the current battle. Veteran free agent addition Kayode Awosika and rookie Jake Slaughter have been contenders since OTAs with Awosika having a slight edge bringing a veteran level of consistency.
Second-year player Branson Taylor inserted his name into the mix early in training camp after being nearly an afterthought heading into OTAs. Taylor has been getting significant run with the first team and received glowing praise from head coach Jim Harbaugh and the training staff. The battle appears to be clearly shaping up as fight between Awosika, Taylor and Slaughter and the first official depth chart reflects that by listing Awosika or Taylor or Slaughter.
Every roster group has the rookie undrafted free agents listed last in their position groups, seemingly until earned and proven otherwise. The only exception to this is UDFA edge rusher Nadame Tucker who is listed fifth behind Bud Dupree but ahead of Kyle Kennard.
Tucker was a favorite to impress and make the roster heading into training camp given his connections to defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary last season at Western Michigan. Tucker has been terrorizing backup offensive tackles and racking up sacks in the second week of training camp.
The depth chart lists Tarheeb Still as a starter and the opposite starter being Donte Jackson or Cam Hart. The general consensus was that it would have been Jackson as the clear starter and Still and Hart being on the opposite end.
Could this be a simple PR staff choice or is Tarheeb Still establishing himself at the top of the group? One thing is clear, there are the top three followed by every other corner on the roster. The rest of camp and preseason will be hotly contested for defensive back roles.
The Chargers have one of the top tight end rooms with their top three in the NFL. The depth chart reflects this listing "Charlie Kolar or Oronde Gadsden or David Njoku" to start the preseason. All three have been getting significant action in different personnel packages and the trio could easily rotate in roles and usage based on individual matchups.
The Chargers face the Houston Texans this Thursday which will not feature any of the regular starters according to Jim Harbaugh. The rotations throughout the game should mirror the unofficial depth for the most part and will be the first opportunity for many of the rookies to make an impression and possibly the beginning of a last stand for some of the players on the roster bubble.

title: The Chargers Rookie Playmaker Who is Quickly Becoming Impossible to Overlook
full_text:
Brenen Thompson was already an intriguing name for the Los Angeles Chargers going into the offseason. However, the rookie is giving Chargers fans even more of a reason to pay attention.
There is still a lot to learn about what Thompson can bring to Los Angeles, but his first few months with the team have certainly caught the attention of those watching closely. The speedster has already made his presence felt, which is very promising to see early on.
Now, Thompson has an opportunity to prove his college football career was not a fluke. His speed and big-play ability give him a unique skill set in Los Angeles.
Brenen Thompson started his journey at Texas, which led to him transferring to Oklahoma. where he played two seasons, only having 471 total yards. To me, this is where his story gets interesting. His time in Oklahoma never really showed what he could become, then he transferred to Mississippi State where he had a breakout year. Having over a 1,000 receiving yards and six touchdowns, and breaking multiple school records, showing elite level skill, and being a reliable target.
His time in Mississippi compared to Oklahoma felt like he finally found the right situation to show what he really could do. He took advantage of his opportunity and show he could be a legit playmaker. It was a major change in his college journey, and it gave the Chargers something to believe in when they drafted him.
Thompson went from being overlooked to one of the more productive wide receivers at the collegiate level. That one season ultimately changed the way people view him and put in on the path to the NFL.
The rookie's speed is by far the most noticeable aspect of his game early in preseason. That being said, his ability to regularly get open and make plays is what stands out to the coaching staff.
Chargers writer Omar Navarro on Chargers.com stated "So far, the rookie continuously finds himself as a target by Herbert during the team drills, garnering praise from his fellow teammates and coaches already".
Every single day it seems like Brenen Thompson makes an elite-level play on the practice field. Whether he is blowing past a defender with his speed or making an incredible catch look easy, Thompson keeps grabbing the attention of every single person around him.
Getting consistent opportunities from Justin Herbert during team drills says a lot about where Thompson currently stands. For a player who just arrived in the league, he looks like someone who is evolving every time he steps foot on the field. I truly expect him to flourish into an elite target.

title: Akheem Mesidor Cooks Joe Alt, LG Battle Narrows as Chargers Wrap Second Week of Camp
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have wrapped up their second week of fall 2026 training camp with a Sunday practice at the Bolt. Two weeks through camp and heading into the first of three preseason games has positioned the Chargers in a positive position heading into the preseason with roster battles heating up and clearing up as well.
The Chargers have held several practices with pads and the pads were absolutely needed to start narrowing and advancing position and role battles. The preseason games will be of high importance for many of the players fighting for roster spots and roles, but the foundation is laid in practice. Several of the key position battles have heated up through the first two weeks. Let's dive in to where the battles currently stand and discuss several highlights from Sunday's practice.
The battle for the starting left guard job is one of the most hotly discussed and contested open jobs on the Chargers heading into the 2026 season. After losing former first-round pick Zion Johnson to the Cleveland Browns in free agency, the Chargers have opted to fill the vacancy with a battle royale between multiple players.
Since OTAs the original three players expected to compete for the role, Trevor Penning, Kayode Awosika and rookie Jake Slaughter, have seen two new additions to the competition in veteran Trey Pipkins and 2025 sixth-round pick Branson Taylor.
Throughout the second week of camp three, players have stood out in the battle and received the initial reps with the first team during padded practices. As expected Kayode Awosika was in the lead as described by head coach Jim Harbaugh and rookie Jake Slaughter, despite initially appearing to fall behind in the battle has surged to finish the week .
The biggest surprise in this competition is second-year player Branson Taylor, who started Sunday's practice with the first team at left guard. Harbaugh praised Taylor's effort in the offseason to remake his body and said the reports from executive director of player performance Ben Herbert and the training staff were overwhelmingly positive.
All three players seem to be positioning themselves for the final fight for the starting job over the next week and half or so. The Chargers released their first unofficial depth chart following practice and lists all three as potential starters at left guard.
Harbaugh put a timeline on when the team would ideally name their starting offensive line by approximately the second preseason game. Slaughter may have the edge if he proves himself worthy, the team has the highest investment in him as a second-round pick this year, but if Taylor or Awosika truly lock down the position, it will give Slaughter more time to develop.
Akheem Mesidor utilized a nasty spin move, often as a counter, during his final season at the University of Miami. Hall of Fame edge rusher Jason Taylor was his position coach at Miami and he and teammate Rueben Bain were well-trained and utilized polished pass rush moves.
Mesidor recently mentioned on the Chargers Weekly podcast that he specifically wanted to go against Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. He views the competition as beneficial to prepare for NFL action
There’s no better regular-season prep for Akheem Mesidor than Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. pic.twitter.com/QJmegDf8yY
Mesidor got his competitive wish to face Alt again on Sunday. He used his spin move to beat Alt cleanly to the inside. One-on-ones are hard to judge because in a real game the right guard may have been standing right there to help, but the rookie getting a win over Alt is good for both players to sharpen up during camp.
The Chargers have position battles for beyond the starting left guard position. The cornerback room after the top three will be fiercely contested throughout camp and the preseason as will the depth of the safety group.
The linebackers and edge rushers will all face a tough battle for the depth roles available to those units. Several tough decisions may be made at roster cut-down day.
Players in those battles for roles and roster spots turned it up at Sunday's practice with several noteworthy plays. Edge rusher Nadame Tucker secured another sack today while Kyle Kennard won several reps on the edge as well. Both received praise from defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary after practice.
Undrafted cornerback Avery Smith , continues to make plays and linebacker Junior Colson showed up as a blitzer. The coming weeks of practice and preseason games will be vital to sort out these depth battles.

title: Rams Get Mixed Reviews in Joint Practice Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams had their first of two joint practices this summer. On Tuesday, the Rams practiced against the Dallas Cowboys as they prepare for their first preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Historically, head coach Sean McVay has found more value in joint practices rather than preseason games as it’s a more controlled environment.
Given that the practice was in Woodland Hills and not Oxnard at the Cowboys’ facility, media reporting was limited. The Rams don’t allow the media to comment on specific personnel or report certain details from practice.
Reviews of the Rams’ performance were pretty mixed. Still, McVay seemed pleased with the overall takeaway from the practice.
“There was a lot of good work that we got today against an excellent opponent, just bouncing back and forth. I thought the team periods were competitive and most importantly, we can learn,” said McVay. “These are opportunities for us to grow even though we don't game plan it. We're just testing our rules. There was a lot of good stuff really from both sides and I look forward to looking at the film and diving into how we can learn from it.”
According to team reporter Stu Jackson , quarterback Matthew Stafford threw one interception, but was flawless otherwise. Jackson noted an interception from Quentin Lake and the pass rush getting to Dak Prescott without Myles Garrett. After practice, Stafford made sure to compliment the offensive line, especially in the run game.
The Athletic’s Nate Atkins noted that the Rams’ secondary won the day. Said Atkins, “The Rams’ secondary mostly won the day, thanks to some help from the pass rush. And what stood out was the versatility in their approach.”
Lake on lock. 🔒 pic.twitter.com/IybGv21Lq5
However, given some of the reporting limitations, it was mostly Cowboys media commenting on the practice as it was happening. According to many Cowboys media members , the Rams’ offense struggled at times against Christian Parker’s defense.
The Cowboys’ linebackers reportedly stole the show, especially Dee Winters and Justin Barron. Barron had a pair of interceptions on Stafford and Stetson Bennett. Wide receiver George Pickens also made some plays against the Rams’ secondary.
3️⃣ INTs Have yourself a day, @justinbarron22 👏 #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/Dfv4SLCtmK
Reading the Rams’ coverage, it’s easy to come away with the takeaway that they had a very strong joint practice. On the other hand, Cowboys media would have you believing that they dominated the afternoon.
At the end of the day, the answer is likely somewhere in the middle, and it doesn’t matter as much as many want it to. That’s not to say that joint practices don’t matter. McVay clearly finds value in them. With that said, there’s no game planning involved, and winning a joint practice doesn’t equate to winning games in the regular season. It matters in the same way that the preseason doesn’t matter.
This is simply a chance for the Rams to compete against a different defense and test out some things that they’ve been working on. Since the start of training camp , the Rams have been going up against the same group of players on the other side. Tuesday was an opportunity to compete against another set of players and go against a team that feels different. The Rams aren’t going to show their entire hand against a team that they are set to play in December.
While the Rams may not have been their sharpest, there were still strong moments and McVay seemed pleased with the work they got in. That’s the important part. The Rams will have nearly a month to make adjustments based on what they learned and continue building toward Week 1.

title: Rams Get Positive Puka Nacua Injury Update, Remain Cautious With Myles Garrett
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams wrapped up their joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday, but it didn’t come without its share of injuries . Wide receiver Puka Nacua left practice about 45 minutes early and did not return while edge rusher Myles Garrett sat out practice completely.
Head coach Sean McVay said that he wasn’t sure exactly what happened to Nacua.
“He was not able to finish practice so something happened. I'll have an update on it. I'm not sure exactly what that was,” said McVay. Added quarterback Matthew Stafford, “I'm not really sure what the issue was but nobody ran up to me in a panic, so I don’t think it was anything too major.”
NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport confirmed that it was nothing major for Nacua. Rapoport reported that Nacua is dealing with some minor soreness in his groin and that the team was just being cautious.
#Rams WR Puka Nacua, who left practice while walking with a trainer, is dealing with minor soreness in his groin, I'm told. The team is just being cautious.
Nacua wasn’t the only player the Rams were cautious with on Tuesday. After missing three consecutive practices during training camp , Garrett returned to the field for the final two days. He also practiced when the team got back to Woodland Hills. However, Garrett was held out once again for the joint practice with the Cowboys due to some swelling in his knee. McVay said that Garrett felt 85 percent, but the team erred on the side of caution.
“We just erred on the side of caution,” said McVay. “He wanted to be able to be out there, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he's able to return to full performance and feel like himself. There's nothing to be concerned about. It was just us erring on the side of caution.”
The Rams have been cautious all offseason with key players on both sides of the ball. Stafford has been practicing every other day while the Rams have held out wide receiver Davante Adams with rest days. Left tackle Alaric Jackson has missed some time as he manages blood clot medication and edge rusher Byron Young has missed practice with some knee soreness.
It shouldn’t be surprising that the Rams are being cautious with injuries and their star players. It does the Rams no good if Myles Garrett hurts his knee in August when they’re going to need him in November. The focus remains staying as healthy as possible for the start of the regular season. The goal is winning Week 1, not a joint practice against the Cowboys.
The Rams will start preparing for their preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs. As in past years, no starters or key depth players are expected to play during the preseason, with health being the priority.

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua Facing Potential Suspension for Week 1 vs. 49ers
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams wrap up training camp and get ready for the regular season, they could be without their star wide receiver when they play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. On his podcast on Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter said that Nacua’s case is one of several that are under review and being investigated by the NFL.
“Right now, there are some things going on behind closed doors that we don’t have full access to that are going to have a significant impact on the season,” said Schefter. “Cases I believe are now being reviewed include that of the Rams’ wide receiver Puka Nacua…it’s possible when the Niners and Rams play in Australia, it’s within the realm of options that Puka doesn’t play in that game.”
Potential discipline looms over a group of NFL players, including Rams WR Puka Nacua and Packers RB Josh Jacobs. Cc: @tyschmit 🎧 https://t.co/mTwS98lcWO pic.twitter.com/e5fW2ZoQwV
Following the Rams’ loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game, Nacua was seen out on New Year’s Eve and made headlines. Nacua allegedly bit a woman on the shoulder, leaving a mark. The victim has filed a civil lawsuit against Nacua. While no court date is currently set, Nacua's attorneys recently requested to push back a key witness deposition after September 7.
Nacua spent time in rehab this summer as he worked to grow as a person . He has been on his best behavior throughout training camp and didn’t hold out despite being in the final year of his rookie contract.
It’s unclear how long Nacua’s suspension would be and if one occurs before the regular season. The NFL still needs to go through its own independent investigation. The league also tends to let the legal process play out before making a decision. If Nacua is suspended for Week 1, it would be a significant loss against a division rival.
Schefter also noted that Alaric Jackson’s case from the offseason is under review. Jackson was arrested on felony domestic battery. However, the charges were dropped . While the charges were dropped, that doesn’t mean that the NFL can’t still hand out a suspension. This would be Jackson’s second offense against the personal conduct policy.
The cases remain under review and are still being investigated, according to Schefter. However, discipline is still a potential option. “By the time the regular season opens, we’ll have more clarity as it pertains to Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackson,” said Schefter.
This is certainly going to be something to monitor over the next few weeks. The league typically announces its disciplinary actions after law enforcement and independent league investigations conclude.
The Rams are heading into a season with Super Bowl expectations. Suspensions and injuries are among the few things that could derail those expectations. These situations were completely avoidable, and the Rams may now have to face the consequences. The Rams have a difficult schedule to open the season with their first four games against the 49ers, New York Giants, Denver Broncos, and Philadelphia Eagles. They will certainly want to be at full strength for those games and get off to a strong start.

title: 5 Key Things to Watch During Rams-Cowboys Joint Practice
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to practice against the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday in Woodland Hills before they start preparing for the preseason. Head coach Sean McVay typically rests all of his starters and key depth during the preseason, opting for the more controlled environment of joint practices.
These reps during joint practices will be the only ones against a different defense for the Rams’ starters before Week 1. It’s a chance for the Rams to see if what they’ve been installing is working and if adjustments are needed. Here are five things to watch as the Rams get ready to practice against the Cowboys.
The Rams put a lot of focus on improving their secondary this offseason . They signed Jaylen Watson and traded for Trent McDuffie. Against the Cowboys, the Rams’ secondary will get an immediate test as they go up against a good quarterback in Dak Prescott as well as one of the best wide receiver duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Watson and McDuffie go up against Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on a daily basis. However, it will be interesting to see how they do against another good wide receiver pairing. The Rams likely won’t show a ton, but we will get a first look at how the Rams deploy their secondary and how they envision McDuffie, Watson and Quentin Lake fitting together.
While the Cowboys no longer have Micah Parsons, this is still a defense with a strong front. Quinnen Williams can be dominant and Kenny Clark is one of the better nose tackles in the NFL. Rashan Gary brings good speed off of the edge and presents some challenges. Donavan Ezeiruaku was ejected from a Cowboys practice last week and was seen throwing a punch. If the two sides get heated, he’s one to watch.
That group will be a good test for the Rams’ offensive line. Williams and Clark give the Cowboys a strong interior, which should present a challenge for Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila and Kevin Dotson. Gary’s speed will be a good test for Warren McClendon on the right side. In these settings, it’s always interesting to see how the offensive line performs.
Throughout the entirety of training camp, CJ Daniels was someone who consistently impressed . The Rams may not have a true WR3, but if Daniels can continue performing at that level against another defense, the rookie could carve out a role in the offense.
It will be interesting to see how much work the second-team offense gets. If they do get some work, Daniels will likely be part of the rotation. The next couple of weeks will be important for Daniels as he looks to carry what he did during training camp into joint practices and the preseason.
The biggest trade of the offseason was undoubtedly the Rams trading for Myles Garrett. While Garrett spent some of training camp dealing with lower-body soreness, the defense finished training camp on a high note . The Rams have had to focus on Garrett when going up against him in practice. Now the Rams will get to see how he impacts another team’s offensive operation.
Garrett has the ability to take over games, which is why the Rams traded for him. While this isn’t a game, they will still get to see him go up against an offensive line other than their own. Tyler Guyton has shown some positive moments, but Garrett could make things very difficult for the Cowboys on Tuesday.
When Sean McVay was asked how he would deploy the quarterbacks in the preseason , he wasn’t sure if Stetson Bennett would play, but said that Ty Simpson certainly would. If Bennett performs well during the joint practices, it wouldn’t be surprising for McVay to make the decision to rest him through the preseason. Bennett performed better than expected during training camp and the Rams seem to feel comfortable with him as the backup.
With Stafford practicing, it’s unlikely that Simpson gets too much of a look against the Cowboys’ defense. Most of the reps will be split between Matthew Stafford and Bennett. Still, it would be nice to see Simpson get a few reps against another defense, especially as the Rams prepare for the preseason.

title: Rams May Have Let an Intriguing Offensive Lineman Slip Away Last Summer
full_text:
Over the past few seasons, the Los Angeles Rams have had one of the strongest rosters in the NFL . Unlike the 2023 and 2024 seasons when the Rams had several open roster spots, the roster has been very competitive the last two years.
That has resulted in some difficult roster decisions. During roster cutdowns last year, the Rams made two controversial cuts, moving on from linebacker Chris Paul Jr. and offensive lineman Willie Lampkin. Paul Jr. was a fifth-round draft pick and was seen as a potential steal.
Meanwhile, Lampkin was considered one of the top center prospects, but his smaller size led to him going undrafted. He had a great preseason before getting hurt. While the Rams tried to sneak him onto IR during roster cutdowns, the Philadelphia Eagles claimed him off waivers.
Lampkin has been a bit of a camp darling during training camp for the Eagles and is expected to make the team as a guard.
“You've really seen Willie continue to get better,” said Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni. “He has the ability to play on the inside at center or guard, good versatility, smart guy, really athletic. He's been fun to watch at camp. We find ourselves as coaches when we're watching tape, just kind of being like, 'Man, Willie did it again.'”
Nick Sirianni on Willie Lampkin: "You've really seen Willie continue to get better and be more -- and you notice him even more once the pads have come on. He has ability to play on the inside at center or guard, good versatility, smart guy, really athletic. He's been fun to watch…
As the Rams head into 2026, they lack some depth on the interior, especially at center. Justin Dedich is currently managing a hand injury, leaving Keagen Trost as potentially the best guard depth. The Rams do have Beaux Limmer as both center and guard depth. Limmer has experience, but he struggled when he played at guard last year in place of Kevin Dotson. He’s certainly more comfortable at center, but despite playing admirably in 2025, he had rough moments there as well.
It’s hard to get too disappointed about losing an undrafted free agent, but there’s a good chance Lampkin ends up being “one that got away.” Last year during the preseason, Lampkin graded as the fifth-best center and ranked third in run blocking via Pro Football Focus.
Willie Lampkin (5'11" 290) pancaking four Cowboys defenders in week 1 of preseason pic.twitter.com/pkbm7DoV86
Lampkin’s versatility at guard and center is part of what makes him so valuable. It’s also something that the Rams lack in their offensive line depth. Dedich played center in college, but has only played 18 snaps at the position for the Rams, which all came in the 2024 preseason. Limmer hasn’t shown that he can be trusted at both spots.
The Rams did sign Austin Blaske as an undrafted free agent and also have Dylan McMahon, who has spent the last two years on the practice squad. However, Lampkin outplayed McMahon last year and looked set to make the roster before his injury.
One of the biggest questions on the Rams’ roster is their offensive line depth. A lot of that concern is at tackle, where the Rams only have Trost and David Quessenberry. However, the same can be said on the interior, especially at center. That’s a spot that Lampkin certainly could have filled.
Again, it’s hard to criticize the Rams too much for losing Lampkin. His injury played into the decision and the Rams hoped he would clear waivers so they could put him on IR. It’s rare for teams to claim players with an injury designation, which is what the Eagles did. While it didn’t work out for the Rams, Lampkin’s performance is certainly worth monitoring and remains a significant ‘what if’.

title: Ranking Every Rams Rookie Heading Into the Preseason
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have wrapped up training camp and are shifting their focus to the preseason as they continue preparing for Week 1. The preseason will be an important time for the rookies as their snaps will become limited once the sole focus becomes the regular season.
Rookies such as Ty Simpson and Max Klare will be looking to capitalize on reps that they won’t get once the regular season begins. Meanwhile, CJ Daniels will try to impress the coaching staff and hope to carve out a role in the offense. Here’s how the rookies stack up as the Rams head into the preseason.
It’s going to be difficult for Keenan to make much of an impact as a rookie. The Rams have Poona Ford and Ty Davis ahead of him on the depth chart. That doesn’t mention that Aaron Donald could be returning . Keenan should see plenty of work during the preseason.
With Davis Allen out with an injury, some opportunities have opened up for Klare. The preseason will be big for Klare. It’s unlikely that the Rams will play Colby Parkinson, Terrance Ferguson, or Tyler Higbee. Given Allen’s injury, Klare will get plenty of looks early in games. The preseason will be a great chance for Klare to get experience.
Trost is one of the more intriguing players to watch as the Rams head into the preseason. Justin Dedich hurt his hand earlier this offseason, leaving Trost as the ‘sixth man’ on the offensive line. There hasn’t been a lot said about Trost and it hasn’t been clear if the Rams have been playing him at just one position or cross-training him at guard and tackle. Trost should get plenty of work over the next month, and if he plays well, the Rams can feel good about him as depth.
Head coach Sean McVa y provided some clarity on how the Rams will handle the quarterback position during the preseason. While it’s unclear if Bennett will play, Simpson will certainly play. With Simpson, it’s only a matter of whether he plays the entire game like Bennett has done in the past or only part of the game. The preseason will be big for Simpson, as it’s a chance to apply what he’s learned during practices in a live-game setting.
After a strong training camp, fans will undoubtedly be excited to see what wide receiver CJ Daniels does during the preseason . It wouldn’t be surprising to see Daniels be a favorite target for whichever quarterback is on the field. If Daniels carries what he’s done during training camp into the preseason, his case to be in the WR3 rotation will only grow stronger.

title: Rams Add Experienced Special Teams Option to Crowded Cornerback Room
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams added another option at cornerback ahead of the preseason . On Monday, the Rams signed cornerback Zech McPhearson, the team announced. McPhearson was a fourth-round pick by the Philadelphia Eagles in 2021.
Throughout his career, McPhearson has appeared in 33 games. While he was drafted as a cornerback out of Texas Tech, most of his impact has come on special teams. McPhearson has played 683 special teams snaps during his career, totaling 13 special teams tackles.
After being drafted by the Eagles in 2021, he was released during roster cuts in 2024. He spent the 2024 season on the Jacksonville Jaguars’ practice squad and then was released last year after being placed on injured reserve.
McPhearson has typically been a good tackler, which is why he has some value on special teams. Pro Football Focus graded him as the 11th-best tackling cornerback in 2022. If the Rams keep McPhearson on the practice squad, it will be for his value and experience on special teams. The Rams have prioritized special teams value with some of their practice squad candidates, including linebcaker Tomon Fox and others.
As the Rams get ready for their first preseason game on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs, it is likely that McPhearson is simply a camp body. However, given his experience, especially on special teams, he could fight for a spot on the practice squad.
It’s unlikely that McPhearson earns a spot on the Rams’ roster. The Rams have good depth at cornerback behind Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson at the top. Emmanuel Forbes remains the third cornerback with Josh Wallace behind him. Forbes provides good depth on the outside while Wallace has good inside-out versatility.
Heading into training camp, the Rams were looking for depth behind Forbes. However, Cam Lampkin was consistently a standout and should have a strong case to make the final roster.
Despite the emergence of Lampkin during training camp, the Rams don’t have a lot of experienced depth behind him. Alex Johnson and Alzillion Hamilton were previously set to get a majority of the preseason snaps. Johnson spent last season on the Rams’ practice squad while Hamilton was an undrafted free agent signing this year.
Late last week, the Rams placed cornerback Dre Norwood on injured reserve. Norwood heading to IR gave the Rams a need for cornerback depth heading into the preseason. Even if McPhearson is unlikely to make the final roster, the next few weeks are essentially an audition for the practice squad or a chance to put out some good tape for other teams.

title: Rams 53-Man Roster Prediction: One Player to Watch at Each Position During Preseason
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams wrapped up training camp late last week and are now back at Woodland Hills as they prepare for the preseason. While much of the Rams’ evaluation process takes place on the practice field, the preseason will be important for several players fighting for a roster spot. It could be the final opportunity for some to impress the Rams’ coaching staff or put out good tape for other teams around the league.
With the preseason set to begin, here’s an updated 53-man roster prediction, along with one player at each position who needs to perform well.
The three quarterbacks are pretty set in stone on the roster. Bennett is someone who the Rams seem confident in as their backup while Ty Simpson continues to develop. As the Rams head into the preseason, it will be a good opportunity for Simpson to get some live-game reps and apply what he’s learned in practice to the field.
This is my first roster projection with the Rams keeping only three running backs. While that may leave them without some depth at running back, it is something they’ve done in the past. Williams and Corum could give them the confidence to do it. This scenario may be even more likely if Aaron Donald returns. Jarquez Hunter will need to have a good preseason to earn a spot on the roster.
It’s going to be interesting to see whether the Rams keep five or six wide receivers. Given that the offense is moving to more 12 and 13 personnel, there is less need for six wide receivers. Many will be excited to see what CJ Daniels does in the preseason , but Xavier Smith could be on the bubble. Smith needs to show special teams value to make the final roster.
The preseason will be a good opportunity for the Rams to see what they have in Max Klare. This group of five players is pretty set, but with the position being so deep, Klare likely won’t see a lot of playing time once the regular season begins.
It’s worth noting that Justin Dedich is on the NFI list with a hand injury and the team will hope he’s back in time for the regular season. With Dedich out, the Rams should get a good look at rookie third-round pick Keagen Trost. Trost could see time at tackle and guard in the preseason. If he performs well, it should give the Rams some confidence in him as depth.
This group of four at linebacker feels safe, but the Rams have also kept three in the past. Still, it would be hard to see them moving on from a player like Dolac. Elias Neal and Kai-Hill Green should get plenty of work throughout the preseason. At least one of those two will be a candidate for the practice squad.
When Aaron Donald decides to return, it could change some of the roster construction math. Ty Hamilton didn’t have a strong rookie season and the Rams could move on from him. Hamilton will need to have a strong preseason and show some growth, even if it’s unlikely the Rams give up on him after just one year.. Donald returning may force the Rams to make difficult decisions elsewhere on the roster.
The Rams feel pretty good about their edge rushers . Myles Garrett and Byron Young are a great starting duo. Josaiah Stewart has taken a step forward and looks to be a solid rotational piece in year two. With that said, the Rams have added several free agents at the position. They’ll try to get some depth on the practice squad with Tomon Fox, Keir Thomas, or Wesley Bailey. Whoever has the best preseason may earn that spot.
While Cam Lampkin has had a strong training camp, he’ll need to continue that into the preseason. Given how well he’s played, it may be hard to sneak Lampkin onto the practice squad. The Rams will also be watching Alzillion Hamilton and Alex Johnson closely for practice squad depth.
This is one of the deeper safety rooms in the NFL. Tanner Ingle is a key special teams player, but his roster spot isn’t locked up by any means. Ingle could be a final roster cut if Donald does return. Nate Valcarcel played well in the preseason last year and is a player to watch.
The Rams didn’t bring in any competition for Harrison Mevis or Ethan Evans. With that said, it will be important to see some consistency from that duo during the preseason.

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From Rams Training Camp
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams wrapped up training camp late last week and have since returned to Woodland Hills as they prepare for the regular season. Following a practice that wasn’t up to standards on Wednesday, the Rams finished training camp on a strong note . Here are seven takeaways following the conclusion of training camp.
Heading into training camp, a lot of attention was on the backup quarterback battle between Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson. However, it may have been an exaggeration to call this a competition . That’s not to say that Simpson performed poorly or that Bennett blew the coaching staff away with his level of play.
With that said, throughout the entirety of training camp, Bennett was treated as the Rams’ backup quarterback. When Stafford was on rest days, it was Bennett leading the first-team offense. Bennett got all of the reps that would typically be designated for the Rams’ backup quarterback.
“When you look at Stetson, you can see he carries a certain type of aura and swag when he enters the field,” said running back Blake Corum. “He's not scared to cut it loose. He goes out there with utmost confidence and his form is beautiful.”
That says a lot coming from one of Bennett’s teammates and the coaching staff echoed that throughout training camp. Bennett has seemingly taken the next step and given the Rams the confidence to be the backup behind Stafford. That doesn’t hamper Simpson’s development at all and only benefits the quarterback room.
If there was one rookie that many were excited about before training camp, it was wide receiver CJ Daniels. That’s especially the case given the opportunity at wide receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Daniels would have the opportunity to compete with Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith.
When the Rams broke from OTAs, Daniels approached Adams and asked about some things that he could potentially work on.
“We talked about a couple of small things,” said Adams. “I saw a lot of good stuff from him during the offseason program and he came back and did exactly those things.”
Daniels remained attentive during training camp and was praised for how often he asked questions. Adams has taken Daniels under his wing a little bit, which can only benefit the rookie. Unlike players such as Smith and Mumpfield, Daniels offers size and play strength that the Rams don’t have with their wide receiver depth.
Daniels may not have impressed in the same way that Nacua did during his rookie training camp. However, Daniels consistently caught everything thrown his way and built a rapport with Bennett. He’ll be a player to watch during the preseason. The Rams likely won’t have a singular WR3, but Daniels could be in the rotation.
There are two players in the Rams’ offense who could take the next step this season. Two names that have consistently come up are Blake Corum and Terrance Ferguson.
Corum has been working out all offseason to build on last year and continue creating explosive plays. It wouldn’t be surprising to see him carve out an even larger role in the offense in 2026. Williams also noted that Corum looks leaner and more explosive.
“He's just getting more and more comfortable. He's so conscientious,” said McVay. “He does a great job of understanding what we're trying to get done.”
There hasn’t been a lot of buzz around Terrance Ferguson out of training camp from those within the Rams’ building. However, outside media that visited throughout the two weeks noted Ferguson and how he’s looking like a player ready to take that next step.
The Rams will likely rotate their tight ends and won’t have a true top tight end. Still, Ferguson will play a large role in what the Rams want to do.
“I don't expect anyone in particular to come out on top,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “I think those guys push each other and challenge each other and are so versatile that you're just excited to see who ends up coming to life based on what the defense wants to do. We can move those guys all around the field.”
When Albert Breer visited Rams training camp, he noted that Ferguson has had a fantastic offseason . The Athletic’s Nate Atkins has said that the ideal outcome for Ferguson is to lead their tight ends in catches and yards. Ferguson is someone who could see a significantly increased role this season.
Throughout the entirety of training camp, Aaron Donald remained the top storyline for the Rams. After the team traded for Myles Garrett, there has been growing speculation that Donald could return. A specific timeline hasn’t been set, but it was reported by the team that Donald had a second workout at the team facility last week.
“He looked great,” said McVay. “It was really more for him to continue to do the things that I've shared with you guys. He looked great and he’s still continuing to go through his process.”
McVay wasn’t in attendance for Donald’s workout , but defensive line coach Giff Smith, team trainer Reggie Scott, and strength and conditioning coach Justin Loveett were there. Things are continuing to trend upward on the Donald front. Now that the Rams are back at Woodland Hills, a decision could come soon.
Over the offseason, the Rams made three big moves to help improve their defense . They added cornerback Jaylen Watson in free agency before trading for his teammate in Trent McDuffie prior to the draft. Toward the end of OTAs, the Rams traded for Myles Garrett to help improve the pass rush.
During training camp, Garrett was as advertised and helped the defense finish on a strong note as they head to Woodland Hills. Garrett has undoubtedly been the Rams’ best defensive player. With that said, McDuffie and Watson have helped elevate the secondary as well.
Adams and McDuffie have had their share of competitive battles during training camp. McDuffie’s versatility and coverage instincts have been evident.
“I can honestly say I don't know if I'll get a better look than what I get from Trent out there,” said Adams. “I don't like putting big expectations, bulletin board material or any of that but at the end of the day, I can't remember the last time I felt about another corner the way I feel about him.”
Watson has provided stability on the other side as well with his combination of speed and length. That’s something that the secondary lacked last season. This is a defense with pieces that are starting to come together as the Rams get closer to Week 1.
There has been a lot of attention on Ty Simpson’s development. There will be some who will be critical that he hasn’t taken over the backup quarterback role from Bennett. However, those are the same people who remained critical even after Simpson arguably had his best days of practice once the team put on pads.
Simpson’s situation is a case where multiple things can be true. It’s very likely that he is behind Bennett. That’s to be expected in an offense as complicated as McVay’s. However, that doesn’t mean he isn’t more talented than Bennett and isn’t continuing to get more comfortable in the offense. It’s also true that the Rams tend to bring rookies along slowly.
A huge positive with Simpson has been his willingness and proactiveness to learn . Simpson has been praised for asking all of the right questions to quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone and to Matthew Stafford. He’s been a sponge on the practice field and in the quarterback room, which is exactly what you would want to see.
“He has come in [and] figured out the areas that he's got to improve each day,” said Scheelhaase. “Ty has done a really good job learning from each and every day. Whether he's out there taking the rep, whether he's absorbing it, he's asking all the right questions in the meeting room so you appreciate that.”
The Rams are playing the long game with Simpson and where he ends up on the depth chart going into the preseason or the regular season doesn’t matter. Simpson is being brought along at his own pace and the Rams are sticking to that process.

title: Rams Defense Continues to Make Noise After Strong Finish to Training Camp
full_text:
Any team coached by Sean McVay is going to receive plenty of praise for its offense. However, over the last week, it has been the Los Angeles Rams’ defense that has made noise in practices. The defense finished training camp on a strong note and then, as the team returned to Woodland Hills on Saturday, it was once again the defense that won practice.
According to Greg Beacham of the Associated Press, the defense won the final two days of training camp at Loyola Marymount University.
Rams training camp Practice 10: Defense won the past 2 days at LMU overall; Shaun Dolac had a pick-6 off Stetson; Emmanuel Forbes & Quentin Lake came up big in coverage; Cam Lampkin stood out again in a strong camp; Lot of varied work for the TEs today, including Max Klare.
The defense carried that momentum as the team returned to Woodland Hills to start preparing for the regular season. On Saturday, an interception from safety Kam Kinchens highlighted the afternoon.
On Wednesday, the Rams didn’t have a strong day offensively, leaving McVay upset at the overall level and poor execution. However, that was not the case on Saturday, despite the turnovers on offense.
“A lot of those plays were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution,” said McVay. “The plays that happened today, there were a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively…I thought the defense was great today and it wasn't as good for the offense, but it was more of great defense than it was bad offense.”
It hasn’t hurt that the defense has gotten Myles Garrett back in the mix after missing three practices toward the end of training camp. As noted by The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue, Garrett has the ability to take over a practice and had a pick-six off of a screen pass on Saturday.
Out at Rams practice today. They might have to start giving that Myles Garrett guy more “veteran rest” days. Can totally take over a practice drive. Including a pick six right off a screen and high-step into the end zone late in the session.😳
While the Rams’ defense wasn’t necessarily a weakness last year, the front office made a point to improve several key areas that let the team down towards the end of the season. The Rams improved the secondary with players like Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. They also took advantage of the opportunity to acquire Myles Garrett in a trade with the Browns.
Garrett was as advertised during training camp. However, McDuffie has provided a boost to the secondary. The Athletic’s Nate Atkins recently wrote that McDuffie has been the single biggest boost to the roster. Atkins noted McDuffie’s versatility, coverage instincts, and communication.
When it comes to the Rams, it’s going to be the offense that carries the roster. That’s where the team’s primary focus is with players like Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and Davante Adams. With that said, the talent on the defensive side of the ball finally matches the talent on offense. The Rams will win games because of the offense, but it’s going to be their defense that becomes the backbone of the roster and reason the Rams win the Super Bowl.
As the Rams break from training camp and head back to Woodland Hills, the defense has started to find its stride. The players that the Rams are counting on to step up, such as Garrett and McDuffie, are doing just that. If that continues into the regular season, the Rams will very likely match the high expectations that have been set for them.

title: Why I’m Buying Early Hype Around Raiders' Tonka Hemingway
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders kick off their preseason Thursday night when they host the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium. The Cardinals are coming off a walk-off defeat to the Carolina Panthers in the NFL Hall of Fame Game, 33-30, and the Raiders hope to continue Arizona's preseason misfortunes this week.
Training camp and the coming weeks of the preseason will open opportunities for players to find their place on the roster or force head coach Klint Kubiak , his staff, and general manager John Spytek to make difficult roster cutdown decisions.
One player who has stood out so far in camp is Raiders defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway , a former fourth-round draft selection from last spring who emerged as a quality depth player late in the season. Hemingway flashed at times in 2025, but was too inconsistent, with some discouraging moments.
However, all the former South Carolina standout has done this summer is prove he could be a key defender within the defensive front rotation. If there is one player I am buying the early hype on ahead of Thursday night, Hemingway is that player.
I spent some time watching Hemingway's game film for this piece, and one of the things that stood out most to me was his effort down to down. Everything he did last year, right or wrong, was at 100 percent effort, with his motor far from in question for anybody. I enjoyed his versatility in alignment, whether he was a 5-tech, 3-tech, or playing from the 1- or 2i-tech.
Hemingway has been showing up in camp, which is a terrific sign for the Raiders' defensive line as a whole. Thomas Booker IV, Jonah Laulu, and Adam Butler are fortified in their place in the interior odd front; Hemingway is making his presence known throughout camp and generating chaos in the process.
I don't expect Hemingway to be a starter right away. Still, his pass-rush arsenal is impressive to watch, and he knows how to make his presence known in the backfield at all times. That's valuable for a defense, and Hemingway has done enough to show Leonard and Kubiak that this is his time to be an impact defender.
There are many young and hungry defensive players ready to contribute. Hemingway is one of those young players. This gives the front seven depth and reliability this season, based on what we have seen at training camp. If this goes on, Las Vegas could have a very productive defensive front this fall.

title: Updated Raiders Depth Chart Ahead of First Preseason Game
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have completed training camp and released their most recent depth chart. On Thursday, the Raiders will face the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium. It will be the first time the Raiders take the field under head coach Klint Kubiak.
The Raiders took several strides in training camp. The changes implemented and the hard work put in during positional battles in camp have made an early impact on the depth chart. Las Vegas' depth chart has a few changes from what was expected entering training camp.
Las Vegas aims to turn things around after several disappointing seasons that led to the firing of multiple head coaches, most recently Pete Carroll. Kubiak knows the work to rebuild the Raiders is just beginning. He recently gave insight into how the development process has gone so far.
“Well, I think I would say, a compliment our players, is that it's not so much about listening to me; it's about what it takes to win. We want to win. Our players want to win. And the things that it takes to win is for us to be together and be connected and operate as one unit,” Kubiak said.
“So, I think it just shows the maturity of our group, knowing we're going to point things out. But at the end of the day, they decide what kind of team that they want to be, and thus far they've showed us they're a mature group that they want to go win games the right way."
Las Vegas needs as much physical action against other teams as possible, while minimizing injuries, to further solidify its depth chart. While many positions on the depth chart have been settled, several more remain and will need the full slate of preseason practices and games to confirm.

title: Raiders Training Camp Report 15:  What Happened At Allegiant
full_text:
LAS VEGAS, Nev.—Today marks day 15 of the Las Vegas Raiders' full-team training camp, and tonight at here at Allegiant Stadium they just conducted their 11th practice of camp in front of their faithful fan base.
This practice was not as feisty as the others, and it shouldn’t have been.
Klint Kubiak has multiple new players, so they got to get a feel for them before their first actual game here on Thursday versus the Arizona Cardinals, but it was also a time to celebrate the historic Raider Nation.
For this fan base, it isn’t just a rooting interest; this is their life.
Raider Icon Matt Millen once described the Raider Nation to me as, “31 teams in the NFL the fans think they are part of the team, but with the Raiders, they are the only team that the team thinks the fans are part of them.”
That was the purpose of this practice.
Three things stood out most to me.  Not it wasn’t anything schematic, as opposing teams could, and probably were, in the house.  What did stand out was significant.
2. Kubiak’s desire fulfilled. Earlier today at the team headquarters, Kubiak made his expectations for tonight very clear. “Tonight's really important. Really excited about going and being in front of our fans, being on the grass that we're going to play on. Coaches communicating with the headsets; really important for the whole operation. Obviously, it's my first game in there. Played a few games on the other side of the stadium, but it'll be really important for players and coaches to get familiar with our surroundings so that we can play our best football on Thursday night."
Several of the rookies from smaller schools could be seen looking fondly at their surroundings.  Fans need to remember these are 21- 23-year-old kids who have dreamed of the NFL all of their lives.  For them, it wasn’t a practice; it was a fulfillment of a dream.
With the jitters out of the way, the new veterans learned the locker room and stadium, where to go, and this team is ready for Thursday.
3. Fernando Mendoza mania is on full display. Mendoza jerseys and signs were seen all over the stadium welcoming their new hero to the Raider Nation. The number one overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, who had NFL executives drooling, thrilled the crowd with whatever he did. This fan base understands the weight on the current Heisman Trophy winner and National Champion’s shoulders, and they already love him.

title: Where Raiders Can Still Improve Amid Roster Rebuild
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders project to be one of the most improved teams in the NFL in 2026, even if that doesn't lead to overall team success right away. The talent they've brought in is undeniable, but it's fair to assume there will be some growing pains for a team with a new head coach and quarterback.
Klint Kubiak has his work cut out for him if he wants to turn this franchise around, but his first offseason as a head coach has gone about as well as anyone could've hoped for. Looking beyond 2026, what are some things this team still needs before it can be a contender year in and year out?
By definition, Tre Tucker is the WR1 on this team. However, when you compare him to other teams' first options, he's in the bottom tier across the league. There is a caveat to this: Brock Bowers will be this team's top pass-catcher, but eventually, the Raiders have to get someone in that receiving room to alleviate some pressure off of him.
They've drafted plenty of young talent and are hoping one of them takes a leap this season, but if they don't, I can see this front office trading for a wide receiver . This team should optimize the time Fernando Mendoza is on a rookie contract, so they need a dominant wide receiver sooner rather than later.
The Raiders have Maxx Crosby , yet it never feels like their defensive line can generate enough pressure. Their linebacker and defensive back rooms have improved to the point where there's less pressure on Crosby to carry their defense now, but he's still their lone star on that side of the field.
The hope is that they can get another star to play alongside him, but all their attempts to do so have failed. I like their addition of Kwity Paye, and if they can continue to add talent to that defensive line, even if it isn't a player of Crosby's caliber, the line should get to a point where it's good enough. I think they can start by getting a better nose tackle to anchor their pass-rush.
The Raiders have made significant strides in improving their offensive line, namely signing Tyler Linderbaum to a massive deal. And yet, I still feel as if there are improvements to be made. I think the rookies they drafted should be able to take the starting jobs from the veterans on their offensive line, but relying on those late-draft-pick rookies to develop into starting-caliber offensive linemen for multiple seasons is a gamble.

title: Establishing Keyron Crawford's Role in Raiders' Rebuild
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders used free agency and the NFL Draft to quickly address several of their most pressing roster issues on both sides of the ball. Those issues went beyond just the starters on offense and defense, as Las Vegas has lacked depth across the board for many seasons now.
Raiders general manager John Spytek added several rookies who will begin the 2026 season in a reserve role, but will likely have a chance to make an impact. Rookie edge rusher Keyron Crawford is one of those players, as he is undeniably talented, but also needs further development.
Las Vegas has long had one of its defensive end positions solidified by veteran Maxx Crosby. However, they have failed to find many consistent options at their other defensive end position, let alone at the reserve edge-rushing positions. They hope Crawford helps eliminate that need.
Crawford's addition is, on paper, a quiet but critical part of the Raiders' defensive rebuild. So much so that the Raiders let go of veteran defensive end Charles Snowden shortly after drafting Crawford, even though Snowden played significant minutes in recent seasons.
Like most rookies finishing up their first training camp in the league, Crawford still has a ways to go to be fully prepared physically and mentally for his rookie season. Raiders defensive line coach Travis Smith recently shared his thoughts on where Crawford's development stands.
"He's done a great job. He came in, he's played in a couple different schools. Obviously, he came in right now completely raw, just like any of the other rookies. There's some things we moved him around, like we talked about the flexibility of multiple positions early,” Smith said following training camp.
“We're kind of finalizing, but settling him in his one position along with the other guys, too. So, he's been phenomenal. He's one of those guys that's very hungry, eager to learn, stays after, is early, asking questions, shooting late night texts, sending videos off the iPad. So, he's another guy that, within the whole group, is a very, very, very fun and competitive group to coach because all they do is compete every day. It doesn't matter the drill."
Crawford still has a lot to prove, as Las Vegas has essentially figured out its starters along the defensive line. The rookie has also been a little banged up in training camp. As the preseason and regular season ramp up, Las Vegas needs Crawford to stay healthy and produce.
Smith elaborated on Crawford's role entering the season.
"For sure, he's on the edge right now. He's one of our edge defenders. He plays both sides. He's going to be setting the edge with a point of attack,” Smith said.
“He's going to be an edge rusher when we get into pass rush situations. He's competing in that group with Maxx [Crosby], Kwity [Paye], Malcolm [Koonce], Cian [Slone], Patrick [Johnson], Rasta [Jahfari Harvey], and B-Jack [Brennan Jackson], and he's doing a really good job."
Moving forward, the Raiders' defense is following the lead of Smith and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. This should mean vast changes for a Raiders defense that has lacked talent in recent seasons, but received an additional wave of talent throughout the offseason.
As the Raiders transition to a 3-4 defense, they will continue to search for edge rushers who are fast and physical, like Crawford has the potential to be. Smith noted that despite the change in Las Vegas' base defense, Crawford and the rest of the edge rushers' jobs are basically the same.
“When it comes down to it, it's really not that different. They're setting edges at the point of attack, they might have a little stunt footwork, hit some line movement. Their CBR chase players on the backside of runs, and then they have to win one-on-ones and make sure they're disciplined in their rush lanes when they're rushing,” Smith said.
“So, it's all about how we make the complex simple as a staff and as coaches, but what the bottom line comes down to is this position is hard, and how hard the man plays, which will make up for any other little thing or complexity of a system that we give them."

title: Raiders Rookie Report: Who Is Rising (and Falling) on Depth Chart?
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders added several talented players to their roster this offseason. Although they were productive in free agency, they were even more productive in the NFL Draft, adding 10 players who each have a chance to make an impact during training camp, and potentially beyond.
Las Vegas' training camp practices have helped Klint Kubiak's coaching staff get a better idea of what the players can do. Of the 10 players the Raiders drafted this offseason, some are rising up the depth chart, and some are falling.
Some of the 10 players Las Vegas added via the draft are neither rising nor falling, but doing exactly what they were expected to do, even in a reserve role, such as Trey Zuhn and Dalton Johnson. Below is a list of players rising and falling.
Las Vegas' need for competent cornerbacks left the door wide open for any cornerbacks on the roster looking to secure a roster spot. The Raiders' group of cornerbacks has long been an issue, as they have spent most of the past few seasons searching for multiple cornerbacks.
The Raiders have drafted three cornerbacks in the past two seasons and added two more via free agency. Rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses has begun climbing up the depth chart in training camp, as he has shown he may have some of the best cover skills on the team aside from Eric Stokes.
It will take the Raiders several more offseasons to fully rebuild their CB group, but it is unquestionably one of their top goals. With Stokes and Taron Johnson leading the way, Las Vegas now needs other cornerbacks on the roster to step up.
The Raiders play in a division with some of the best quarterbacks in the league; they must prepare their cornerbacks as if this is the case. So far, Masses looks to be part of the answer moving forward. Defensive backs coach Joe Woods recently shared his thoughts on Masses' development.
"He can cover. I'm all about getting on the body just in terms of being tight whenever we play press. He has that skill set,” Woods said following training camp.
“There’s some guys in the past that he reminds me of in terms of quickness, like Denzel Ward had that extreme lateral quickness where he can get on the body. He has that same type of trait. Not saying he's Denzel, he's got a long way to go, but there are some really good things that he's doing."
Cleveland has not done anything particularly wrong; however, he has not stood out much either, and that is part of the problem. Cleveland also plays along the interior defensive line, which is arguably the position group Las Vegas has the most talent at; this is also a factor in his fall.
Cleveland was a seventh-round draft pick. So, it is not a bad thing for him to be "falling" down the depth chart. If anything, it is to be expected, but there are things the rookie can do to trend upward instead of downward. It will be up to him to figure those things out and execute.
Along with Masses, Benson has seemingly taken a positive step forward with each training camp practice. Also, along with Masses, Benson plays a position the Raiders will handle by committee, opening the door to any player who can prove their value at the position.
Benson has quickly become one of those players, as Las Vegas continues to figure things out at wide receiver. He will also provide value to the Raiders on special teams, as his speed makes him a threat whenever he gets his hands on the ball. Raiders quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan explained.
"Malik has done a great job. We're happy he's here. I know Fernando's happy he's here. I think when you have all of the young guys that come together, there's a benefit obviously to that. Just learning the subtle nuances and the body language," Sullivan said following training camp.
“If that can help the anticipation, then we're able to get that ball out and have that timing that we talked about, which everybody likes. Certainly, the o-line coach likes it. And not taking sacks or making bad decisions, so that's definitely a benefit for us."
