title: Max Brosmer Is a Surprise Winner From Kyler Murray Earning Vikings QB1 Job
full_text:
The Vikings' training camp isn't close to being over , but one position battle is. Hours before Tuesday's practice, ESPN' s Adam Schefter reported that the Vikings have ended their quarterback competition , naming Kyler Murray as the QB1 with less than a month to go before the regular season. As such, J.J. McCarthy's bid to be the No. 1 sign-caller is over.
ESPN sources: the Vikings have named Kyler Murray their starting QB. pic.twitter.com/VBE4azfGoF
Despite having yet to play a game in a Vikings jersey, Murray's strong training camp performance made it abundantly clear that the QB1 job was his to lose early in training camp. More often than not, each passing practice solidified that fact, leaving McCarthy with an uncertain future in Eagan.
Of course, Murray being named the starting signal-caller doesn't only impact McCarthy. The Vikings' decision also means that Max Brosmer's outlook with the franchise could look much different than it did at the start of training camp.
Vikings fans had high hopes for Brosmer after joining the Vikings as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Minnesota last offseason. He showed promise with 364 passing yards and two touchdowns (with an interception) in three preseason appearances, leaving fans with hope that he and McCarthy could be a solid QB tandem for years to come.
Most of that goodwill was stripped away when Brosmer was forced to make his first NFL start against the Seahawks in Week 13.
Although there's nothing wrong with losing to the eventual Super Bowl Champions, Brosmer did little to provide optimism , going 19-for-30 (63.3%) in the pocket with 126 yards and four interceptions in the 26-0 loss. He looked more poised in the three appearances that followed (including a start), but it wasn't enough to avoid being a huge question mark this offseason.
Fast forward to Murray being named the Vikings' starting arm, and the conversation will shift to who will be the QB2 and QB3.
Given that McCarthy has left much to be desired (both in his early career and this offseason), head coach Kevin O'Connell might be more comfortable giving the backup job to Carson Wentz, who's a former NFL MVP finalist with 99 career starts and a Super Bowl ring under his belt. It's also worth mentioning that Wentz has looked solid in training camp, with Vikings OnSI' s Jason Harmon remarking about his mechanics last week .
In a world where Wentz is named the QB2, it's hard to imagine McCarthy sticking around as the third-stringer—whether he wants to or not. Having him in the QB3 spot would be a distraction, and the Vikings would be better off cutting their losses and trading him elsewhere, with a potential deal leading to dead cap hits of $3.1 million in 2026 and 2027 , as well as $2.7 million in savings this year, per Spotrac .
Besides, having a former first-round pick as the QB3 isn't exactly great for optics.
Having Wentz as the backup quarterback with Brosmer learning under him as the QB3 isn't a bad idea at all. Yes, the former Golden Gopher left much to be desired in Year 1; however, Brosmer is only 25 years old and could look more at home with another season in O'Connell's scheme. If it works out, great. If not, it wouldn't be a huge loss, as the majority of his cap hit—just over $1 million—will come off the books with a cut at any point.
Other than Murray being at the top, the QB room's pecking order is still malleable. Brosmer's outlook might not be glistening at the moment, but it's brighter than it was as recently as a few days ago. If he can string together some strong practices, as well as capitalize on any preseason opportunities he gets, there's a good chance that Brosmer could be the Vikings' QB3 once Week 1 of the regular season arrives.

title: Chuck Demmings Is Stealing the Show: What It Means for His Vikings Outlook
full_text:
Entering the 2026 NFL season, the Vikings' cornerback depth chart seems concerning.
While returning starters Byron Murphy Jr. and Isaiah Rodgers are solid players, there is a lack of depth behind them. Former Steelers defensive back James Pierre was signed this offseason, and Dwight McGlothern flashed potential, but there was a desperate need for another cornerback to step up and prove they can be a contributor this season.
That's why Chuck Demmings's standout performance at training camp shouldn't be ignored.
The Vikings surprised a lot of people when they selected the Stephen F. Austin defensive back in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The small-school cornerback wasn't a player on the radar of many fans, but he should have been, as Demmings continues to make waves early in training camp .
So far, Demmings has been the star of the Vikings' training camp. The 6-foot-1, 193-pound defensive back has looked like a player who should have been selected several rounds earlier during the draft.
Reports of him matching up well against Vikings' star wide receiver Justin Jefferson and having a strong motor to finish plays have earned him a massive amount of praise for a rookie who earned a 74 production score and an 81 athletic score from Next Gen Stats on NFL.com.
Demmings's ascension in training camp should only continue to cement him as one of the cornerbacks who will make the 53-man roster for the Purple and Gold this year. Not only that, but he is well on his way to earning a considerable amount of playing time in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit.
Assuming Demmings can keep his momentum going through the remainder of practices and the preseason ( which begins Saturday vs. the Giants ), he will likely be in line to be the top backup for Pierre and Rodgers, perhaps even gaining a rotational or situational role from Flores.
Although he is only 23 years old and didn't play against elite competition at the college level, Demmings is the kind of player who would have no fear going up against some of the best receivers the NFL has to offer. He could showcase that if he sees some of Giants WR1 Malik Nabers this weekend.
Not only does he have great size and strength for his position, but his wingspan measured nearly 6-foot-6 at the NFL Scouting Combine , and he ran the 40-yard dash in 4.41 seconds. Those traits will help him go one-on-one with any opposing pass-catcher and do so effectively.
The path is clear for Demmings to continue impressing the Vikings. At this point, it wouldn't be shocking if he started a few games this season if the coaching staff calls his number. With his talent and the skills he has showcased so far, it isn't far-fetched to think that he could be a player to watch climb the ranks into a permanent starting role in the future.

title: Demond Claiborne Could Have a Bigger Vikings Role Than Expected as His Electric Camp Continues
full_text:
The Vikings used pick No. 198 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft to select Wake Forest running back Demond Claiborne. They selected the speedy rusher to improve the team's rushing attack, which struggled last year, averaging 108.3 rushing yards per game (23rd).
Veteran running back Aaron Jones agreed to a substantial pay cut to stay with the Vikings this season. Meanwhile, his backup, Jordan Mason, is back after leading the team in rushing yards (758) and rushing touchdowns (6). While that duo handled a majority of Minnesota's ground attack, three other halfbacks accounted for 155 offensive snaps.
With Ty Chandler on the Saints roster and Cam Akers a free agent, there are some snaps available to be distributed. Training camp is a great place to earn those opportunities , and Claiborne is making a great case to take those snaps.
When surrounded by such high levels of talent, it can be difficult to get noticed. That hasn't been a problem for Claiborne, who has been turning heads at training camp .
Recently, Jones spoke with Ben Goessling of the Minneapolis Star Tribune and had positive things to say about the young running back.
"(Demond is) a special back in this league. I get to mentor him up and show him the way," Jones said. "I told him I want him to be successful; I want to see him go on and get paid and those kinds of things. He’ll be playing in this league as long as he wants to, but just got to lock in here and take care of the business.”
Jones has been around some special players during his time in the NFL. Claiborne's 4.37-second 40-yard dash time at the NFL Scouting Combine was impressive, but seeing him in training camp only hammered home how fast he truly is .
Tai Felton gunner rep with Demond Claiborne returning the punt. pic.twitter.com/dsfsRHowhY
Excitement about Claiborne's speed has many fans hoping he can make the Vikings' 53-man roster . His lightning footwork will be a great complement to Jones's complete game and Mason's physical presence.
If the Purple and Gold only go with three running backs, they will have a tough time choosing between returning rusher Zavier Scott and the dynamic rookie. Scott has experience on his side, entering his third season with the Vikings after rushing for 114 yards on 32 carries in 16 games last year.
However, if Claiborne continues to have a great training camp, he could force head coach Kevin O'Connell's hand. The Vikings would have no choice but to keep him as the RB3 and cut Scott, whose entire $1,005,000 salary would come off the books , according to Spotrac .
Preseason is right around the corner , and it will be another opportunity for Claiborne to showcase his skills that have him being called "special" before he even takes a regular-season snap. His first test comes Saturday afternoon against the Giants, who allowed the second-most rushing yards per game last season (145.3).
If the 22-year-old speedster can do that, he will all but ensure himself a Vikings roster spot and a key offensive role during the 2026 NFL season.

title: Time's Up for Murray and McCarthy: O'Connell Must Decide Starting Quarterback
full_text:
No quarterbacks were harmed in the execution of this quarterback competition.
When Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell talked at the podium before the team’s night practice on Sunday, he noted that Kyler Murray and JJ McCarthy have both gotten a 50-50 share of the total reps throughout training camp. While local rep-counting experts have tracked Murray with nearly three times as many reps with the first team in the midst of the quarterback competition, neither QB can say that they haven’t gotten their chance to throw as many footballs as possible to state their case.
Murray has put together several days when he and Justin Jefferson have connected repeatedly. He has also had multiple practices that look like he hasn’t gotten a hold of the offense yet and the success rate of his reps is mediocre.
McCarthy started out slowly but has increased his aggressiveness in recent days and had a number of high-quality throws downfield. He has also shown the same propensity for inconsistency that caused the Vikings to seek a veteran starting quarterback this offseason.
Neither QB can claim that they have been wronged by the head coach’s plan.
It seems that O’Connell wanted to push Murray as hard as possible to get him to lock into the offense and motivate him. With McCarthy, it appears O’Connell wanted to get a true evaluation of how far he has developed over the last year, give him every opportunity to prove that he can still become the team’s starting QB and develop him along the way.
Now as the Vikings prepare for the start of the preseason, there are two directions that they can go. The first is to name Murray the starter and lean completely into him with the rest of the reps throughout training camp. The other is to truly commit to the competition and begin giving McCarthy an equal share of reps with Jefferson, Jordan Addison, TJ Hockenson and the first-team offensive line.
The argument for going in the first direction would be that Murray needs every single rep from here on if he’s going to be totally comfortable heading into Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. Standing off to the side and watching McCarthy isn’t helping him build a deeper knowledge of an offense that was described by Jefferson as “complicated.” If you were hoping that a home-run hitter was going to blast as many dingers as possible, you wouldn’t have them watch someone else take hacks in the batting cage.
If Murray was shredding the defense every day, then it would be fine to let things go on as long as the Vikings want. But the fact that he has seemed comfortable some days and uncomfortable on other days means that if he’s going to be the QB1, he needs as much work as humanly possible in the month leading up to a vital game against the Green Bay Packers.
On the other hand, if O’Connell isn’t sold at all on what he’s seen from Murray, then it’s time to give McCarthy every opportunity to succeed in the QB competition.
We have heard all the excuses and explanations for McCarthy’s struggles , and those don’t change the facts about how he played. But it’s true that he’s a young quarterback and only played 10 games before this year. That shouldn’t end any and all chance that he can still become an NFL starter.
If the coaches believe that he’s been locking in lately and there’s a chance he’s turning a big corner, then he needs to play with the most important player in the franchise. He had a big throw to Jefferson in the night practice , but it was one of only a handful of targets between the two during this entire camp.
The Vikings probably won’t utilize the preseason games for the QB competition based on O’Connell’s track record. He hasn’t wanted the first-team offensive players like Jefferson and the O-line to play more than one series in order to avoid any senseless injuries. So the marquee event would be the Vikings’ joint practices with the Baltimore Ravens that take place on August 19th and 20th.
If it reaches that point, then we will be sure that McCarthy has kept up with Murray throughout the summer and that there’s still a chance of him starting.
The question is whether O’Connell wants to take it that far.
Either way, the Vikings’ head coach has given each QB plenty of opportunity to state their case. Now they have reached a fork in the road.
It’s time to either let Murray get down to the business of being QB1 or let McCarthy truly have his say. Staying the path that this QB competition has gone on is not particularly good for anybody.

title: Vikings 53-Man Roster Projections 1.0: Whose Outlook Is Bright Before Preseason Opener?
full_text:
EAGAN, MN — It’s been roughly two weeks since the Vikings kicked off their 2026 training camp , and some players are starting to make their presence felt consistently. The quarterback conversation never ends, rookie defenders keep making plays, and weapons in the passing game continue to impress.
After attending the team’s last seven practices, several names are making a surprising push to stick around once training camp ends. The Vikings will get their first taste of preseason action when the team heads east to face the Giants this Saturday, Aug. 15,  giving us our best look at the current roster in a competitive environment. We will finally get to see what head coach Kevin O’Connell and defensive coordinator Brian Flores can get from this roster when they’re not battling one another at TCO Performance Center.
But why not have some fun and make some very early predictions in the meantime?
With 10 practices in the rearview mirror, here is how I would see the 53-man roster shaking out based strictly on what I've seen so far .
If you asked me today who starts for the Vikings at QB in week one, it's Kyler Murray. Even though neither QB has truly proven to be consistent, his highs have been higher than what J.J. McCarthy has shown, and this gives him the edge for now.
There is a very real chance the Vikings trade the “loser” of their QB competition, but until that plays out, Max Brosmer appears to be the odd man in a room likely to carry three QBs into the season, but would be QB3 if either Murray or McCarthy are traded. The team could likely try to place him on the practice squad, but another QB-needy team may take a flyer on the former Gopher.
The team will have an interesting decision in the running back and wide receiver rooms. If they carry only three RBs, they’ll have flexibility to carry an additional pass catcher. Based on what we’ve seen from camp so far, I have Zavier Scott and recent addition Jordan Mims being cut. We know KOC loves his passing offense to be the focus, and the WR room is just too impressive so far to ignore.
Unfortunately, the RB room will likely be the one making the additional space. Demond Claiborne has started to come on, showcasing his explosive speed that could be a true threat whenever he hits the field. Scott will likely end up on the practice squad, and given the up-and-down health of the room, may still get called up during the season.
Max Bredeson has more than secured his job in camp so far. C.J. Ham's heir apparent has already impressed with his physicality and blocking.
Carrying six wideouts may seem excessive for some teams, but the Vikings' pass-heavy offense thrives with a plethora of options at its disposal. So far through camp, this room is making too much noise to ignore.
Tai Felton has been one of the more impressive stories of camp; Myles Price is proving to be more than just a return man  and Dontae Fleming has been the image of consistency every day. Jeshaun Jones has been impressive as well, and has a real chance to battle Fleming for spot six .
Early offseason star and Georgia UDFA Dillon Bell has been disappointing so far and will need a wild few weeks to make a push. I’d expect both to be practice squad additions.
T.J. Hockenson enters 2026 under a watchful eye. His production has been less than many would hope, and the team may need to look at younger options in the future. Ben Yurosek and Bryson Nesbit have had their moments so far in camp, but Gavin Bartholomew has been the most impressive TE in the entire room so far.
#Vikings QB JJ McCarthy throwing to Gavin Bartholomew, who is having a nice camp so far. (Via Vikings IG) pic.twitter.com/xg9FMCmpL3
Bartholomew has had multiple impressive catches and has slotted in seamlessly to the offense.  A feat made even more impressive when you consider he missed the entirety of his rookie season in 2025. Maybe he could prove to be the long-term answer at the tight end spot.
The Vikings experienced the pain of a rotating offensive line in 2025 and hope that their unit can stay healthy and effective in 2026. Blake Brandel moved to center last season for the first time in his career and appears to be the favorite for the starting job this season.
The team still has questions at center, but hopefully Brandel or Michael Jurgens can prove to be the answer during preseason games. If not, I can see general manager Nolan Teasley finding an option on the market or via trade.
Brian Flores is already showing hints of the different variations he hopes to utilize along the defensive front, but these five big men are the ones who have stuck out to me most. Veteran Isaiahh Loudermilk has a strong case to push someone else out from a different position group to make the team based simply on size and experience. His production in game action will go a long way towards swaying that possibility.
This group is truly the key to the Flores scheme. Depending on how the front lines up, these guys can end up doing radically different things. Big worry here? Injuries to one of your starting OLBs. I see this group as the No. 1 option for a free-agent addition before the season begins.
Jake Golday may also rotate in and out throughout the preseason, allowing him to provide potential value as a rotational piece here once the season kicks off.
This has been a fun room to follow through the starting phases of camp. When Jamal Adams was first signed, it seemed that Ivan Pace's days in the room may be numbered . Oh, how things can change. Pace has been impactful so far through camp, and with Adams changing his number to play safety and LB, I feel much more confident about Pace's job security than I did before.
Golday is going to be the most interesting defender to keep an eye on this season, especially since he's already rotating in with the pass-rushers.
Flores has already shown a number of variations for his CB group, including James Pierre and Charles Demmings both taking first-team reps defending the slot.  Demmings has stolen the show throughout camp . His physicality is a perfect fit for what Brian Flores has wanted from his corner room.
Pretty boring practice all in all, both QBs looked fine at times, both had iffy moments. McCarthy missing his targets with no defense early is probably the most standout moment. Charles Demmings continues to be the star of camp.
McGlothern is a bubble guy who's yet to truly stand out, but carrying only four at the position would worry me. Zemaiah Vaughn needs a huge preseason to make his way in.
This group is going to be fascinating to watch take shape.
Joshua Metellus has had his best production as a free-roaming utility defender; Harrison Smith may or may not return at some point; Jamal Adams is practicing at safety but is listed at LB; Tavierre Thomas is here for his special-teams play, which makes his role the clearest of all.  Rookie Jakobe Thomas is a heat-seeking missile who needs continued development on the parts of his game that aren't just knocking guys to the ground.
Will Reichard is quickly ascending as a top kicker in the NFL, a far cry from the misery Vikings fans are used to at the position. Andrew DePaola is entering his seventh year with the team and is one of the more dependable players at his position. The real competition here is at punter, where Johnny Hekker looks to have the edge.
Rookie punter Brett Thorson is likely to be retained on the NFL's International Pathway Program, allowing him to develop for the franchise and eventually step into the role.

title: Vikings Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times and TV Channels
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings will take one step closer to finalizing their 53-man roster now that their 2026 preseason is set to begin. While training camp is a great tool to help players stand out to head coach Kevin O'Connell & Co., the upcoming exhibition slate will give the Vikings a better idea of where everyone on the roster —especially those on the bubble—stands ahead of the 53-man cutdown date on Sunday, Aug. 30.
With the action picking up this weekend, here's everything that Vikings fans need to know about the preseason, including the dates, start times, and TV channels for all three exhibition games.
The Vikings will take to the road to face the Giants in this summer's preseason opener. The two NFC franchises collided in Week 16 last season, resulting in a tightly fought 16-13 win for Minnesota, capped by Will Reichard's 30-yard game-winning field goal with just over four minutes remaining.
This matchup is exciting solely for the fact that it will be fans' first chance to see the new faces—rookies and veterans alike—in action. The Giants will also be hungry to make a statement after three consecutive seasons without a postseason appearance, meaning they should give the Vikings a solid enough test to remind them that meaningful football is back.
Preseason games are intriguing, but that's more so after a week of joint practices. That's exactly what the Vikings will experience in the middle of August, when they go head-to-head with the Ravens in practice before hosting Lamar Jackson's squad at U.S. Bank Stadium a few days later.
History doesn't always predict the future, but it's safe to say that the Vikings would like to buck a recent trend vs. the Ravens, even if it's only the preseason. Minnesota is 3-5 in eight all-time clashes with Baltimore, which includes losing 27-19 in Week 10 of the 2025 season. That loss started a four-game skid for the Vikings, effectively ending their postseason dreams.
We'll also have a better idea about the Vikings' 53-man roster projections at this point, meaning fans can expect to see more backups here than they did against the Giants.
The preseason excitement will conclude in the Mile High City when the Vikings pay a visit to the Broncos just two days before the 53-man roster deadline. It's going to be the final opportunity for bubble players to prove themselves , whether that means snagging an every-week job or a spot on the practice squad.
Either way, the pressure will be at an all-time high for everyone involved.
Coming off a 14-win campaign and an AFC Championship Game appearance last season, the Broncos will be a challenging opponent to close out the summer.
The Vikings haven't played the defending AFC West champions since a Week 11 Sunday Night Football matchup in 2023, which saw the Broncos notch a one-point win (21-20) after wideout Courtland Sutton scored a touchdown with just over a minute remaining in the game.
A lot has changed for both sides since that late-November collision, leaving it to time to tell if the Vikings can beat the Broncos to enter the 2026 regular season on a high note.

title: Vikings Training Camp Thoughts (8/9): QB Conundrum Continues at Night Practice
full_text:
EAGAN, MN — The Vikings are less than a week from their first preseason game of 2026 against the Giants at MetLife Stadium, and they still do not have a clear separation in their quarterback battle between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy.
The team held its annual night practice on Sunday in front of a sold-out crowd at TCO Stadium, a perfect opportunity for one QB to make a statement and drive the discourse in one clear direction. Unfortunately for Murray and McCarthy, they drove it straight into a ditch.
Here’s a breakdown of the night for both QBs and why their performances on Sunday are a microcosm of this entire competition.
There was a period of time on Sunday where it looked like McCarthy could dominate Murray under the primetime lights. His performance in 7-on-7 work featured some of the best throws I’ve seen McCarthy make through camp.
Of particular note was a throw to Myles Price (h/t VikingzFanPage) on an out route that went against nearly every narrative used against McCarthy: a layered, accurate ball to his left.
Great throw by JJ McCarthy to Myles Price. (Via Vikings IG) pic.twitter.com/XfASmuK05S
McCarthy also had great completions to tight ends Ben Yurosek and Bryson Nesbit, looking decisive as he completed each of his six attempts. Then came full team drills.
Once 11-on-11 action kicked off, McCarthy struggled. His most notable throw came on a deep shot to Justin Jefferson down the right sideline,  a rare sight for the two in their time together. The pass was underthrown, but still counted for a deep completion. McCarthy would then struggle to find consistency the rest of the night, ending 6-for-17 in 11-on-11 for the night per SKOR North ’s Judd Zulgad.
McCarthy was on the wrong end of the daily Charles Demmings highlight, a corner blitz where the rookie defender would have knocked McCarthy into next week if not for the red jersey. He did have two impressive throws in a situation to end practice, hitting second-year wideout Tai Felton both times before taking a sack and throwing consecutive incompletions to end practice.
What started with the potential for a dominant night sputtered into missed passes and indecision. Now, it was up to Murray.
Guessing which version of Murray you will see daily has been the ride of Vikings camp so far. While he has proven capable of incredibly impressive days, he has also thrown up some absolute duds. Sunday was his chance to change the narrative when it mattered most.
Murray had eight fewer pass attempts than McCarthy and a higher completion percentage for the night, but that does not tell the full story. Some of Murray’s earliest completions came on short lobs to his TEs that gained barely a yard, if that. He seemed to avoid many of the deep pass attempts that he impressed with earlier in the week,
Murray also had two interceptions; the first appeared to bobble into the hands of James Pierre, and the second came via a leaping Isaiah Rodgers Sr. Murray eventually found a rhythm in the last drill of practice, flashing his mobility and ripping a touchdown to Jordan Addison in a two-minute scenario.
Overall, though, it seemed too little too late.
If you were hoping the Vikings would have their QB situation figured out before their first preseason game, you’ll have to keep waiting. O’Connell told the press pool yesterday that he is still not ready to make the final call , according to Bring Me The News ' Will Ragatz.
Unsurprisingly, Kevin O’Connell is not naming a starting QB right now. He’s happy with their plan so far and notes the rep split has been about 50-50, which has given them a lot to learn and coach on. Says “nothing has really changed” with the timeline for a decision.
In the meantime, the discourse will continue to grow more intriguing until one QB fully separates.
Arguments can be made for continuing the competition or shifting reps one way, but for now, here’s what we know: Murray shows radical day-to-day inconsistency, while McCarthy shows inconsistency from drill to drill. The team simply has too much at stake to enthusiastically bet it all on either variety of roller coaster we've seen so far.
Neither is exactly comforting for Vikings fans or O’Connell.

title: The Biggest Decision the Patriots Must Make Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
FOXBORO --- In less than two days, the New England Patriots will have to play their first preseason game of the summer. They just finished their joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts and will now have a closed walkthrough before the game.
But now the Patriots' coaching staff has an important decision to make, and it's one that coaches across the league can sometimes struggle with around this time in the NFL schedule. How much, if at all, should they play their starters?
We know with certainty not to expect Drake Maye out there. Head coach Mike Vrabel spoke to reporters before the joint practice , and all, but confirmed it.
"I wouldn’t anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday, but that’s all subject to change," Vrabel said before Tuesday's practice. "That’s where my mindset is right now, standing here today. It’s important that we get the work in and get things accomplished that we are looking to get accomplished. That can always change, but I wouldn’t anticipate that happening right now."
So we know that against Indianapolis, the quarterbacks will likely be a mix of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Who'll start that game is unclear, even to the players. DeVito told reporters that he doesn't have a clue what the plan is right now.
"I think about my rookie year, I was told that morning how much I was playing in the game," DeVito said. "I'll just prepare like I'm gonna play the whole game and then whenever they tell you whatever you do, that's how it is."
But the quarterback position isn't really the one in dire need of confirmation. The Patriots have to figure out what to do with the rest of their roster . Most teams will try to get their starters, at least most of them, some snaps during the summer to get them back into the swing of things.
Veterans, like tight end Hunter Henry, defensive tackle Milton Williams and wide receiver A.J. Brown, should get some time on the field at some point in the next three weeks. But how many snaps is the question.
Other times, the Patriots have let their youngsters play for quite a long time. Last year, undrafted wideout Efton Chism III fought his way onto the roster because he wasn't able to be taken off the field. He scored touchdowns in each of the first two games he played in, and was given that long leash as a rookie.
It's just knowing what buttons to push at the right time. For Vrabel, it's looking like this week's battle against the Colts will be more about the depth pieces than trying to get the veterans adjusted to game speed.
"That’s really the only reason that we do these joint practices," Vrabel said when asked about using joint practices to evaluate players who won't play in games. "It will be a lot of the frontline players and whoever’s available. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work today will get extensive work in the game on Thursday.
"That’s just how it goes. So, let’s see how today goes, and we can always adjust and plan accordingly."
In New England's practice, some longer-tenured guys got heavy workloads. Brown led the team with five catches . Henry had four and worked with both the first and second offensive units. Linebacker Robert Spillane was on the field for quite a while.
However, there are some players that fall right into the middle of the depth chart that could be interesting choices. Does Kindle Vildor, the free agent cornerback who replaced Christian Gonzalez Tuesday, get rest because of a lack of depth or playing time because he's not promised a spot. The same goes for the depth offensive linemen who might be in roster limbo right now (Dametrious Crownover, Andrew Rupcich, James Hudson).
That's not to say that the Patriots won't give their stars some reps during the preseason (keep an eye on next week's joint practice/game with the Philadelphia Eagles).
But the team needs to figure out the line between resting valuable players in non-valuable games, and keeping their players ready for the regular season.

title: Winners From Patriots Joint Practice vs. Colts: A.J. Brown Remains Top Target
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots walked off the practice fields in lock step with the Indianapolis Colts after their joint practice. Both sides looked solid moving the ball, and some Patriots made their mark known during 1-on-1 and team drills.
But which Patriots stood out among the rest?
For the first time all training camp, the Patriots were able to line up and hit another team. Here's the players that rose to the challenge Tuesday.
The Patriots certainly don't need a new starting quarterback, but DeVito has been making strides as the second-in-command. He's taken full control of the second-string offense and continued to look the part against the Colts.
He went 2-for-6 in 7s and 11-for-16 in 11s, with several long throws being the highlights of the day. His 50-yard touchdown to Mack Hollins on the first play of his two-minute drill was just the cherry on top for an already-impressive summer.
"He continues to learn, and with it being a new system, I think it got his attention a little bit better, as opposed to saying, 'Hey, I know what this is,' and kind of taking it for granted," head coach Mike Vrabel said pre-practice. "I think he’s really done a nice job."
Brown remained the No. 1 option for the Patriots' passing attack . It started off with a win over Sauce Gardner in 1-on-1s, a play that led Sauce Gardner to hop on social media and write about it in a now-deleted post .
Once the teams began full squad reps, Brown was finding the ball early and often. Working in tandem with Drake Maye, Brown led the Patriots with five receptions. One of those would have been good for a 10-yard touchdown, an in-breaking route where he slipped through two defenders near the goal line.
Just one day removed from signing a two-year extension to stay with the Patriots , Henry was a constant factor on the field. Not just with the starters -- where he'll be all season -- but with the second unit as well.
Maye's first two completions of the day were to Henry, one of them a 25-yard catch and run down the right seam. Later in the practice, he spent time with the backups, catching two passes (and a touchdown) from DeVito. It was a fantastic joint practice for the player who was excited about facing a new team.
"It’s the first time we’re a full team. We’re all going to wear the same color and cheer on each other in a way instead of going against each other," Henry said Monday. "It’s always fun to have those battles throughout camp and all of a sudden just kind of come together as a team and try to build that."
Ponder remained with the top defense, and it's starting to stick that the second-year edge rusher belongs in the NFL . He recorded an impressive batted down ball at the line of scrimmage, leaping in the air to make contact, before eventually recording a would-be strip sack later in the practice.
Vrabel said before practice that veteran Harold Landry is still working his way back from a knee injury suffered last year, so until he returns to the field, it's looking like Ponder has played his way into the starting lineup for Week 1.
But how could Gonzalez be a winner? He didn't even appear at practice! Considering how depleted the Patriots' secondary was without Gonzalez and Carlton Davis (limited, hamstring) on the field, it just was more evidence that the 24-year-old deserves a new extension .
The Patriots rolled out Kindle Vildor, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada with the first-string defense -- who have each looked good at points in camp -- but it just wasn't a good fit. The Colts' offensive weapons, including Josh Downs and Tyler Warren, were running wild during team drills.
"Everybody's expected to be able to come in and compete at the highest level that they're able to compete against," safety Dell Pettus said after practice on missing Gonzalez. "We love having Gonzo out here, and if he's just not able to go for whatever reason it is that day, whoever comes in next is supposed to come in and be held at the same as level as he is."
The final play of practice helped leave a good taste in the mouths of Patriots fans. With Riley Leonard and the Colts driving on a two-minute drill, the pass across the middle got deflected near the 10-yard line. Saunders, the second-year safety fighting for a spot on the team, was in the right place at the right time to nab the interception (his second of training camp).
"John, he keeps getting better," Pettus said on Saunders. "He's always been a playmaker when it comes to getting his hands on the football. He just continues to grow."

title: Everything We Know About Patriots' QB Plan for Preseason Opener
full_text:
FOXBORO --- We now have a better idea of who to expect to see at quarterback when the New England Patriots host the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday evening.
After working against the Colts' starting defense throughout Tuesday's joint practice, Drake Maye is not expected to play in the Patriots' preseason opener.
“I wouldn’t anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday, but that’s all subject to change," Mike Vrabel said prior to practice on Tuesday. "That’s where my mindset is right now, standing here today. It’s important that we get the work in and get things accomplished that we are looking to get accomplished.
"That can always change, but I wouldn’t anticipate that happening right now.”
Vrabel also mentioned the importance of the work from joint practices, as each team's starters get to face each other for an extended period of time. In a preseason matchup, the reps would be more limited.
Maye being out on Thursday would open the door for Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton to split time on Thursday. However, DeVito has yet to be told what his workload will be.
"I have no clue," DeVito said when asked about his role against the Colts. "I think about my rookie year, I was told that morning how much I was playing in the game, I'll just prepare like I'm gonna play the whole game and then whenever they tell you whatever you do, that's how it is."
Maye not playing on Thursday would be a shift from the Patriots' preseason plan a year ago, but would closely resemble Vrabel's preseason tendencies from when he was the head coach of the Tennessee Titans.
Last year, Maye started in the preseason opener against the Commanders and stayed in through two drives. Backup Joshua Dobbs played the next four drives, up until the end of the first half. Undrafted free agent Ben Wooldridge came in after halftime and finished the game.
However, last year's preseason opener was also the first-ever opportunity for Vrabel's coaching staff to work with Maye in a game setting. Now, with a year under their belts working with each other, Maye's expected inactivity on Thursday would follow a trend set by Vrabel in Tennessee.
Starting quarterback Ryan Tannehill did not play in the preseason opener during any of Vrabel's final three years with the Titans -- after the NFL shifted to a three-game preseason slate. As Maye continued to grow in the Patriots' system, Vrabel anticipates him getting that same treatment as Tannehill this Thursday.

title: Patriots, Colts Joint Practice Notebook: Backup QB Goes Deep, Nearly a Fight
full_text:
FOXBORO --- For the last few practices, it's clear that the New England Patriots were getting tired of hitting each other . They finally got the opportunity to hit another team Tuesday, as the Indianapolis Colts came to town for a one-day joint practice.
It was a good day of work, with both sides getting plenty of reps on each of the two fields next to Gillette Stadium. It also gave us highlights for both sides on offense. The passing attacks looked good and it gave the fans in attendance a lot to cheer about.
Here's what stood out from the Patriots' 14th training camp session of the summer, including how one backup quarterback continues to launch the football through the stars.
The Patriots got some good news on the defensive front, seeing defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Charles Woods return to the field. Barmore, who had missed the last two practices, was a limited participant and didn't partake in any team drills. Neither did cornerback Carlton Davis, who was working his way back from a hamstring injury.
Wide receiver Kyle Dixon, cornerback Christian Gonzalez, safety Mike Brown and long snapper Julian Ashby were all absent, as were edge rusher Harold Landry (PUP) and safety Brenden Schooler (NFI).
Gonzalez's absence was not surprising. As he continues to work his way through contract negotiations, the player so willing to play in pads with his teammates was not spotted during today.
There were some really good moments from New England's two quarterbacks (Behren Morton didn't take a team snap). Drake Maye went 4-for-6 in 7s and 15-for-23 in 11s. He looked sharp across the middle, and did have a nice scramble out of pressure, but his day ended with a tough interception to Colts safety Camryn Bynum. He was looking in the direction of DeMario Douglas in the end zone, but an underthrown ball allowed Bynum to leap up and pick it off.
Backup Tommy DeVito aired the ball out all morning. He finished the day going 2-for-6 in 7s and 11-for-16 in 11s. DeVito had the confidence to launch some passes, including touchdowns to Mack Hollins and Eli Raridon. He's continued to be one of the biggest risers throughout camp.
For the receivers, A.J. Brown (five catches), Hunter Henry (four), Raridon (four) and Hollins (three) all had nice days. Hollins was on the receiving end of a 50-yard touchdown from DeVito -- where he pretended to spike the ball through the goalposts after burning the Colts secondary. It looked like DeVito connected with Raridon on the ensuing two-point conversion.
The practice began with 1-on-1s between New England's receivers and Indianapolis' defensive backs. Everyone's favorite drill of training camp started off with a bang: Brown vs. Sauce Gardner. The route, a quick comeback on the outside, was won by Brown after the cornerback slipped and the Patriots fans erupted.
Here you go (via @PatriotsCLNS ): pic.twitter.com/aDNGYx0IcF https://t.co/0sLZqMd8h8
It was the only rep between the two stars, with Garner taking to social media after practice to write "all this from a 1on1 rep? & a 8 yard sit route at that? its a reason that's the only one yall saw."
Other winners including wide receivers Kobe Prentice, Efton Chism III and Cameron Dorner, each with a pair of wins. For the Colts, Josh Downs beat Marcus Jones (who was flagged for holding) and began jawing at the Patriots cornerback after the play.
Henry's four catches were the second-most on the entire team , and those came with both the first- and second-string offenses. Henry caught his first two passes of the day in 11s, connecting with Maye down the seam for the practice's first chunk play.
He also got several snaps with the backups, hooking up with DeVito for a pair of grabs, including a touchdown in the back of the end zone.
For both sides, it felt like the offenses had the better results. Yes, there were two interceptions thrown (Bynum's on Maye, and Patriots safety John Saunders Jr. picked off Riley Leonard on the day's final snap), but overall, the offenses won the day.
New England's run defense and pass defense had cracks, both for different reasons. The Colts ran behind Jonathan Taylor for a lot of their 11s plays, putting pressure on a Barmore-less defensive front. In the passing game, Kindle Vildor, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada got extended look as starters, which didn't go too well for the Patriots.
There was some nice plays, including pass breakups from Bradyn Swinson, Elijah Ponder and Marcellas Dial . Ponder also added a strip-sack during 11s, one of the biggest plays of the day for the Patriots.
The Patriots have been very disciplined during the start of camp, but there was a clear message drilled into them from the coaching staff.
"Obviously, there’s going to be some pushing and shoving," head coach Mike Vrabel said prior to practice. "If you throw a punch, you just have to head over and run hills or do something with Frank (Piraino) and his crew because that’s what is going to happen in the football game, and I don’t anticipate that happening."
There was almost a fight, however. On a special teams drill, Colts defensive end Durell Nchami was in the middle of a little skirmish. It didn't seem like any Patriots players were escorted off the field, but edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins and Dre'Mont Jones both appeared in the middle of the pile. Nchami spent the rest of practice walking with a member of the Colts staff witih his helmet off.
"It's different, but it all goes back to how we want to play as a team, man, and how we want to do things. We can't worry about how they practice or how they run their plays or whatever. We gotta stick to our details." - defensive tackle Milton Williams on maintaining structure in a less-structured practice.
The Patriots will have a walkthrough tomorrow that is closed to both the public and the media. In the meantime, the team will host an official ribbon-cutting event for the recently-built New Balance Athletics Center at 2 p.m.
On Thursday, the Patriots will host the Colts for their first preseason game of the summer. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. from Gillette Stadium.

title: Patriots Keeping Their Options Open When It Comes To Caleb Lomu
full_text:
FOXBORO --- Caleb Lomu played left tackle in college . He's been asked to play both left and right tackle with the New England Patriots. He's also been mentioned as a player who could play guard.
The Patriots have kept their options open when it comes to their first round pick.
Lomu was at right tackle for most of training camp to this point , working with the second-string offense and sometimes replacing Morgan Moses in the starting offense. For the Patriots' scrimmage on Friday and practice on Monday, he was back on the left side. It was clear he's more comfortable on that side, but it's still a work in progress to nail down both positions.
"It's been good being able to learn both sides of the line just to understand the playbook a little bit more," Lomu told reporters after the team's 13th practice of the summer. "It's a little bit difficult at first. It's different footwork, different hand placement, going the opposite way on plays and from one side, but it's been helping me a lot.
"Being able to get more playing time and just understanding the playbook a lot more."
It's been an up-and-down summer for the Utah rookie . Sometimes, he's struggled in 1-on-1s and got beat almost immediately. Other times, like Monday, he was a perfect 3-0 against some of the Patriots' quickest edge rushers.
The Patriots haven't officially penciled him in to either side for the preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts this week, but it wouldn't come as a surprise to see him get snaps at both spots.
"It's throwing with a different hand, kicking with a different foot," Lomu continued. "But then, it's just, you know, playing tackle - the position I've played my whole life. So a few kicks, few practices after that starts to feel a little bit more comfortable."
So Lomu is getting comfortable at the tackle position, but what about guard? The Patriots' depth at guard is thinning out, as the team recently traded away Caedan Wallace and might need to rely on veterans Ben Brown/Andrew Rupcich to hold down the fort as backups.
The Patriots haven't ruled out the possibility of moving Lomu to guard, maybe not full time, but for a brief time to get his feet wet there.
"I mean, I think that there's — whether we have injuries or things, but I think that guys are working in there," Mike Vrabel said on Aug. 4. "James (Hudson) is getting some reps inside there, and there will be a time where you guys will see Caleb work in there. So, we're just looking to find the best combination of guys for the season."
Lomu's start to his rookie season hasn't been ideal from a pure win/loss standpoint. Sure, he's getting his reps, but it's not always the best result. According to Lomu, that's actually the best kind of beginning .
"Everyone that is out on this field belongs to be here. And so, I’m not going to win every rep, and I know that," Lomu said. "I’m either winning, or I’m learning. And so those reps that I don’t win all the time. I’m learning from that. What did I do to lose that rep?
"And whatever I did, just don’t do that again. But I know I’m not going to win every rep. And so especially in the one-on-ones, it’s a place to try different things and to try different techniques that you use."

title: Three Things To Watch When Patriots Host Colts For Joint Practice
full_text:
On Tuesday morning, the New England Patriots welcome the Indianapolis Colts to town for a joint practice. With the two team's starters likely to get more work against each other than they will in Thursday evening's preseason matchup, here are the four biggest things to watch during practice.
The Patriots made two splash moves at the receiver position this offseason, signing former Packer Romeo Doubs to a four-year $68 million contract and trading for A.J. Brown from the Eagles.
While Maye and Brown struggled to connect on the first few days of camp prior to full pads coming on, their chemistry has taken a significant leap since then. While Doubs' camp has not been at the same level as Brown's, he has shown some flashes, including an over-the-head catch on Christian Gonzalez on Monday.
. @DrakeMaye2 to Romeo art 🎨🖼️ pic.twitter.com/cabmp7sAeW
In a competitive practice with a new team coming into town, can Maye's momentum with Brown and Doubs continue to build, or will the Colts' defensive backs give the Patriots' newest offensive weapons a reality check?
Indianapolis has one of the league's best running backs in Jonathan Taylor, whom was recently rewarded with a two-year $44 million contract extension. The three-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in rushing touchdowns (18) last season, while tacking on just under 2,000 all purpose yards.
Throughout training camp, New England has experimented with three linebacker sets which puts Chad Muma in with starters Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss. While Muma was a key defensive contributor at the beginning of his career with the Jaguars, he spent last year primarily as a specialist with the Colts and Patriots.
Now slated to have a significant role in Zak Kuhr's defense, how comfortable will Muma look on Tuesday against one of the NFL's best rushing offenses?
On a similar note, undrafted free agent Khalil Jacobs seems to currently control the Patriots' fourth linebacker spot. If he plays any snaps against Indianapolis' starters, keep an eye out on how comfortable the 22-year-old looks out on the field.
While the Patriots' defensive line has gotten the better of the offense in camp, Tuesday will provide a true benchmark of where the two sides stand.
The Colts' offensive line, headlined by six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, tied for the seventh-fewest sacks allowed in the NFL last season with 29. For perspective, the Patriots' 48 sacks allowed was tied for the ninth-most.
With Indianapolis coming to town, New England's front four -- headlined by Milton Williams and Christian Barmore -- get a worthy challenger to compete in a good-on-good matchup.
On the other side, the Colts' defensive line should provide a similar challenge for the Patriots' offense. Veterans DeForest Buckner, Arden Key and Grover Stewart, plus 2024 first-round pick Laiatu Latu, have each solidified themselves as key contributors in the NFL.
On both sides of the ball, if the Patriots are able to hold their own in the trenches against an impressive Colts team, it could be a sign of a bright 2026 season in New England.

title: Why the Patriots RB3 Battle Isn't Nearly as Close as Fans Think
full_text:
FOXBORO --- Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson are penciled in as the New England Patriots' top two running backs, and it's been that way since last season ended. It's the RB3 role that's been up in the air for 2026 , and for a while, it felt like a healthy competition.
Between Terrell Jennings (who opened up training camp on the non-football injury list), Lan Larison, Jam Miller and Myles Montgomery, those four players were in a competition with each other for the third spot. For a long time, it felt like it was wide open.
With Jennings on the sideline with what he called a "small thing," Larison began to get the lion's share of third-string snaps. He looked smooth out of the backfield, and both rookies also began to pop.
But all fun competitions must come to an end at some point, and ever since Jennings returned from the NFI list, that RB3 job has been all his . His first practice back was a lower-rep day for him, but ever since? It's obvious the third-year running back is the favorite for that spot.
"I feel really good, man," Jennings told reporters after the team's 13th practice of the summer about heading into a season with a familiar playbook. "It's always good coming in, knowing the playbook is a plus for me, and just knowing the same guys that I've been dealing with for a year now, it's been really good.
"And the coaches, of course, they're gonna coach you hard every year. So just staying sharp on my mental is what that's gonna help me with."
Jennings is the only one of those four that has real NFL experience . In his two years, he's ran the ball 36 times for 106 yards and a touchdown as a rarely-used goal line back. Larison, a rookie last year, didn't play after a preseason injury ended his year.
Both rookies, one drafted (Miller) and one undrafted (Montgomery) have gotten reps in team drills so far, but don't seem like they're on a path to make the roster just yet.
It's obvious at this point that Jennings is the front runner for that third job, both in the amount of reps he's taken and in how he plays. His running style is drastically different from those behind him.
"I would say my aggression, and I play big, so that's what I like to bring to (the field)," Jennings said. "I can run hard as well, and I can also get on the edge and run."
Before Jennings returned, Larison was taking most of the snaps at RB3 . Even Miller and Montgomery got some extended looks out of the backfield. Since he's passed his physical and strapped the pads on, it's clear Jennings has the upper hand.
The running back room as a whole knows that there's a competition for the final spot. Still, they're keeping their spirits high as they head into the dog days of the preseason.
"We're pretty close, I'd say, as a room," Larison said last week. "It's pretty friendly competition. We all try to help each other, and if we see anything, we're always talking, communicating. We want the best for each other."
Jennings, the longest-tenured one of the four backups , has a similar mindset. It's certainly one that can help the rest of the room, but for Jennings, keeping that same headspace will ultimately win him the job come Week 1.
"It's good. I mean, we're friends, but we want to feel like it's a real battle out there," he said. "Like we telling each other, 'Yeah, man, you better tighten up because I'm coming right behind you. So it's a good, healthy, healthy bond that we got, but it's also competitive."

title: Hunter Henry Calls Contract Extension With Patriots A 'True Blessing'
full_text:
FOXBORO --- Heading into his 11th season in the NFL, and sixth with the New England Patriots, tight end Hunter Henry is grateful for the time he has spent in the league.
Henry signed a two-year contract extension on Monday morning, and is now slated to be in New England through the 2028 season.
"It means a lot man, it means a lot to me and my wife and just organization as a whole man," Henry said. "The Kraft family has taken me in, they've been so good to me and my family, giving me a chance kind of in the middle of my career to come over here."
After spending the first five years of his career with the Chargers, Henry signed with the Patriots in March of 2021. His time in New England has been comprised of milestones both on the field and off of it.
"First, personally, I've had three kids here," Henry said. "So I've raised a family here. That's always going to mean something to me for the rest of my life."
In addition to starting his family in New England, Henry expressed gratitude toward Patriots Nation and the Boston area.
"We've just appreciated it the whole time," he explained. "We really have, we've enjoyed the area. Enjoyed this fan base, man. I feel like I've really appreciated things a lot, and it's just a blessing. It really is. It's a true blessing to be able to do this 11 years."
Henry's appreciation for the Patriots organization is complemented by impressive seasons on the field. Since signing with the team, he has set career-highs in receptions (66 in 2024), yards (768 in 2025) and touchdowns (nine in 2021). The three-time team captain has had plenty of individual success in New England, and played a major role in helping the team bounce back from consecutive four-win seasons.
"To get to where we got to last year and then continue to try to build to this year, it's been a lot of fun," Henry said. "I mean, being a part of that process, to be kind of a piece of that in the grand scheme of things. So man, it's a true blessing to be a part of it."
While Henry has received contract extensions in both the Mike Vrabel and Jerod Mayo eras in New England, he originally was signed by the team with Bill Belichick at the helm. The legendary Patriots head coach played a significant role in Henry's development.
"I feel like I grew so much as a player under him," Henry said. "I feel like in the middle of my career, I had a lull a little bit, maybe a complacency and just, I was a solid player. And I saw the game in a good way, but I feel like he really opened my eyes to a lot of different things and how to see the game."
A part of Henry's on-field success can also be attributed to dealing with less injuries than he had to in the first half of his career. While with the Chargers, he missed 25 games in five years. Since joining the Patriots, he has missed just four games in the same time span.
"The best ability you can have in this league is availability," Henry said. "Unfortunately, early in my career,  I battled some injuries. Some real injuries, though, like things that kind of were out of my control. A broken (leg) bone, a torn ACL, I had a (lacerated) kidney."
Henry has been the definition of consistent with the Patriots. He has caught 40 or more passes in each of his five seasons with the team, the second-longest streak by a tight end in franchise history behind Ben Coates. Two of those seasons came with Drake Maye as the signal caller.
"That's my guy and just a special person," Henry said when asked about Maye. "Just a guy that--we've grown really close to over the last few years, and excited to kind of build that relationship off the field but also on the field. He's just a special player to be around."
With his new contract, Henry will now be able to continue building his relationship with Maye in New England over the next three seasons.

title: Patriots Training Camp Notebook: Prepping For Joint Practices
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots returned to the practice field after taking the weekend off, and it was a slower-paced day as the team gets ready for their preseason opener. It was closed to the general public, but Gillette Stadium employees lined the stands to cheer on the team.
After what was an eventful morning -- including signing Hunter Henry to a two-year extension and releasing Caedan Wallace -- the Patriots' 13th training camp practice wasn't as eventful.
Let's open up the training camp notebook and see what stood out.
Several players who missed Friday's session, including fullback Reggie Gilliam, wide receiver Cameron Dorner, offensive tackle Will Campbell and cornerback Carlton Davis, all returned. Davis left practice halfway through and was limited after returning for the first time since getting hurt on July 28.
Defensive tackle Christian Barmore was absent, as was wide receiver Kyle Dixon, cornerback Charles Woods and long snapper Julian Ashby. Dixon left Friday's practice early with a member of the training staff with an undisclosed injury.
Safety Brenden Schooler (NFI) and edge rusher Harold Landry (PUP) were both absent as well.
Some of the sessions throughout the day were slower walkthrough-type drills, but for the quarterbacks, it was a solid day throwing the ball. Drake Maye led the way , going 5-for-7 in 7s and 11-for-17 in 11s. His best throw? That's coming up shortly.
Tommy DeVito, who also aired the ball out at times, finished 6-for-7 in 7s and 8-for-13 in 11s. Behren Morton didn't get any reps during 7s, but did go 4-for-7 in 11s.
Will Campbell didn't take part in any team drills in either of the last two practices, working as a limited participant on Thursday before missing Friday. In his place, Marcus Bryant took over the starting duties at left tackle (he was at right tackle today).
Campbell, in his clunky left arm brace , took part in all the team drills from the left side today. It was nice to see him return to the field, though he didn't look 100% when he was out there. Caleb Lomu got work in as the second-string left tackle, as he went 3-0 in 1-on-1 drills with the defensive line.
Casey Rogers, come on down! The recently-signed defensive tackle had himself his best day as a Patriot, batting down a pair of passes during team drills. The former New York Giants player came to New England after a successful free agent workout, but is on the outside looking in when it comes to sticking around on the roster.
Ashby missed his practice of the summer this year, which led the Patriots to sign free agent Niko Lalos this morning. Lalos was with the team throughout the spring, and was sporting No. 54 on the field at practice today.
Why was Ashby out? Well, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss , he's dealing with a minor ankle injury that isn't expected to hold him out long term.
For now, Lalos will be the one tasked with snapping the ball in practice (and potentially in the preseason game against Indianapolis).
Two separate plays, two similar results for Efton Chism III and Romeo Doubs. During 11-on-11s, both receivers got jump balls thrown their way in the end zone. For Doubs, he leapt over Christian Gonzalez for the score, tumbling to the ground and celebrating with his teammates in a CPR-type celebration.
A few plays later, DeVito connected with Chism on a similar throw. This time, Chism jumped over Marcellas Dial and held onto the score with two hands. It was a nice day for slot receivers making their names known in the back corner of the end zone.
It was a busy day for Chism , who caught seven total passes. Backup tight end Jack Westover also caught four.
"I don't like publicly declaring my goals, I like to keep those kind of internal, but just keep being myself. Try to be as consistent as I can be on a day-to-day basis as a person, as a player, as a father, as a husband, and just continue to grow." - tight end Hunter Henry on his goals for 2026 after inking a two-year contract extension.
The Patriots will do battle against the Colts for their first of two joint practices this summer. Both Mike Vrabel and Shane Steichen will address the media and six Patriots players will speak after the session is done.

title: Why Patriots Traded Backup OL Caedan Wallace After 2 Seasons
full_text:
FOXBORO --- The New England Patriots, more than an hour after agreeing to a two-year extension with veteran tight end Hunter Henry , continue to reshape their roster.
After it was originally reported that the Patriots were releasing offensive guard Caedan Wallace, the Patriots announced that they've traded him and a 2029 seventh round pick to the Miami Dolphins for a 2028 sixth round pick.
To fill his place, the team has re-signed long snapper Niko Lalos after a brief stint in the spring, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss .
Wallace, who was one of three remaining draft picks from New England's 2024 class (along with Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial), had a very up-and-down career with the Patriots. He was drafted with the 68th overall pick in the third round, but really struggled to make his mark on the active roster.
Originally drafted with the hopes of being the team's future left tackle , Wallace eventually switched to guard when Mike Vrabel was hired ahead of the 2025 season. He played in just six games (two starts) as a rookie before an ankle injury ended his season.
One season later, Wallace played in just four games in what was mostly a healthy scratch year.
Going into this year, he was competing for one of the backup guard jobs in what was a pretty slimmed down depth chart. He had switched from the right side in college to the left side in the NFL, before another transition to guard.
The team already had Mike Onwenu, Ben Brown, Mehki Butler and Andrew Rupcich as holdovers from a year ago, but also added Alijah Vera-Tucker, JonDarius Morgan and Jacob Rizy during the offseason.
"I actually like guard, a lot," Wallace said in 2025. "It’s different, and different is always fun for me. I’m learning new stuff every day. It’s really fun, it’s really, really fun. I like hitting people, and at tackle, you have to think a little more. At guard, you can kind of fire off and get your face in stuff more."
Wallace wasn't expected to be a starter, but a strong spring from Rupcich became a roadblock for the 26-year-old to make any upward movement. It would have been tough for him to switch back to tackle , considering the team's hefty investments in the draft the last two years (Will Campbell, Marcus Bryant, Caleb Lomu, Dametrious Crownover).
It also didn't help Wallace's case that he got tangled up in a 1-on-1 drill earlier in camp. He would leave practice early with a member of the training staff.
It caused him to miss a few sessions, and while he did return to the field, it was clear that the missed practices helped boost the stocks of some of the other players gunning for a spot.
Wallace originally opened up camp repping as one of the two guards on the second-string offense . But on July 31, one day before Wallace's injury, his spot with the second team was taken over by Butler.
While he would return from his injury, Wallace didn't get back into the second unit. He would miss the team's final practice of the week on Aug. 7 before a two-day break.
Wallace, obviously, was not in attendance for New England's 13th training camp practice of the summer Monday morning.
Wallace was a player that didn't feel like he was making the roster to begin with. Him being released felt like the expected course of action for the young lineman, but it just came earlier than expected. For the Patriots to get a draft pick back for him is a total win in my eyes.
Solely based on numbers, Wallace never felt like he was cracking the 53-man roster. Good on the Patriots for getting some sort of compensation for him. https://t.co/MitEjIBs60
The Patriots now add a second sixth rounder in 2028, their sixth draft pick for that year. They've already traded away their first rounder to the Philadelphia Eagles for A.J. Brown, and their seventh rounder to the New Orleans Saints (along with Ja'Lynn Polk).
The seventh rounder shipped away is the first draft pick moved in 2029 for New England.
Wallace now heads to Miami looking for a fresh start with a team expected to be in the basement of the AFC East. He's not the first Patriots offensive lineman who has tried to reshape his career with the Dolphins. Both Isaiah Wynn and Cole Strange spent time in South Florida after their Patriots tenures in recent years.

title: Saints Defense Dominates Again as Offensive Mistakes Pile Up Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints were back on Airline Drive on Tuesday as they continued preparing for their first preseason game of the season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday.
The defense continued to dominate the offense, which is commonplace at any level during the preseason. However, the situational mistakes have continued and, to make matters worse, most of the day focused on late-game situations.
Here are some of the takeaways from today’s practice.
On the first team offense, nothing necessarily changed.
Tyler Shough was the starter at quarterback, a position he had held since the second half of last season. Spencer Rattler took reps with the second team while Zach Wilson took snaps with the third.
At running back, Trevor Etienne and Alvin Kamara both took reps with the first team. Audric Estime also took reps with the first team as Moore wanted him take reps there as well.
In the receiving corps, Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson were the starters on the outside while Devaughn Vele was the starter in the slot. The second team consisted of the rookie duo of Barrion Brown and Bryce Lance , along with veteran Kevin Austin Jr.
At tight end, both Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant both rotated with the first team. Rookie Oscar Delp took reps with the second.
On the offensive line, it was the usual with Kelvin Banks and Taliese Fuaga starting at left and right tackle, David Edwards and Cesar Ruiz at left and right guard with Erik McCoy at center.
On the defensive line, Carl Granderson and Chase Young were the starters on the edge while Vernon Broughton and Nathan Shepherd were the No. 1 guys on the interior.
At linebacker, veteran Kaden Elliss was starting alongside Danny Stutsman . The latter has been slowly but surely locking up the starting role over longtime mainstay Peter Werner.
In the defensive backfield, nothing changed. Just like in the past couple of practices, Quincy Riley and Kool-Aid McKinstry were on the outside while Justin Reid and Jonas Sanker manned the safety positions.
Defensive tackle Davon Godchaux was off to the side after rolling an ankle, and Rezjohn Wright hurt his hip during Tuesday's practice.
Other than that , defensive end Cam Jordan was not available again at practice today because of a hamstring injury.
Defensive lineman John Ridgeway III i s dealing with a back issue and remains day to day.
Second-year running back Devin Neal was still off to the side doing rehab work for a hamstring issue and is day to day as well.
Pete Werner (groin) was back in uniform but did not appear to participate in any full-team drills.
The Saints’ strongest position group may be the defensive backfield with the amount of depth it has.
We saw that today with Martin Emerson Jr. The fifth-year cornerback out of Mississippi State had three pass breakups and an interception on the day. He should have had two if he had hauled one in during the second 11-on-11 session.
Carl Granderson made several big plays as he gave right tackle Taliese Fuaga all he could handle off the edge. Granderson was constantly forced pressure off the edge. He also had a presence in the passing game as he had an interception and nearly had another as well on the play right before it.
There were several plays stood out throughout the day.
Austin made several catches throughout the day, including a 25-yard touchdown catch on a nice ball from Rattler.
While it might of been a mixed day for him, Shough made some nice throws as well.
One that stood out was when he spiraled a touchdown throw on 4th down in the red zone to Johnson on a fade route in the back of the end zone over tight coverage from McKinstry to end the second session of 11-on-11 in a quasi two-minute drill.
He also made a nice play later in practice where he used his feet to escape pressure and found Tyson in the middle for a first down.
Riley snagged an interception from Shough to end the main practice session.
Shough was 15-for-27 and threw two interceptions on the day. Despite a rough start to practice, Rattler was 7-for-9, but he also threw an interception. Wilson was 9-for-15 (60%) and did not turn the ball over, but also did not necessarily do anything to separate himself from Rattler.
However, the most concerning thing about the offensive struggles is the lack of situational awareness, something that has been a recurring issue.
The most egregious one came when the offense faced third-and-2 with 14 seconds remaining during a full-field hurry-up drive and committed a costly false start. Shough bailed his offensive line out by converting a fourth-and-1 with a touchdown to Johnson.
However, Johnson committed another false start on the first play with just under 45 seconds on the clock in another 11-on-11 session.
The good thing for the Saints is that its just the preseason and these things can be ironed out before the season starts.

title: Saints Preseason Schedule 2026: Dates, Times, TV, Opponents
full_text:
After two weeks of the players in the franchise going up against each, the New Orleans Saints will finally play another team when it begins their three-week preseason slate starting on Saturday.
New Orleans opens up the preseason slate with a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday at the Caesars Superdome before traveking to play the Los Angeles Rams (Aug. 22). Both games are set for a 3:00 p.m. kickoff. The Saints wrap up the preseason against rival Dallas Cowboys (Aug. 28) in Arlington for a 7:00 p.m. start.
Here is some info about all three teams along with the dates, times, locations and how you can watch all three games.
The Jaguars are coming off their first playoff appearance since 2022 and the most wins in a single season in franchise history after a 13-4 season under Liam Coen , who is entering his second year on the job.
The biggest question for the Jaguars throughout training camp is the running back spot. Travis Etienne has departed for the Saints. The battle is between Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr . Those are tough shoes to fill, considering Etienne rushed for 1,000 yards or more in three of the last four seasons.
The Los Angeles Rams are coming off a 12-5 season and an appearance in the NFC Championship Game, where they lost to eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .
The Rams made the biggest offseason move of the summer when they received All-Pro defensive end Myles Garrett from the Browns in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. Garrett is the reigning Defensive Player of the Year after breaking the single-season sack record with 23 sacks. It was the second time he won the award.
There’s a chance we might see first-round draft pick Ty Simpson , who was shockingly drafted by the Ram with the 13th overall pick. He’s currently battling with Stetson Bennett for the backup role and could be the heir to the keys to the offense when reigning MVP Matthew Stafford retires.
Unlike the previous two franchises mentioned, the Dallas Cowboys have been a massive disappointment. Dallas has missed the playoffs for two consecutive seasons, finishing 7-10 in both. This came after three straight 12-win seasons.
While quarterback Dak Prescott and the Cowboys lit it up offensively by finishing second in the league in total offense, they also finished 30th in yards allowed and had the league's worst passing and scoring defense.
That resulted in the Cowboys drafting five defensive players with seven picks, with their first two picks being safety Caleb Downs of Alabama and Malachi Lawrence of UCF in the first round.
