title: Saints’ Kelvin Banks Jr. Reveals Key Focus After Impressive Rookie Season
full_text:
New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is entering his second NFL season after an impressive rookie campaign.
Drafted ninth overall by the Saints, the 6-foot-5, 315-pound lineman became just the third Saints left tackle since 1978 to start every game at the position, earning consensus All-Rookie honors and a spot on the 2025 PFWA All-Rookie Team.
Banks allowed only five sacks and three accepted penalties across 681 pass-blocking snaps while ranking second among all rookie linemen in run blocking, according to Pro Football Focus.
Banks knows exactly where he wants to improve entering his second NFL season: consistency.
“Honestly, for me, it was more consistency because it'll be multitude of reps,” Banks said. "I'm looking flawless, taking the great set, doing this and that, and— and looking good. And it'll be that one or two reps where it's like, 'Oh, dang.' You know what I'm saying? Just making sure I clean the small mistakes up that I may be making throughout the game, whether it's getting fatigued or just not fully thinking throughout the play and just going out there and playing. So just small stuff like that is what I kind of took away from last year.”
Now, Banks is looking to clean up those small mistakes, build on his strong debut and help lead the Saints to an NFC South title and their first playoff berth since 2020.
Banks’ development is also tied to the growth of fellow offensive tackle Taliese Fuaga . With a full season together under their belts, the two young tackles are pushing each other to take another step, and Banks believes their shared work ethic could help them develop into one of the NFL’s top tackle duos.
“I mean, we literally just got done on the field after practice,” Banks said after the session on Aug. 6. “We were out there for an extra 30 minutes doing extra different sets and working different stuff that we may have slipped up on in practice. So I'll say that's the thing that excites me the most because I know how bad we want to be one of the best tackle duos in the league. So (it's) that eagerness to understand that we both have that same mindset.”
Fuaga, who played left tackle in 2024, started 13 games at right tackle for New Orleans in 2025.
While Banks and Fuaga give the Saints a young foundation at tackle, veteran David Edwards has brought another element to the offensive line room at guard.
Edwards, who is entering his eighth season in the league, has started 77 of the 103 games he played for the Los Angeles Rams (2019-2022) and Buffalo Bills (2022-2025), two of the league’s best teams. He was a starter for the Rams when they won Super Bowl LVI.
Banks believes Edwards’ experience, intelligence and personality have allowed him to quickly fit in with the group.
“He's brought a lot. Savviness, smarts, laughter,” Banks said. He's bringing everything to the room. I mean, he's definitely a guy who fits in well with our scheme and let alone not just our scheme, but our OLI room as a whole. So he's been a great piece to our puzzle, for sure.

title: Saints have an Intriguing New Weapon in Athletic Rookie Tight End Oscar Delp
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints drafted tight end Oscar Delp with the 73rd overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and they had good reason: his athleticism and speed are stuff you cannot teach.
Delp, a 6-foot-5, 245-pound Georgia product, had an impressive pro day as he registered a 4.49-second 40-yard dash and a 38-inch vertical. In four seasons with UGA, Delp totaled 70 receptions for 854 yards and nine touchdowns in his career.
It will be interesting to see how the Saints use Delp with veterans Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant . Regardless, the Saints have been delving into multiple tight end packages and Delp’s versatility could be used there.
Delp is in a loaded tight end room led by Johnson and Fant, so he may not get the most playing time as of right now. However, his versatility could get him on the field and Delp wants to do whatever he can to get on the field and help his team win games regardless of the role.
“Right now, I'm just trying to find a way to get on the field. I know that he's been very successful with tight ends in his past, and I feel like I can bring something to the table. And we got a lot of very talented guys in our room and just different ways to get us on the field. Anything they need me to do,  I'm willing to get out there and just help us be successful.”
Delp has had a chance  to learn from the Saints’ veteran players on how to approach everything as a professional from the film room to being on the pratice field.
“It's been great. A lot of learning, a lot of growing. I’m very fortunate and blessed to be in the tight end room with some vets and some guys. I've got some games under their belt to just learn a lot from everyone, just taking everything in.”
Delp said that Georgia helped him transition to the NFL. That makes sense because the Bulldogs have been one of the NFL’s talent factories since Kirby Smart took over in 2016, especially at the tight end position. Since 2017, Georgia has produced seven tight ends that ended up being draft picks, including Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers .
“I think Georgia did a tremendous job preparing me and other players for the transition from college football to the NFL. I've talked to guys for years while I was in college, figuring out what's different and what happens in that transition. It's just like everyone said about Kirby — he's very big on developing players and practicing hard, and here it's a lot more mental.”
“It's not going to be as bang-bang every day as it is in college, where you're practicing six days in a row, basically scrimmaging for two hours a day. And I think they've done a really good job preparing me to be a receiving tight end, a blocking tight end, wherever they need me. I've done it in college, and I feel comfortable doing whatever they want me to do in this offense.”
A lot of Saints fans are excited about this year’s offense. That’s because they have Tyler Shough coming back after a strong rookie season, a reenergized running back room with Travis Etienne joining the franchise and a deep receiving room led by Chris Olave .
Delp has liked what he’s seen from the Saints’ offense, and he has a first-person view of what it will ultimately look like.
“I mean, I think it's just very explosive. I mean, I think it'd be a really explosive offense. You know, we got the guys to run the ball when we need to run the ball, and then we got the dudes who can go out on field and make big plays. I really think that, you know, the sky's the limit for this offense. And, you know, with the guys like Tyler and Spencer (Rattler) back there, I mean, you know, I think we have a really, really special team.”

title: Drew Brees' Hall of Fame Speech was the Ultimate Love Letter to New Orleans
full_text:
Few athletes have ever become as synonymous with a city as Drew Brees has with New Orleans
Nearly 20 years after arriving in a city that was processing the destruction that Hurricane Katrina brought to the city, Brees was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame , adding the sport’s highest individual honor to what was already a loaded resume.
After all, Brees brought the city of New Orleans a Super Bowl championship, broke many of the NFL’s passing records while active, and of course, one of the most meaningful player-city relationships that we have seen in professional sports.
During his induction speech in Canton, Ohio, Brees made sure New Orleans – the city that embraced him when a torn rotator cuff nearly derailed his career – remained the center of his story.
The circumstances that brought Brees and New Orleans together made their eventual success even more remarkable.
Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans and the Gulf Coast on Aug. 30, 2005, killing nearly 1,400 people, displacing hundreds of thousands and would end up being the costliest natural disaster in U.S. history. The Saints were forced to spend the 2005 season away from the Superdome and finished 3-13, leaving the franchise facing an uncertain future of its own.
Brees was at a crossroads as well.
He suffered a 360-degree labrum and rotator cuff tear in the regular season finale in 2005 while a member of the San Diego Chargers, an injury serious enough where people thought his career would bever be the same at best.
Despite those concerns, the Saints took a chance and signed him to a six-year, $60 million contract with New Orleans on March 14, 2006.
This came after the only other team to go after him, the Miami Dolphins, backed away from Brees due to concerns around his throwing shoulder , giving a chance for not only Brees to resurrect his career but to give hope to a city that desperately needed it.
Brees did not just give a city hope, he gave it 15 years of jubilation, transforming the Saints into perennial contenders and leading the franchise to its first Super Bowl championship in a 31-17 win over New Orleans native Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts. He also became one of the most prolific quarterbacks in NFL history and one of the most beloved athletes New Orleans has ever known.
"New Orleans ... You trusted me with the soul of the city, and I would’ve died to protect that calling." 📺 @ProFootballHOF Enshrinement on ESPN/NFLN pic.twitter.com/S0avpW9hDS
Nearly two decades after taking a chance on New Orleans — and New Orleans taking a chance on him — Brees stood in Canton surrounded by family, friends and members of the Who Dat Nation who made the trip to witness his induction.
When it came time to explain what New Orleans meant to him, Brees made it clear that New Orleans is a special city and the bond forged in 2006 never disappeared.
“New Orleans has been through a lot to the point where in some cases the feeling was we may have lost everything,” Brees said. “It may never come back the same. Storms teach us that our greatest treasures aren’t the things we own. They’re the people we love, and the way we show up for one another. It reminds us to hold our loved ones a little closer, to love a little harder, to laugh a little louder, and to never take a single day for granted. Sometimes it takes losing what can be replaced to truly appreciate the things that can’t.
"New Orleans, you accepted me; you embraced me; you believed in me but more importantly, you trusted me with the soul of the city and I would have died to protect that calling.”
As the saying goes, “If you love New Orleans, it will love you back.”

title: Pete Werner's Starting Job Suddenly in Jeopardy as Danny Stutsman Surges
full_text:
There are always offseason position battles in the NFL, and the New Orleans Saints are no exception.
Second-year linebacker Danny Stutsman has taken first-team reps ahead of veteran Pete Werner for the second straight practice, the clearest change in Wednesday’s rotation. This move also is the most seismic of them all as Werner has been a starter for the Saints since his rookie season, racking up 408 tackles with 256 of them being solo.
However, Werner did struggle a bit last season, as he had a 46.8 tackling grade and a 15.8 missed-tackle rate, according to Pro Football Focus. Combine that with Stutsman being drafted in the Kellen Moore era and a completely different defensive playcaller in Brandon Staley when they took over last season, and Werner may be in trouble.
Nonetheless, Moore said Monday that the changes were “no big deal,” adding that the Saints were going to rotate their players throughout training camp. Even so, that competition still matters to players like Stutsman and Werner, both of whom believe they belong in starting roles.
“There’s a respect between everyone in the room, but it’s the kind of job that you want to win. Every day you’re fighting out there and putting your best thing on tape.”
Stutsman was a fourth-round pick by the Saints in 2025 as a potential successor to DeMario Davis . While that may seem far-fetched because he was drafted in the middle of the draft, his production made you believe that he was a steal.
While in college, Stutsman recorded over 100 tackles in each of his final three seasons while at Oklahoma. He posted a career-high 125 tackles as a sophomore in 2022 and finished his time as a Sooner with 376 total stops — ninth in school history — along with 36 tackles for loss, eight sacks, three interceptions, four forced fumbles, and eight pass breakups.
Now, Stutsman has a shot to live up to his “draft steal” label and claim a starting role in the linebacking corps inside the same building where Rickey Jackson, Sam Mills and Jonathan Vilma once roamed.
“That’s a dream,” Stutsman said when asked about the possibility he wants to be a starter. “That’s kind of why you wake up. That’s motivation. At the end of the day, you want to contribute as much as you can for the defense to do as much as I can.

title: Saints Have One Position Battle Everyone Should Be Watching
full_text:
There are a lot of position battles going on on Airline Drive as the New Orleans Saints are using the preseason to determine the depth chart and who will make the final 53-man roster.
There are plenty of intriguing position battles. With Tyler Shough holding down the starting quarterback role, Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson are battling for the backup role. There’s also some interesting developments on the defensive line as John Ridgeway III has become one of the biggest standouts.
However, the biggest position battle everyone should pay attention to is in the receiving corps.
As it stands, $132 million man Chris Olave and first-round draft choice Jordan Tyson have seemingly locked up the first two spots in the receiving corps. However, one spot remains open.
Battling for the job are third-year wideout Devaughn Vele and rookies Bryce Lance and Barrion Brown .
Vele became a favorite target of Shough in the second half of the season, catching 26 passes for 238 yards and a touchdown in his final four games before missing the last three due to injury.
Lance was an All-American wideout at North Dakota State, accumulating over 2,139 yards and 25 touchdowns. The 6-3, 204-pound receiver was drafted by New Orleans on the fourth round.
Brown was drafted in the sixth round by the Saints after accumulating 2.060 yards and 12 touchdowns at both Kentucky and LSU from 2022-25. He made most of his noise as a kick returner, taking back a kick return for a touchdown at least once in all four years.
Without a doubt, Brown has been making the most noise of the three as each and every practice he is making a standout play or two,
"I knew he was an explosive player, but I didn't know he could play like that,” Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks said. “He's a dog, man. Even from the first practice, I seen him make some cuts, and run some routes and explode off the ball, and I was like 'yeah, he's going to be special.'"
Saints head coach Kellen Moore has been impressed with Brown’s mental fortitude during training camp and how well-prepared he is in practice and practice out.
“I think his just focus and his urgency to be really well-prepared,” Moore said. “I think he does an awesome job. I think that's, that's one of the parts that I'm most impressed by him, because I think that's the hardest part for these young guys: the physical part. They've played football, there's an acclimation part of that, but there's so much more of a mental wear and tear on them, um, with the preparation side, and sometimes that impacts their ability to go out there and perform. And so for Barrion, he's been really assignment-sound he's been really detailed, and so, all that credit goes to him getting ready.”

title: Rookie Wide Receiver's Suspension the Latest Shakeup in Saints' Receiving Corps
full_text:
A rookie wide receiver for the New Orleans Saints has suffered a tough break.
On Thursday, Brock Rechsteiner was suspended for the first six games of the 2026 season, Nick Underhill of New Orleans.Football first reported . No reason has been officially given by the league but more details should emerge.
Brock Rechsteiner has been suspended by the Commissioner for the first six games of the 2026 season.
While this is a blow for Rechsteiner, he will still be eligible to participate in all preseason activities before the official reduction to 53 players. That includes the Saints’ preseason games against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 15, Los Angeles Rams on Aug, 22 and Dallas Cowboys on Aug. 28.
Because Rechsteiner is an undrafted free agent, the next month is critical for the former Jacksonville State product to make the final roster. However, he is a longshot to make the final roster, even more so with the latest news.
While his football exploits are unknown to most, several members of his family are household names.
His father and uncle are both former professional wrestlers who wrestled as Rick and Scott Steiner with the latter also going by the name “Big Poppa Pump.” Both are members of the WWE Hall of Fame.
His older cousin, Bronson, who goes by the ring name Bron Breakker, also wrestles in WWE and is considered one of the company’s future stars.
While Rechsteiner’s situation is not necessarily a huge hit to roster, it’s another notable shakeup in the receiving corps.
Mason Tipton is still on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) as he continues to recover from surgery on his tibia that stems from a groin injury he suffered before last season’s regular season finale against the Atlanta Falcons.
You also have to account for Ja’Lynn Polk’s sudden retirement on Aug. 2, something the people inside the building did not expect. Polk was acquired by the Saints last September but was never able to wear a black-and-gold uniform. That’s because he was sidelined by a shoulder injury, causing him to miss the entire 2025 campaign.
Head coach Kellen Moore did not offer any details about why Polk decided to walk away from playing football other than that it was a “personal” decision.
“He just felt like this was the best decision for him on a personal level,” Moore said. “And so, you know, love that guy. He did an awesome job through the entire process here (over) the year-plus we had him.”

title: John Harbaugh's Fingerprints Are Already All Over Giants Training Camp
full_text:
John Harbaugh's immediate impact on the New York Giants can be seen at every practice, from the way drills are being done and the attention being paid to each detail to the players' fatigue at the end of the sessions.
Of course, the club won't face its first quiz until Saturday's preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings at MetLife Stadium. But make no mistake about it: There is a different feel to the team as it goes through the third week of training camp, and its preseason record will not alter its preparation or its mission.
"We have a chance to be a good football team," Harbaugh said this week. "We're doing a lot of good things right now. Okay. Where do we go? This week, we told the guys the focus is execution, for sure, but the focus this week is technique. From now until Saturday, our individual focus is on your technique. All the little things to make you successful.
"Even at the end of practice when you're dead tired, that's a fourth quarter, win the game type drill, and you're down by 14. Okay? That's focus on your technique. Because if your technique is good, you can win the battle of fatigue. And that's what we're working on. So, I think that set us up for that. Now go forward this week and do that same idea."
The team already has gone through six fully-padded practices - sometimes in high heat, humidity and even rain. And the players aren't getting as many in-session breaks as they have under previous coaches, but they apparently understand the blueprint.
"Man, these days do stack on you, but as I said, it’s camp; it’s supposed to be hard. It isn’t really supposed to be easy," linebacker Brian Burns said.
"These days do stack on you, but it isn’t doing nothing but making us stronger. So, I'm glad to go through that with these boys, and everybody's still working hard, even though they're sore, don't feel like it, unmotivated. But that's part of camp."

title: Giants' Offense Working Toward Cohesiveness as Defense Sets the Pace in Camp
full_text:
The best way to summarize the New York Giants training camp so far is that it’s been a tale of two units.
The defense has been ahead of the offense almost from the get-go, which is to be expected, but the hope was that by now, the offense would at least start to catch up.
That hasn’t exactly been the case. But offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said there has to be a degree of patience exercised.
“There's going to be highs and lows through this process. We talk about it as a staff, like you can’t – we have to make sure that as we go through this journey, we never get too high and we never get too low.
Today was an average practice, maybe below average. It wasn't good enough. He knows that. We know that. We'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles – there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and during the season, but how do we react? When you can get it on tape, evaluate, and try to show them what they're doing right and what they're doing wrong, it happens quicker.
Part of the problem has been quarterback Jaxson Dart’s struggles to adapt to the new offense, which has him working more under center. Dart has had some highs and lows as he works at his own pace, and Nagy said there has been forward progress.
“Every quarterback's a little bit different based on what you're doing in the offense,” Nagy said.
“I would say, if we're evaluating Jaxson, which we are, and you sit there and you look at – I just go back personally to OTAs, and when we were first teaching this thing, we spent phase two just kind of trying to teach this thing ground up in buckets and phases, and not necessarily plays.”
Meanwhile on the defensive side of the ball, coordinator Dennard Wilson has been generally pleased with how his unit is coming together, particularly against the run.
“We're connected up front right now. We're playing with good vertical knock-back. We're setting the edge,” he said.
“I think the defensive ends and outside linebackers have been outstanding in setting the edges, and we have some linebackers that fill gaps. They come downhill with a sense of urgency. They're big players. They're aggressive, and everybody's playing with their hat in their hands.
“The biggest thing is just their eyes. They know what they're looking at, and they're fitting accordingly. And if we have something that we mess up, we correct it, we make it right, and then we come out and execute again.”
Wilson is particularly excited about the variety of talent he has at his disposal.
“It's very exciting. We built a system here. Not just the coaches but the players as well. We put in a system that's in place that the system has a lot of complex things to it, but the system is easy for them,” Wilson said.
“It looks complicated to others, but it's easy for them because it's conceptual teaching. So, the joy of being able to get guys to move in different spots, they're running the same thing over and over. You don't know where it's coming from.”
“For me, it's just exciting to see these guys grow together, exciting for them trying to be detailed and disciplined every day and coming out here and flying around and flying to the ball as fast as they can.”
WR Jalin Hyatt (leg), WR Juju Smith-Schuster (knee), C John Michael Schmitz (concussion), OL Lucas Patrick (knee), and CB Paulson Adebo (unknown) were among those not spotted at practice. This was the second straight day Adebo didn’t practice in the team drills; he did do some light work in the individual session on Monday.
Over to the side with trainers were cornerback Greg Newsome II (knee) and Dru Phillips (knee), and receiver Malik Nabers (knee), the latter of whom worked with trainers for about 90 minutes.
The cornerback depth is becoming scary with Adebo, Phillips and Newsome dealing with injuries. While it’s still early enough in the week, it’s looking more and more that the starting cornerbacks in Saturday’s preseason opener against Minnesota will be Deonte Banks and rookie Colton Hood, with Ar’Darius Washington the likely candidate for the slot.
Banks has been having a strong summer, having built off a strong spring, and is a player we’re looking forward to seeing in live game action.
Continuing the participation report, inside linebacker Abdul Carter (hand/finger) and defensive lineman Chauncey Golston (head) returned to practice. Carter sat out Monday’s session while Golston left about midway through.
Rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa, who at one point during Monday’s practice had his neck checked by a trainer before returning to finish out the session, was kept out of team drills on Tuesday, replaced by Daniel Faalele.

title: Giants Reportedly to Host CB Terrion Arnold for a Visit
full_text:
The New York Giants are starting to get banged up across the board, but no position has been as hard hit as the cornerback spot.
The Giants, who currently have slot cornerback Dru Phillips (knee), Paulson Adebo (unknown), and Greg Newsome II (knee) sidelined, are reportedly planning to host former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold on Wednesday for a visit, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
Arnold has appeared in 24 regular-season games for the Lions with 22 starts. He has one career interception, 18 pass breakups, 91 tackles (70 solos) and one fumble recovery.
Arnold’s planned visit with Big Blue has triggered questions about the long-term injury statuses of Phillips, Adebo, and Newsome and how the length of their respective absences could affect the depth at the position.
The Giants could simply be doing due diligence just in case the injury bug further hits the position group.
New York is already looking at potentially having to roll with Deonte Banks and rookie Colton Hood on the perimeter and defensive back Ar’Darius Washington in the slot when they host the Minnesota Vikings for the preseason opener this weekend.
Adding a player of Arnold’s caliber would give the team’s defensive secondary depth a big boost.
Arnold, the Lions’ first-round pick (No. 24 overall), was released by Detroit in June after he was accused of off-field indiscretions
His attorneys released a statement that “there is no credible evidence” linking the cornerback to the allegations brought against him.
Since his release by the Lions, Arnold has drawn interest from around the league , including the Colts, Jets, Seahawks, and Texans. His legal case is still pending, but he is free to engage in discussions with teams about his next stop.

title: Giants Have a Glaring Weakness at Center — And an Old Friend Could Be the Fix
full_text:
The New York Giants have invested heavily in their offensive line this offseason, bringing right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor back on a three-year, $39 million deal and using the No. 10 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft on right guard Francis Mauigoa.
Still, the unit has one significant glaring weaknesses.
Center John Michael Schmitz Jr . is entering his fourth season as a starter. He has improved since his abysmal rookie season, but still gave the Giants average center play at best in 2025. Schmitz allowed 14 pressures and one sack, posting a mediocre overall PFF grade of 60.8.
Schmitz suffered a head injur y during a training camp practice on Friday and has since missed two practices. Meanwhile, his backup, Lucas Patrick, has been dealing with a knee issue, which has raised questions about whether he can be counted on for the season.
Bryan Hudson, who came to the Giants in 2024 after a stint on the Lions practice squad and with the Patriots, has been working with the first-team offense.
Hudson has drawn positive reviews from Harbaugh, who said, “I think he's done really well. You know, it's funny because we did feel like we needed to get him in there, even with the twos, and then now with the ones, and he's risen to the occasion so far.”
That all said, the position group, which also includes newly signed Brenden Jaimes, is still painfully thin and is one more injury away from catastrophe. The Giants need to consider bringing in another, more experienced option.
The Giants decided to move on from veteran offensive lineman Greg Van Roten this past offseason. Whether that was because they wanted to upgrade or Van Roten was looking for more than what the team was willing to pay isn’t known.
But given the situation at center, it might not be a bad idea to revisit a possible third season in Blue for the Long Island native.
Van Roten recently worked out for the New England Patriots, but as of this moment, no deal has been agreed to. That means that Van Roten is still interested in playing somewhere and is thought to still be in playing shape.
While it’s understandable that the Giants want to get younger and more toward a people-mover type of offensive line, the versatile Van Roten isn’t necessarily a bad option should Hudson and Jaimes not deliver in the upcoming preseason slate.
In 2025, Van Roten, playing at right guard, finished with a 97.7 pass-blocking efficiency rating . In 2024, he saw 138 snaps at center in place of Schmitz and gave up just two pressures, none of which were sacks.
Bringing in Van Roten wouldn’t just help reinforce the center spot, but he’d also help to reinforce both guard positions, where depth is also something of a concern.
In short, it makes too much sense not to explore a reunion with Van Roten given Schmitz’s history of missing multiple games every season he’s been in the NFL, and the current state of the offensive line’s interior depth.

title: Jaxson Dart's Newfound Patience Is Paying Off for the Giants, Darnell Mooney Says
full_text:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart knew that learning a new offense that required pushing him outside of his comfort zone was going to take time.
But the second-year quarterback, who has been described by his teammates and by his head coach John Harbaugh as someone who seeks perfection on every play, needed to realize that slow and steady wins the race.
Dart’s newfound patience is, in fact, one of the biggest strides he’s made since camp started, according to wide receiver Darnell Mooney.
“At first, I would say he was pretty pissed off with a couple of things at the beginning because a lot of guys are trying to figure out everything,” Mooney said on Monday.
“We're trying to learn the playbook. Now that the guys know the playbook, everything's running a little bit smoother. He's not having to help everyone out. We can help him out. He's calming down more so that he can play quarterback. He doesn't have to help out everybody so much.”
It’s hard to blame Dart for taking the initiative to make sure that everyone is on the same page. Some might even say that it was a case of him doing too much, but again, it’s a sign of his commitment to making things work in the new offensive system and doing all he can to get the Giants back on the winning track.
Harbaugh echoed Mooney’s observation about his quarterback’s growing comfort level.
“I do think the comfort level operating all the different elements and options that he has at his disposal has been big,” Harbaugh said.
“I mean, we've made a lot of progress with that. You know, the motions, the shifts, the getting us in and out of certain plays–I see that.”
The Giants have done everything possible to ensure Dart’s transition to the new offense and his career trajectory continues to point upward, including giving him taller receiving targets such as rookie Malachi Fields and tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have shown a propensity to get open and separate.
Mooney said he’s been impressed by what the young gunslinger has shown.
“Amazing, amazing talent. Has a nice strong arm. As you can see, all the guys, the defensive players, were happy that he slid on one of the plays. He's being smart, and he has his legs as well. All around great quarterback,” he said.

title: Giants Training Camp Update: Injury List Grows, But No Major Concerns Yet
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. – The New York Giants wasted no time getting back to the physical, fast-paced nature that has been the hallmark of head coach John Harbaugh’s practices, running through a nearly 2.5-hour session, their first of the summer at their East Rutherford headquarters.
Speaking of the East Rutherford headquarters, it’s become virtually unrecognizable given the construction project that will include renovating the locker room, the weight room, and more. That construction was part of the reason why the team went to West Virginia to start camp.
Harbaugh was asked how much the construction has impacted things.
“I can't sit here and lie to you and say it doesn't. It does. It's not the Taj Mahal over there. We have to make it better. It's as good as we could do right now, but you learn real quick what you need,” he said.
The Giants head coach added that Giants team ownership has been very responsive to ensuring the team has what it needs, and he cited the grass practice fields as an example.
“The fields were playing poorly in the spring. They went to work on the fields. We actually hired somebody, too. And the fields played great today; it was a major improvement,” he said.
Harbaugh then shrugged and pondered if maybe the circumstances were a test of the players’ collective mettle.
“We have a lot of work to do to make that better. But the players didn't bat an eye. They understand the circumstances. And it's gritty,” he said.
“So, maybe it's just what we needed. Maybe God said, ‘I need you to be a little grittier as a football team, so we're going to put you in this park over here.’”
The injuries are starting to pile up, though there doesn’t appear to be anything that might be long-term according to Harbaugh.
Receiver Juju Smith-Schuster, whose chance at a roster spot is fading away, continues to deal with a knee issue. Center John Michael Schmitz is still recovering from a head injury suffered during the penultimate practice at The Greenbrier. Center Lucas Patrick continues to deal with a knee issue.
Add to the list inside linebacker Abdul Carter, whom Harbaugh said has a hand/finger issue. But Harbaugh was quick to add that Carter’s issue wasn’t serious and that there was a chance he could be back to practice on Tuesday.
Slot cornerback Dru Phillips remains sidelined with a sprained knee. And cornerback Greg Newsome II also has a knee injury that limited him to individuals but kept him out of team drills. Harbaugh said that Newsome will be fine, however.
Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston left about midway through the session with what Harbaugh said was a head injury. Receiver Jalin Hyatt was dealing with a lower leg issue.
Quarterback Jaxson Dart appeared to injure his ankle, but he didn’t come out of practice. Right guard Sisi Mauigoa was also checked for something, but Harbaugh said it wasn’t for a concussion. Whatever it was, it didn’t sideline the first-round pick.
Receiver Malik Nabers still isn’t ready to take part in team drills, even on a limited basis. Nabers worked in individual drills and ran routes against air at the start of practice. The hope is that Nabers eventually gets into some team drills as camp winds down, as that would be a big boost for his readiness for the Week 1 opener against the Cowboys.
Defensive lineman Darius Alexander was in the right place at the right time to pick off a Jaxson Dart pass that defensive back Ar’Darius Washington tipped. Alexander plucked the batted ball out of the air and took it to the house amid cheers from his teammates.
Alexander, by the way, has been having a solid camp, continuing his solid spring. It’s safe to say that he’s making a very strong case for a starting job on the defensive line.
Darius Slayton beat rookie Colton Hood, who bit on a double move, for a touchdown in a two-minute drill.
Malachi Fields had another impressive outing. He was consistently getting open and catching balls thrown his way as he made a case for a sizable role in the offense in his rookie season.
The Giants didn’t really do much with the deep ball in this session, though that was by design.
Not a very good day for backup quarterback Jameis Winston, who missed several easy targets. He did have a perfectly thrown ball to tight end Thomas Fidone, who took it upfield for about a seven-yard gain.
Not a good day either for rookie running back Damon Bankston, who lost a fumble to the defense. That’s not how to make the team, young man!
So far, so good for Bryan Hudson, who has been working with the first-team offense with Schmitz sidelined.
I didn’t see any hiccups in the center-quarterback exchange, which is always a good thing. Not surprisingly, Harbaugh thought that Hudson had done well with his opportunities.

title: Jaxson Dart Explains What the Giants Value Most About John Harbaugh
full_text:
John Harbaugh is a leader of men. He broke into the NFL as a special teams coordinator and was never an innovative offensive or defensive play-caller. But what the New York Giants head coach can do is motivate players and establish a disciplined, winning culture .
That is what excites fans most about his arrival. People acknowledge his recent big-game stumbles with the Baltimore Ravens, but they also recognize the verve he injects into a locker room. This franchise has been missing the very qualities that Harbaugh embodies.
Jaxson Dart explained what the Giants value most about the Super Bowl XLVII champion .
"The way that he carries himself just as an individual, a man, it's something you can really, really respect day in and day out," the second-year quarterback told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Brian Baldinger at training camp.
"I think the biggest thing is he's never trying to change anybody from who they are. But he's putting out his culture, his plan. It's for us to buy into. We trust him because of how great of a coach he is."
"We trust him because of how great of a coach he his" 🤞 @Giants QB Jaxson Dart on new HC John Harbaugh @MikeGarafolo | @BaldyNFL pic.twitter.com/q0PBJCRdUE
How Harbaugh connects with Dart and the other young members of this squad will be vital. Fortunately, it sounds like he is doing quite well in that regard. A firm hand is necessary from time to time, however.
Harbaugh sent a strong message to his 23-year-old signal-caller when he personally assessed Dart a 15-yard taunting penalty for throwing the ball at cornerback Greg Newsome II after scoring a touchdown at practice. Such indiscretions have consequences in an actual NFL game, so hopefully Dart learned his lesson.
John Harbaugh is a players' coach who preaches accountability, a combination that is effective yet all too rare. With his endless passion and impressive credentials, he will ideally command respect from the entire roster and staff. That is the first step.
The Giants must be a cohesive unit. There may be days when players resent their head coach for grueling summer practices, but if everyone stays on the same page from a football perspective, then positive results should follow.
New York's place in the standings will ultimately define Harbaugh's time in the Meadowlands. No amount of flattery will change that. However, it is the very traits that Jaxson Dart and others have highlighted that can help the Giants succeed moving forward.
Harbaugh will continue to instill his philosophies as the opening kickoff quickly approaches.

title: Nabers' Next Step, a New Depth Chart and More: What to Watch at Giants Camp This Week
full_text:
Technically, the New York Giants , who are back at their East Rutherford, New Jersey practice facility, are still in training camp mode for the time being.
But with their preseason opener fast approaching, head coach John Harbaugh could be looking to shift gears a bit in terms of getting the players more acclimated to what a regular workweek might look like while still holding competitions.
To be clear, no, the Giants aren’t necessarily going to “game plan” for any of their three preseason opponents, the first of which, the Minnesota Vikings, comes to town this Saturday. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that Harbaugh doesn’t have specific things and/or players that he wants to see.
There are still questions about the receivers, the cornerbacks, and depth on the offensive line that all need to be sorted out. The readiness of the team will also undoubtedly be a focal point as they prepare to start hitting guys in different colored jerseys.
Here’s a look at some other emerging storylines for the week ahead.
For the most part, the Giants came through the first two weeks of training camp relatively clean as far as major injuries are concerned.
But there are still some guys who were banged up last week, including slot cornerback Dru Phillips (knee) and center John Michael Schmitz (head injury). Phillips, per Harbaugh, is probably going to be “a little bit.” But it’s probably too soon to say if he’s in danger of missing Week 1.
Schmitz is dealing with a second head injury in as many years. He dealt with one in Week 7 of last year, missing that game. So the Giants will likely be cautious with him since this is his second one in less than a year.
Schmitz’s projected backup, Lucas Patrick, is also reportedly dealing with a knee ailment, which led to the team signing Brenden Jaimes. And outside linebacker Brian Burns has been nursing an ankle injury, though that hasn’t necessarily kept him off the field all that much.
Receiver Malik Nabers’ comeback trail has been nothing short of impressive, with the receiver not only doing a little bit more every day with no notable setbacks, but he also got involved with some team drills during a walkthrough practice last week.
That raises the question of whether he’ll start being worked into team drills at a faster pace as soon as this week, to take things a step further in his rehab.
If that occurs, that would be the next big milestone in Nabers’ return from a torn ACL, and a huge boost to the team’s offense.
The Giants will be releasing their first depth chart of 2026, and although it’s not official, it should provide a good look as to where things stand at positions such as cornerback and receiver.
Deonte Banks has been making a strong case for a starting cornerback role, so it is of interest to see where he ends up being listed. And how does the receiver unit stack up?
Again, the depth chart that is coming out isn’t necessarily reflective of how the coaches see things. Still, it’s a decent enough starting point, along with observations from camp, to confirm theories about how certain position units are taking shape.
Historically speaking, a team’s defense is always going to jump out ahead of the offense for the simple reason that they have the advantage early on in practice in that they can’t be properly blocked.
This was the case for the Giants, but once the players became acclimated to working in pads, the offense started to slowly catch up, stringing together two solid days of work toward the end of the team’s stay at The Greenbrier. Will the offense continue to take steps forward, or were those two impressive days an outlier?

title: Giants 2026 Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times, and TV Channels and Matchups
full_text:
The New York Giants are set to play three preseason games before kicking off the regular season against the Dallas Cowboys at home on Sunday, September 13.
The preseason games will offer head coach John Harbaugh his most complete look yet as to how well the team he and general manager Joe Schoen assembled is taking shape.
While there will be no game-planning or strategy involved in the preseason games, Harbaugh’s past teams have generally been successful in winning, the head coach  having won over 40 preseason games over his career.
While to some it doesn’t matter what the outcome of the preseason games will be, for Harbaugh, who is trying to get the Giants back on track, they matter to him because it’s never too soon to start winning, even if the results don’t affect the playoff seeding at the end of the year.
Here is a closer look at the Giants’ three preseason opponents.
Saturday, August 15th at 1:00 p.m. ET MetLife Stadium
The Giants get their first preseason test against the Vikings, another NFC team hoping to make the playoffs this season after a disappointing 2025 campaign. This early preseason game will provide valuable insight into the state of the top roster battles remaining for the Giants.
The Giants and Vikings last played each other in Week 16 of the 2025 regular season. Minnesota won that game by a score of 16-13, holding Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart to just 33 passing yards on the day. The Vikings lead the all-time series with 20 wins to the Giants' 13.
Saturday, Aug. 22 at 4:00 p.m. ET Hard Rock Stadium
Before their Week 2 preseason matchup, the Giants and Dolphins, who seldom see each other on the gridiron, will hold a joint practice in Miami.
The two teams last faced off in Week 5 of the 2023 regular season, with Miami winning that game 31-16.
This is a dramatically different Dolphins roster, though, as new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan has made sweeping changes since arriving. The two teams have played only 11 times in the regular season, the Giants leading the series 7-4.
Friday, Aug. 28 at 7:30 p.m. ET MetLife Stadium
The Giants will return to MetLife Stadium for their final preseason matchup against the New York Jets, a game in which the Giants will be the road team.
The two MetLife Stadium neighbors have played each other every summer since 1969 in what’s an unofficial “battle of New York.”
This summer, the Giants may end up seeing a pair of familiar faces in quarterback Geno Smith, who was with Big Blue for the 2017 season, and former safety Dane Belton, who made the jump to Florham Park during this past free-agency cycle.
Last year, the Giants topped Gang Green 31-12, the Giants notching a 3-0 preseason record, the first time they went undefeated in the preseason since 2014 when they went 5-0 that summer.

title: Giants Camp Surprises: Nabers Ahead of Schedule, Cornerback Battle Wide Open
full_text:
With the New York Giants having wrapped up their 10-practice stay at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, the camp pretty much went as expected in terms of intensity and tempo.
“I think we got a lot better,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “We're much further along than we were when we started. I think we can look back and say that we've come a long way.”
He’s looking for the team to keep that up.
“It's just a matter of keeping your head down and staying after it every day.”
Even Harbaugh, though, will admit that there is still a lot of work to get done in the remaining time before the start of the regular season. And within that time, there are sure to be twists and turns to add to what we view as the biggest surprises to have emerged from the first two weeks of training camp.
Before camp started, everyone knew that the cornerback spot vacated by Cor’Dale Flott would be open for someone to win it. The primary competition for that spot was expected to be the trio of Deonte Banks, rookie Colton Hood, and free-agent Greg Newsome II.
In retrospect, we should have known better, as Harbaugh is not in the business of handing out scholarships to guys just because of their contracts or draft pedigree.
The Giants have been working different combinations at the cornerback spots, with Banks really pushing for one of the spots while Newsome has been pushing equally as hard for another.
That has left Paulson Adebo, who a year ago was one of the team's top free-agent signings, fighting to retain his job.
Many people have been sleeping on Banks given his inconsistencies that have led to struggles, but without question, Banks has the skill set that fits what Dennard Wilson wants to run. If he can continue stringing together good practices, he might emerge as one of the starters on the perimeter this year.
Look at most 53-man roster projections, and they’ll all have receiver Jalin Hyatt not making the roster. But that doesn’t mean that the coaching staff isn’t trying to help him out.
Hyatt, who really doesn’t offer much on special teams, has done a little bit of gunner work in an effort to increase what he has to offer to a football team.
While that probably won’t help his case for a roster spot with the Giants, it’s still a nice move on the part of the coaching staff to exhaust every possibility with the disappointing third-round pick and give him a chance to put additional stuff on film so that he can land somewhere once final cuts are announced.
The Giants took a flier on first-round draft bust Evan Neal, whose size and physical traits undoubtedly appealed to head coach John Harbaugh as he looks to build a more physical offensive line.
But despite his second chance, Neal doesn’t appear to have moved the needle in terms of earning more reps. He was mostly stuck with the third-team offensive line in drills and is not thought to have stood out once the pads go on.
There is still a matter of the upcoming preseason games for Neal to make his case.
Considering how Harbaugh said that Neal sat before him back in the offseason with an enthusiastic attitude and a plan to get better at his craft, it’s still a little bit of a surprise to see that Neal hasn’t been able to make headway in his quest for a roster spot.
Barring a solid showing in the preseason games, it looks like Neal will have to salvage his NFL career elsewhere.
When we last left Malik Nabers, the Giants had just completed their mandatory minicamp, with their star receiver having not been spotted working on the side with trainers as he continued his rehab from a torn ACL.
But then, as the mandatory minicamp wrapped up,  general manager Joe Schoen and Harbaugh both expressed cautious optimism that Nabers would be good to go by Week 1.
Turns out Nabers was indeed a little further along than anyone outside the building thought anticipated, and that’s a good development for a Giants offense that needs its top receiver in the lineup, especially as quarterback Jaxson Dart continues to adjust to working more under center and working with more timing plays.
As was widely expected, Harbaugh ran a physically demanding camp which included six practices in a row, three of which were in full pads. That had some people a little nervous about injuries, given the rotten luck this team has had in that department in years past.
While the Giants didn’t come through the first two weeks completely clean injury-wise—center John Michael Schmitz (protocol), receiver Juju Smith-Schuster (knee), offensive lineman Lucas Patrick (knee), outside linebacker Brian Burns (ankle), and cornerback Dru Phillips (knee) are among those who are dealing with ailments—Harbaugh indicated that those injuries don’t appear to be long-term issues that should keep the players sidelined for the Week 1 opener.
Perhaps even more important, though, is that the players were able to withstand the rigors of Harbaugh’s camp, a testament not only to the individual work each guy put in but also to the strength and conditioning staff, which undoubtedly kept close tabs on the workloads to ensure that no one was overtaxed.

title: Jets Preseason Schedule: Dates, Times and TV Channels
full_text:
The New York Jets are just days away from beginning their preseason slate, meaning it will only be a matter of time before head coach Aaron Glenn and his staff finalize the 53-man roster. Until then, every player on the roster bubble must capitalize on each chance given to them between now and the Aug. 30 deadline, with the preseason being the biggest opportunity to garner goodwill.
The upcoming exhibition slate will be the first crack for Jets rookies and veterans alike to give the fan base a sense of optimism ahead of the regular season. For those wanting to get in on the action, here's everything to know about the Jets' preseason, including the dates and how to watch each game.
After engaging in back-to-back joint practices on Tuesday and Wednesday, the Jets will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the preseason opener at MetLife Stadium. Things will be even more interesting after multiple fights broke out at the first co-practice.
Glenn & Co. will be out for revenge after falling 29-27 to the Bucs in Week 3 last season. New York made a strong comeback effort despite trailing by as many as 17 points; however, a 36-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin as time expired crushed a lot of dreams that afternoon.
It remains to be seen who will be suiting up here, as well as how much they'll play, but Friday's clash will be a good chance for the Jets to test their offseason additions. Whether that's David Bailey— who's been crushing it throughout training camp —or a new veteran arrival like Minkah Fitzpatrick, New York fans will have plenty of reasons to tune in, regardless of the outcome.
The Jets' lone road preseason game will take place in the Steel City. All eyes will be on Mike McCarthy as he prepares for his first year as the Steelers' head coach, giving the Jets every reason to play spoiler on the road and sow some seeds of doubt. Considering how New York is 3-3 in its last six matchups against Pittsburgh, anything is possible.
The Jets also have added motivation stemming from a 34-32 loss to the Steelers in the 2025 season opener. It was a back-and-forth contest that ended on a low note. Much like the loss to the Bucs, the Jets saw their lead over the Steelers evaporate when Chris Boswell connected on a massive 60-yard field goal , giving Pittsburgh the lead with 1:03 remaining on the clock.
Glenn & Co. will also be closer to finalizing the 53-man roster at this point, meaning we'll likely see fewer lineup regulars and more bubble players in the mix. Either way, a win over the Steelers would provide some much-needed confidence ahead of the preseason finale.
As is a preseason tradition, the Jets and Giants will duke it out at MetLife Stadium at the end of the month. The Jets lost by 19 points when they collided last summer, but also notched a 10-6 win over the Giants in their last instance as the "home team" back in 2024.
Nevertheless, given that the two New York teams combined for seven wins last year, it's safe to say that both will want to end the preseason on a high note.
The 53-man roster deadline is only two days after this collision, adding to the pressure that all the players involved will feel. Most roster spots will be decided by then, meaning it'll be crucial for each active Jet to give it their all. Otherwise, they might quickly find themselves on the unemployment line, with it not being guaranteed that another team will come calling.

title: Early Geno Smith Concerns Could Leave the Door Wide Open for Jets QB Controversy
full_text:
As training camp moves along and the start of the preseason quickly inches closer , the quarterback room remains a major focal point for the Jets ahead of the 2026 season.
While projected starter Geno Smith spoke out about the multiple speeding violations and a domestic dispute with an ex-girlfriend that was ultimately closed, that does not change the distraction-filled offseason he has endured. Now, the focus has shifted to his up-and-down performance on the field and the confidence that he needs to instill as QB1.
Smith started off training camp showing why he is a massive upgrade under center for the Jets with his accurate passing and smart decision-making, but it didn't last long. His turnover-prone history has always been a cause for concern and a risk the Jets knew they were taking when they acquired him in a trade with the Raiders earlier in the offseason.
On Tuesday, there was some good and bad from Smith as the team took part in a joint practice with the Buccaneers. According to ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini, Smith " was sharper toward the end, in the red zone , but still not a great practice." He finished 10-of-16 with two interceptions, two touchdowns and a couple of sacks.
Geno Smith was sharper toward the end, in the red zone, but still not a great practice. Had him at 10-for-16, with two INTs, two TDs and a couple of sacks. Offense a little of sync. Good day, though, for TEs Ruckert and Taylor. Isaiah Williams making his move. https://t.co/cTN1BX98yL
Despite the history of turnovers and Tuesday's uneven showing, coaches have made it clear how confident they are in their veteran signal-caller. That said, rookie QB Cade Klubnik has played well over the offseason and could lead to Jets fans wanting a switch early in the season, especially if the turnover woes persist for Smith.
While the offense has struggled to get on the same page at points during training camp, Smith brings his leadership and gives the Jets the experience they have been lacking under center. After all, this was an offense that scored the fourth-fewest points per game (17.6 ppg) and one that has utilized at least three different starting QBs in four of the last five seasons, so his return to the organization was welcomed by coaches and teammates.
Throw in his early statement at training camp under new offensive coordinator Frank Reich's scheme and a plethora of weapons down the field, and it is hard to see him not being the starter under center for at least the majority of the season, if not the entire 2026 campaign. With that said, Smith has thrown nearly as many interceptions (32) as TDs (40) the last two seasons, so there is at least an opening for someone with the upside that Klubnik brings to pose a challenge.
Klubnik has certainly looked like a rookie QB at times throughout the offseason, but the joint practices with the Buccaneers will provide an excellent test for him to show that the flashes can continue to outweigh the mistakes. For the most part, though, Klubnik has been one of the biggest winners of training camp so far with his decision-making, arm talent and accuracy.
In other words, Klubnik has outshined Bailey Zappe and Brady Cook for the QB2 role and should be in the driver's seat to serve as Smith's backup. Now into the third week of training camp, the Jets have to feel better about their backup QB role as Klubnik continues to live up to the hype and put himself in position to learn from the veteran Smith as he develops more confidence and familiarity with the offense.
While the coaches continue to support Smith and put the offense's trust in his control, the turnover-prone history is still hard to ignore, and it would not be the worst thing for a talented rookie like Klubnik to earn some more trust from fans for the starting position.
This appears to be Smith's job to lose for the 2026 season. Rightfully so for a team that could really use some stability at QB, but fans could easily run out of patience with him in the early going if the turnovers become an issue and the option is there to turn to Klubnik.
As much trust as Smith has earned so far with the Jets, this is a team that still needs to take that next step and show that it can win more games with the talent it has put together. If Smith does not make a statement out of the gate and the Jets are back in a familiar position, it may not take long for fans to lose trust and want a switch under center.

title: 4 Winners & 3 Losers From Jets' 1st Joint Practice with Buccaneers: David Bailey Keeps Shining
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. — It's time to separate the men from the boys. The Jets, after weeks of competing against themselves , got the opportunity this week to battle against another NFL foe. While the Buccaneers are not on the 2026 schedule, their pedigree gave the Jets a chance to show just how much they have improved .
Joint practices are always a delicate balance. Fans want their team to play well during the week of buildup, but understand that it's normally not a clear indicator of future success.
Jets fans will be hoping that remains the case, as the Buccaneers appeared to "win" the day with a fiery start to practice that included four separate fights on different fields. While New York did manage to make things competitive later on, it felt like a day Tampa Bay will be confident in winning as opposed to the latter.
As always, there were plenty of winners and losers throughout the day. Let's go to each one now.
It was obvious from the first snap. David Bailey was the Jets' best player on either side of the field today. In one-on-ones, he completely embarrassed Buccaneers tackle Luke Goedeke to the point where the young tackle false-started on the final two plays of the drill. After getting an early jump on the last rep, Goedeke tried to smack talk Bailey, who promptly threw a punch and started a brawl.
Excellent fire and speed, but the Jets would like to see more discipline from their second overall pick (more on that later).
In team drills, Bailey was just as dominant, picking up multiple sacks, including one against Tampa's starters where he orchestrated an excellent rip move and would have tackled Baker Mayfield within two seconds of the snap coming to him.
David Bailey would have just recorded a sack in team drills. Oh man what a move 👀👀 #Jets
Jets fans have never seen a player show this much of an impact in his first-ever training camp. If Bailey can put this together come Week 1, we could be looking at the next great superstar edge rusher.
Let's start with the positives. First, Geno Smith's red-zone period remains his strength, as he threw two touchdowns in the period. Cade Klubnik was also quite solid, albeit with some missed throws as well. New York's quarterback room salvaged the day at the end.
But it doesn't take away from the poor start.
Isaiah Williams finds himself wide open for a deep completion. Geno found him despite pressure. Next play is picked off with Geno going across his body. Just ugly day for Geno #Jets
In a two-drill sequence, Smith failed to complete any pass beyond five yards and was picked off twice, including one that would have gone for a touchdown. Much of New York's offensive struggles stemmed from the defensive blitz disguises that Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles used throughout practice. It was a good lesson to learn from in that case.
But it does not take away from the fact that the Jets' offense stumbled through most of practice. And a big reason for that was Smith's inaccurate throws and poor decision-making.
Tuesday was the best day of training camp for second-year tight end Mason Taylor. He also came through with his best catch. On the first play of a red zone drill, Taylor lept up into the air and caught a deep pass across his body. It was a difficult catch for any receiver to make. But Taylor made it.
That's the kind of play the Jets will need from Taylor going forward, especially with Kenyon Sadiq in workout clothes as he recovers from hernia surgery .
More importantly, Taylor lived over the middle of the field and caught several passes on the day with large completions. Without any drops, the LSU product showed why he is a key cog in the Jets' passing offense today.
Over the last few seasons, it appeared that the Jets struggled mightily with discipline. This year might be the same, and the several fights showed why. Whether it was Armand Membou checking a Buccaneers edge rusher after a play, or Bailey throwing a punch after winning a rep, the Jets need their best players on the field at all times if they are going to be better than last year.
Yet another fight: Membou and A’Shawn Robinson. Membou had his helmet ripped off and took umbrage. And that triggered a melee. #Jets
Fighting won't help anyone. In Membou's case, he watched from the sidelines at the end of practice due to his last fight. New York cannot afford to lose him, and today was a good reminder of that.
Add in several false start penalties and holding calls and the Jets still have a long way to go here.
Mayfield found plenty of wins on the day while attacking zone coverage. What he struggled with was throwing one-on-one, especially against Brandon Stephens. In his second year as the starting corner in New York's secondary, Stephens made multiple good plays in coverage throughout the day.
His best came in a team session and a one-on-one deep shot to Chris Godwin. Mayfield's pass was on the money, but Stephens stepped up in a major way to come through with an excellent deflection. It was the kind of play that showed his improvement from last year.
The Jets are going to have two main problems this season on defense if Tuesday's practice is any indicator of the future. First, New York's aggressive nature with their edge rushers will leave them susceptible to screen passes. Tampa Bay saw plenty of big offensive plays thanks to that very concept.
Second is their four-man front. The Jets built their defense with the unofficial goal of turning more to a 3-4 alignment. In doing so, though, the team also showed its desire to run with four-man fronts. Throughout the last week, the four-man fronts have been gashed against the run, just as they were today.
New York's defensive line is going to be better than last year. But it will be a challenge if they can't win with four down linemen and need five to do so. It's something to look out for going forward.
Before practice, Jets receiver coach Shawn Jefferson turned heads when he called Isaiah Williams the "heartbeat" of the offense. Normally, that title should befall the likes of Garrett Wilson or Smith. Instead, Williams showed exactly why today.
He wasn't perfect. Williams dropped a touchdown pass in the red zone late. But throughout the day, he seemed to be the only one willing to mix things up against the Buccaneers' defense, which had toyed with the Jets' offense.
In one run play, Williams decked a Buccaneers linebacker while blocking. On the next play, Williams made a catch and came up jawing at the opposition.
It's good to have those types of players on the roster. It's even better that Williams continues to show his mettle every time he touches the ball.

title: 3 Most Important Jets to Watch in Friday's Preseason Opener: Cade Klubnik's NFL Debut
full_text:
It’s been over seven months since we’ve seen the Jets, and that streak ends on Friday with the team taking on the Buccaneers at MetLife Stadium after a week of joint practices .
Although it’ll be exciting to see Gang Green finally play a somewhat meaningful game, fans shouldn’t expect to see any of the star or marquee players suit up. If they do, it’ll only be for a drive or two.
Instead, we should expect the Jets' coaching staff to use this game to deploy players in a position battle or at the back end of the depth chart. These additional reps provide the coaching staff with an opportunity to evaluate the players and the strengths of each position group.
With that being said, here are three Jets’ players to keep an eye on against the Bucs.
Cade Klubnik is coming off an impressive week in training camp, which he capped off with a 60-yard completion to Isaiah Williams in last Saturday’s scrimmage . Overall, the 2026 fourth-round pick has had a solid camp and is in a strong position to obtain the QB2 role, especially as his success continued against the Buccaneers on Tuesday , per Jets OnSI 's Nick Faria.
Taking a look across the field, #Jets secondary has held their own as Cade Klubnik delivered a nice throw to Ruckert for a deep completion. Good stuff from the rookie.
However, camp play alone won’t secure him the job. Klubnik must stand out in preseason play to increase his chances of earning the backup spot and convince the organization not to add another quarterback to the group.
Although general manager Darren Mougey didn’t indicate that he’s bringing in another quarterback, he was asked about potentially adding a veteran to the room before the start of training camp. Mougey responded that he’s always checking the market for players at all positions.
If Klubnik wants to shut down talks about potentially bolstering the quarterback room, he must protect the football and prove he's capable of moving the offense downfield.
Entering training camp, Chip Trayanum wasn’t considered a candidate to earn a roster spot. Despite this, the Jets’ unofficial depth chart lists him as the RB3 alongside Isaiah Davis and ahead of Kene Nwangwu.
Of course, this list should be taken with a grain of salt given that it was compiled by the team’s communication staff rather than the coaching staff. But with Davis sidelined for the next couple of weeks with a knee injury, Traynaum has a chance to make a strong impression .
Traynaum’s bruising, down-hill running style makes him an intriguing player to watch against Tampa Bay. If he can pick up tough yards after contact and secure the football, he could put himself in a position to earn a spot on the practice squad.
Another surprise from New York’s unofficial depth chart list is Tyler Baron being on the fourth team behind Kingsley Jonathan and Nathan Voorhis.
Baron is already considered a long shot to make the final 53-man roster, but his listing on the depth chart shows that he has a lot of ground to make up. Despite this, he displayed some potential last season, recording four pressures in 48 pass-rush snaps , per Pro Football Focus.
Against the Buccaneers, Baron must showcase his development as both a pass-rusher and run-defender as he competes for a roster spot in a crowded edge rush room. New York ranked amongst the worst teams in both categories last year, and if Baron can prove to be an effective contributor in either area, it could significantly improve his chances of making the roster.
But if he fails to capitalize, don’t be surprised if Baron ends up being a cut candidate by the end of August.

title: One Jet Whose Offseason Struggles Shouldn't Worry Fans
full_text:
As the Jets head into the third week of training camp and prepare for their first preseason game against the Buccaneers on Friday, the 2026 roster will begin to take shape even more as players get a chance to impress on the field against some different competition.
Someone who impressed last season and is one of the most important players on this team is defensive end Will McDonald IV, who led the Jets with eight sacks in 2025 and excels as a pass rusher. He acknowledged that he needs to improve against the run, an area the Jets were the fourth-worst group in last season, but there have been some causes for concern regarding his quiet offseason play so far.
That said, there are a few reasons why concerns regarding McDonald's offseason are overblown.
McDonald has since bulked up as he tries to improve against the run and is athletic for his position. He still needs to show more at training camp after what has been a silent performance so far, but the 15th overall selection in 2023 is the only player on the team the last two seasons to record more than six sacks, and his explosiveness has made him difficult for opposing teams to slow down.
Additionally, second overall draft pick David Bailey has been one of the biggest winners of training camp so far, and the early buzz surrounding him is certainly warranted as the hype continues to explode . That alone has created some additional pressure and only amplified the silent showing that McDonald has had thus far.
Both Bailey and McDonald have similar strengths and weaknesses, excelling against the pass while still trying to improve and make some gains against the run. Of the eight sacks that McDonald registered last season, four of them came against the Cleveland Browns, so it is imperative that he becomes more of an every-down player and not just someone who can come in and have a big performance before taking a step back.
With that said, McDonald is credited with 18.5 of the Jets' 68 sacks the last two seasons, so there is a good chance he replicates that success once again . For a team that had the second-fewest sacks (26) in the league in 2025, that level of pressure from McDonald cannot be ignored, even if he has not boasted Pro Bowl-caliber numbers and is lacking some of the big plays you would expect from a former first-rounder.
After all, Pro Football Focus gave McDonald the 37th-ranked pass-rush grade (71.0) out of 115 qualified edge defenders last season. Granted, his overall grade (59.2) was just 85th, and his run-defense grade (41.6) was a dismal 112th, but he still brings some explosiveness and athleticism to a unit that has depended on him to be a constant disruptor on the edge.
At the same time, the 2026 season will be a critical one for McDonald as the Jets decide if he is worth keeping around in the long haul . The Jets brought in free-agent acquisitions Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare, with both possessing better skills as run defenders. Enagbare, specifically, is already making a strong impact against the pass.
Throw in the fact that McDonald only played 57.48% of the Jets' total defensive snaps in 2025, and it is even clearer that he needs to step up as a more reliable down-to-down defender—especially with the increased competition he is facing at the position now.
Even with that in mind, McDonald has shown to be the type of sack artist the Jets have lacked as a whole recently. Sure, he still needs to develop into more of an all-around edge defender the team can feel comfortable with alongside Bailey, but he has become one of the most valuable components of the Jets' pass rush and should not be doubted yet despite a silent outing in training camp.

title: 3 Jets Are Thriving (While 2 Struggle) in Training Camp: Bailey, McDonald Heading in Opposite Directions
full_text:
Looking back at the first two weeks of the Jets' training camp, fans should feel encouraged and optimistic about how the team looks heading into joint practices and their first preseason opener vs. the Buccaneers on Friday.
The position battles have been highly competitive, the revamped defensive line continues to impress, and Geno Smith has provided stability and hope at the quarterback position.
While this year’s training camp looked significantly more promising than the previous few, it also had its share of struggles. The battle for the QB2 spot has been underwhelming , while the secondary hasn’t played up to expectations.
As the Jets head into the third week of training camp, let’s dive into the three Jets who are thriving and the two who are struggling.
No one has shined brighter than David Bailey in the first two weeks.
The former Texas Tech Raider has been everything and more than what fans expected him to be when the team selected him with the second pick in this year’s draft. So far, he’s stood out as one of the best defensive players in the practices, consistently creating pressure against Armand Membou and Olu Fashanu.
While his elite explosiveness and arsenal of pass-rush moves have stood out the most over the course of camp, all eyes have been on the rookie’s play against the run. Although Bailey wasn’t regarded as a bad run-defender in college, earning a 76.4 run-defense grade , per Pro Football Focus, last season, it’s widely viewed as an area he must develop in.
From last Saturday’s practice, it appears Bailey has shown signs of improvement in containing the run on the edge. Jets OnSI’s Nick Faria also noted that his run defense took a “step in the right direction," which is an encouraging sign.
The 2026 season is an extremely important one for Will McDonald IV, as he’s eligible to sign a contract extension next offseason. However, the former 2023 first-round selection has gotten off on the wrong foot.
One of the areas McDonald needed to improve upon was as a run-defender, as he posted a41.6 run-defense grade last season, ranking 112th among 115 qualifying edge rushers. Through the first two weeks, McDonald has remained relatively quiet in this area.
The four-year veteran was also expected to be New York’s best pass-rusher. Instead, both Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare have been putting more pressure on the quarterback and have been more productive than McDonald.
If McDonald wants to earn a lucrative extension next offseason, he’ll need to become a consistent contributor against the run while replicating the pressure production he showed in the 2024 season.
There were several reasons why the Jets traded back into the first round to select Omar Cooper Jr, and the former Hoosiers receiver continues to show why New York was so eager to get him.
Cooper has flashed his playmaking ability and stretch-field potential throughout camp, as he’s already emerged as a down-field target for Smith. His electric 4.42-second 40-yard dash speed , combined with his refined route-running, gives him the tools to be a dangerous receiver alongside Garrett Wilson.
The Jets desperately needed more explosiveness in the passing game after finishing last with just 27 completions of 20-plus yards last season. With Cooper in the mix, New York is hoping the rookie can change that.
While he’s had some up-and-down moments in camp, he’s firmly established himself as the WR2 behind Wilson.
When the Jets claimed Jason Sanders off waivers in June, the assumption was the former 2020 first-team All-Pro kicker would quickly establish himself as the starting kicker.
Unfortunately for Sanders, that hasn’t happened yet. The kicking job competition between him and Cade York has been one of the more intriguing camp battles, but Sanders hasn’t done enough to separate himself from the battle .
Although he’s been the more efficient and consistent kicker in the past, he’s struggled to find that consistency in camp. Last Thursday, Sanders converted on just two of his five attempts, missing from 47, 51, and 53 yards, while York nailed three of his four attempts.
With preseason coming up, Sanders must find his rhythm or risk losing the job to the younger kicker.
When the Jets signed Dane Belton in free agency, hardly anyone anticipated that he would emerge as a legitimate candidate for the starting safety spot alongside Minkah Fitzpatrick.
But through these first two weeks, Belton has done exactly that. The former 2022 fourth-round pick has had multiple pass breakups, an interception, and has consistently made plays at the line of scrimmage.
While he’s been one of the few surprises in camp , we shouldn’t be that shocked. Last season, Belton had 120 tackles and forced four turnovers–the same number of takeaways the Jets’ defense produced as a whole.
If Belton can continue to make plays, he’ll strengthen his case against Andre Cisco and Malachi Moore for the final starting safety spot.
