title: 3 Jets  to Watch During Joint Practices With Buccaneers: Cade Klubnik's 1st Real Test
full_text:
When the Jets and Buccaneers take the field to open joint practices on Tuesday, they'll do so with plenty left to prove.
Tampa is coming off a year in which they missed the postseason for the first time in five years. They also have contract questions about their starting quarterback, along with a head coach on the hot seat. New York, meanwhile, has its own hot seat for head coach Aaron Glenn and a young roster that is trying to be better than the three wins they managed to grab last year.
As is always the case with joint practices, each team has players with a spotlight on them with something to prove. Today, we'll go over the three Jets to watch throughout this week's joint practices with the Bucs.
The jury is still out on Cade Klubnik. In some practices, he looks like an excellent quarterback with the potential to be even better than his fourth-round draft selection. In other practices are filled with key mistakes.
In short, Klubnik has looked like a well polished rookie: major flashes but obvious concerns at times.
The next few practices against the Buccaneers defense will be an excellent test for him. Throughout camp, the one consistent positive is that the moment hasn't looked too big for Klubnik. Even when he makes a mistake, he doesn't look overwhelmed on the next play.
Will that continue against Tampa Bay head coach Todd Bowles's exotic blitz packages? Will he be able to accurately deliver passes against Tampa's maligned pass defense?
If Klubnik is going to prove his worthiness of being the immediate backup to Geno Smith, then these joint days of work will be a key part of the test.
Arguably, the group under the most pressure this week will be New York's secondary. They have gone back and forth with the Jets' offense, but joint practices against Baker Mayfield and Tampa Bay's passing unit will be the deciding factor if the group really is improved or if their wins are nothing more than blips on the radar.
Chief among the questions will be whether AZ Thomas can handle himself against Tampa's collection of top wideouts like Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. Egbuka had an excellent rookie season, while Godwin's 2025 was full of injuries.
If Thomas can hold his own, it won't just prove to the Jets he's capable of locking down some of the best receiving corps in football, but also show he's ready to be the full-time starter in his cornerback position battle .
It's been the summer of AD Mitchell for well over a month now. The former Colt has looked like the perfect complement to Garrett Wilson thanks to his route-running and speed. If he's able to put it all together this year, the Jets' offense will be far more exciting than people realize.
This week will be an interesting test, though.
The Buccaneers do not have a true All-Pro-caliber cornerback on the roster. In many ways, their secondary is the weakest part of their team. If Mitchell is going to take the next step in his development and standout summer, he'll need to have a big week against the Bucs.
He's certainly capable of it, especially since Tampa Bay was 27th in terms of passing yards allowed last season. So long as Mitchell keeps up his quality level of play, the Jets' offense will continue to look solid.

title: My Thoughts on Jets Fans' Concerns About Training Camp 'Toughness'
full_text:
My latest appearance on "The Jake Asman Show" on Sunday ended with an interesting question from a listener .
The main question posed was an interesting one: should the Jets be practicing harder and more physically, in a similar vein to the Giants, than they have to this point?
One fan pointed to the Giants with new head coach John Harbaugh as a prime example of a team working for over two and a half hours on the field to be ready for the season. In their mind, Harbaugh coming from a winning program means the Jets should try to emulate Big Blue's physical practices rather than the more classroom-heavy focus the team currently has.
But there are multiple ways to have a successful training camp, and Gang Green's training camp has been just as competitive as any other.
Gone are the days when physical training camps were a requirement for teams around the NFL. Contenders such as the Eagles and Rams are notorious for shorter practices and instead focusing on efficient work throughout the day.
Other teams like Harbaugh's past roster in Baltimore and the Chiefs are notorious for more grueling practices as well as stretching the limit of their work to the maximum allowed by the CBA.
Some Jets fans will point to the Chiefs and Harbaugh's past as reasons to have longer, more physical camps. But preparing for a year is not an exact science. The Eagles and Rams have had plenty of success with their efficient approach. They've also been relatively healthy when the later parts of the season arrive.
Coincidence? Not quite. Teams that focus heavily on injury prevention tend to be the ones that don't have to worry about missing a key player towards the end of the year. The Jets understand this and appear to prefer to be a team that has their full collection of talent for as long as possible.
In the grand scheme of things, Glenn is not wrong to push for efficient practices . He believes that preparing the team does not need two and a half hours on the field and instead focuses on specific situations within a game. New York notoriously practices in-game moments (third-and-four or second-and-long situations) as a way to prepare the team.
Will it work? Only time will tell. But to assume that the Jets will not be as prepared as the Giants will be because Harbaugh has them out for longer is nothing more than folly. An NFL season is more about a war of attrition. Harbaugh, specifically, should know this, as several of his most recent teams have missed the playoffs due to a rash of injuries.
Again, perhaps a tougher training camp schedule does not immediately correlate to more injuries later in the year. But there's a reason why organizations like the Eagles and Rams have become consistent contenders. Their lighter practices show that there is more than one way to be prepared for a season without running an old-school style camp.
Glenn is hoping for the same with his team.
It'll be up to the Jets to prove him right on the field when the games actually matter.

title: Jets Miss Out on Perfect Opportunity to Bolster OL Depth Before Preseason
full_text:
The Jets are getting into the thick of training camp as their preseason opener against the Buccaneers quickly approaches on Friday.
While much of the focus at this point is on settling some position battles and narrowing down the roster to 53 players , it is also not the worst time to pivot to free agency when an opportunity presents itself.
Although offensive tackle and 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace made perfect sense after the Patriots released him on Monday, it did not take long for the Dolphins to acquire him in a trade along with a 2029 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, per ESPN reporter Mike Reiss.
Trade! The Patriots announce that G Caedan Wallace has been traded to the Dolphins along with a 2029 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
The 26-year-old entered training camp as a backup before getting demoted to third-stringer. Prior to that, he appeared in six games and made two starts in an injury-riddled rookie season before making the move from tackle to guard ahead of his sophomore season, which included four more games.
With that said, he could have been the depth piece the Jets needed on the offensive line, especially if you consider the struggles that Max Mitchell, the current backup at left tackle, had last season with a 27.8 pass-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus in 19 opportunities. Outside of 2024, he has not been a great blocker, and the competition from Wallace could have either lit a fire under him or gotten something out of Mitchell.
As someone who was moved to guard last season with the Patriots, Wallace could have given the Jets more depth and versatility if things worked out differently. While the Jets have strengthened their OL in recent years with fellow first-round picks Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou, the depth behind them centers more around players who are still trying to prove themselves.
From Mitchell and Chukwuma Okorafor to the addition of undrafted free agents Courtland Ford and Xavier Hill, the potential signing of Wallace would have added more competition to the position when you factor in his unproven career up to this point as well.
The Jets ultimately re-signed Mitchell to a one-year, $2 million deal earlier this offseason. He has 17 career starts with the franchise, but the No. 111 pick in the 2022 draft has failed to deliver with nine sacks allowed and 28 hurries across 568 pass-blocking snaps, per PFF .
With only one year on his deal, it is entirely possible that the Jets give up on Mitchell if the struggles persist . Not to mention, Wallace still has two years remaining on his rookie deal, and the Jets are in the top half of the league in cap space ($27.3 million, 11th), according to OverTheCap , so it would not have taken much to cut Wallace if everything went south anyway.
Furthermore, Wallace ended up with another AFC East franchise, and it would not have been a tall task for Gang Green to acquire him, considering the low price the Dolphins got for him. There is also some familiarity with Fashanu after the two were teammates at Penn State, which is just one more sign of the missed opportunity the Jets had here to increase the competition on the OL and potentially create a spark that otherwise has been missing from the depth pieces.
Instead, Wallace finds himself elsewhere in the division, and the Jets head into the preseason slate after squandering an opportunity to add to their OL depth. Facing the Dolphins twice per season, though, it won't take long to find out if the Jets were right to avoid making a trade offer to the Patriots.

title: 3 Key Matchups Jets Fans Must Know Before Joint Practices vs. Buccaneers: All Eyes on the Secondary
full_text:
For two weeks, the Jets have competed heavily amongst themselves to prove that last year's three-win campaign was nothing more than a fluke under head coach Aaron Glenn. Over the last 15 years, though, New York fans know better than to hope without seeing drastic improvement on the field.
If the Jets are going to take the next step as a rebuilding roster, then their first true test comes this week with joint practices against the Buccaneers on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Since Tom Brady arrived back in 2020, the Buccaneers have been a perennial playoff team, with appearances in five of the last six seasons. Despite missing the postseason last year, Tampa Bay remains a playoff contender.
Which is why the Jets will be keen to watch three specific matchups throughout the week to see how good their talent stacks up.
This is the matchup every Jets fan will want to see. Through the first two weeks of camp, second-overall pick David Bailey has been nothing short of spectacular as an edge rusher. His quick get-off is one of the fastest I've ever seen. He is also improving in run defense as each practice comes.
Going up against Armand Membou and Olu Fashanu has been a good test . Now a different one is about to begin. Wirfs is an All-Pro and five-time Pro Bowler. He is Tampa Bay's best offensive lineman and has been since he was drafted, as shown by his having the second-best overall Pro Football Focus grade among tackles last season (92.7).
For as good as Membou and Fashanu are, they are still very young and developing. Wirfs is already an excellent player. This will be an important test for Bailey. Standing out in camp practices against your teammates is one thing.
Dominating against an All-Pro is something else. And it's why this matchup will have everyone keeping an eye on the trenches this week.
Without Mike Evans on the roster, the Buccaneers have the perception of a lesser receiving core. That couldn't be further from the truth, though. After an excellent rookie season, the Bucs are hoping for Emeka Egbuka to take the next step in his development. The veteran presence of Chris Godwin should help as well.
It will be a difficult week for the Jets' new-look secondary .
AZ Thomas, Brandon Stephens, Jarvis Brownlee, and even Nahshon Wright will be tested in ways they simply haven't been to this point. If they perform well, it could send a message to the Jets' coaching staff that the group is ready to take the next step on their own.
If the Jets' defensive backs struggle, though, it may very well be a red herring for further concerns going forward. Going up against Geno Smith and New York's receiving core in practice is one thing. It will be a different test altogether with Baker Mayfield— who had a revenge game against the Jets last season—in tow.
A small contingent of Jets fans was clamoring for the organization to draft the edge rusher out of Miami over the likes of Bailey and Arvell Reese. Through the start of camp, it looks like the Buccaneers came away with a top player at just the 15th overall slot.
It will be a different test than the one New York's offensive tackles have dealt with throughout camp. Rueben Bain Jr,'s's short arm length (the reason for his draft drop) hasn't been seen as a legitimate concern so far. Will that be the case when the Jets' superior tackles go against him?
As for Membou and Fashanu, Bain's raw power should give them a good test as opposed to dealing with Bailey's speed for the last few weeks. A strong couple of days from both players should prove they are both more than ready for the start of the season.

title: 5 Winners And 4 Losers from Day 10 of Eagles Training Camp: Jake Elliott Has Been Near Perfect
full_text:
Another day of Philadelphia Eagles training camp has passed. Another day some players shined and some disappointed.
There's starting to become a clearer picture of how this roster as shaped out, and who will be the players to watch this preseason. Tuesday's evaluations of practice and the overreactions said it al l.
With the Eagles having a walkthrough on Wednesday, who are the winners and losers from Day 10 of practice. This is a good indicator how how things are going for some players this summer.
Elijah Moore: The wins keep coming for Moore, and the stacking up of good practices. Moore is starting to show his deep-ball ability, as he connected on a 47-yard touchdown pass from Jalen Hurts that was arguably the play of the day in practice. Moore is making a push for a roster spot, and deserves the nod over Holywood Brown right now. Let's see how Moore plays this preseason, but there's a lot to like when it comes to his roster chances.
Jake Elliott: On a windy morning, Elliott shined when it was his turn to kick field goals. Elliott went 6-for-6 in practice, and improved to 25-of-26 this camp. That's why the Eagles didn't bring in competition for Elliott this summer, as they believed he would fix whatever physical and psychological issues he had. Elliott has been excellent kicking in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and needs to transfer that to NFL stadiums -- including his own this fall.
Micah Morris: Getting back on the field has been a plus for Morris, as the sixth-round rookie is starting to show his physicality. Hurts when a player misses time, especially when that unavailability allowed Willie Lampkin to pass Morris on the depth chart. The Eagles have been working Morris at left and right guard, and he's played well at both spots. There may be a roster spot for Morris after all.
Tyler Steen: The breakout player this year may be Steen, who had a solid year at right guard last season considering Cam Jurgens and Lane Johnson were injured. Steen has been consistent in 1-on-1s and had a victory over Jalen Carter on Tuesday (which isn't easy to do). The Eagles will go as far as the offensive line can take them and if Steen continues to improve, they may be the best unit in the league again.
Byron Young: Another good practice for Young, as he beat Drew Kendall and sacked Andy Dalton when the second team offense was out there. Kendall has had a good camp (and a good day on Tuesday), so this was a massive win for Young. There's a case to be made Young deserves more snaps this year, and he's earning them -- even as the No. 4 defensive tackle in a loaded position.
Cameron Williams: There isn't much depth at tackle behind Fred Johnson, and Williams proved it on Tuesday. Tarron Jackson was signed two days ago and easily beat Williams in 1-on-1s for a sack. No matter how you slice it, not a good look. Is Williams even going to be on the 53-man roster? Someone may have to be that fifth tackle, but Williams has not helped his chances. This is why it's hard to envision Johnson getting cut.
Will Shipley: The hits keep coming for Shipley, who hasn't been good through 10 practices . Running backs were working on blitz pickup on Tuesday, and Shipley was struggling in that department. Whether Shipley earns the RB3 job or not is up in the air, but he has to show something this preseason to prove he's worth keeping around. Elijah Mitchell is out of the competition after he was waived with an injury settlement and Dameon Pierce has been solid -- if not spectacular -- in camp. The job is still Shipley's to lose.
Tariq Woolen: The best player in Eagles minicamp this spring has been okay this summer. Woolen hasn't been great, but also hasn't impressed. He gets beat on a lot of moves in 1-on-1s and hasn't flashed in coverage. Woolen is still a starter and his evaluation will come starting Week 1. He just hasn't been as dominant as he was in the spring. Woolen will need to work on defending out routes through the rest of camp.
Hollywood Brown: Feels like every day Brown shows up here. He had a drop in 1-on-1s on Tuesday and the bad practices are stacking up. Darius Cooper has been great and Elijah Moore has been racking up good practices, which puts Brown on the bubble for a roster spot. Again, how did we get to his point? Brown needs a sharp preseason -- probably more than any player on this roster.

title: Overreactions From Day 10 of Eagles Training Camp: Eli Stowers Set For TE2 Role?
full_text:
Hard to believe, but the Philadelphia Eagles are through 10 training camp practices.
There have been plenty of developments over the first 10 practices open to the media, and practice 10 had no shortage of storylines. preparation and game tape come into play, a sthe Eagles get set to fac ethe Baltimore Ravens in Week 1 of the preseaosn Saturday night.
With this practice, a few observations came into play. Thanks to observations, we have overreactions.
Which overreactions are overreactions and which are reality?
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Stowers had a good practice on Tuesday, making a few strong catches and becoming a valuable red zone target in this offense. He's had a string of a few good practices , which is a massive improvement over the poor start to this camp.
Stowers isn't under the "losers" section of camp anymore . He has bene improving over the past week, enough where there should be some consideration for the TE2 role over Johnny Mundt. Is Stowers ready for that job?
If Stowers continues to improve and makes plays in the preseason, he'll get out of the disappointing rookie class. Stowers has shown a lot of positive gains in the past few practices, a very encouraging sign for the Eagles.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Moore had the highlight play of Tuesday's practice, catching a long touchdown pass from Jalen Hurts. This is the type of deep ball prowess the Eagles are seeking from one of the wideouts in their offense.
Every day, Moore is making a case to be on this roster. He should be on the 53 over Hollywood Brown if we stopped the count after 10 practices. Moore just keeps getting better and better as the practices wear on, even now he's catching deep passes in these sessions.
There's a lot to like about Moore, who runs smooth routes and has been making good catches when Hurts targets him. He could be the WR5 on this team, and he's also a veteran (like Brown).
If the choice right now is between Moore and Brown, Moore gets the nod.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Robinson has been another player that has had his fair share of criticism. He's had a slow start to this training camp and also found himself into the cut candidates section , but that may be changing.
Not only did Robinson have a sack on Tuesday, but he's been getting into the backfield of late. This is a positive development from a player who was stuck on the third team the majority of camp. Robinson still has a ways to go, but has this in his back pocket.
Being a fourth-round draft pick form last season buys you some time. Robinson is getting the benefit of the doubt here, and he'll likely make the roster if he shows enough improvements. Right now, that seems to be the case.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Boy did this blow up for no reason. DeJean was listed as the starting safety on the Eagles depth chart (which is complied by the communications department), but that is partially true.
DeJean is the starting safety in the base defense, which the Eagles run less than 20% of the time. He goes to the nickel defense, which the Eagles run over 80% of the time. When DeJena is in nickel, either Marcus Epps or Michael Carter are the starting safeties -- a battle that is still going on.
The depth chart is the depth chart, but the Eagles have DeJean in the slot for a reason. No need to overreact here.

title: Ranking Eagles WRs After 10 Training Camp Practices: How Close Is Elijah Moore To Bubble
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver battle has been one of the most intriguing ones of training camp. The WR2 battle was settled early, but so was the WR5.
There is another battle that emerged as a result of Darius Cooper playing well. Who is going to be the WR4? This battle will be settled over the preseason an din the next couple weeks.
After a week of practice, all the wide receivers on the roster were graded -- based on how they performed in training camp practice. This time, let's do wide receiver rankings with two weeks and 10 training camp practices in the books
Where does each wide receiver stand with Week 1 of the preseason this weekend?
The Eagles aren't going to rush DeVonta Smith back from a hamstring injury, and nor should they. They can Smith in bubble wrap until Week 1 at this rate, since he will be the WR1.
This passing game can't flow without Smith, and they need him in order to win football games. Smith is set to take his game to the next level, but the Eagles have to make sure he's 100% on September 13.
Wicks has taken the reins as the WR2, having a strong first week of practice. While Wicks has played well, Makai Lemon has been inured and Hollywood Brown has been underwhelming.
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni is a fan of Wicks, comparing him to Keenan Allen on multiple occasions. All Wicks has done is run routes well and catch the football, becoming a trusted weapon in the offense.
The Eagles just have to see Wicks play in a game. That will come Week 1.
There's a argument that Cooper could be ranked higher than Wicks . Every practice Cooper has shined, emerging from a bubble player to essentially a roster lock.
Cooper is more than a WR5 in this offense. He could be the WR4 and maybe even a WR3. Thanks to Wicks and Cooer, the Eagles can take this slowly with Makai Lemon (which isn't the most ideal scenario).
If the Eagles are looking for a red zone target, Cooper may be the guy.
Moore has played his way to a roster afterthought on the roster bubble , maybe even a roster spot (pending on if he can beat out Hollywood Brown). The Eagles could use a slot receiver with makai Lemon on the mend, which is where Moore enters the picture.
Moore has typically been a good route runner, and a fresh start with the Eagles may have been what he needed. He's making it difficult for the Eagles to cut him.
Brown has been underwhelming in camp, getting outplayed by Cooper and Moore. He was a dark horse for the No. 2 spot in camp, but has fallen to competing for a roster spot . The Eagles have $5 million reasons to stick with Brown, and he'll get every opportunity this preseason.
The final roster spot may be between Brown and Moore. This preseason will be important for both wideouts.
Lemon has missed a week of practice, but even when he was practicing the rookie first-round pick wasn't standing out. Fair to state Lemon has been a disappointment so far .
Every practice Lemon misses, he does't get the opportunity to work with Jalen Hurts and the offense. The timing hasn't been there with Hurts because Lemon hasn't practiced and he has a lot of catching up to do.
Don't expect Lemon to be a major contributor in this offense come Week 1 at this rate.
Watkins still has the speed to make plays, but he's a long shot to make this roster. He has gotten open on some deep balls this camp, even if the results haven't been there.
Perhaps Watkins ends up on the practice squad again. He's adapted to the new offense.
The success in the spring hasn't translated in the summer. Cooper took the WR5 job from Wilson early, and Wilson hasn't been a threat for the job. He's unlikely to make the roster at this point, no matter how well he blocks.
Covey had a good start to training camp prior to a hamstring injury keeping him out for around a week. The best chance Covey has of making this roster is punt returner, but even that is a long shot.
Another player who could find a way onto this team as kick returner, Ezukanma has made a few nice plays in training camp. He's still considered a roster long shot.
The former seventh-round pick has made some nice catches in camp, even getting some looks with the second team due to all the injuries at wide receiver. Toure will get a lot of reps this preseason.
The former minicamp standout -- and third-round pick of the 49ers -- hasn't been noticeable this summer. He's another one that could improve his stock this preseason.

title: Hollywood Brown Losing Grip on Roster Spot as New Training Camp Battle Emerges
full_text:
Two wide receiver battles were the talk of the early portion of Philadelphia Eagles training camp. Both have been settled .
Dontayvion Wicks is going to be the WR2 come Week 1 while Darius Cooper locked up a roster spot as the WR5. Thanks to Cooper becoming the darling of camp, a new wide reciever battle has emerged.
Could Cooper actually become the WR4 come Week 1? Maybe even the WR3?
Let's focus on WR4, as that job is wide open . Cooper has played his way onto the Eagle sroster (again), as it would be shocking if he didn't make the 53-man roster. Elijah Moore has also had a good camp, playing his way towards a roster spot -- even though he's still on the bubble.
Where does that leave Hollywood Brown? Is there a way Brown doesn't make the 53?
This WR4 battle is going to play a significant role in the rest of training camp and the preseason. A battle no one saw coming.
Brown is a veteran wide receiver, who the Eagles signed a $5 million deal for this season (fully guaranteed). Essentially, the Eagles have $5 million reasons to give Brown this job.
While $5 million isn't "real" money in NFL circles, the Eagles are going to give Brown every chance to hold off Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore. Brown hasn't had the best start to camp, not being the deep-ball receiver he was in the spring (with shells and shorts on).
Brown still has a dynamic to the Eagles offense with his ability to track down deep passes and the proficiency to generate yards after the catch. The Eagles also aren't relying on Brown to carry the pass game either, which will be the job of DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, and Dontayvion Wicks.
There are reservations regarding Brown's roster spot, but Brown still should make this team. Pressure is mounting based on how Cooper and Moore are performing in camp.
All Cooper has been doing this camp is stack up good practices. He's become one of the most trusted pass catchers for Jalen Hurts, even having close to double-digit receptions on Day 9 of training camp. Monday was Cooper's best practice to date, a showcase of how good he's been ithis summer.
Cooper has been the third-best receiver this summer , and there's a case to be made he's been the second-best wideout in camp (over Dontayvion Wicks). Cooper continues to shine when given the opportunity, and is in serious consideration for the WR4 spot.
There's a bigger role for Cooper on this roster, based on how he's played this summer. He's the most improved player on the roster.
Thanks to the emergence of Wicks and Cooper, the Eagles can ease Lemon into the offense whenever he comes back. Lemon has been out for a week with a hamstring injury, and the Eagles don't believe it to be a long-term concern.
Lemon should still be the WR3 by default since he was a first-round pick. This isn't someone the Eagles can redshirt, no matter how well Cooper has played. What does it mean for the Eagles that an undrafted free agent from last season is currently better than their first-round pick from this year?
Writing off Lemon is premature, but there are concerns when he'll figure things out this year -- or if he can figure them out.
Moore has stacked up some good practices as well, and basically plays the same role as Brown. He's not better at tracking the deep ball like Brown is, but he's a crisp route runner and can makes tough catches.
If the Eagles want the quarterback to get the ball out quickly, Moore is a good fit to get open and make the play. Perhaps Moore just needed a fresh start aftera  few tough years.
The biggest competition for Brown's roster spot is Moore, who is only making $1.175 million this year. Moore (26) is also three years younger than Brown (29), so he's someone the Eagles could further develop.
Bottom line -- Moore is making it difficult for the Eagles to cut him.

title: What We Learned On Day 10 of Eagles Training Camp: Elijah Moore Pushing For Roster Spot
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Day 10 of Eagles camp is in the books, an hour-and- 45-minute run-heavy “green” practice, featuring everything from a live field-goal period to the always-fun 1-on-1s where the running backs try to hold off the linebackers in pass protection.
The team periods are always the highlight, and that was no exception today, with the highlight coming on a long developing route that got Elijah Moore matched up with Andre’ Sam in single coverage. Jalen Hurts took advantage with a strike for a 47-yard touchdown.
Overall, though, it was a run-heavy session with plenty of pistol mixed in with under-center reps. By and large, the top three backs: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley looked effective, but it’s tough to gauge when there is no tackling to the ground.
Hurts also had an impressive connection on a fastball to Dontayvion Wicks on the sideline.
The offense one-upped the defense in a penalty-plagued four-minute period, while the first-team rushing attack came through to convert with just two Barkley runs.
Defensively, Jalyx Hunt added to his impressive summer by harassing Hurts throughout the session, Cooper DeJean flashed on an inside blitz that got home, and Quinyon Mitchell had another interception in 7-on-7 work.
Mitchell got dinged up during 1-on-1s and did not return for the rest of team drills. The All-Pro was getting worked on by trainers and put his helmet on, indicating a desire to get back in. However, this time of year, the Eagles are going to remain cautious.
With Jonathan Jones already out with a shoulder injury, second-year player Mac McWilliams got Mitchell’s first-team reps.
-- The Eagles started team work with a field-goal period. While Jake Elliott was practicing, the wind picked up considerably, and he pushed two kicks to the left. When things went live, Elliott adjusted and made all six of his kicks – from 32, 37, 40, 44, 46 and 50.
The Eagles also tried a pooch punt from Elliott, which Braden Mann nearly downed near the goal line, before it slipped in for a touchdown.
Long snapper Rocco Underwood seemed to be more consistent today with his FG snaps.
-During a bracket drill, Zack Baun had a little fun with Britain Covey, tweaking the WR from the back of the bracket before tackling him after the swipe from the underneath defender. Covey got his revenge on a second rep by using his short-area quickness to slip by Baun untouched.
-- Spent a lot of time watching the RBs trying to hold up in pass pro against the linebackers. It wasn’t pretty with Jihaad Campbell and Smael Mondon standing out.
Campbell dipped around Bigsby with ease, and Mondon had fullback Carson Steele overmatched with speed on two reps. Zack Baun took Barkley on an outside move and undrafted rookie Deontae Lawson used an inside move to dispatch of newcomer Ja’Quinden Jackson.
The best rep for the backs was Barkley handling Mondon on the final opportunity.
-- There was also a competitive 1-on-1 pass-rushing period. Moro Ojomo got the first signature win by using his speed to get past Drew Kendall. Jordan Mailata put together a nice rep to stop Hunt in his tracks while little-known Jose Ramirez used technique and effort to outlast John Ojukwu.
Ty Robinson, who has been a little better in recent days, used a move to beat Jake Majors on two reps and Willie Lampkin had to hold on two occasions against the impressive Ojomo. Markel Bell kept developmental prospect Josh Weru at bay and Tarron Jackson got into the thick of things with an awesome spin move that left Cam Williams in the dust. Jackson also got the better of Ojukwu.
Uar Bernard is still a work in progress and was handled by veteran Michael Jordan and Zion Wilson exploded past Kendall before the inetrior backup responded on a second rep.
-- Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard remains on the Active/PUP list for now with his strained pec and doesn’t appear close to a return. DC Vic Fangio said that Greenard, who was again watching practice intently, will be out at least another couple of weeks.
-- After leaving Monday’s practice early, Lampkin was a full participant on Tuesday, working at both center and guard.
-- The list of those who didn’t practice was: WR Danny Gray (concussion), OLB Keyshawn James-Newby (right ankle), CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder), WR Makai Lemon (hamstring), RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), WR Johnny Wilson (knee), and S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring). LB Chance Campbell (groin), and  Covey (hamstring) remained limited.
-- The offense/defense team drills started with a backed-up period. The Eagles came out in 12 personnel with Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt at tight end. The receivers were Dontayvion Wicks and Hollywood Brown. Moore came in as the slot WR on third down.
Barkley was able to convert with a few solid runs. The defense responded with the second team when Byron Young bursted through for a safety of Andy Dalton.
Tanner McKee was successful with the threes by finsing Erik Ezukanma on a 3rd-and-2 after Shipley did the dirty work to make it manageable
-- Those returning kicks on Tuesday were Bigsby, Cooper, Covey, Moore, and Brandon Hayes. Interestingly, Shipley was not part of the group.
-- Some other standout defensive plays were Jakorian Bennett recording a nice PBU on Moore and Robinson registering a sack.
On offense, Eli Stowers made some noise with a nice reception early in practice and Dallas Goedert used his body to shield Baun for a nice reception over the middle.

title: Why Drew Kendall Is Making Strides And Becoming No. 3 Guard As Versatile Interior Backup
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Second-year Eagles’ offensive lineman Drew Kendall is making significant strides in his development and is the clubhouse leader to be the top interior backup on game days.
Kendall, the son of longtime NFL guard Pete Kendall, is a natural center after spending all of his college career at Boston College at the pivot. That said, like any OL backup, cross-training is part of the gig, and the younger Kendall has a leg up there as well due to his bloodline.
In Year 2, Kendall has embraced the idea of versatility while also remaking his body with the help of an NFL strength room and digesting lessons from the proven veterans on hands and coaches Chris Kuper and Greg Austin, not to mention the reservoir of knowledge Jason Kelce can provide.
Kelce, the Eagles’ former All-Pro center and likely future Hall of Famer, was helping out at camp for most of the past week.
The challenge of it all is something Kendall is taking head-on.
“Yeah, I like it a lot. It’s just another challenge, going from playing mostly center to now guard,” he said. “Like, I really embrace that. I’m about that as a guy and as a player. It’s never fun to take the easy way out. You want to comb over some things. So, it’s been good. It’s something that I’m constantly working towards and something that you’re always striving to get better at.”
In recent days, Kendall has taken first-team reps at left guard while the Eagles manage the workload of veteran Landon Dickerson. He’s also the second-team center behind Cam Jurgens.
Recently, Kendall and another interior backup, Jake Majors, have been splitting days as the backup center and LG. When Jurgens was forced to leave practice early on Friday, Majors took over as the center because Kendall has been working that practice at OG, so don’t read too much into that. All signs point to Kendall being the guy as the top interior backup.
He credits a combination of factors for his progress.
“I think it’s a lot of things. I can’t point at one,” said Kendall. “I think Steph (Stephanie Coppola, the Eagles’ head performance dietitian) does a great job with us from a nutrition standpoint. I’ve been able to kind of reshape my body a little bit and put on weight in good ways and shed weight in the bad ways. So I feel more comfortable there.
“[The] Strength staff does a great job with us from, getting our bodies right and making sure we’re strong and playing at our best. So I think it’s a combination of learning new techniques from the vets and then working with the great people we have in the building.”
Kendall gauged his current playing weight at just over 300 pounds.
“I’m about 300 to 305, depending on the day. And, you know, with this, you can lose some weight in camp, 305, [is] where I’m at right now. So I feel good.”
Kuper, an interior lineman himself in his playing days, has been a nice fit for Kendall as a mentor.
“He’s been great. He’s fun to work with. You know, he’s a former player, so he kind of understands the everyday grind of it all,” Kendall noted. “So it’s been fun to work with. He’s really smart. He’s played in a very similar system like this, so he kind of understands how to play it. And, you know, as someone who’s learning guard, he played guard at a very high level. So it’s great to learn from him.”
The final piece to the puzzle may be the Eagles’ new blocking scheme, which has received rave reviews from the starters and appears well-suited to Kendall’s athletic profile.
“I think this is one of the systems that can fit my game,” he said. “So it’s been fun to kind of learn it and learn the different tricks that I can use on different plays, use my athletic ability.”

title: Why Eagles Will Be Just Fine If Jonathan Greenard Isn't Back By Week 1
full_text:
The likelihood Jonathan Greenard will make his Philadelphia Eagles debut come September 13 is slim to none.
Greenard hasn't practiced at all in training camp due a pectoral injury he suffered this summer, and was placed on the PUP list prior to the start of camp. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio didn't give a positive update towards Greenard's progression.
"We're not gonna see him for another couple weeks at least," Fangio said.
A couple weeks is very vague. Greenard will still have to get into football shape, but it doesn't appear he'll be back for the first two weeks of the preseason at minimum.
The Eagles don't have to rush Greenard back , as they have 33 days until the season opener. The decision on Greenard will have to come sooner, as he'll have to be off the PUP list by cutdown day on August 30 -- which is 19 days away.
If Greenard remains on PUP, he'll have to miss the first four games and won't count towards the 53-man roster. The situation doesn't appear to be that dire, but there's a chance Greenard won't be ready for Week 1 (even if the Eagles take him off the PUP).
If he isn't ready, the Eagles will be fine without Greenard for a few games.
Hunt is a significantly better player now than he was at this time last year. This is the same Jalyx Hunt that led the Eagles in sacks and interceptions last season, the first player in franchise history to accomplish that feat.
In this training camp, Hunt has been explosive. Hunt has been using his inside move to get to the quarterback consistently, taking advantage of playing the strong side (right side) in Greenard's absence. He has the makings of a pass rusher set for his first double-digit sack season.
The Eagles will certainly survive for a few games without Greenard with Hunt as the No. 1 pass rusher.
The Eagles just didn't have the depth at pass rusher last year, which forced them to sign Za'Darius Smith after the first game of the season. Smith even retired midseason, deciding his heart wasn't into football anymore.
Who were the pass rushers to open last season? Hunt, Nolan Smith, Josh Uche, and Patrick Johnson. Azeez Ojulari -- who was signed during the offseason -- was a healthy scratch that night.
The Eagles invested more money into the position this offseason, signing Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa (who they were fortunate to sign in June). Epenesa has been getting to the quarterback with the second team and Ebiketie has flashed in certain practices.
The top four of Hunt, Smith, Ebiketie, and Epenesa can get the job done for a few games. Ina  17-game season, the Eagles will need Greenard to get to a Super Bowl -- but the depth at pass rusher this year buys more time.
Assuming Greenard isn't ready by Week 1, does this open up the door for Graham to return?
The Eagles have been quiet with their conversations with Graham , preferring to keep them in house. Graham wants to return at some point in training camp to get in football shape, and that deadline is coming -- since he'll need about two weeks to actually get into football shape.
Graham would be the ideal No. 5 pass rusher if Greenard isn't ready, but it's also notable the Eagles brought in Tarron Jackson this week . Jackson is a long shot to make the roster and missed all of last season with an injury, but the Eagles are familiar with him.
If Greenard won't be ready, perhaps that's when Graham gets the call. That decision by the Eagles is coming soon.

title: A Beast And A Film Star, Why Willie Lampkin Is Making Case For Eagles Roster Spot
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Willie Lampkin turned the Eagles' training camp upside down and gave it a shake during Day 8 of training camp on Saturday, holding his ground and stonewalling pass rushers Zion Wilson and Gabe Hall during one-on-one drills.
The undrafted free agent interior offensive lineman has been opening eyes throughout camp . So much so that the Eagles PR staff decided to make him available to talk with the media after Monday's practice. Except Lampkin left practice early with an undisclosed illness. That took him off the interview list.
It’s not easy to make an NFL team when you’re considered short, and Lampkin is listed at 5-11. He may be more like 5-10. It takes persistence and belief in yourself to make it happen. Lampkin is a wide-body, though, with a lot of power and strength packed into his 290-pound frame.
“Willie's a beast,” said teammate and fellow interior lineman Drew Kendall. “Willie's great. He's fun to work with, too. Like, he's a great guy, brings a lot of energy. So, he's been fun, you know. It's been fun to kind of do that with him together. But I think he's having a great camp.”
So do his coaches, including the top dawg himself, Nick Sirianni.
“You notice him even more once the pads have come on," said the coach. “He can play on the inside at center or guard; good versatility, smart guy, really athletic. He's been fun to watch at camp.”
So much so, that Sirianni said he and his coaches love watching his practice film.
“We find ourselves as coaches when we're watching tape, just kind of being like, 'Man, Willie did it again,’” he said. “Willie's getting some really good guys to go up against. That's tested every day, and we're just looking for him to continue to grow and continue to show what he can do because it's about consistency. We all want consistency, to have that steady growth of getting better, but you're building trust.
“I think Willie is building trust with his teammates because you build trust by consistently doing what you're supposed to do out there, and Willie's been doing that. I know not only the coaches, but we're all impressed by Willie.”
Impressed enough to win a job? The Rams cut him at the end of camp last year with an injury, after signing the first-team All-American out of the University of North Carolina. The word was L.A. wanted to get him back to the practice squad, but the Eagles swooped in to claim him.
Lampkin is likely battling to be the second interior option behind Kendall. Jake Majors, who is 6-3, has had a solid camp and is in that battle, too, as are rookie sixth-round pick Micah Morris and maybe even seven-year veteran Michael Jordan.
Either way, Lampkin will have to put whatever injury he suffered on Monday behind him and do it quickly if he wants to give himself a chance.

title: 5 Winners And 3 Losers From Day 9 of Eagles Training Camp: Quinton Mitchell Shows All-Pro Talent
full_text:
Day 9 of Philadelphia Eagles training camp was a long one, as the Eagles emerged from an off day with a padded practice in the dead heat of summer.
With the preseason opener coming up on Saturday, the Eagles are preparing themselves for some football against actual opponents. In the meantime, a few camp practices won't hurt.
Players are emerging in this sessions, as seen in the practice observations and overreactions to the top storylines . What about the winners and losers from practice?
Day 9 of Eagles training camp had quite a few on both sides.
Darius Cooper: Every single day Cooper seems to be mentioned here. This shows how good of a camp Cooper is having . Cooper caught a lot of passes on Monday, including beating Riq Woolen on an out route that was noticeable. He's continuing to catch passes in the middle of the field and beating defenders to the ball. Cooper earned his place on the 53 last year and is making his case for an expanded role this year.
Quinyon Mitchell: An interception off Jalen Hurts won the game for the defense in the 2-minute drill team portion of practice. Hurts tried to thread the needle against Mitchell, but he's an All-Pro for a reason. Hurts had a good practice and the offense moved the ball, yet Mitchell was there to make the play that mattered. Mitchell has had a good summer and he's showing why he's the bets cornerback on the team.
Elijah Moore: Another player that continues to stack up good practices, Moore had two noticeable catches that resulted in big gains for the offense. Moore has showcased his speed after the catch, something the Eagles thought they were getting when they signed Hollywood Brown. Moore is making his case for a roster spot, as he's taken advantage of the injuries at wide receiver. The Eagles will have a decision to make in a few weeks with Moore.
Tariq Castro-Fields: Someone who has had a good training camp but his roster chances are slim is Castro-Fields. He had a pass breakup on Monday, continuing a summer of making plays. Castro-Fields was on the practice squad last year and the year prior, and is very familiar with the system. he may have a practice squad spot again with an opportunity to get elevated this year.
Michael Carter II: There is competition for the starting safety spot, and Carter II is pushing Marcus Epps for that job. Carter II is making plays at safety, including a nice pass breakup against Eli Stowers (who has shown signs of improvement). The Eagles are learning they can live with both Epps and Carter starting next to Andrew Mukuba, which is a good sign for the safety position.
Andy Dalton: Monday wasn't Dalton's best day, as he was off throughout the practice -- missing targets and couldn't get into a rhythm. This hurts Dalton in the battle against Tanner McKee -- who is catching Dalton -- but it was just one practice. These things do happen. The QB2 battle has gone back and forth, pending on the day.
Rocco Underwood: These was some monitoring of how Underwood is looking at long snapper. He didn't have a great session, as Underwood was missing snaps high and was inconsistent in getting the ball to Braden Mann. The Eagles may need to look for competition for Underwood, but have a few weeks to make a call on that. The season opener is September 14.
Hollywood Brown: This is more of what Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, and Elijah Moore are doing than what Brown isn't doing. The three mentioned are just having better camps than Brown, which puts Brown on the roster bubble . Brown just hasn't stood out like those three, which makes a conversation if he's going to be on this roster legitimate. He can turn things around this preseason, as there will be opportunities to make plays against teams that aren't the Eagles secondary.

title: Eagles Training Camp Roster 2.0: How Many Spots Are Available And Who's On The Bubble
full_text:
There have been several changes to the Philadelphia Eagles 90-man roster over the first nine practices of training camp, yet the goal remains the same.
The Eagles are still a Super Bowl contender, a team that should compete with the best in the NFL. The 53-man roster just has to be set.
With the second 53-man roster projection in, there's a blueprint for how he roster will turn out. How many spots are actually available on the roster?
Based on this breakdown -- this is how many roster locks we determined the Eagles have, how many players likely have a spot, and who's on the bubble.
Roster locks -- 35 ( up from 30 prior to camp )
Likely to make roster -- 8 (down from 13 prior to camp)
Players on roster bubble -- 28 (down from 31 prior to camp)
28 players are basically vying for 10 spots with cutdown day on August 30.
Roster locks : Jalen Hurts
Players on bubble: Tanner McKee, Andy Dalton, Cole Payton
Based on how the QB2 situation has played out, Dalton has the early head here. He has the edge over McKee for the backup quarterback spot, but McKee is also on track to make the roster (assuming he doesn't get traded).
Payton doesn't deserve a roster spot right now. He's too careless with the football and throws too many interceptions. The only way he makes the roster is if the Eagles trade McKee or Dalton at this stage.
Roster locks: Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby
Players on bubble: Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce
Little to no shot: Carson Steele, Ja'Quinden Jackson
Shipley was likely to make this roster entering camp, but there's a competition for RB3 now. This battle is between Shipley and Pierce, but Pierce is nursing a hamstring injury right now.
This job still belongs to Shipley, even if he's having an underwhelming camp. Shipley is still a bubble player thanks to the competition with Pierce.
Roster locks: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon
Likely to make roster: Darius Cooper
Players on bubble: Hollywood Brown, Johnny Wilson, Britain Covey, Elijah Moore
Little to no shot: Samori Toure, Quez Watkins, Danny Gray, Erik Ezukanma, Brandon Hayes
A lot has changed at wide receiver over the first nine practices. Cooper isn't a lock to make the team, but he's playing his way to that status. There are some questions regarding Brown's future on the roster, especially with how he's performed in training camp.
Moore is a bubble player, but he's played his way into competing for a roster spot. Covey just returned from a hamstring injury and was having a solid start to camp. There's still a battle for WR5, even if Cooper isn't a part of it.
Roster locks: Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt
Players on bubble: Cameron Latu, E.J. Jenkins
Little to no shot: Stone Smartt, Grant Calcaterra
There's still the chance the Eagles keep four tight ends, yet they have their top three for the 53-man roster. Latu could play fullback, so he's on the bubble. Jenkins is a key on the field goal unit, as he has a shot (he's also been a part of the roster for several years).
If the Eagles keep four, it will come down to how Latu and Jenkins perform the rest of the way.
Roster locks: Jordan Mailata, Lane Johnson, Markel Bell
Likely to make roster: Fred Johnson
Players on bubble: Myles Hinton, Cameron Williams
Little to no shot: John Ojekwu
This position is set with the top four players. There's concern whether Johnson can make the 53 due to Markel Bell taking over the No. 3 tackle job, but Johnson got the first team reps at right tackle when Lane Johnson needed a rest on Monday.
Johnson should make this roster, as there's little depth behind him. Hinton has a shot as a guard/tackle, but he'll have to play his way towards that fifth tackle spot. There is a roster spot available here.
Roster locks: Landon Dickerson, Tyler Steen
Players on bubble: Michael Jordan, Micah Morris, Willie Lampkin, Hollin Pierce
The battle for the No. 3 guard beelongs to Drew Kendall, who we're listing as a center. Kendall is the top guard option behind Dickerson and Steen, taking first team reps when Dickerson gets a breather.
Lampkin has jumped Morris on the depth chart and is playing his way towards a roster spot. The Eagles have liked how Lampkin has been making plays in practice and standing out on film. He may be ahead of Jordan too.
Roster locks: Cam Jurgens, Drew Kendall
Players on bubble: Jake Majors
Kendall has been one of the bright spots in camp, seizing the No. 3 guard spot and also duplicating as the backup center to Jurgens. The Eagles are giving Majors a long look here, just in case Kendall is needed at guard.
Majors went from a long shot to a bubble player. He's had a solid camp.
Roster locks: Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa
Little to no shot: Joshua Weru, Keyshawn James-Newby, Jose Ramirez, Tarron Jackson
The Eagles have been set here, enough where Epenesa played his way to a roster lock. That demonstrates how well Epenesa has played in the absence of Greenard, who is on PUP with a pectoral injury.
If the Eagles go six pass rushers, this is the Brandon Graham spot. There is no indication of a Graham return right now, but Graham would like to be back at some point in training camp.
Roster locks: Jordan Davis, Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young
Likely to make roster: Uar Bernard
Players on bubble: Ty Robinson, Gabe Hall, Zion Wilson
Little to no shot: David Blay
The Eagles have four roster locks at defensive tackle, thanks to how well Young has performed this summer. Bernard is expected to make the roster as a way for the Eagles to protect him from being claimed off waivers.
Who's going to be the sixth defensive tackle? Robinson hasn't played well through nine practices, and there's a case to be made Hall is outplayed him. Don't sleep on Wilson either.
Roster locks: Zack Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Jeremiah Trotter Jr.
Likely to make roster: Smael Mondon
Players on bubble: Chance Campbell
Little to no shot: Deontae Lawson
There are three starters at linebacker on the Eagles, which shows the strength of this position. Mondon should also as a spot on this roster, but Vic Fangio gave the warning not to sleep on Campbell.
The Eagles may go five off-ball linebackers if Campbell plays well enough. This is why he's a bubble player, elevated from a long shot.
Roster locks: Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, Tariq Woolen, Jonathan Jones
Likely to make roster: Kelee Ringo
Players on bubble: Mac McWilliams
Little to no shot: Tariq Castro-Fields, Shawn Wade, Jakorian Bennett, Ambry Thomas

title: Steelers Linked to Ridiculous QB Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't even played a single preseason game, but talks regarding their trade deadline plans have already developed.
Of course, the only trade deadline moves that matter to the Steelers are the ones surrounding Aaron Rodgers. The team's starting quarterback is in his final NFL season, according to the man himself, and the organization understandably wants to do anything it can to deliver him another Super Bowl victory.
But some believe it's more likely to go completely off the rails. That's what Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio proposed on a recent appearance on Pardon My Take. After 19 years of avoiding losing seasons, the Steelers might be staring down their first one in two decades under new head coach Mike McCarthy. If that happens, Florio believes the Steelers might try to move Rodgers to give him one more postseason run.
"There's a chance this thing goes sideways," he warned. "You get to the trade deadline, you can have Aaron Rodgers maybe asking to go somewhere that may need a quarterback. Some contender that may need a quarterback because 'Get me the hell outta here, this is my last year. I want to have a chance to play into the postseason.'"
Could we see Aaron Rodgers be traded at the deadline if the Steelers season tanks? pic.twitter.com/txneoKW1RR
The Steelers are undoubtedly focused on the Vince Lombardi Trophy. The way they are preparing for the year and moving through training camp, it's clear that the belief within the organization is that they are a legitimate contender.
That belief isn't shared around the NFL, however. And that's what Florio points out during his appearance on PMT. He outlines the timeline he imagines the Steelers are working with, around Thanksgiving. By then, the team might be out of contention, and their hands might be tied.
"If we're (the Steelers) not contending by Thanksgiving," he stated. "Why do we want to play out the string with Aaron Rodgers?"
That's all fair and good, but does it align with the organization's goals and plans? The obvious answer is no, as the Steelers have no plans to deal the future Hall of Fame quarterback. Instead, the team believes they can help get back to the Promised Land once more.
If Rodgers does become available, what teams would have any interest? Florio proposes that a team that is in contention but in need of a quarterback would be the most likely option.
Realistically, what team fits that description? No team does, because no NFL team can contend without a competent starting quarterback. Injuries can change things, but right now there is no possible landing spot for Rodgers outside of Pittsburgh.

title: Germie Bernard Has Huge Opportunity After Steelers WR Injuries
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have been very impressed with the work of rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard. The team's recent second-round draft pick arrived at camp ready to compete, and it didn't take long for him to cut into the first-team snaps.
The Steelers may be calling upon the rookie receiver to play a pivotal role in the team's preseason opener. Top wideout Michael Pittman Jr. suffered an upper-body injury during a recent practice, and he's been limited in the team's final practices before taking on the Green Bay Packers. In addition, top receiver DK Metcalf was a spectator as the team took things inside for a recent practice.
For Bernard, it's another opportunity. Of course, this one comes with just a bit more pressure, as he gets acquainted with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers and the rest of the first-team offense.
"It's a great opportunity to get in there with A-Rod and kind of just learn everything about him. Learn his signals and everything," he said. "I'm still asking questions from DK (Metcalf) and Pitt (Pittman Jr.), so those guys are doing a great job of teaching everybody in the room and making sure that everybody is falling in line."
Based on how the practice reps have gone so far, the Steelers are ready to give Bernard a huge opportunity against the Packers. The young receiver has been playing plenty with the first-team offense, and if both DK and MPJ are not active, that leaves him and Roman Wilson as the top options.
Luckily for Bernard, he thrives on being available in any and all situations. It's something he believes he has always brought to the football field, and versatility remains a top priority as he establishes himself as a professional.
"Just being versatile," he stated. "That's something I hold dearly to my heart just because it presents me with a alot of opportunities."
Bernard does not lack confidence, but can he match that with production on the field? That will be the toughest challenge for the rookie receiver, who will have to create chemistry with more than one quarterback against the Packers.
Asked what he tries to do when filling in for players like DK and Pittman Jr., Bernard kept it simple. Sure, he can't replicate the size those two hulking pass-catchers inherently provide, but he can bring something even better: himself.
"I'll be myself," he said.
And the Steelers are planning to let Germie be himself in the preseason opener. Now, let's see where that takes him.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Has Preseason Plans
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't announced if Aaron Rodgers will play in the preseason or not, but it sure doesn't sound like the 42-year-old wants to.
Speaking with the media, Rodgers made it very clear that he doesn't see the benefit of preseason games for himself or many other veterans.
"It's preseason. It's not real football," Rodgers said. "So if I do great. If not, great. Preseason's a lot different. Teams don't run anything anymore, they just really don't. It's good to see guys with pads on, under the lights, how they react to the nerves. But it's not real, regular season football."
So, it's hard to imagine he'll be out there. If he's not, he still has intentions to improve the Steelers during the three exhibition games.
"I like to be on the headset and calm everybody down," Rodgers told Steelers On SI. "Usually, the first game, it's a little hectic on the headset. So I like to be the voice of reason, occasional dad joke or one-liner. Just keep everybody settled in a little bit."
"Well, their age, really. They're young kids. They're excited about learning, open to some extra coaching from me," Rodgers added about Howard and Allar. "They ask questions. They want to do it right. They watch what I do and try and mimic that. Or if I do something they don't understand, they ask a question. And the best part of it is Tom [Arth] gives me a lot of latitude in the room to speak up and to talk about things or stop the film and say, 'What are you thinking here?' And quarterback, just like all things, can be over-complicated to make it seem more difficult than it might be sometimes. It's not easy, but you can simplify things and that's what I'm trying to help them with."
The ears he'll be speaking into on the headset will be Mason Rudolph's, Will Howard's and Drew Allar. For Howard and Allar, this will be their first NFL game ever, meaning the nerves will certainly be high for the young quarterbacks.
Rodgers will be able to be a calming presence while offering advice as they navigate a game for the first time.
For Rudolph, it's likely more of a "how can I help you" situation. The 31-year-old is in the midst of a quarterback battle with Howard and could create maybe an uncloseable gap if he plays well against the Packers. Rodgers will be a helping hand in doing so while watching from the sideline.
The Steelers will be without a number of players in their preseason opener. Rookie tackle Max Iheanachor (shoulder/neck) will likely be out after missing the last week of practice. Wide receivers DK Metcalf (unknown) and Michael Pittman Jr. (leg) will also miss the game after not practicing.
Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson will start in their places. Dylan Cook will start at right tackle, as he's been throughout training camp.
Defensive tackles Sebastian Joseph-Day (unknown) and Logan Lee (unknown) and offensive guard Steven Jones (unknown) have also missed practice time and are not expected to play. Defensive backs Jaquan Brisker and Brandin Echols (ankle) likely won't either as they work through injuries. Echols remains in a walking boot since injuring his ankle.
Rookie running back Eli Heidenreich is expected to play after missing time with a hamstring/groin injury. Heidenreich told Steelers On SI that he feels much better and is ready to go out there on Thursday night against the Packers.

title: Steelers Get Good Injury News on Rookie Eli Heidenreich
full_text:
It appears Eli Heidenreich is set to return and will play in the Pittsburgh Steelers ' first game of the preseason.
After missing a handful of practices in recent days as the second week of training camp transitioned into the third, Heidenreich told reporters that he feels good from a health perspective after taking some time off and is trending in the right direction.
"Health-wise, I feel great," Heidenreich said. "I took a few days off, I'm sure you guys saw that, but I'm healing up."
When asked if he'll be a full-go in the preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, Heidenreich stated that's the plan.
"The plan today was to practice," Heidenreich said. "It got changed up a little bit today, but yea as far as I'm concerned."
With Heidenreich back on the field and ready to go heading into Pittsburgh's bout against the Packers, it won't come as a surprise if his number is called a ton at Acrisure Stadium later this week.
Coming into training camp, Heidenreich was lumped in with the likes of Kaleb Johnson and Travis Homer as the top candidates to snag the last spot or two on the 53-man roster at running back.
With Johnson handling a steady workload behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle while Lew Nichols has emerged as one of the stars of camp, however, Heidenreich is in a precarious position next to Homer.
It doesn't help that Heidenreich missed multiple practices, as previously mentioned, especially as a rookie who is still acclimating himself to the NFL.
The seventh-round pick's versatility provides a nice boost to his stock and the overall intrigue surrounding him, though. Whether it's at running back, on special teams or perhaps a snap here and there at wide receiver, the fact that Mike McCarthy and his staff can get creative in how they deploy Heidenreich means he has several avenues through which he can make the roster.
Because he's buried so far down the depth chart at this point, it more or less feels like his fate as a likely cut candidate is well on its way to being cemented. There just isn't room on the roster for him.
Heidenreich could still make up for lost time by catching a few passes out of the backfield and holding up in pass protection while thriving in whatever role(s) he handles on special teams, but it's hard to imagine it being enough to snag an initial 53-man when it's all said and done.

title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Steelers QB Plan in Preseason Opener
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't yet made a concrete decision on who will start at quarterback in the team's preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers, but they at least have an outline.
Head coach Mike McCarthy told the media that while the team is still drawing up their plan and will have more to report back on once additional meetings are conducted, his likely intention is to go with three groups - one that will go through a series or two, a second that will finish out the first half from there and a third that will stay on the field for the second half.
Regardless of which quarterback falls into those respective categories, it'll be an opportunity for the backup battle to take center stage between Mason Rudolph and Will Howard, the latter of whom will play in the first game of his professional career next to Drew Allar , even if it's not technically an official contest.
Ahead of his Steelers debut after a hand injury kept him out of the preseason and on the reserve/injured list through Week 11 as a rookie last year, Howard couldn't contain excitement to finally get out on the field against Green Bay while speaking with reporters on August 10.
“I’m so fired up,” Howard said. “I can’t wait for the game, but obviously I’m trying to take it day by day. It’s still camp. But, you know, sometimes you can’t help but look forward a little bit and start getting excited just to be out there in live game reps.”
Howard has the most to both gain and lose among all of Pittsburgh's signal callers. The 2025 sixth-rounder has been up-and-down during training camp, with a good start to his time in Latrobe this summer before a rather poor finish to his second week there.
Rudolph entered camp as the No. 2 quarterback behind Aaron Rodgers, and nothing has changed on that front thus far. The 31-year-old has been as steady as expected, and while it's not always exciting with him, he's the type of stabilizing veteran presence that any team would covet as their backup.
As a result, Howard must go above and beyond both against the Packers and in each of Pittsburgh's following two preseason bouts in order to make up enough ground in the race for the No. 2 job to hold any sort of suspense leading into final roster cuts at the end of the month.
Allar, on the other hand, just has to show progress week-over-week and prove that he has taken steps forward when it comes to his mechanics, footwork and processing.
The third-round pick is a lock to make the 53-man roster as the No. 3 quarterback, meaning he isn't facing the same type of pressure that Howard or even Rudolph are at the moment.
Still, some conclusions are going to be drawn about Allar based on he performs this preseason whether it's right or wrong, and jumping out to a strong start against the Packers would provide a good foundation for the rookie to work off of.

title: Steelers QB Battle About to Take Off
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' quarterback battle hasn't been too eventful during training camp. Mike McCarthy came to Latrobe and announced that Mason Rudolph would work with the twos and Will Howard would work with the threes. Since then, nothing has changed. Everything could very soon, though.
The Steelers will host the Green Bay Packers in their preseason opener, putting McCarthy's offense on display for the first time, but most likely not with Aaron Rodgers.
Instead, it'll be his backups. Rudolph will probably start the game, getting the first opportunity to put the quarterback battle to an end. If he doesn't, Howard will roll out there as the second passer to take the field. From there, anything is possible.
This is the first opportunity Howard has had since the start of camp to win the QB2 job behind Rodgers. He was given a chance during OTAs and minicamp but clearly didn't do enough to hold onto the gig. Rudolph surpassed him and has since grown his lead quite a bit over the last two weeks.
Howard can change everything if he goes out there and lights up the Packers defense.
"I’m so fired up.," Howard said. "Obviously, I’m trying to take it day by day, and it’s still camp. But, sometimes you can’t help but look forward a little bit and start getting excited just to be out there and [get] live game reps — because I haven’t played in over a year in live game reps. I think the last time was the national championship. So, I’ve been champing at the bit for a while to get out there with the guys in a real game-like setting — uniform on, helmet on."
Howard needs to go out there and showcase that all of the upside McCarthy talked about this offseason is real. That he does have starter potential and is taking strides with his mechanics, and putting it on the field to produce results.
If he can, there's a chance he can walk into the second preseason with a real opportunity to prove his worth as the QB2 this season. Nothing will be decided after one game. At least nothing positive. But he can set himself up to head into the last two exhibitions with a real QB battle.
If he doesn't look good, the competition is all but over. It would take Rudolph, who's been in plenty of these games before, to look just as bad, if not worse. Chances are, that doesn't happen.
It's all on Howard. But this is the first real moment of a quarterback battle since the start of training camp. If he takes advantage, things are about to get exciting.

title: Baker Mayfield Could Take Less Money to Join Steelers
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers , in all likelihood, are going to have another quarterback search next offseason.
The 2027 NFL Draft is the Steelers' best option to find a true long-term solution, but Baker Mayfield could become one of the few coveted free agents at the position in recent years after extension talks with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven't led to an agreement.
If Mayfield does in fact hit the open market instead of inking a new deal with Tampa Bay, being franchise-tagged or even tag-and-traded, Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio stated during an appearance on "Pardon My Take" that he believes the former No. 1 overall pick may consider taking a discount in order to head to Pittsburgh.
"I could see him taking less money to go to Pittsburgh," Florio said.
pic.twitter.com/1S94bJiny4
After years and years of mediocrity at quarterback, the Steelers surely understand that trudging along with their plan of cycling through stop-gaps at the position isn't going to get them anywhere in the long run.
The likes of Aaron Rodgers, Russell Wilson and Justin Fields haven't done anything to inspire confidence or really uplift the team as a whole in their respective tenures with the organization over the past few seasons, though it's been just enough to notch back-to-back playoff appearances and 10-win campaigns.
Rodgers is back for the 2026 season, but he's made it clear that the door isn't open for a return next year.
Unless Will Howard or Drew Allar take a huge leap forward and somehow show Pittsburgh that they're ready to be passed the torch, which doesn't feel particularly likely, Omar Khan and Mike McCarthy are going to have to go back to the drawing board next offseason.
As stated before, the 2027 NFL Draft has a strong group of quarterback prospects and should be the Steelers' focus when it comes to putting an end to their annual quest for a franchise signal caller.
If Mayfield comes available, however, it would only be right for the team to at least put some feelers out and consider the possibility of bringing him in.
He is a notch or two above Pittsburgh's other recent veteran additions at the position and would boost its chances of becoming more of a force in the AFC. Furthermore, with McCarthy feeling like somewhat of a bridge head coach to get the most out of the team's current core, Mayfield would fit into the Steelers' M.O. in that regard before they potentially readjust and retool a few years down the line.
Unless Mayfield would actually consider taking less money than he'd otherwise be expected to garner, though, perhaps around the $50-million-per-year mark or so, Pittsburgh might be wise to stay away.
The team could free up the necessary cap space to land him despite only having a projected $3.939 million available for 2027 as of right now, per Over the Cap , but it really does feel like the Steelers should just turn the page and put their full attention towards the 2027 draft class.
Mayfield wouldn't be a disastrous addition for Pittsburgh by any means, though it would continue to show a complete disinterest in getting younger and opening a new chapter, which isn't a smart way of viewing things.

title: Steelers Share Concerning Max Iheanachor Update
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were elated by rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor's performance at training camp.
But as has been the case with plenty of Steelers this summer, the team's standout offensive lineman suffered an injury midway through the second week of camp. At first, the team characterized the injury as minor and projected that he would return during the team's third week of camp.
That's not the case, however, as Iheanachor will miss the team's latest practice. Not only that, but head coach Mike McCarthy shared no further details on when they expect the young tackle back on the field.
"Max will not be out there today," he said.
At the time of this story, Iheanachor only went through a few reps in individual drills during practice.
After being asked about Iheanachor's return to practice, McCarthy was also asked about when he would return to practice. When asked directly if he had a timeline for Iheanachor, McCarthy had nothing more to offer.
"No, I don't," he said. "Sorry."
His response could mean one of two things. The first is that the injury is more severe than initially believed. That would obviously be the worst-case scenario for the first-round pick.
The second option is that McCarthy has no intention of revealing injury details before he's mandated to do so by the NFL. Sure, McCarthy didn't provide the most encouraging update on Iheanachor, but what if no update is a good thing for the rookie? We don't know, as McCarthy has held this information incredibly close to the vest throughout camp.
With the youngster off the field, it gives veteran Dylan Cook a bit of breathing room. Last year's left tackle by the end of the season, Cook has been charged with shifting to the right and beating out the upstart Iheanachor.
It hasn't been easy for Cook. Before Iheanachor's injury, he was outplaying Cook, and it wasn't very close. Cook was slated to be a backup on the right side.
But, that can all change with the team's first preseason game coming up. Cook has a few more practices to stand out, and can take things to the next level when they take on the Green Bay Packers.
The injury also opens another door for Broderick Jones. Recovering from his own injury, he's received more opportunities and praise from the coaching staff. With his experience playing both left and right tackle, he might be relied on even more without Iheanachor.
