title: Steelers Add Two Wide Receivers Before Preseason Opener
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- With training camp nearing the finish line, the Pittsburgh Steelers continue to tinker with the group at St. Vincent's College. With their first preseason game against the Green Bay Packers upcoming, the team has some premier position battles set to reach the next level.
Despite this, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy and his staff are still looking for the ideal group to enter the regular season with.
With a few more training camp practices and preseason action ahead, the Steelers made a few roster moves to begin the week. According to the Steelers PR Department, the team added free agent wide receivers Cornell Powell and Isaiah Winstead. In corresponding moves, the Steelers waived receiver Colton Dowell and designated offensive tackle Lorenzo Thompson as Waived/Injured.
Both Powell and Winstead bring a mix of professional experience to Pittsburgh, and they will bring a new crop of competition for the bottom of the wide receiver depth chart.
Powell was originally drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs, selected in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL Draft. He's appeared in three NFL games, all coming with the Chiefs during the 2022 season. In addition to Kansas City, he's spent time on the Seattle Seahawks and Houston Texans' practice squads, spending last season in Houston.
What the Steelers might find appealing about Powell is his special-teams ability. His only NFL snaps came as a member of the special teams, and his NCAA career contained a bit of pop in a returning role. He collected 197 yards on eight kickoff returns as a member of the Clemson Tigers.
Winstead had a slightly different path to the NFL. Undrafted during the 2023 NFL Draft, he received his first professional opportunity with the San Francisco 49ers. He was a practice squad member for the 2023 campaign, before signing in the UFL the following year. In the subsequent seasons, he's bounced around the UFL and the CFL before. This past UFL campaign, he recorded 474 receiving yards and three touchdowns with the Louisville Kings.
Like Powell, Winstead has the chance to push for a spot at the end of the roster. The Steelers have the receiver position seemingly solidified, but there is always room for changes.
With these two new additions, the Steelers parted with two players who hadn't made much of an impact so far. Neither player received a strong opportunity over the first two weeks, and now they will look for a new opportunity in the NFL.

title: Five Observations From Episode Two of Seahawks Hard Knocks
full_text:
Hard Knocks Episode Two is officially a go. It was another phenomenal showcase of what’s going on at the VMac as the Seahawks prepare to defend their title. As always, the production is a mixture of entertainment and information, fluff and substance. It remains a must-see for any Seahawks fan. But what were the major themes of this week’s episode?
The early seconds of the episode picked up where the first episode left off, in a manner of speaking. Derick Hall, the edge rusher who was rewarded with a $42 million dollar contract extension in the offseason, was getting just a little too excited during practice, hitting too hard and getting too close to the quarterback. Quickly, Mike had seen enough.
He sent Derick off the field, amid protests, in response to his refusal to amp things down. When this event happened, and how soon it happened after the brawl depicted in episode one, isn’t clear, but it does seem to establish a trend. Hall is one of the instigators in camp so far, and he’ll need to find a way to crank it down now and bring it back up for the season.
We had an expanded look at the scene later in the episode as well, making it one of the biggest emphasis points of the episode. Mike Macdonald wants to protect his quarterbacks, especially this early in camp, so his frustration is understandable. And while there was some anger, ultimately, it was a learning moment for Derick.
One of the highlights of the episode was the cameo by Mitch Johnson , coach of the San Antonio Spurs. He and Brian Wright (San Antonio’s General Manager) had a short conversation with Macdonald in Mike’s office. They exchanged notes, with Mike talking about how his training camp process has changed from last year to this year.
It was a cool moment, two successful professional coaches in different leagues trying to find ways in which they could help the other. Mike has spoken about how he feels like you can learn things from experts in other sports, and it speaks to his focus on chasing edges. And perhaps Mitch picked up something that will help him on his quest to his first title.
One extended sequence in the episode focused on Sam Darnold’s spin rate, of all things. Darnold, apparently, puts more spin on the ball when he throws it than any other quarterback in the league. The average rate is around 570, and Darnold is around 100 more than that. According to Jake Peetz, this creates a more catchable and accurate ball.
I can’t say I’ve ever heard of spin rate when looking at and scouting quarterbacks, and I don’t know about the science behind it actually being easier to catch a fast-spinning ball. But for whatever it’s worth, Cooper Kupp expressed his belief that the faster spin is superior, so I suppose it’s another thing that Darnold is getting right so far in Seattle.
One of the recurring recreational activities the players partake in during camp, going back to last year, is shadowboxing. I can’t say I came out of the episode with a great understanding of exactly how the game worked, but to make a long story short, it’s a way for the players to bond and remain in competition with each other, as a sort of rock-paper-scissors game.
It gets players who typically don’t work with each other to interact, and it sure seems like they’re having plenty of fun doing it. If nothing else, it’s a non-violent way for the players to settle disputes, which is always appreciated. I don’t think I’d be very good at it, but they’re having a good time, and that’s all that matters.
The episode included a brief discussion of the Terrion Arnold conundrum , as the Seahawks have an opportunity to make a play for him in free agency. Obviously, the issue is complicated, with his legal issues and felony charges making it unclear if he’ll even be allowed to play. But Schneider makes it clear he believes he can help the team.
I can understand why the squad would be tempted to allow Mike Macdonald to get an opportunity to coach someone as talented as Terrion Arnold. Furthermore, one scene involved a discussion about how they had inquired with Jalen Milroe, who developed a relationship with Arnold in college. We even got to see some of the workout Arnold had in the VMac.
There was plenty of fun content as well, like Leonard Williams’s affinity for gardening and Derick Hall’s truck hobby. Nick Emmanwori’s pool rehab got a couple minutes. A sledgehammer-based competition of strength between Mason Richman and Rylie Mills was used to settle a particularly physical moment on the field. The mock game got some focus as well.
All in all, it was another great look into the team. It gave fans just about everything they could want. Three more episodes left. We will be seated.

title: Seahawks Rookie Jadarian Price Gets Huge Comparison to Pro Bowl RB
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are expected to feature first-round pick Jadarian Price heavily in their run game this season.
While Price will have a role in the team's running back committee, he has the potential to break out and be a true lead back. Per a report from ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler , Seahawks defensive back Julian Love compared Price to a prime Dalvin Cook, which is a massive compliment.
It's a bold statement for Love to compare Price to Cook before the rookie from Notre Dame even takes an NFL snap, but the vision is there.
Cook, in his prime, had a violent running style. When he saw an opening, he would attack it with force. That's similar to what we saw Price do in his limited action at Notre Dame behind Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick in this year's draft.
The two also have similar builds. Cook stood 5-10 and weighed 210 pounds, while Price is 5-11 weighing 209 pounds. Cook has a bit more muscle than Price, but the latter is still just 22 years old and has plenty of room for growth. If Price can reach Cook's prime, the Seahawks should have something very valuable.
In Cook's six seasons with the Minnesota Vikings from 2017-22, he was one of the top running backs in the league.
Cook averaged just under 1,000 yards per season with the Vikings, and that came even with him missing 17 games across his first two seasons due to injury. That's a good baseline for Price, but there will be some struggles for him to hit that number with the Seahawks.
Cook was far and away the best running back with the Vikings while he was there. Nobody was really challenging him for carries on the roster. With the way the Seahawks want to run the ball, it will be hard for Price to achieve that status.
The Seahawks plan to use two or three running backs throughout the season, as Zach Charbonnet should get carries once he returns to the field from his torn ACL recovery. Emanuel Wilson should also see some action after signing a one-year deal with the team during the offseason.
The Seahawks' committee should allow them to stay healthier throughout the year, but it hurts Price's chances of becoming one of the top running backs in the league in his rookie year. If he impresses and is clearly the best running back, Seattle might opt for a change in the middle of the year. The vision is that Price will be part of a whole running back room that will try to beat you in multiple ways.

title: Biggest Surprise From Seattle Seahawks Unofficial Depth Chart vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The defending champion Seattle Seahawks will be in action this Saturday as they host the Dallas Cowboys in Preseason Week 1 .
Even with their top players such as Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Sam Darnold, Leonard Williams, and Devon Witherspoon all returning, Seattle has multiple positions up for grabs. One of the most prominent spots is at running back, a position that was vacated when Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker signed with the Kansas City Chiefs .
Making things even more interesting at running back is the injury suffered by Zach Charbonnet. During Seattle's playoff run, Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL and hasn't been cleared for action. The Seahawks attempted to fill that void with rookie Jadarian Price, who they selected in the first round of the NFL draft out of Notre Dame.
Price worked behind Jeremiyah Love with the Irish, but has all the traits to be an effective lead back. His skill set fits well with the Seattle offense and he entered the offseason as the expected starter. On the first unofficial depth chart, however, that's not the case.
The depth chart, which was shared by Field Gulls, has Price as the RB2 behind third-year pro George Holani.
The first unofficial Seahawks depth chart is here! This was presumably put together prior to Emmanwori passing his physical, otherwise everything else is up to date. pic.twitter.com/HRzClSuxOF
Holani has been a standout for the Seahawks during camp, which comes as a surprise to no one. Holani has often been able to impress during offseason work as well as the preseason. Due to the depth at running back, he hasn't been able to do much in the regular season.
In two years, Holani has 25 attempts for 83 yards and one touchdown. This season could be his chance to carve out a larger role in the offense and if this depth chart is any indication, he will be given the chance to do exactly that.
The EDGE is another spot of interest, where Derick Hall is listed as the backup behind DeMarcus Lawrence while the starter across from Lawrence is Uchenna Nwosu.
Nwosu had seven sacks last season while starting 11 of the 16 games he appeared in, but Hall signed a three-year extension worth $42 million , suggesting he could be in for a starting spot. They also have Ty Okada listed ahead of rookie Bud Clark as the starting safety across from Julian Love.
Of course, this is an unofficial depth chart and there could be several changes before the regular season, but that doesn't mean there aren't some surprises.

title: Anthony Bradford Gives Seahawks Contract Extension Update
full_text:
One of the biggest Seahawks subplots of the offseason has been the contract extension drama with Devon Witherspoon . And it’s not hard to understand why. Spoon is one of the best players in the league and will almost certainly set the market at his position with his new deal. However, there’s another Seahawk entering his fourth season who could get his new deal.
Yes, I’m talking about Anthony Bradford . Not the first player that comes to mind when you think about early contract extensions. His generally inconsistent play and countless mistakes have turned him into something of a punching bag. Many Seahawks fans lament the fact that the team hasn’t yet replaced him as a starter. And yet, the team seems to like him .
Anthony Bradford says on @933KJR the Seahawks haven’t approached him about a new contract: “There’s nowhere else I would rather be. I feel like my heart and soul is in Seattle. I feel like I am a Seahawk.” Should the Seahawks extend Bradford? pic.twitter.com/UzLbRPIdN3
We’ve heard Macdonald praise Bradford on multiple occasions and indicate that, by their metrics, he’s a very good player. While that doesn’t necessarily guarantee they view him as a long-term part of their roster, it certainly opens the door to the possibility. If they do, better to extend him now, at a cheaper rate, before he has what will likely be his best season.
However, according to the man himself, the Seahawks haven’t yet opened the door on the conversation. On 93.3 KJR Radio, Bradford said that the team hasn’t discussed a new contract with him yet, which would pretty strongly indicate that they intend to go into the season with things as they are. Bradford, for his part, sounded enthusiastic about a long-term deal.
“There’s nowhere else I would rather be,” he said. “I feel like my heart and soul is in Seattle. I feel like I am a Seahawk.” Bradford has played a lot of football for the Seahawks over the last three years, including 98% of the regular season snaps in 2025. He’s certainly justified in feeling like a Seahawk. But that’s no guarantee of a commitment in a salary cap league.
The Seahawks are focused on extending superstars like Devon Witherspoon and Leonard Williams . They’ve already extended Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Charles Cross, and Abraham Lucas. Extensions for players like Byron Murphy, AJ Barner, Grey Zabel, Nick Emmanwori, and Sam Darnold are coming up. The books have to be balanced.
That balancing act is a big reason why the team allowed contributors like Ken Walker, Coby Bryant, and Boye Mafe to leave in the offseason. I would certainly group Bradford in with a group like that as opposed to the above one. You have to have your priorities in line. And while I don’t dislike him, I’d be hard pressed to consider Anthony Bradford to be a priority.

title: Mike Macdonald Shares Jalen Milroe Plan for Cowboys vs. Seahawks
full_text:
One of the most intriguing subplots of the 2026 preseason for the Seattle Seahawks is how Jalen Milroe will play . For the moment, he’s firmly the #3 QB on the depth chart, so there’s a pretty good chance the preseason will be his only opportunity to play. And even if that’s not the case, many of his chances will likely be trick plays and misdirections.
Coach Macdonald was asked about how playing time decisions are made in the preseason, where the team has both veteran Drew Lock and Milroe on the roster behind Sam Darnold, so the question is a bit more complicated than it might be on other teams that only have two. Macdonald kept it vague, but it sounds like we’ll see more Jalen this preseason.
Sounds like there may be more Jalen Milroe during the preseason than last year. Mike Macdonald explains they are figuring all that out right now. pic.twitter.com/E3mKsvMLAA
“We’re working through that right now. I think we might take a little bit of a different approach this year on how we play our quarterbacks,” Macdonald said. “But Drew needs a lot of game work as well. Everybody needs work. So how do you do it? Even Sam.” While he doesn’t overtly say it, I suspect that the takeaway here is that Milroe might see more opportunities.
Going back to 2025, Milroe was the most utilized quarterback across the three preseason games. He threw 39 passes against Lock’s 34 and Darnold’s 4, also throwing in 15 rushing attempts to Lock’s 5. If you want to take Macdonald’s words as an indication that Darnold might get more time instead, that’s valid, but my guess is we’re getting more Milroe.
Starting quarterbacks getting minimal throws in preseason is relatively common, and the Seattle offense is very similar to the one they had last year, so I don’t think Darnold needs much more than a couple drives. Milroe, on the other hand, needs the opportunity to show that he’s progressed from last preseason and might even be capable of playing now.
The Seahawks have a lot of draft picks in the upcoming 2027 draft, and there are some appealing quarterback prospects. If Milroe doesn’t show improvements this season, I wonder if the team might be motivated to pivot off of him and try to find a different developmental backup. And since he’s the third stringer right now, the preseason is his shot to do that.
If this team commits long-term to Sam Darnold this upcoming offseaso n, this might be a moot point. But I can’t help but feel that Milroe’s chances of being a part of this organization going forward hinge on him playing well this month. And it sounds like Mike will give him that chance.

title: Seahawks Visit With Spurs, Talk Victor Wembanyama in 'Hard Knocks' Preview
full_text:
It's common practice in professional sports for coaches to talk shop in an attempt to learn from each other, even if they don't coach the same sport. That's part of the reason why Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald hosted San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson and general manager Brian Wright.
Johnson is from Seattle, so the connection isn't all that random. The two coaches have a lot in common as young upstart leaders who are trying to build off of their early success in their careers. In a preview for the second episode of " Hard Knocks ," Macdonald and Johnson are seen talking about their respective teams and how they can find some commonality.
Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald and Spurs coach Mitch Johnson share leadership tips and talk Victor Wembanyama on Hard Knocks tonight 9pm ET on @hbomax . pic.twitter.com/yAyG8u2PZ9
"The challenge I had was: How do you deliver the same message to the majority of the guys? You're also trying to make them think that we're all new, and you're trying to get them to understand that this is who we are. It's really important that they hear it," Macdonald said.
"And next one is our style of play, which is a good time because we're kind of in the meat of camp ... I think of it in terms of like, we're in the install phase of training camp, so we're installing our systems, I'm installing our culture."
Macdonald, Johnson and Wright then began sharing stories about how San Antonio scouted French phenom and 2023 No. 1 overall pick Victor Wembanyama, who led his team to the NBA Finals in just his third professional season.
"Our CEO saw him. He was in the gym, and it just happened to be in the gym. I wasn't planning to see him. He was 16, or just about to turn 16, and came back after his trip. I think he is the greatest player I've ever seen in my life," Wright said.
"Literally, 12 months later, we put the plan in motion to turn the team over and have the chance to draft him in a couple years."
Johnson added how Wembanyama has always put the team in front of himself, which is something Macdonald has stressed with the Seahawks. Wembanyama has also stressed about wanting to be the greatest basketball player ever, which is another way the two teams can align.
Macdonald has spoken about putting the team ahead of oneself throughout the entirety of his tenure with the Seahawks, but especially in this year's training camp. Most of the players in the locker room saw firsthand how that philosophy led them to a Super Bowl and how it could lead them to another one this year.
While the Seahawks and Spurs have different challenges in their way of reaching their goals, it's clear that the two teams have relatively similar thought processes. Considering the fact that they have been some of the most successful teams in their respective sport, it seems like their way of thinking is the way moving forward.

title: The Latest on Nick Emmanwori's Injury in Seahawks Training Camp
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive back Nick Emmanwori is recovering from ankle surgery, and he hopes to be on the field with the team for the Week 1 opener against the New England Patriots on Sept. 9.
Emmanwori is making steps in the right direction, but they might not be fast enough to be healthy and ready to go for the team at the start of the season.
Emmanwori did pass his physical to clear him to return to practice, which is a big step in the right direction. However, ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler is reporting that Emmanwori is not guaranteed to play in Week 1.
Emmanwori, 22, missed three games for the Seahawks last season due to injury early in the year, but once he got over his Week 1 ailment, he made it through the rest of the year. The Seahawks were holding off on surgery for a while, but they felt that this was the best path forward to ensure that the second-year pro would stay healthy for the long haul.
With Emmanwori on the sidelines, the Seahawks have a difficult task in replacing him because he often plays multiple positions. Emmanwori is usually in the nickel role, but he can also play safety and even linebacker.
In regards to the safety spot, the team will likely give an increased role to D'Anthony Bell, who has had a strong start in training camp so far. Bell was with the Seahawks last season until he was shockingly cut. In late December, he was claimed off waivers by the Carolina Panthers but signed back with the Seahawks during free agency.
The team could also give second-round pick Bud Clark more reps as he looks to make an impact in his rookie season, similar to how Emmanwori did for Seattle. Third-round cornerback Julian Neal has been dealing with a leg injury of his own, but he also has a chance to fill in for Emmanwori while he is out.
The goal is to get Emmanwori back on the field before Week 1, and the team will do everything in its power to make that happen. If he has to sit for a game or two, there is a decent amount of depth that can ensure the team will be able to move forward without him.

title: 3 Potential Storylines for Seahawks' Hard Knocks Episode 2
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks fans will be turning on the television for the second episode of " Hard Knocks " at 6 p.m. PT. Fans can watch tonight's episode on HBO or stream it on HBO Max.
This episode should chronicle the last segment of training camp leading up to the team's fan fest practice at Lumen Field this past weekend. Here's a look at three things that could become storylines in the latest episode.
The Seahawks made Jaxon Smith-Njigba the highest-paid wide receiver in the league this offseason, even if it was only for a little bit of time after the Los Angeles Rams extended Puka Nacua. Yet, JSN did not receive much screentime during the premiere last week.
It wouldn't be a surprise to see Smith-Njigba get a little bit more screen time and possibly a one-on-one feature during the episode. Smith-Njigba went from 1,130 yards in 2024 to 1,793 yards in 2025, which led the league. He was first-team All-Pro and the offensive player of the year. He's one of the more recognizable superstars for the Seahawks, so fans should be curious as to what he's been up to during the offseason.
Hard knocks loves a good undrafted free agent story, and Montorie Foster could be that for the Seahawks this season.
Foster is not a rookie after playing on the practice squad for the team for a little over a month last season. His story is the quintessential feel-good one. After going undrafted out of Michigan State and suffering an injury during training camp last offseason, Foster returned to his native Ohio and became a substitute teacher. He continued to train and healed enough to earn a spot on the practice squad in Seattle on December 30. About six weeks later, Foster was a Super Bowl champion.
He has been one of the players to watch during training camp so far, and he's making a case to be a surprise addition to the 53-man roster.
The episode should end with the team practicing at Lumen Field for Fan Fest, which is a full-circle moment for defensive back A.J. Finley. Finley tore his ACL at last year's Fan Fest, and he sat out the entire 2025 campaign as the Seahawks wound up winning a Super Bowl.
Finley is fully healed and hoping to make an impact for the 2026 team, and he showed a little bit of what he can do in his return to Fan Fest. Finley picked off quarterback Sam Darnold during practice, which led to a massive celebration from the defense.
It should be exciting to see how that moment plays out on tonight's episode.

title: The Biggest Decision Seahawks Must Make This Week vs. Cowboys
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into their first preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys with a lot of question marks surrounding their roster.
One of the top position battles the team is dealing with is the backup quarterback role, which Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe are fighting for. The Seahawks also have to figure out how many reps they want to give Sam Darnold and the first-team offense.
The Seahawks should want to keep Darnold rested, but they may also want to get some of the rest built throughout the offseason. Every team operates differently, but giving Darnold and the first-team offense a series or two could be the right decision as they ramp up their progress going into the regular season.
There is less than a month between now and the start of the regular season on September 9 against the New England Patriots. Darnold and the offense should get some reps.
Expected Playing Time: 1-2 Series, 1st Quarter
The big decision the Seahawks have to make is in regards to who comes in after Darnold. There is an argument to be made for both Lock and Milroe, but as the veteran backup, Lock gets the likely first look.
Lock was the team's backup last season, but he didn't have to start any games because Darnold stayed healthy and strong throughout the entire season. Lock has one year remaining on his deal and 28 NFL starts to his name since he was a second-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft by the Denver Broncos out of Missouri. Lock has not done anything to lose the backup job, which is why he should get the first chance to back up Darnold in the preseason.
Expected Playing Time: 1-2 Series, 2nd Quarter
The preseason is the opportunity for the Seahawks to truly see what they have in Milroe, who has stacked some good practices during the first part of training camp. There is a chance Milroe could overtake Lock for the backup job , but he will have to do a lot during the preseason in order to shake things up.
Milroe will likely get to play the entire second half against the Cowboys, which will give him the chance to earn more reps and get better as a quarterback. The Seahawks might also want to incorporate other packages for Milroe, just to see where they can utilize him. This is what the preseason is about.
Macdonald can experiment with his team without the penalty or threat of losing a football game, so he should get as creative as he can, creating sub-packages and ways for Milroe, the team's third-round pick in the 2025 draft, to be on the field.
Expected Playing Time: 4-6 Series, 3rd and 4th Quarters

title: What Jake Bobo's Training Camp Return from Injury Means for Seahawks
full_text:
Every practice is critical for the Seattle Seahawks during training camp . Some role players get the chance to elevate themselves in the depth chart and get more chances on the field. Wide receiver Jake Bobo entered training camp feeling great after a new contract with the Seahawks. His momentum fell short early during training camp as he suffered a hamstring injury.
On Monday, Bobo returned to the field after nearly two weeks , but not without some development with the team. He returns to the team with his regular spot, but with some changes elsewhere.
Usually, when a non-starter is out for nearly two weeks during training camp, their spot on the 53-man roster is in trouble. With Bobo and the Seahawks, however, there is an understanding that he is more valuable than his regular-season stats from last year. He is among the wide receivers who spent the most time on the Seahawks’ roster.  Bobo is entering his fourth season in the league, all of them in Seattle.
Bobo has caught 34 receptions for 323 yards and three touchdowns in his three years. He has, however, played in 45 games and made three starts. He made a pivotal 17-yard touchdown catch in the NFC Championship win over the Los Angeles Rams. This was easily the biggest play in his career .
Ultimately, he is one of the best run blockers from the receiver corps. He also provides great effort and knowledge to the Seahawks’ offense. Even with a new offensive coordinator in Brian Fleury, Bobo feels comfortable with the offensive schemes and how he is best utilized. There could be potential big moment games where he might be the top receiver . Regardless, he is one of the heart and souls of the receiver corps. He isn’t going anywhere.
Bobo’s absence did, however, open some room for a possible seventh receiver spot to be addressed. With him out, this allowed second-year draft pick Ricky White III, veteran Cody White, formerly undrafted second-year Montrorie Foster Jr. and rookie Emmanuel Henderson to take advantage of the extra reps in practices. Both Cody and Ricky White spent some time on the Seahawks’ roster last season.
Both Henderson and Foster, however, have been some of the best performers in the last few practices. They are making a great impression this training camp before the Seahawks are set to take on the Dallas Cowboys. Bobo’s absence got them some great reps in practices. They can follow it up with a big game in either of the preseason games.

title: Raheem Morris Receives Another Vote of Confidence From a 49ers DB
full_text:
Another 49ers defensive back is loving how Raheem Morris’s defense is benefiting them.
It makes sense since Morris is a defensive-backs-oriented coach. First, it was Renardo Green , thrilled with the defense. Then, it was Ji’Ayir Brown , who raved about it. Now, it’s second-year safety Marques Sigle with another vote of confidence in Morris.
“With Raheem, he’s allowing us to be aggressive, play to our skill set,” Sigle said. “It’s making it for us to just not think and allowing us to be playmakers. I feel that’s better for us. I feel we have the type of guys to just go out there and play and not react.”
It shouldn’t be surprising that Morris’ defense is favorable to the secondary. That’s been a common factor for every defense he’s run on every team he’s been on. That’s his staple.
It’s part of what made him a great fit for the 49ers. Their cornerbacks fell off last season, outside of Upton Stout. Their safeties were massively underwhelming as well.
The 49ers needed their entire secondary to improve significantly this year. Now, with Morris at the helm, the entire secondary looks poised to break out this season. It could end up being the best season for a 49ers secondary under Kyle Shanahan.
The only time they had an incredibly strong one was in 2020. That was when Nick Bosa was out for the season with a torn ACL, among many other injured players that made the pass rush irrelevant.
This year’s group of defensive backs can be better than the 2020 one, even though they had Jason Verrett. The 49ers don’t have a secondary player as good as him on their roster.
But what they lack in stardom, they make up for in quantity. A trio of Stout, Green, and Deommodore Lenoir under Morris can be a top-five unit. And if Morris’ system can propel the safeties, they’re cooking with fire.
Given how every defensive back has been thrilled with Morris’ defense, I’d imagine they will all perform collectively at an adequate level. It’ll surpass last season at least, which isn’t an astounding bar to clear.
Still, Morris appears to be the right coach to unlock and push the 49ers’ defensive backs. Time will tell if he truly is the answer.

title: What the 49ers' Plan is for the Starters in the First Preseason Game
full_text:
The first preseason game is right around the corner for the San Francisco 49ers .
It's always an exciting buildup because it's the first time seeing what a team will look like. However, since it's a preseason game, there's no guarantee that the starters will play much, if at all.
In the past, the 49ers have either sat most of their starters in the first game or only let them play for a series or two. On Tuesday, Kyle Shanahan revealed what the 49ers' plan is for the starters.
"There won't be many starters playing," Shanahan said. "We'll see with injuries today and stuff. That doesn't mean none, but we've got to balance that out. We haven't told the players yet, so wait until we do that with them this afternoon.”
It's not surprising that most of the 49ers starters won't suit up against the Tennessee Titans. They got their quality reps when they held a joint practice with them .
That is what Shanahan has always valued more than anything. Since they received those reps, there's no point in the starters playing in the first preseason game.
Now, that doesn't mean every single starter will be inactive. The 49ers don't have that many players to afford that luxury, given all of their injuries.
I'd anticipate Renardo Green playing, a few offensive linemen like Jake Brendel, and even Ji'Ayir Brown. But players like Dre Greenlaw, Mike Evans, and Osa Odighizuwa, I wouldn't expect.
This is totally fine for the 49ers to do after they had a successful joint practice, according to reports. Most of the starters deserve this rest and protection from playing a pointless game.
Besides, the second preseason game is when Shanahan tends to play the starters mostly. That is where you'll see two or three series from the majority of starters.
Although I still wouldn't expect Christian McCaffrey, Trent Williams, Fred Warner, Greenlaw, and Evans to be out there. Those are players who are prohibited from preseason action.
If they are going to suffer an injury, it has to happen when it matters in the regular season. The last thing they want is for them to get hurt in an exhibition, costing them part of the year, if not more.
Plus, they're players who don't need the preseason ramp-up. They're revved up during training camp and don't hold back.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Reveals the Truth About Nick Bosa's Injury
full_text:
There was always something fishy about Nick Bosa missing 49ers practice for over a week with "soreness." That's not a diagnosis that typically keeps a player out for so long.
It turns out that Bosa has more than just soreness, which is what I suspected in a previous article . On Tuesday, Kyle Shanahan revealed the truth about Bosa's injury.
"Tendinitis. It's a pretty normal thing with ACLs," Shanahan said . "It's a normal thing. That's why we've got to be smart here for week to week. No concerns about him, it being more than that."
Well, that's interesting. If it was always tendinitis and it wasn't a concern, why conceal it? If it's so "normal," why is it initially being downplayed?
The 49ers treat injuries to players like a secret formula. Shanahan could've said this from the beginning and it wouldn't have been suspicision.
But now that Bosa has missed a couple more practices since he last spoke, he knows the 49ers can no longer downplay it or keep it hidden.
So, Bosa is week-to-week with tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee, but it's normal. If it's tendinitis and his knee is potentially swollen, this could be an issue throughout the season.
Bosa could play one game, then all of a sudden his tendinitis flares up for a week, keeping him out of the next game. It's a tricky scenario because of how unpredictable it is.
That means the 49ers can't count on Bosa to play all 17 games. He made it through six practices before his knee gave him issues.
How on earth is he going to play for most of a season? It feels like Bosa is more likely to play in seven games than 17. That's how concerning this is.
On one end, it's awesome that he didn't suffer anything significant. On the other end, this does carry some significance if it leads to him missing a handful of games or being limited.
Time will tell how this works out for Bosa and the 49ers. One thing is for sure: they need him out there every game. Their pass rush is irrelevant without him.
Rookie Romello Height can't be their top option on the edge. He'll only be effective when Bosa is on the field, which means everything is reliant on Bosa.
The 49ers better hope their secondary plays well this year because that is where the strength of their defense will be.

title: The Good and Not So Good from 49ers-Titans Practice: Stribling Outplays Tate
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just wrapped up Day 11 of training camp, which was a joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. Here's who stood out. Keep in mind that after practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan said Nick Bosa is dealing with knee tendinitis that is related to his ACL recovery . More on Bosa in a minute.
Outplayed Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who was the fourth pick in the draft. Tate didn't catch many passes, and when he did make a catch, he often had to lay out. As opposed to Stribling, who caught a team-high 7 passes during 11-on-11 team drills, and caught them in stride. He was Brock Purdy's go-to guy, particularly outside the red zone where Stribling's speed stretches the field and stresses defenses. Cornerbacks give him such a big cushion, which opens up underneath routes for him. He's a terrific complement for Demarcus Robinson, who's more of a possession receiver and red-zone specialist. Stribling isn't currently a huge threat in the red zone, but he could develop that part of the game in time. Expect him to get a ton of playing time and targets this season as long as he's healthy.
He's not particularly fast, but he's big and tough and dependable, similar to Jauan Jennings. Robinson is fearless over the middle, he has a big catch radius and he's at his best in the end zone where he made two catches today. Theoretically, Mike Evans can do all these things even better, but he has been injured for most of camp, while Robinson hasn't missed a day. Don't be surprised if Robinson outproduces Evans this season, simply because Evans is older and breaking down.
It's funny, when the 49ers practice against themselves, Tonges often is an afterthought, for whatever reason. Maybe the coaches want to see what other players can do. But today, in a competitive practice against another team during which Christian McCaffrey is not participating, suddenly Tonges is Purdy's security blanket. Today, he caught multiple passes downfield. He needs to be a constant fixture in the offense this year, even after George Kittle comes back. Because Kittle is coming off a torn Achilles and won't be able to carry the offense the way he has in the past.
Shredded a talented defense while missing a starting running back, a starting tight end and two starting wide receivers. With the exception of one day, Purdy has been lights-out in training camp. As opposed to Titans quarterback Cam Ward, who never seemed to know where he wanted to go with the football.
Undercut and intercepted a pass over the middle thrown by Cam Ward. Brown isn't the fastest safety and he has a troubling tendency to give up long catches over his head, but he also breaks confidently on passes in front of him, as he did on this play. Unfortunately, after the play, he ran over to Cam Ward, mockingly handed him the ball and got flagged for taunting. In fairness to Brown, he doesn't make good plays that often, so he was excited.
He's not going to intercept passes, and he will get beaten by practice squad players occassionally during 1-on-1 drills. But he's also the cornerback on the 49ers who's best suited to match up with No. 1 wide receivers because of his size and speed. And today, he used those traits to shut down rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate. We've also seen Green shut down Pro Bowlers such as Davante Adams as recently as last year. Green clearly raises his game when it matters.
Made a diving interception on a pass thrown by Will Levis. Robinson is the 49ers' most intriguing young cornerback. He has an outside chance to make the 53-man roster if he has a strong preseason.
The 49ers' starting defense started practice using a five-man front with Dugger standing on the line of scrimmage as the third linebacker. This is a look the 49ers want to use against two-tight-end formations this season, and Dugger is the key to it, because he's built like a defensive end, and yet he played safety in college, so he's a hybrid player. He can set the edge against the run and drop into coverage as well. He just might start right away.
Returned yesterday from a concussion and instantly became the second-string left guard, which means he's one injury or benching away from becoming the starter. As opposed to Connor Colby, who has been demoted to backup right guard behind Dominick Puni. I expect Willis will finish the season as the starting left guard, because the current starter is Robert Jones, and he's a veteran stopgap who won't be on the team next year.
Still hasn't practiced or shown up to practice since last Monday. Today, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Bosa is suffering from knee tendinitis that is related to his latest ACL rehab. Shanahan said that tendinitis is common during these recoveries. Still, it seems Bosa's injury is worse than the 49ers initially let on. And that's a problem, because he essentially is their pass rush. The 49ers should trade him before the season starts if they can find a taker. Maybe they can trade him to the Raiders straight up for Maxx Crosby.
Missed his second practice in a row with "tightness." Shanahan said McCaffrey's injury is nothing to be worried about, but that's what he said two years ago when calf tightness ended McCaffrey's training camp early and eventually caused him to miss the first eight games of the season. And just today, Bosa's "soreness" magically became knee tendinitis. So, it's impossible to know what's really going on with McCaffrey and how severe his issue is. We'll find out soon enough.
Suited up for practice, but didn't actually compete against the Titans. He watched Stribling and Robinson compete and play well. Two years ago, Evans was way better than those two. Now, he moves around as if everything hurts.

title: 8 Biggest Takeaways from the 49ers' First Depth Chart
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers released their first unofficial depth chart of the preseason . Since it is named unofficial and will change once the preseason starts, it is not the biggest piece of information. However, there are some notable pieces of information that can give us a baseline of what to expect.
What are the biggest highlights?
49ers first UNOFFICIAL depth chart is out for preseason opener Thursday vs Titans, who are here in Santa Clara today for joint practice pic.twitter.com/pIwakPL6qa
Not only was Connor Colby not the starting left guard, but he was also listed at right guard, with Carver Willis backing up Robert Jones on the left side. Colby started training camp with the first-team, but appears to have already lost his spot.
The team did not choose who their backup running back would be. Both were listed on the same line. This could be good for the rookie who typically starts from behind. Still, James has not been healthy and could make up ground when he does return.
Robinson went from roster bubble to potentially starting. He was listed ahead of Christian Kirk and De’Zhaun Stribling as the third receiver with Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans.
Brett Toth was signed to fill the backup center role. He has been banged up, but the progression of Nugent might be the story. He is pushing Toth for the backup spot. Now, the question is whether Toth enters the left guard competition.
Halton is a rookie who has missed time. Still, it is notable that he is behind second-year lineman Sebastian Valdez. Valdez spent last year on the practice squad and is now trying to make a push for the roster. He has to hold off Halton and two rookie UDFAs, Bryson Eason and James Thompson.
Reports have been that Nick Martin has gotten work at the SAM . However, he was listed behind Dre Greenlaw as the WILL. Gifford was the starting SAM, with Jaden Dugger and Jalen Graham behind him. Their body types fit the role better than Martin.
The same five the team finished the season with are listed as starters. This is notable because the team brought in an influx of competition. Nate Hobbs is listed as the backup slot, so he is not pushing Renardo Green in the way that Jack Jones is.
Deebo Samuel is first-team on kick returns while Cowing is leading the punt return unit.

title: 2 Reasons 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Quad Injury Is Still Problematic
full_text:
A handful of 49ers players have been out of action at training camp due to injuries.
One of the notable players who has been out of practice is Mike Evans. He’s dealing with a quad strain that he sustained well over a week ago, which the 49ers have assured is nothing serious at all.
“He’s got a little quad right now,” said Kyle Shanahan. “I know Mike probably believes he could be back right now. We’re being smart with him, but he’s going to be good to go.”
Evans was able to suit back up in pads on Tuesday, but didn't participate in the joint-practice portion with the Tennessee Titans. Regardless, for a "little" quad strain, to miss that many practices is problematic. Here are two reasons explaining why it is.
Being out of five practices is stunting the connection Evans was building with Brock Purdy . These two need training camp for their rapport to come together.
I’m sure it’s at an adequate level now, but for them to be clicking perfectly on all cylinders, they need reps in training camp. The last thing they want is to figure it out during games.
They can’t be wasting precious game snaps trying to get on the same page. They should already be there, if not close to it. Evans being out of practice hurts that, which is why Purdy is connecting with rookie De’Zhaun Stribling a lot.
Don’t be surprised if Evans and Purdy aren’t consistently on the same page for the first half of the season. Should that come to pass, and I think it will, Evans’ absence will be the cause of it.
Evans’ quad strain isn’t a massive concern, but it could be indicative of his 2026 season. Soft tissue injuries in a soon-to-be 33-year-old player can linger throughout the season, especially for one who had a hamstring issue last year.
His quad strain can be the first sign and a reminder that his body is breaking down. It’s not surprising to see given his age and the mileage. If anything, it’d be surprising if he was mostly healthy.
This is the risk the 49ers took on Evans. He could easily struggle to suit up and miss a handful of games. Without him, the 49ers’ offense will take a hit. It’ll also prove that Evans is entering a “washed” part of his career.

title: 49ers Guard Battle Takes Major Turn With Carver Willis Return
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' left guard competition is finally starting to heat up. After the team started things with Connor Colby as the first-team option in the first week or two of camp, they are starting to shuffle things up, and we are seeing a different blend. Now, rookie fourth-round pick Carver Willis has returned from his concussion.
He did not get mixed in with the starters yet, but Willis did immediately jump in with the second-team at left guard . The 49ers elected to push Colby to right guard and let Robert Jones, who had been getting work with the second team, jump in with the ones.
The 49ers also signed Doug Kramer, who will step in as the third-team center. Some of the reason is that Brett Toth, One who was the backup center, is banged up. Drake Nugent jumped from third team to the second unit, but the 49ers still needed someone to play with the third string. So, they signed Kramer.
At the same time, when Toth comes back, he could end up being more involved in the guard competition. While none of Jones, Toth, or Willis has been able to take the job from Colby, one thing is for certain, and that is that Colby is not winning the job on his own.
So, while it has just been Jones getting work with the first-team now that they have moved Colby to the right side, the other two should start to get more work with the first unit as well.
Willis is intriguing because he is a former left tackle in college . It means there has to be a transition, but at the same time, he is plenty athletic and capable of shifting inside. The 49ers' current starter at right guard was a tackle in college who kicked inside and thrived.
However, Toth is a great veteran to have. The 49ers liked his versatility, and while he has been working at center, they might want to get him some work at guard.
The player getting the most work with the first group right now is Jones. Jones was with the Dallas Cowboys last year, but did not play a single snap due to a neck injury. Before that, he did start for the Miami Dolphins.
The preseason is going to shape this competition that appears to have only just begun.

title: 49ers Coach Opens Up about Rookie Jaden Dugger's Intriguing Transition
full_text:
While it has been hard to get a good read on the progress of San Francisco 49ers rookie fifth-round pick Jaden Dugger, a lot of that has been because of the coaches' decisions and not his. However, linebackers coach K.J. Wright made it clear that the lack of development in one specific thing is a good thing when it comes to the long-term potential of the young linebacker.
KJ Wright on Jaden Dugger’s versatility: “It’s really powerful. He can play in space. He can go to MIKE linebacker. He can go down on the EDGE. On third down, I can see him roaming around the guards. You can do so much with that guy and when you look at him, when offenses start… pic.twitter.com/CSJnMtm5jH
As Wright mentioned, right now, Dugger is likely stressed, and things are moving fast for him. It is hard for any fifth-round rookie to adjust to the NFL. The 49ers are asking him to play multiple different roles.
However, his ability to play middle linebacker, dime backer, or edge rusher on any given snap is what Raheem Morris is looking for out of his defense. He calls the plays ‘Fever backers ', and they are adjusters who can change the alignment of the defense without changing the personnel.
Dugger is a perfect fit for this role.
There is likely a downside and a positive aspect to this.
The downside is that it is hard to see him getting on the field in a significant role right away. He is learning a little bit of everything, but that means that he is not fully NFL-ready in any area.
The 49ers' linebacker room is deeper than others, and the thought leading into training camp is that he has to push to make a roster spot, given he was taken so late.
However, the 49ers are not going to cut a player they are so high on in training camp with the physical attributes he has. It does mean there is a good chance he will be inactive to start the year, unless he can carve out a role on special teams.
Still, it puts the 49ers in a great spot when it comes to his development. They are able to slow-play him and let him work in different roles at practice without exposing him during the games.
The big question is going to be what type of role they use him in during the preseason. Does he align solely at linebacker, and if so, what role? If he's behind Fred Warner as the MIKE, or is he behind Dre Greenlaw in the WILL? There is a lot to follow for a player who might not play at all this year.

title: Four Late 49ers Additions Could Play Major Roles in Preseason Opener
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers edge rusher room has a lot of injury questions. It has caused the team to sign four new players who were not with the team when training camp opened. Based on the injury status and practice reports in the room, there is a good chance that all four are going to get significant playing time in the 49ers first preseason game.
Nick Bosa has been in and out of the lineup as he recovers from his ACL injury. The odds of him playing in the preseason are low. Mykel Williams has yet to return from his ACL injury and Keion White has been banged up in training camp as well.
So, Sam Okuayinonnu and Romello Height are the two players most likely to make the roster and suit up for the 49ers. Still, the 49ers are mostly looking for Height to step into a pass rush specialist role. So, the team is going to see a lot of the four new additions.
Bell has bounced around the NFL and has made active rosters for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Atlanta Falcons and Miami Dolphins. Last year he played 114 defensive snaps and 132 special teams snaps for the Dolphins, so he is NFL capable.
Okoronkwo is the most likely to stick on the 53-man roster . He was a solid rotational rusher, but he suffered a pec injury last year with the Philadelphia Eagles that sidelined him for the season. Still, he is familiar with Raheem Morris, and he should get a lot of the snaps as the backup speed rusher behind Height.
Henry was signed this summer and has a chance to make the roster. However, he last saw the field on defense in 2024. He made the Cleveland Browns active roster later into the 2025 season, but played just five snaps on special teams. This is a massive opportunity for him.
Leo has bounced around the NFL since being a 2023 sixth-round pick. The last active roster he made was in 2024. He has stuck in the NFL and will get cleanup opportunities in the preseason. However, he will mostly be fighting to make the practice squad.
Bell and Okoronkwo have legitimate chances to make the 53-man roster, and Henry and Leo could stick on the practice squad due to the injuries and depth questions.

title: 49ers Training Camp has Raised More Questions than Answers
full_text:
A week and a half of 49ers training camp has passed, and the projections for the 2026 season look worse than before the team hit the practice field.
The 49ers have been hit by a wave of adversity, from an unforeseen car accident that kept head coach Kyle Shanahan away from his duties to a wave of injuries that feeds into a mysterious substation theory.
These sobering outcomes have sucked all of the preseason optimism out of the fanbase.
Yes, the 49ers can still be good in the upcoming season, but as of now, expectations have simmered as injuries continue daily.
On the offensive side of the ball, the team has suffered injuries to almost every skill position player, with a high-upside player in wide receiver Ricky Pearsall ruled out for the season. The injuries at that position kept rolling in with Mike Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling and running backs Kaelon Black and Jordan James.
The 49ers offense is already without George Kittle, who tore his Achilles at the end of last season.
This leaves Christian McCaffrey as the only healthy high-usage skill player from the 2025 season, and he had one of the highest usage rates of all time, which, for McCaffrey’s health, shouldn’t be repeated. Plus, he missed Monday's practice with "tightness."
Without the projected skill players, the 49ers offense is behind and losing chemistry because the team had to sign players who won’t be on the roster by the time training camp finishes.
On the bright side, quarterback Brock Purdy is reportedly having the best camp of his career, and if he can bring this play consistently, it will improve the team around him.
The defensive side of the ball will need to set the tone for the 49ers in a slightly adjusted scheme under new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris.
Coach Morris should be a good breath of fresh air, adjusting a scheme that has made a few schematic changes throughout the past 10 years.
Even then, the defense still has question marks, with Nick Bosa missing practices the past week with mysterious soreness, as well as questions about how the defense will adjust to a new scheme.
The defensive line looks improved from last season, which is great, given that the team had the fewest sacks in the NFL by a wide margin.
The cornerbacks are good but have struggled to force turnovers. Deommodore Lenoir is a lockdown corner, and Upton Stout is a physical nickel, but he lacks size against bigger receivers. On the other side, Renardo Green is good but needs to work on making plays on the ball.
I don’t expect much from the 49ers safeties; Ji’Ayir Brown hasn’t been good, lacking speed and instincts. I liken Brown’s instincts to Malik Mustapha’s; they both seem to be late on back-breaking plays.
Marques Sigle may have the highest ceiling in the safety room. Last year, in limited playing time, Sigle showed the ability to be in position to make plays but needs to work on finishing them.
The linebackers are improved from last year, with more depth and Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw back in the lineup. Nick Martin, who has been the third linebacker most of camp, will need to show his abilities throughout the preseason.
If the 49ers want a successful 2026 season, the team will need to find answers to these questions throughout training camp and into Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams.

title: One Buccaneers Player Who Missed Last Season Has Jason Licht Fired Up
full_text:
Buccaneers 2025 fourth-round pick David Walker has been very impressive throughout training camp to this point. Walker has been able to make a great number of plays in practice, having plenty of would-be sacks against backups and starters alike.
One person who is very excited to see what Walker can do this 2026 season is general manager Jason Licht.  According to Jason Licht, when speaking to WDAE, the excitement for Walker is "on an even plane" with that of rookie Rueben Bain Jr.
Now that is a pretty bold comparison for Licht to make, as Bain was the fifteenth overall pick in the most recent NFL Draft and Walker was a fourth-round selection last year. However, both players have looked very impressive in training camp so far and should be a very bright spot in a hopefully new and improved pass rush for the Bucs' defense this season.
Licht is not the only person in the Buccaneers organization to give praise to Walker. Speaking to the media on August sixth after practice, here is what head coach Todd Bowles had to say about what he's been impressed with regarding Walker.
"Just his energy and his athleticism [have] showed up," Bowles said. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves. He moves like an inside [linebacker], but he plays outside [linebacker] and he [has] great power. To see him out there playing fast and not worried about his knee is great."
Another player who had a very good impression of Walker was veteran pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad.
"He has a motor. The good ones, as far as [defensive] linemen and pass rushers, and all that good stuff, they play with a motor, and he plays with a motor. For his size, he knows who he is and the things that he [does], he [does] well. He's been having a [great] camp, so it's impressive."
Time will tell how much of an impact Walker will have this upcoming season. He's still competing for reps with a lot of players, including Muhammad, Bain Jr, and other veterans like Yaya Diaby, Anthony Nelson and even Chris Braswell if he does make the final roster. However, the organization certainly has a lot of high hopes for the young second-year player.

title: Will Baker Mayfield Play in Buccaneers' First Preseason Game vs. Jets?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gone through 10 days of training camp, including their joint practice with the New York Jets on Tuesday. After all of that, it's almost time for the team's first preseason game of the year.
The Bucs are set to face the Jets Friday, and when they do so, they'll be looking to evaluate many of their rookies for the first time under the lights. These games can be very important for that evaluation, and as a result, it's also important to make sure other players on the squad can play well enough around them to properly evaluate them.
With that in mind, head coach Todd Bowles has the decision on whether or not to play his starting quarterback in Baker Mayfield. The option is also worth considering in the wake of a potential injury to backup quarterback Jake Browning on Tuesday.
So will the Buccaneers play Mayfield in their first preseason outing this season?
Mayfield is not set to play during Tampa Bay's preseason game on Friday against the Jets. Initially, quarterback Jake Browning was set to start that game, but he injured his back during the first day of joint training camp, so his status on Friday is in jeopardy, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud.
Bucs No. 2 QB Jake Browning appeared to injure his back. Todd Bowles had no update but Browning was expected to start Friday vs Jets. He said Baker Mayfield will not play.
That makes sense. Mayfield is the team's starting quarterback, and it would be unusual to play him in the first preseason game of the year unless he specifically requested it as some quarterbacks do.
That being said, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield plays during the preseason at all. Last year, he skipped out on preseason entirely — he was slated to play during the team's second week of preseason against the Pittsburgh Steelers last year, but Bowles decided against it at the last minute and did not play him at all during the preseason.
There's a chance that a similar scenario could happen this preseason, too. For now, though, the Bucs will have to figure out what they plan to do on Friday if Browning isn't able to go — reps will be split between QBs Jalon Daniels and Connor Bazelak, if that's the case.
The Bucs play the Jets at 7 p.m. on Friday.

title: Baker Mayfield Wants His 'Lick Back' in Buccaneers 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers started out 6-2 in 2025, and things were looking up for quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield was an MVP candidate, and vibes were great in Tampa Bay.
Those vibes didn't end up continuing throughout the season, though. The Bucs went 2-7 over their last nine games and, presumably due to injuries, Mayfield's play deteriorated. Some thought that head coach Todd Bowles' job was in danger, but he kept his job and plans to coach the Bucs in 2026.
Mayfield and the rest of Tampa Bay's squad, who were there for the 2025 season, weren't happy about how it ended. Mayfield recently had a contract saga this offseason, where he placed a training camp deadline for an extension that he and the team did not meet, but he's stressed that he's all ball from here on out after that saga has come to a close.
Mayfield may be unhappy about his contract situation, but in a recent appearance on the 4th & South podcast with Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette, he seems far unhappier about what happened last season — and he's solely focused on fixing it.
Mayfield was very vocal about his disappointment after he couldn't get an extension done with the Bucs. He told Fournette and Landry that if some people are unhappy with that, it's too bad — but he promised to rectify the team's mistakes from last season this year.
"I've always worn my emotions and thoughts on my sleeve. If you like that, that's great. If you don't, that's too bad — I'm not gonna change for you," Mayfield said. "There's the business side of football. Yes, we all play this for a job, but they know that when it comes to gamedays, I'm ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026 — we didn't play well enough in 2025, so it's on go."
Baker Mayfield on contract negotiations not distracting him from how he’ll come to play in 2026 for Bucs. “They [team] knows when it comes to gamedays, I’m ready for a good season. I want my lick back in 2026. We didn’t play well in ‘25. It’s on go.” (via @4thAndSouthPod ) pic.twitter.com/zeGjg5V9rG
Tampa Bay and Mayfield could be in the position to do just that this season. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson could be a better option at offensive coordinator than Josh Grizzard, and new offensive weapons like running back Kenny Gainwell and wideout Ted Hurst could improve the offense in a big way.
There's still quite a bit of time until Mayfield can try and get that lick back. For now, though, the Bucs will continue joint training camp passes vs. the New York Jets this week before a preseason game on Friday.

title: Multiple Fights Occur at Buccaneers Joint Practice vs. Jets
full_text:
Today was the first day of joint practices between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the New York Jets, and to say that things got heated in practice is a bit of an understatement.
Multiple fights occurred during practice today between the two teams, with defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson being involved in one, per Jeff Dubrof, and offensive guard Luke Goedeke being involved in two, per Ralph Vacchiano .
The first fight that Goedeke was involved in included rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who wanted to go against Goedeke in one-on-one drills, which then resulted in said fight. This is what Goedeke had to say on the incident, per Pewter Report:
︀︀“Well, [David Bailey] called me out in one-on-ones and wanted to go against me and lost, and then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare], I believe, came from the side and just cheapshotted me."
Bucs RT Luke Goedeke on the practice fights with the Jets on Tuesday: “Well, [David Bailey] called me out in 1-on-1’s and wanted to go against me and lost. And then tried shoving me after that, and 52 [Kingsley Enagbare] I believe came from the side and just cheapshotted me." pic.twitter.com/AIP6fG7nw2
The Bucs were already dealing with some pushing and shoving matches occurring in their own training camp practices before making the jump to New Jersey to practice with the Jets. This is usually the time of year when teams get very antsy and are typically ready for live game reps and the regular season.
It is also important to remember that these two teams do have a bit of recent history. They played each other in a close matchup last season, where the Bucs would win 29-27. The Jets, however, came very close to winning said matchup on a blocked field goal that gave them the lead late. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn would then be seen dancing down the sidelines as the Jets took the lead over the Bucs.
Also, the Bucs have spent a good amount of effort this off-season improving their mentality and grit when it comes to the roster. Players like A'Shawn Robinson were added to players like Luke Goedeke to give the team more of an edge and to help change some of the more laid-back attitude the team had in the past couple of seasons.
Overall, fights during practices are not ideal, but not surprising. Football is a very physical sport, and these things happen all the time. The Bucs and Jets face off on August 14th in the Bucs' first preseason matchup and should have another joint practice on the schedule soon. We'll see if more fighting occurs.

title: What Stands Out From the Buccaneers' First Unofficial Depth Chart
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in New York to face off against the Jets during joint practice, which will culminate in a preseason game on Friday. The Bucs will have quite a few decisions to make once they see how their players look against other NFL teams over the next three weeks.
As of right now, though, they have at least a small idea. The Buccaneers put out their first unofficial depth chart of the year, and while it's mostly standard fare, there are a few interesting things to note.
Here's what we can glean from the Buccaneers' first depth chart of 2026:
The Bucs have released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 season. — Rueben Bain Jr. named starter — SirVoccea Dennis still listed as starter — Jacob Parrish starts over Benjamin Morrison at outside CB pic.twitter.com/AOHBHOFviO
Perhaps the biggest thing to note about the depth chart is what's going on at outside cornerback.
As it stands, defensive back Jacob Parrish looks to hold the starting outside corner spot alongside Zyon McCollum. Parrish, who excelled at the nickel corner spot last season for Tampa Bay to the tune of two interceptions, was moved to the outside room this offseason after the Bucs drafted Miami standout Keionte Scott to fill in at the nickel spot.
Parrish notably displaces Benjamin Morrison, who was set to fill that role alongside McCollum this offseason. Morrison injured his hamstring after the first OTAs practice and has not practiced in team drills since then, so he's had no opportunity to show his worth against Parrish so far. With that in mind, the ranking makes sense.
That isn't the only interesting development on the defensive side of the depth chart, though.
Many Buccaneers fans and NFL draft pundits are excited to see what second-round pick Josiah Trotter can do at the linebacker position for Tampa Bay this season. At the moment, though, he isn't listed as the team's starter.
Last year's starter, linebacker SirVocea Dennis, remains the incumbent starter on the first unofficial depth chart. Trotter has made some big plays in camp so far, but at the moment, it seems the team is valuing Dennis' experience in the system as training camp continues.
Edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. is listed as the starter on this depth chart, so it doesn't appear to be a matter of rookies not being placed as starters. That being said, Trotter has certainly made more splash plays than Dennis has over the course of camp, so it would be no surprise to see him overtake Dennis at some point this preseason.
The Bucs will wait to see how he plays in a game scenario, it seems. And if Trotter lives up to the hype from training camp so far, he should see himself climb the depth chart.

title: Why I'm Buying the Early Buccaneers Hype Around Ted Hurst
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in New York for joint practice sessions with the Jets after completing their first couple of weeks of training camp before their first preseason game.
There have already been a handful of standouts in camp, including the reemergence of David Walker and rookies Rueben Bain Jr. and Joshiah Trotter, who are showcasing exactly why the Bucs took them with their first two picks in the NFL Draft.
However, there has been another standout, this time on the offensive side of the ball, that I am buying the hype of: rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst.
The Bucs drafted Hurst in the third round, despite the young wideout coming from a lower-level program.
The thought is that it would take Hurst some time to adjust to the NFL and develop certain portions of his game.
And while there are still some areas of improvement as he continues his growth in acclimating to the league, the early reports are undeniable.
Hurst has been receiving early praise from his teammates and coaches alike, and for good reason.
With the Bucs' wideouts in and out of practice, for one reason or another, Hurst has stepped in for some first-team reps and continues to show why the Bucs took him in the third round.
He has looked fluid in and out of his breaks, which is spectacular given his six-foot-four frame, fast, mentally focused, strong at the point of attack, and great hands. And that doesn't even account for the fact that Todd Bowles loves how fast the rookie has picked up on the knowledge side of things.
Once looked at as a physical freak athlete that would need time to develop, it's time to really slow down and imagine how big of a role Hurst will have in the Bucs' offense that is already one of the more talented in the league.
While we are buying the early hype surrounding Hurst, he will have to continue this success into joint practices and the preseason to show he can do it against opposing defenses in live action.
Not only that, but continuing to be consistent will be key if he hopes to earn valuable reps alongside the likes of Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, Jalen McMillan, and even Tez Johnson.
Many have already started to make comparisons of Hurst to Buccaneers legend Mike Evans, and while we can see why, I don't believe he has to be Evans for him to be successful in Tampa Bay.

title: Is Todd Bowles's Patience Wearing Thin With Injured Cornerback?
full_text:
In contrast to the ongoing contractual issues surrounding some key veterans, the young players on the Buccaneers' roster appear to be trending in the right direction.
Not only are young defensive players like Jacob Parrish, Rueben Bain Jr., Josiah Trotter and Keionte Scott all making their impact felt during training camp, but offensive players like Tez Johnson, Ted Hurst, Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan are also turning heads.
Unfortunately, though, one promising young player for the Buccaneers who has not made a positive impression is cornerback Benjamin Morrison.
When Morrison slipped down partway through the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Bucs GM Jason Licht felt as though the talent was too much to pass up. Even if Morrison's injury history was the reason he was still on the board.
Although Morrison was able to recover from the hip surgery that cost him the majority of his final season at Notre Dame, it didn't take long for him to find the sidelines again as a pro.
Quad and hamstring injuries plagued Morrison throughout his rookie season, and when it was all said and done, he suited up for just 10 games total and made a minimal impact when he was on the field.
Heading into the 2026 offseason, Morrison — and the fans in Tampa — were optimistic that with a healthy training camp the young corner might finally be able to realize his talent at the NFL level.
Unfortunately, though, Morrison's OTAs and minicamp were cut short due to a soft tissue injury, and he's been on the sidelines for the entirety of training camp.
Following the Buccaneers' most recent practice this past weekend, Bucs' head coach Todd Bowles was asked about Morrison's recovery progress. Although he didn't say much, his response spoke volumes about how he feels.
"He's the same as usual," Bowles said.
Although Bowles isn't the type to openly criticize his players, this comment is a pretty clear indication that the Bucs' head coach's patience is wearing thin regarding Morrison's lack of availability.
Further emphasizing the frustration of all parties should be the fact that Morrison had a clear path to earning playing time this year, with the team having moved on from Jamel Dean, their best corner last year.
Does Morrison's most recent injury, or Bowles' comments about his availability, mean that Morrison couldn't carve out an important role on this football team? Absolutely not.
But based on how frequently Morrison has been on the sidelines as opposed to the practice field so far this offseason, it's safe to assume that he will have an uphill battle to earn his coach's trust, and ultimately, playing time on Sundays.

title: Buccaneers Sign New Cornerback, Part Ways With Injured Player
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have gone through nine days of training camp already and are set to undergo some more tough joint practices against the New York Jets this week. To do that, they need healthy bodies.
The Bucs have done better in that regard than a lot of teams so far in camp, but one room has suffered. Tampa Bay's cornerback room has been beat up for a bit, and with a big joint training camp on the horizon, the team needs a healthy player to take some reps and land in the rotation.
The Bucs signed that player on Monday, and it's a familiar face. The team announced that it brought back cornerback Roman Parodie, and in return, waived CB Kemon Hall with an injury designation.
Bucs announce they’d signed CB Roman Parodie and waived/injured CB Kemon Hall.
The Buccaneers bring back Parodie from the 2025 preseason, where he was with the team and then subsequently released. Parodie attended Ohio University, where he recorded 124 total tackles, 28 passes defensed, four tackles for loss, four fumble recoveries, three interceptions and one forced fumble.
On the way out is Hall, whom the Buccaneers signed this offseason alongside former San Francisco 49ers CB Chase Lucas. The Bucs had hoped that both would provide depth and be able to play in a pinch if needed, but both of them became injured in training camp.
As a result, Hall and Lucas have both been waived with injured designations by Tampa Bay, and Parodie will take advantage. Parodie did not spend time with another team in 2025, but he did play for the Houston Gamblers of the UFL during the spring this past year.
He'll have his first chance to impress this upcoming week, when the Bucs face the Jets both in a joint practice and a preseason game. Parodie will likely get reps early, and Tampa Bay will be watching closely to see if he makes the most of them.
