title: Buccaneers Injury Tracker: Who's Hurt as Tampa Bay Travels to Play the New York Jets?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are heading up to New York to face off against the Jets for a joint training camp practice, both for a joint practice and for a preseason game later that week. When they do so, they'll have a few players dealing with injuries.
Injuries of various severity are expected for an NFL football team, but head coach Todd Bowles has indicated that everyone is expected to make the trip to Florham Park to meet the Jets. There are a few players who could end up getting back in action during that time, and a few who will likely continue to watch from the sidelines during the intense joint practices.
Here's what the Bucs are dealing with on the injury front as they head to Florham Park:
Tristan Wirfs injured his hamstring during a conditioning test, per Bowles. He's been sporadically seen in and out of practice, but he's never participated. Recently, he's worn his jersey while watching drills with the team, so that could be a good sign.
Bowles insinuated that Wirfs could potentially get some reps during the team's joint practice with the Jets this week, but given how intense those can be, it seems unlikely. Either way, seems like he could return sooner rather than later.
Vita Vea supposedly also injured his back during that very same conditioning test and has not been practicing. He's mostly been watching the defensive line during camp in his practice jersey without participating. General manager Jason Licht told reporters the Bucs don't want to turn "a minor thing into a major thing."
The real reason Vea is likely a non-participant, however, is his current contract row with the Bucs. Vea wants an extension and has requested a trade, but it looks like neither side is currently willing to budge when it comes to that problem. Until that problem is solved, Vea will probably sit out.
Tez Johnson has had a strong training camp so far, but it could be a bit until we see him again. Johnson strained his groin during last Tuesday's indoor practice, and as a result, the Bucs will likely be cautious and keep him out of action for a bit until he's ready to play.
David Sills also injured himself during that Tuesday night practice. He appeared to have a wrap around his knee when he did so, and since then, he has not practiced. The severity of his injury is currently unknown as the team travels to New York.
Guard Billy Schrauth suffered a knee injury at some point during last week's training camp days that resulted in a brace on his knee. Bowles said that he's "sore" and "banged up" that knee, and that he'd "miss a few days" — beyond that, the timetable is unknown for Tampa Bay's fifth-round pick.
Wide receiver Jalen McMillan "banged knees" with another player, per Bowles. He was initially held out of camp for a few days, but he participated in individual drills during Sunday's training camp session.
It's unknown what McMillan's timeline is, but if he's already participating in individual drills, he should be on the right track to participate in team drills sooner rather than later.
Wideout Kameron Johnson did not participate in Sunday's training camp day. It's unknown what injury he has or what his status is, but Kameron has a history of injuries in Tampa Bay, so he could be in danger of losing his roster spot if the injury is long term.
This injury has probably generated the most controversy among Buccaneers fans. Morrison injured his hamstring after the first day of OTAs, and since then, he hasn't participated in team drills. Morrison has occasionally done individual drills during camp, but he has mostly been relegated to watching the team — when he's out on the practice field at all.
Bowles hasn't given a ton of real updates on Morrison. He initially insinuated he'd be back at some point soon after the first week of camp, but his demeanor on that has changed. When asked about his status on Sunday, Bowles said it was the "same as usual."
It would behoove Morrison to get on the field sooner rather than later, because if he doesn't, there are plenty of other defensive backs who have shown out in camp who could threaten his spot.

title: 5 Buccaneers To Watch During Joint Practice With The Jets
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have their first joint practices coming up with the New York Jets before they take them on in the team's first preseason matchup on August 14th.
This means that there are plenty of players to keep an eye on who have been doing well for the Bucs and will look to build on the momentum against the Jets in said joint practices. Let's take a look at some of the more important players to keep an eye on.
Trotter has shown so far that he has the ability to be a starting inside linebacker this upcoming season next to veteran Alex Anzalone. Trotter has showcased the ability to stop the run and cover the occasional running back and tight end during practice at Bucs camp.
Trotter will have his work cut out for him against some new tight ends with the New York Jets, specifically Kenyon Sadiq, which should help prepare Trotter when going up against more athletic tight ends.
The Bucs' third-round pick has done a very solid job in camp, especially in the red zone as a big-body wide receiver who can be a bit of a safety blanket for quarterback Baker Mayfield and the other quarterbacks.
Now, Hurst will be able to go up against different corners on the Jets and can figure out how to play against different styles of cornerbacks.
David Walker has been doing a fantastic job as a pass rusher for the Bucs in camp so far and has beaten just about every offensive lineman that he has gone up against. Now, Walker will go up against some different competition on the Jets and can look to keep building on the momentum he has from the Bucs' practices.
It should be a good experience for Walker to go up against more of a greater variety of linemen on the Jets and get more comfortable playing against NFL teams in his first full training camp.
Zyon McCollum has overall had a solid training camp to this point. While he hasn't been a lockdown No. 1 cornerback, he's still done a solid job and hasn't made many, if any, bad plays throughout the course of training camp to this point.
McCollum will look to continue to prove that he is the No. 1 cornerback of this football team in its joint practice against the Jets and a new slew of wide receivers that New York has brought in this off-season.
Chris Godwin has been on a great path so far this training camp. Godwin has looked great and healthy in training camp so far to this point and has all the makings of the new WR1 in this offense after Mike Evans left for the 49ers.
With that being said, it will be very interesting to see how Godwin continues to build momentum for himself going up against the Jets for a joint practice in the near future. The Jets have added a few new members of their secondary this offseason, and it should be some good work for Godwin to play against some different players as he continues to build on his good health and good play.

title: 4 Major Takeaways from Titans' Heated Joint Practice with 49ers: Day 3 Rookie Continues to Shine
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans and San Francisco 49ers held a heated joint practice on Tuesday. Both teams will square off again on Thursday night in a preseason contest at Levi's Stadium.
Tuesday's practice between the Titans and 49ers was incredibly physical, as there were multiple fights and it seemed like there was extracurricular activity after nearly every play. San Francisco clearly wanted to set the tone and get under Tennessee's skin.
Though tempers flaring was the main storyline of the day, there is still a lot to discuss from practice on Tuesday. Let's take a look at the key takeaways for the Titans.
After a quiet start to camp, Carmona has been making a ton of noise in recent practices , and Tuesday was no different. According to ESPN's Turron Davenport, the fifth-round rookie received early first-team reps at right guard during the scrimmage period against the 49ers. In practice, Carmona contributed a key block on a Cam Ward touchdown pass, though the rookie also committed a costly false start during an end-of-practice two-minute drill.
Tuesday marked the second straight practice Carmona worked with the starting offense, and head coach Robert Saleh praised the Arkansas product for earning his opportunities . However, Saleh also confirmed that right guard is still an open competition.
"You gotta earn it to get in there [with the first-team], but he's been doing a nice job," Saleh said about Carmona. "But like I said, with that right guard spot, we're gonna keep working to find the best player for it."
Carmona is definitely in the running for the starting right guard gig with Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater. We can now officially call this position battle a three-player race entering the preseason opener.
It was an up-and-down for quarterback Cam Ward and the offense. According to Davenport and Buck Reising of A to Z Sports, the passing game was in sync early , as Ward started with a few completions to wide receivers Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate. Rookie running back Nicholas Singleton also had a few nice runs .
However, it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. Will Levis threw an interception , Mitchell Trubisky struggled to evade pressure, and Ward also had his missteps. The Titans' QB1 tossed a pick-six to 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown and failed to lead Tennessee to a score on the aforementioned two-minute drill to end the day. Ward went 16-of-23 on the day , with a touchdown to Ridley and running back Tony Pollard, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com.
One guy who had a splendid day was wide receiver Xavier Restrepo, who led the team with five catches, including two touchdowns, per Jim Wyatt of Titans.com. Restrepo is continuing to showcase his playmaking ability and is building a compelling roster case.
It's clear Brian Daboll's offense has a lot to work on, but it wasn't all bad at the same time either. The group should learn from Tuesday and use it to bolster their attack.
The Titans' secondary has had its struggles in camp containing Tate and Elic Ayomanor, but there hasn't been much panic. However, facing a new opponent on Tuesday, the unit didn't look much better.
ESPN 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner reported strong days for San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy and wide receivers Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling. Reising also noticed Robinson beating Titans safety Amani Hooker for a touchdown.
Additionally, Bonta Hill of NBC Sports Bay Area & California said that Purdy hit on a lot of downfield strikes on Tuesday, and David Lombardi of The San Francisco Standard jotted down multiple touchdowns for 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel during red-zone drills.
Though we're still early in the camp and the preseason, the Titans can't afford to be prone to allowing explosive plays in 2026, especially with the amount of money they committed to starting corners Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott. The secondary needs to step up sooner rather than later.
This was one of the most intense joint practices we've seen in a while. The benches cleared early in practice when 49ers cornerback Renardo Green shoved Wan'Dale Robinson out of bounds. Coaches were able to break things up, but that was a sign of things to come.
There were too many skirmishes and back-and-forths to include, but the major takeaway was offensive tackles Austin Deculus and Dan Moore Jr. getting ejected from practice. According to Nick Suss of The Tennessean, Deculus threw a punch at a 49ers defender within the first 10 minutes and was kicked out. About an hour later, Moore was also thrown out for getting into a fight with 49ers defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa.
San Francisco brought the heat, and though Tennessee responded, it's clear Saleh's squad was flustered at times. We should see growth from the Titans in this area, as the team is still pretty young and just needs more experience.
Saleh confirmed after practice that the Titans starters will play in the preseason contest on Thursday. Saleh added that he'll also leave the starters out there for more than a series, so they should get some good work in.
Overall, it wasn't an awful joint practice from the Titans, but it's evident that they have some stuff to clean up before Week 1. The 49ers have been a consistent playoff contender for nearly a decade, so Tuesday was a fantastic opportunity for the Titans to see where they stand with a few weeks to go in camp.

title: Tempers Flare in Titans Practice With 49ers as Tennessee's QBs Seriously Struggle
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans prepared for their preseason debut against the San Francisco 49ers this week by taking part in a joint practice out west. If today's unofficial meeting between the two teams is any indication, we could be in for a real mess on Thursday, and for more reasons than one.
Not only did tempers flare to an extreme degree in the practice, with both Austin Deculus and Dan Moore being outright ejected, but the Titans quarterbacks reportedly struggled to find their footing overall. Per Turron Davenport, Will Levis threw an interception to Jakob Robinson. Tennessee's long-time depth piece under center has had a rough offseason thus far.
Elsewhere, Cam Ward gave up a pick six to San Francisco's Upton Stout, missing a wide open Carnell Tate, according to Cesar Bass. The cherry on top was Mitch Trubisky being swarmed by the 49ers defense as, in Davenport's words, "No one stopped the pass rush."
Ward would ultimately end up escaping with two touchdowns, but to say that it sounds like a long day for Tennessee's offense overall would be an understatement. It's not quite fair to forge any real worries out of reported practice struggles, but you couldn't be blamed for suspecting that Thursday's game could pan out poorly for the Titans as a result.
Of course, Robert Saleh is fresh off of his latest stint serving as the 49ers' defensive coordinator. That means this practice, and more importantly Thursday's game, each serve as a bit of a homecoming for the head coach.
Having one of his offensive lineman be thrown out of a practice for throwing a punch probably wasn't Saleh's ideal start, but he and Tennessee have time to turn things around before their actual matchup with San Francisco.
Besides, on their home (practice) field facing off against a coach that just ditched their unit, it isn't a huge surprise that the 49ers defense came out and bared their teeth. After all, that bunch has been consistently known as one of the best in the entire NFL. Try not to take this news to heart, Titans fans.
However, everyone will be looking for a little more composure when Tennessee actually takes the field... to say the least. Preseason or not, throwing punches and picks won't cut it for a team expected to take a major leap this season.
Regardless of the eventual outcome, improvement from the personnel under center would go a long way to quiet the hearts of folks reading the practice reports from today. Levis, if he ends up with playing time, could use a leap following his shortcomings at Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage last week.
None of this is worth panicking over. At the same time, however, the team's optics were far from pretty coming out of this practice. All eyes are on Thursday's game.

title: 3 Players Primed for an Offensive Breakout in the Titans Preseason
full_text:
With preseason competition officially upon us, the Tennessee Titans are getting ready to trot out a Robert Saleh roster in live competition for the first time. Fans have impatiently waited all offseason for a sneak peek, but as the preseason usually goes, we'll likely be looking at depth above all else.
Still, that doesn't mean there won't be opportunities for guys to break out prior to regular season play. Beyond a few minutes for Cam Ward and his starters, we've circled three names that could see a seriosu uptick in production on the offensive side of the ball this preseason.
Titans faithful, watch out for this trio of playmakers, starting Thursday vs. the 49ers this week.
Osborn might be the sneakiest pick on this list. The speedy wide receiver, entering his fifth season in the NFL, had previously made a respectable name for himself with the Minnesota Vikings as a rotation piece.
An uneventful pitstop with the New England Patriots last year dampened his stock, but Osborn's seven-touchdown rookie campaign continues to suggest a ceiling he's yet to return to. He should get a solid share of touches in the preseason and, given Osborn's past and the circumstances of his one-year deal, there's reason to think he could finally snap back into previous form in Tennessee.
Singleton, who was taken in the fifth round of this year's NFL Draft, has a long-term path to taking over the Titans running back room on the whole. He's an extremely talented back with four years of experience at Penn State to back him up. In three of those campaigns, he scored at least 12 touchdowns.
Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are holding things down in that unit for now, but don't be surprised if Singleton comes out swinging in the preseason. Saleh will want to know what he has in this rookie, and Singleton's collegiate metrics point to a player capable of getting hot early in the league.
Restrepo has become a popular roster hopeful for Titans fans, if not only for his college connection with Ward. As he continues to battle for a roster spot, Restrepo's preseason showing could make or break his ultimate bid.
Expect the second-year receiver to come out hungrier than ever, and given his (relative) veteran status on the team, you can also expect Restrepo to get a ton of touches. Few on the roster, if anyone, will have a better chance to prove their place than Restrepo this preseason.

title: Pat McAfee's Comparison for Carnell Tate Should Leave Titans Fans Ecstatic
full_text:
The Carnell Tate train has thoroughly caught fire as clips from the Tennessee Titans training camp begin to emerge online. The rookie receiver is making an early case for Offensive Rookie of The Year with viral toe-taps and one-handed snags that are sending Tennessee fans into a frenzy. But it isn't only those in and around Nashville that are taking notice.
On yesterday's segment of his show, Pat McAfee touched on the Tate trend, dropping only positive remarks about Cam Ward's newest weapon. "This Ohio State wide receiver factory they got cooking might have found the next Terry McLaurin here," McAfee declared, shortly after lauding Tate's acrobatics in practice.
"Not as hyped as everybody else," McAfee went on, "but still unbelievable. That could be Carnell Tate's trajectory, quickly." Football fans may know McAfee for his televised antics first and foremost, but as a former player himself, this praise doesn't present as a grain of salt.
Tate, while a little lengthier than McLaurin, shares his collegiate past as a Buckeye with the Washington Commanders pass-catcher. As McAfee noted, this isn't necessarily a loud comparison, but don't let the non-superstar nature of this bid fool you.
McLaurin is a long-term professional stud, and Titans fans should be thrilled with such an outlook this early in Tate's run.
Not only has McLaurin been to the Pro Bowl twice, but he's also got a hefty share of 1,000 yard seasons to his name. In fact, from 2020-2024, McLaurin met this metric five straight times. The 30-year old playmaker has put together a bejewled career that anyone would be lucky to replicate.
In Tate, the Titans have a receiver worthy of those lofty expectations, if he isn't expected to surpass them.
Taking a player with the fourth overall pick comes with expectations attached, after all. Whether or not it's fair to saddle a rookie with the weight of an offense, or even a franchise (see Cam Ward), is irrelevant to what struggling teams most often ask of their new guys.
Fortunately for Tate, while he certainly appears worthy of a task like that, he won't have to lead the Titans alone. Brian Daboll's offense appears fully equipped to allow Tate to ease into his role as Ward looks to the likes of Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm, and others from under center.
Buckeyes are as Buckeyes do. Tate is the latest Ohio State receiver in a long line of successful draft picks, and his scenario in Tennessee suggests that McAfee's projection is right on the money.

title: 5 Titans Players to Watch Closely in Tennessee's Joint Practice and Preseason Opener vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have a busy week ahead of them in Santa Clara. Robert Saleh's group will square off against the San Francisco 49ers in a joint practice on Tuesday and then play a preseason game with Kyle Shanahan's group at Levi's Stadium on Thursday.
Tuesday's joint practice and Thursday's preseason opener will be the first time we see this new-look Titans squad against another team . Tennessee's starters should see a ton of action in the practice, while depth players and those on the roster bubble will likely dominate most of the preseason game.
With the Titans ramping up camp and finally kicking off the preseason in the coming days, let's take a look at five players to watch closely this week.
Grouping these two may seem odd, but how could I not? Ward and Tate have already built a strong rapport through the first few weeks of camp , with the pair connecting on three touchdowns during Tennessee's most recent practice on Sunday.
Ward and Tate won't see much action in the preseason contest, but the joint practice will be a different story. Tate will likely be matched up against the 49ers' top cornerback, Deommodore Lenoir, who will be a solid test for the No. 4 overall pick. Lenoir has started 64 games over five years since joining San Francisco as a fifth-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
As for Ward, it'll be interesting to see how he picks apart this 49ers defense led by defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. When healthy, San Francisco's defense figures to be one of the top units in the league, but with superstar edge rusher Nick Bosa missing multiple practices in a row due to soreness , they aren't at full strength.
Regardless, Ward and Tate don't have an easy practice ahead of them on Tuesday. They will need to be at their best for the Titans' offense to flourish against a 49ers defense that is still formidable, so Tuesday's practice will tell us how far along Brian Daboll's unit is in its progression, especially his quarterback and No. 1 receiver.
Restrepo is fighting for a roster spot , and though he hasn't had an eye-popping camp, the Miami product has stayed consistent and isn't having many bad days , either.
Though Restrepo should garner some reps during Tuesday's practice, more eyes will be on him during Thursday's game. Restrepo will receive a ton of work, and if he can stand out as a playmaker while also adding value on special teams, the 24-year-old will bolster his roster case.
With the amount of talent in the receiver room, the Titans could opt to keep seven players in the position group instead of the usual six, which would significantly increase Restrepo's roster odds. However, he can't worry about that right now. All Restrepo must focus on taking full advantage of his opportunities, especially in preseason action.
Carmona had his breakout day of camp on Sunday , as the fifth-round rookie finally earned first-team reps and made the most of them. According to A to Z Sports, Carmona contributed multiple crucial blocks on a long run by running back Tyjae Spears, and his helmet came off in the process.
If Carmona can play with that same intensity this week, he could spoil the party for Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater, who have been competing for the starting right guard spot for most of camp.
Like Restrepo, Carmona will see more action in the preseason contest on Thursday. We'll see how the Arkansas product performs as he has a legitimate opportunity to work his way into starting discussions on the offensive line.
The first big test of Latham's make-or-break Year 3 begins Tuesday. With the 49ers' defensive line currently ravaged by injuries , the offensive line, especially Latham, has no excuses to struggle this week and should impose its will.
Outside of being involved in a skirmish with All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons last week and a few updates here and there, we haven't heard too much about Latham since he came off the PUP list, which is usually a good thing for an offensive lineman. Latham has the frame and talent to be a dominant right tackle in this league, but the Alabama product must stay healthy in 2026 and continue his momentum from a strong finish to 2025, when he allowed zero sacks in Tennessee's final four games.

title: Titans Unveil Color Combo as New Uniforms Debut in Preseason Duel With 49ers
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' preseason duel this Thursday with the San Francisco 49ers is exciting for a number of reasons, not the least of which being the team's long-awaited uniform debut. After the Titans announced their new look earlier this offseason, folks from every fanbase widely lauded the look. Now, we know exactly what combo Tennessee is rocking in their first playing in the kit.
The Titans will pop out in white-on-white up top, with their helmets and jerseys both matching the typical road look. The baby blue pants will complete the getup, fully presenting the team's first aesthetic change of any sort since 2018.
Even then, it wasn't as serious an overhaul as the one that the franchise has undergone this year. The Titans' rebrand will be exasperated when seen against a 49ers team known for their own classic, virtually unchanged aesthetic, Tennessee's updated outerwear will clash loudly in the team's technical first contest this season.
Titans to begin their new aesthetic era in ... WHITE WHITE TITANS BLUE pic.twitter.com/qET8q2x7D0
Jim Wyatt also reported that the Titans will go with white socks to tie the bow off on their improved fashion statement. Every detail matters, especially for a franchise making its first statement since wiping the slate clean in every sense of the word.
This complete redo couldn't come at a better time for what has been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past two seasons. Tennessee's combined 6-28 record, marred most recently by Brian Callahan's midseason firing, turned the team into a league-wide laughing stock.
The Titans weren't able to keep up in the AFC South, let alone the rest of the NFL. Under Robert Saleh, however, this is undoubtedly a much different team. Will it be a better team? Everybody sure hopes so, and the team's laundry list of draftees and signees should have a positive impact on the winning column.
But regardless of the eventual result, the Titans' updated palette helps the feeling that the franchise has fully committed to turning the page. Fans were bought into Cam Ward already, but add an impressive run in free agency and guitar strings on the team's helmets? This is a brand new ordeal.
So long as everything goes to plan, it'll be a brand new result, too. As the wait to see this team take the field finally winds down, don't blame Titans fans for dropping a few thousand likes online for a color combo reveal. Let Nashville have this one.

title: Unofficial Titans Depth Chart May Reveal Calvin Ridley's Last Chance to Succeed in Tennessee
full_text:
It's officially that time, Titans fans. The Tennessee Titans have officially released their annual unofficial depth chart ahead of the team's preseason debut! Surely nothing else exciting is on the horizon, right?
As the Titans prepare to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, fans now have the bones of the team's first depth chart under Tennessee's new coaching regime. There are questions all over the board, as per usual with the unofficial chart, but Calvin Ridley's starting spot remains notably untouched.
Assuming Ridley opens the season with WR3 duties, we can likely note this year as his final chance to make a real impact in Tennessee. Regardless of Ridley having fallen far from the initial expectation that he'd lead the receiving unit, what remains is one more opportunity to get this thing right.
For those interested, the #Titans put out their first unofficial depth chart ahead the preseason opener vs the 49ers on Thurs. 👀 pic.twitter.com/9t2tCK1POj
Originally being brought in on a four-year, $92 million deal that painted Ridley more as a misused X factor than an overpaid veteran, it was no surprise to see the Titans community quickly sour when Ridley consistently fell short.
But a few injuries and a voluntary paycut later, and things look a little different for Ridley in Tennessee. Now that the Titans have ditched Brian Callahan and surrounded Cam Ward with a ton of additional pass-catching talent, the onus is no longer on Ridley to produce at a crazy high level.
However, with Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike waiting in the wings, the pressure remains at a low boil. Ridley may not be expected to put up leading-receiver numbers, but if he's given the chance to start in the regular season, Tennessee likely won't wait long for him to blossom.
While Ayomanor is currently being evaluated for a shoulder injury sustained in training camp, he outpaced Ridley last season as a rookie. Again, Ridley missed a huge chunk of the year with numerous injuries, but that plays a part in just how little leeway he has left in Tennessee.
Nobody can speak for the staff, but after Ayomanor managed to haul in four touchdowns while the coaching setup around him was actively crumbling, it's safe to say that he left a sizable impression. Dike also posted four scores, which is icing on the cake for his award-winning efforts on special teams.
Ridley will have a real chance to get back on track with the Titans this season. Yet, as the franchise increasingly gives way to talented rookies all around, it's apparent that Ridley's window isn't near as wide as it used to be.

title: Titans' Carnell Tate Has the Potential to Run Away With Rookie of the Year
full_text:
Carnell Tate isn't coming onto the scene for the Tennessee Titans as the top dog in the wide receiver room, at least not initially. Wan'Dale Robinson is set to hold Cam Ward's main attention for now, but that doesn't mean Tate doesn't find himself in at the top of the running for Offensive Rookie of the Year. One look at the way Tate is moving in preseason reps for the Titans says it all.
After his sensational effort in Tennessee's blue and white scrimmage last week, Tate carried his momentum into a practice performance that had Titans social media buzzing. On Sunday alone, Tate hauled in three touchdown catches in live competition.
One toe-tap touchdown in particular made the rounds online among a fanbase rejuvenated like never before. Is Titans football officially back? That may be pushing it, but Robert Saleh has a scary ROTY candidate in his first year behind the wheel.
Carnell Tate has been ELECTRIFYING throughout training camp and caught 3 TDs during practice today. pic.twitter.com/W1Pc9NpH6V
It's simply a perfect storm scenario in Nashville for Tate to succeed. He's got every facet working for him; all Tate has to do now is catch footballs. If that's the case, we could be in for a memorable season.
In his first campaign, Tate is set to fall somewhere between a limited developmental role and being put in a spot where he has to carry the entire offense on his shoulders. That was Cam Ward's job last season, and even he couldn't manage that cleanly.
Instead, Tate will get to catch breaks behind the aforementioned Robinson (as well as Calvin Ridley, to some extent) as he finds his professional footing. Chemistry won't be an issue with Tate and Ward, but it would be unreasonable to expect any rookie to step into a scenario like the one in Tennessee and immediately become a superstar.
That unfortunately leads us to the one potential roadblock in Tate's path to the trophy.
While Tate will likely end up being "the guy" for Tennessee at wide receiver (assuming he keeps trending positively), some of his competition for ROTY will be thrown into better odds off the bat. Although, that may only be because their overall situations are worse.
Both Fernando Mendoza and Jeremiyah Love, leading the way for the Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals, respectively, will be tasked with shouldering the offensive weight that Tate won't have to.
It's a bittersweet condition, as Tate will benefit from being eased into his spot on the Titans, even if it means he forfeits some of the team's initial spotlight. Still, if Tennessee gets out to a hot start and Tate's burgeoning connection with Ward carries over into the regular season, these technicalities could quickly become moot.
Tate would be the first Titans rookie to win the award since Vince Young in 2006. Only time will tell, but with fall fast approaching, the wait is almost over.

full_text:
The Tennessee Titans officially wrapped up their second week of training camp with a scrimmage at Nissan Stadium on Friday and a practice on Sunday. Robert Saleh's squad will now prepare for a joint practice and preseason game with the San Francisco 49ers in Santa Clara this upcoming week.
The Titans' roster is filled with veteran talent in nearly every position group. However, several of the team's rookie class were the major standouts during Friday's scrimmage and Sunday's practice.
Wide receiver Carnell Tate has drawn most of the spotlight, but two other Titans rookies should also be getting more attention.
Let's start with Tate, who continued his excellent performance from the scrimmage into practice. According to Jim Wyatt of Titans.com, Tate hauled in three touchdowns on Sunday , including a clean toe-tap goal-line score on a beautiful throw from quarterback Cam Ward.
Hibachi Tate pic.twitter.com/1wC2uwMqU8
Tate has looked like a legitimate No. 1 receiver in recent camp practices, and it's hard not to get excited about his potential. The 21-year-old possesses smooth route-running, reliable hands, and plays much faster than his 4.53-second 40-yard dash.

Besides Tate, linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. and guard Fernando Carmona were also standouts. Hill has been stringing together phenomenal practices, and Sunday was no different. The Titans will hit the road for Santa Clara for a joint practice with the 49ers on Tuesday and a preseason contest on Thursday. During this trip, keep a close eye on Tate, Hill, Carmona, and the other Tennessee rookies who could make noise.

title: Titans' Cam Ward and Carnell Tate are Already Forging a Special Bond
full_text:
Carnell Tate going to the Tennessee Titans at fourth overall in the NFL draft came off as a risky move for a lot of onlookers. After hiring defensive specialist Robert Saleh to lead the way and seeing rumored target Jeremiyah Love fly off the board, some folks dubbed this as a panic move.
Yet, anybody in Nashville that is familiar with Cam Ward's game had to feel good about this one from the start. After all, what's the point of putting a player like Ward at the center of your franchise if you don't invest in weapons to suit him?
Signing guard Peter Skoronski to a massive, triple-digit extension was the Titans' latest effort to build long-term blocks around Ward. But in Tate, Coach Saleh and Tennessee appear to have a weapon meant to rise to stardom with Ward.
On Friday, the Titans ran a blue and white scrimmage at Nissan Stadium in front of a small contingent of fans, all of whom were appropriately decked out in the team's new baby blue and red threads. New digs aside, the Titans X account posted a clip of Ward connecting with Tate on a wild one-handed grab.
CINEMA 🍿 @carnelltate pic.twitter.com/g8brMb76b7
The catch brought Titans fans to their feet, and it was only one of a handful of connections that Ward and Tate made throughout the night. Ward's tether to expected WR1 Wan'Dale Robinson was also on full display, but Tate specifically is the development to watch.
Robinson was paid the big bucks precisely because the Titans' brass knew what he was made of. Tate, on the other hand, continues to cast doubt on any of his remaining doubters with flicks like these.
We'll still have to wait for Tennessee to actually take the field to be sure, but Titans fans couldn't ask for more promising signals from Ward and Tate early on.
After all, this duo is in place to serve as the core of the Titans' offense for years to come. How play-caller Brian Daboll handles their budding chemistry this coming season will be crucial to situating them for success in the long run, but it's hard ot imagine that Tennessee doesn't prioritize their link.
This is only the beginning, too. Expect to see clips like these emerging on a weekly basis when football season finally rolls around this fall.

title: Joe Theismann Leaves Stefon Diggs’ No. 7 Decision to Washington — Commanders Daily
full_text:
A few days ago, newly signed receiver Stefon Diggs posted online, saying he wants to use the iconic No. 7 that former Redskins quarterback Joe Theismann wore during his career, including Super Bowl XVII. The number has remained out of circulation except for brief usage by the late Dwayne Haskins, who asked Theismann directly to use it.
Tuesday, Theismann addressed the situation while speaking with 106.7's Grant Paulsen: "The jersey belongs to the football team. I was honored to wear it. I will leave it to the Commanders to make that decision." Now, for those of you keeping score at home, Theismann did not explicitly give Diggs permission to wear No. 7, but he also did not object, instead putting the decision entirely in Washington’s hands.
Talking with @Theismann7 about Stefon Diggs wanting wear his No. 7 that isn't currently in circulation: "The jersey belongs to the football team.. I was honored to wear it.. I will leave it to the Commanders to make that decision.."
This situation brings a decades-long debate back to life among fans who believe numbers should be enshrined and those who do not. One thing the organization needs to get away from is "soft retiring" numbers by not officially retiring them, but also not giving them out. Number legacies either need to be captured and never used again, or embraced and passed on. A good example of a reused number through the years is 17 . Among those who have worn that number are Turk Edwards (who is in the Hall of Fame), Billy Kilmer, Doug Williams, Jason Campbell, and now, in this era, Terry McLaurin. In this situation, Theismann is making the right call by leaving the decision up to the team because it does two things at once. It puts the pressure back on the organization to finally decide the fate of the jersey number while allowing Theismann to come across as a team-first guy in the process. This is low-key a big moment for the new ownership group in terms of how they handle the legacy of the numbers moving forward. Daniel Snyder left the issue to fester in conversations among fans; let's hope, like many of the other things that left with him, that those days are over. To move forward on this, Washington has to ask itself a question. Do they believe adding Diggs is enough reason to put one of its most protected numbers back into circulation? If so, do it and move forward without crossing over this bridge again in the future. If not, retire the No. 7 next season and honor your legend while he is still alive.
Laremy Tunsil has made his intentions clear: after surgery, he is still going to help the younger guys on the offensive line even though he cannot currently help on the field. ESPN's John Keim reported Tuesday that Andrew Wylie said Tunsil told the offensive line he would return to Ashburn for treatment after surgery so he could remain around the team and continue helping the younger linemen he has been tutoring.
One thing to note on Laremy Tunsil: Andrew Wylie said he told the OL that he would return to Ashburn for his treatment post surgery so he can be around the team. Can still help the younger OLinemen he’s been tutoring.
Tunsil tore his left triceps muscle and is out indefinitely , which prompted the team to shift Brandon Coleman back to left tackle. This is beyond what most players would do and means that, while Washington loses his snaps, the team does not completely lose the influence and experience gained when they brought him into the offensive-line room. His third set of eyes could be far more helpful than any coach.

The Burgundy Roundup brings together the best Washington Commanders reporting, analysis, interviews, and other worthwhile reads from around the web, along with selected coverage from Commanders On SI.
While Day 10 of Commanders Training Camp was a shorter, padless session, it did have its moments. Several veterans received maintenance days, which shifted reps to younger players and roster-battle candidates ahead of Wednesday's joint session with Miami. On the day: Joshua Josephs continued forcing his way into the conversation, Antonio Williams produced multiple touchdowns, and Washington’s backup tight ends made several plays. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Allegretti with a helmet and jersey https://t.co/QpjXGnHc55 pic.twitter.com/YyoH89zT8k
The Commanders could use more tight ends to help Brandon Coleman -- Tunsil was part of a double-team pass block only 31.5% of the time; Coleman was part of one 42.1% of the time in each of his first two seasons. Washington also will use more play-action passes from under center -- designed to fool coverages and slow the pass rush. There's also quarterback Jayden Daniels, about whom one AFC executive said "covers up for a lot of sins." Indeed, in practice Daniels has excelled at sliding in the pocket to avoid pressure and find an open target. It helps, too, that Washington just signed receiver Stefon Diggs to pair with Terry McLaurin -- both of whom can create quick separation. And that would help offset the loss of a player such as Tunsil. But Coleman's play will matter as well. He did post a 92.3% pass block win rate the past two seasons. He also had a run block win rate of 77.2%, above the league average of 72.3% in that same period. To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
John is joined by Commanders Safety Jeremy Reaves. They discussed Daronte Jones new defense, the Commanders defense this upcoming season, rookie Sonny Styles, and more!
Diggs wins with refined route running, tempo, and elite footwork. While the 32-year-old wide receiver has lost a step in terms of pure speed, he still has the ability to get the better of cornerbacks on the outside. That said, he thrives in the short to intermediate parts of the field and should be expected to run plenty of deep overs, high crossers and dig routes. Diggs is particularly adept at adjusting his routes to capitalize on space versus both man and zone coverage, with David Blough stating, “In just a couple days – he had four catches the other day, at least 2-3 today – the ball finds him because he finds space.” To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Daronte Jones, 47, was hired from Minnesota after excelling under Brian Flores, who oversaw a defense known for its complex disguises and loaded fronts . Plenty of that has carried over to Washington, where Jones has deployed fronts with three, four and five linemen and mixed and matched along the way. Jones has coached at every level during his two-decade coaching career, from high school through multiple college levels and the pros. He believes his teaching ability is one of his biggest strengths, which he attributes to working in the Louisiana high school system. “When you create a lesson plan, you have to pretty much hit on everyone’s learning styles because everyone learns differently,” Jones said. “We try to do that as coaches so that you’re hitting on every player in that room.” To continue reading this article, CLICK HERE...
Dan Quinn calls Van Jefferson "exacting", and said QBs appreciate him always being in the right spot. Treylon Burks has slimmed down and Quinn said lighter has been able to go longer and faster for him. pic.twitter.com/zvGMuro840
"I'm getting to play everywhere. The shade, the two wide, the three, the four, the five, the six. I'm playing it all, man. I'm loving how I'm getting to just give guys different looks and be all over the place, man. And I think it's going to play to my strengths well, man. You know, give a lot of guys fits." title: Commanders Add LB Curtis Jacobs After Signing DT Byron Cowart
full_text:
The Washington Commanders worked out eight defensive players on Monday. The team liked what it saw from defensive tackle Byron Cowart and signed him Tuesday morning. Tuesday afternoon, they returned to that list and signed linebacker Curtis Jacobs.
We have signed LB Curtis Jacobs pic.twitter.com/ZnWtCxTxpr
The eight players in the workout group were DE Carlos Watkins, DT Byron Cowart, DT Fabien Lovett, DT Justin Rogers, LB Amari Burney, LB Power Echols, LB Devin Harper, and LB Curtis Jacobs. Washington has now signed two of those eight players, one defensive tackle and one linebacker. Jacobs has appeared in 12 NFL games, starting two, for the Patriots and Titans, respectively. He also has spent time on a few practice squads and was a draft pick of the DC Defenders of the UFL, where he had 46 tackles , added a sack, and recovered a fumble across 12 games, including the playoffs. Jacobs was signed for positional depth behind Kain Medrano and Ale Kaho; he can also provide some special teams help. Cowart was signed earlier Tuesday morning following DJ Davidson's unexpected retirement, which created an opening along the defensive front .

title: The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ Tenth Training Camp Practice
full_text:
While Day 10 of Commanders Training Camp was a shorter, padless session, it did have its moments. Several veterans received maintenance days, which shifted reps to younger players and roster-battle candidates ahead of Wednesday's joint session with Miami. On the day: Joshua Josephs continued forcing his way into the conversation, Antonio Williams produced multiple touchdowns, and Washington’s backup tight ends made several plays.
Also do not see Rasul Douglas, Odafe Oweh, Jeremy McNichols, Jeremy Reaves, Amik Robertson….. https://t.co/1qgXlRDQL5
Josephs has been coming on strong as of late, and Tuesday offered up even more evidence that he will be involved somewhere in the edge rotation this season. Starting with the opening fourth-and-goal competition from the 9-yard line: Jayden Daniels completed the pass to Chig Okonkwo, but Josephs beat Brandon Coleman with a rip move quickly enough that the play might have been a sack in live football. Later in the day, Josephs was able to disrupt things again with another would-be sack, this time on Marcus Mariota. It will be interesting to watch Josephs line up against the Dolphins tackles Wednesday to get a good sense of what we are working with there. His quickness and motor are impressive. Antonio Williams took full advantage of several top receivers taking little or no work Tuesday by scoring multiple touchdowns, including one from Marcus Mariota during seven-on-seven work. He added another when Athan Kaliakmanis found Williams for a touchdown during the two-minute period. Stefon Diggs' arrival crowded the receivers room, thinning the chances guys below the top two get, meaning these are the days those guys need to dominate.
Tone in the end zone 🙌 @a_williams2022 | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/23c2UKwVwg
John Bates' injury-related absence has highlighted the battle for the fourth tight end, with more opportunities along the way for Lawrence Cager and Colson Yankoff. Cager grabbed two touchdowns from Mariota, including a seam route on the first play of the two-minute period that left him open for an uncontested score. Yankoff continued to receive a healthy number of targets and added to a camp in which his athleticism and receiving ability have consistently stood out. The two have been forcing the Commanders to decide whether they want a fourth tight end and then who it should be, all at the same time.
knee slide goes crazy @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/FAg9gcP1oz
Daniels was still able to create some positive plays despite the lighter session. That included a fourth-and-goal completion to Chig Okonkwo and other notable additional connections with Van Jefferson and Dyami Brown. Washington was not looking for a huge day for Daniels; maintaining the offense’s rhythm while Washington managed veteran workloads was enough heading into the joint session with Miami.
Trey Amos is dealing with the ankle injury suffered over the weekend, and being ruled out of Wednesday’s joint practice is less than ideal for him and the team's current situation. Amos only recently returned to the practice field, and the Miami session would have provided valuable competitive reps against unfamiliar receivers before the preseason opener. Washington expects to find out more on Amos’ recovery over the next few days. Nick Allegretti not being ready for the Miami session or the preseason game is a major disappointment. While it will give the team knowledge of what is behind him, it will also expose Daniels if there is a breakdown. Every missed Allegretti practice means another day for Washington to evaluate the center combinations it has been using in his absence. On a lighter note, Quinn said Allegretti should return to the field Sunday, and both he and John Bates were in uniform at practice Tuesday, working off to the side.
Good to see Allegretti out here getting some work in on the side field today. Hopefully it’s a positive step toward getting him back on the field soon. 🙌 pic.twitter.com/HfjtLsrRgs
Washington's maintenance plan made Day 10 into a session with more snaps for younger players. Several, including Josephs, Williams and the reserve tight ends, were able to do something with them. Wednesday will give the team a much more useful test against Miami rather than lining up against teammates. Amos’ absence was by far the biggest disappointment from Tuesday, while Allegretti’s expected Sunday return at least gives the staff a clearer timetable at center.

title: Updated Commanders 53-Man Roster Projection After Nine Days of Training Camp
full_text:
After nine days of training camp, the Washington Commanders have learned some things about the roster they spent months building. Some of what they have learned has led to signing more players ; some has shown why they are in the building. Stefon Diggs , Daniel Brunskill, Nicholas Petit-Frere and Fabian Moreau have joined the roster since the first projection, while Nick Bellore, Ahkello Witherspoon, and D.J. Davidson have retired. Before training camp began, back in July, we made some more in-depth roster projections that you can take a look at by clicking here . That said, after nine days of training camp, it’s time to update our 53-man roster projection based on what we’ve seen so far.
Jayden Daniels, Marcus Mariota
Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota are names you were always going to see here, but the real competition at quarterback is the battle behind them. Athan Kaliakmanis and Sam Hartman are competing for developmental value and possibly a practice squad role that could eventually shape the team's backup position .
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, Kaytron Allen, Jeremy McNichols The argument to keep this group of four has only been strengthened since camp began. The only thing to add here since the last projection is that Kaytron Allen's case for the 53 got even better the moment the pads came out. He seeks out contact and looks to run through the defender. Rachaad White is the underrated receiving back, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt added some muscle this offseason and remains the incumbent with the highest ceiling for an expanded role, even though this group still feels like a running back-by-committee approach.
Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Luke McCaffrey, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks , Jaylin Lane, Dyami Brown
The obvious change here from the first projection is the addition of Stefon Diggs , who answers the question, "Who will be WR2," without leaving any doubt. Diggs’ arrival shifts the competition under the top two rather than eliminating it, with Luke McCaffrey, Antonio Williams, Jaylin Lane , Dyami Brown , and Treylon Burks all showing enough value to still be included. Another change from the first projection: we're going with seven receivers here now instead of six. The roster math shifted the moment LB Nick Bellore retired. Jaden Bradley and Van Jefferson sit just outside this group.
Chig Okonkwo, John Bates, Ben Sinnott, Colson Yankoff
While there are no changes here, the biggest storyline involving the tight ends has been John Bates ' injury and the opportunities that have followed for players further down the depth chart. The player who has benefited most overall from Bates' injury is Ben Sinnott, but Lawrence Cager has become a player more people recognize based solely on the number of targets and attention he is getting now. If the team decides to keep four tight ends, he will give Colson Yankoff a run for his money.
Sam Cosmi, Chris Paul, Daniel Brunskill, Nick Allegretti, Matt Gulbin, Brandon Coleman, Josh Conerly Jr., Andrew Wylie, Trent Scott
The offensive line has been the position group that has changed the most since the first 53-man roster projection. The biggest situation obviously centers around Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps, which will keep him out for an undetermined amount of time. With Brandon Coleman and Josh Conerly Jr. as the projected starting tackles for now, and Sam Cosmi at right guard, Chris Paul becomes the most obvious beneficiary at left guard on a completely shuffled line. Nicholas Petit-Frere, Max Scharping, and Daniel Brunskill bring experience and versatility; all three players were signed Saturday and are expected to find their way into the rotation in some form during the preseason.
Odafe Oweh has been balling first 2 days of camp… Feels good to have a good pass rush this year. pic.twitter.com/w1884skuoO
Odafe Oweh, K'Lavon Chaisson, Dorance Armstrong, Joshua Josephs
As camp marches through its second week , the roster battles being put in along the trenches are notable, and the disruption K'Lavon Chaisson has been causing has shifted the conversation from whether he belongs to how large his role will be. The top three is now a lot tougher with Dorance Armstrong back on the practice field, and the moment the pads came out, Joshua Josephs was able to show what he can produce off contact.
Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, Tim Settle, Jer'Zhan Newton, Charles Omenihu
This group is less about cutdown drama and more about how Daronte Jones distributes snaps among several players capable of filling different roles across the defensive front. Daron Payne has looked quite impressive in camp this year as he heads into a contract year . The real story here may be in what role Charles Omenihu plays in the defense, as he can play all four spots on the line. Jer'Zhan (Johnny) Newton is a name to watch. If he can put together an impressive season, the Commanders may find themselves in a sticky situation next year when it's time to pay Payne.
Sonny Styles, Frankie Luvu, Leo Chenal, Jordan Magee, Kain Medrano
Nick Bellore's retirement dropped the roster math on this position from six to five. The loss of Bellore’s special-teams role is more significant than simply deleting one linebacker from the roster, because Washington must replace those snaps somewhere among the younger players it keeps. That said, Jordan Magee and Kain Medrano now have the best chances of earning the responsibilities he previously held.
Trey Amos, Rasul Douglas, Mike Sainristil, Amik Robertson, Fabian Moreau
The biggest change here is that Fabian Moreau has replaced the now-retired Ahkello Witherspoon , and Trey Amos has finally returned from the PUP, giving Washington another opportunity to determine exactly how Douglas, Sainristil, Robertson, and Amos fit together.
Nick Cross, Quan Martin, Will Harris, Jeremy Reaves, Malik Spencer
Based strictly on in-practice performance, Malik Spencer deserves the last spot over Percy Butler. At the same time, if you bring in the complete snapshot that includes experience and roster value, it will be hard to leave Butler off the final 53.
Malik Spencer got 🆙 @SeatGeek | @43kilam pic.twitter.com/jwkFuWNtnK
Drew Stevens, Tress Way, Tyler Ott
The shift here from the first projection is at place kicker, with Drew Stevens seizing control of the battle up to this point. Jake Moody is still in it , but he needs to focus and make it his mission to be perfect in the preseason. Stevens was 34-for-36 through eight practices, while Moody was 28-for-35 and has accumulated all seven of his misses over the last three kicking sessions (at the time of publication). The place-kicker competition is not over yet; preseason pressure is much different than practice.
Overall, outside of the Laremy Tunsil injury, the roster is in a better place now than it was when training camp opened. The first real test will come when they line up for joint practices on Wednesday against the Dolphins. title: Commanders' Jake Moody Continues Watching Kicking Opportunity Slip Away
full_text:
The NFL, already jokingly referred to as the acronym for "Not For Long," is known for chewing most of the sport's best athletes up and spitting them out after a few hard-fought campaigns, a truth arguably no position is more familiar with than the thankless placekicker .
Take Jake Moody , for instance. He's come close to tasting some of the highest highs a kicker can touch, good enough a prospect to earn a top-100 selection by the San Francisco 49ers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Moody connected on 27 of his 33 field goal attempts across the regular season and playoffs as a rookie, including a then-Super Bowl record 55-yard bomb.
In honor of being four days away from the #NFLDraft here is Jake Moody hitting the longest field goal in Super Bowl history pic.twitter.com/qCQwWhjMIg
Unfortunately for Moody, very little has gone his way ever since that very moment. His accuracy, which slightly slipped over the course of those playoffs heading into that crawl to the Bowl, further teetered during a sophomore campaign defined by a subpar 70.6% hit rate . Now, following a third season split between three teams, he finds himself battling for redemption with the Commanders.
He's been pitted against Drew Stevens for the starting kicker job , and Moody's streakiness has returned at yet another inopportune juncture. Training camp viewers had to watch him repeatedly miss from deep, posting distinctly poor marks that threaten to end his bid for another starting gig sooner than anyone could have anticipated.
Jake Moody just went 2 for 6 in this kicking period. Four straight misses from 44, 49, 51, 55. He’s missed 11 kicks in the last 4 practices.
He's, at the very least, a familiar face in Washington. Moody shot an identical 10/11 on both field goals and extra point attempts over six games with the lowly 2025 Commanders , giving him more to work with in measurable situations than the undrafted free agent Stevens.
But just three years after making his debut, it's hard not to express doubt that he'll consistently factor into any positive on-field developments to kick off the fall. His position is a tenuous one; there are only so many regularly performing kickers in the NFL, and a few bad weeks strung together or a particularly strong loss in confidence can throw any momentum off the rails.
Moody was protected for a season thanks to his rookie-year accomplishments and draft-based asset value, but the Commanders won't see him as anything more than an expendable placekicker, especially if he dampens star quarterback Jayden Daniels' chances of guiding the squad to weekly success entering this much-anticipated season. Should he maintain the once-lost 50+ yard burst he'd managed to revive over his shortened Washington stint, that long-range attraction may win him a few more weeks of opportunities.
For now, he finds himself spiraling while attempting to avoid falling out of favor with the Commanders. Should Stevens, who himself remains far from a unanimous favorite, amp up the pressure any more, Moody may have to prepare to find work elsewhere .

title: Washington Expected to Sign Byron Cowart After D.J. Davidson Retirement — Commanders Daily
full_text:
The Washington Commanders are not done making changes to the bottom of their roster, as reports from Ben Standig on Team 980 indicate the team plans to sign defensive tackle Byron Cowart . Cowart would help fill the opening created by DJ Davidson, who unexpectedly retired this past weekend. Cowart has appeared in regular-season games for New England, Indianapolis, and Chicago since leaving the University of Maryland. The four-year veteran has appeared in 51 career games after entering the league as a fifth-round pick of the New England Patriots. In those 51 games, he's started 21, recorded 67 tackles (10 for loss), had seven quarterback hits, 3.5 sacks, and deflected a pass. Cowart spent most of last season on injured reserve with an ankle issue, making his health and how quickly he can get back into football shape a major part of what Washington will have to evaluate. The move fits into the Commanders' broader approach to camp this year of raising the level of competition, rather than just bringing in a bunch of camp bodies. While Cowart will not walk through the door with a guaranteed role, his experience gives Washington another legitimate option behind its established defensive tackles after Davidson’s exit.
The Commanders are expected to sign DT Byron Cowart, per source. 4-year vet (51 games) and ex-Terp. Was one of 8 players to work out for Washington today. IDL depth after DJ Davidson retired. He spent most of last season on IR (ankle).
More shuffling at the bottom of the roster https://t.co/2Ddey9ulpp
Offensive coordinator David Blough spoke to reporters Monday and gave an evaluation of Jayden Daniels as Washington continues installing its new offensive scheme around its quarterback. Blough said the staff tracks Daniels ’ throws and compares his accuracy and completion data across multiple seasons rather than relying solely on how practice looks.
This past Saturday, cornerback Trey Amos left practice early without any reason given by the team.  Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Monday that Amos tweaked his ankle while defending Terry McLaurin on a deep ball. Quinn indicated Amos could miss roughly a day or two while the team evaluates him. Amos just returned to practice Friday after spending the beginning of camp working back from the fractured fibula that ended his 2025 season. This new injury may threaten his status as Washington prepares for Wednesday’s joint practice against Miami.

title: Which Commanders Tight End Has the Most to Gain From John Bates’ Injury?
full_text:
It never seems to take long for injuries to start piling up in the NFL world. Even now, just a week and some change into training camp, the Washington Commanders are already starting to buckle under the weight of an injury list that isn't getting any less cramped with names.
Even if we look past Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps , a brutal break that already looks to throw off the balance of the Commanders' reworked offensive line, Washington fans may have to trek through a good deal of the upcoming preseason before getting a clear look at how the new-and-improved roster will play together.
On the topic of the squad's blocking, a few other key protectors may similarly find themselves ill-prepared for this Friday's kickoff against the Miami Dolphins. Starting center Nick Allegretti has yet to be cleared to fully return from his calf strain, and physical tight end John Bates continues to commit to his own rehabilitation process following a hamstring injury.
All players accounted for at practice except: CB Trey Amos C Nick Allegretti LT Laremy Tunsil TE John Bates
Presently slated as the Commanders' second-string tight end , the latter mention is much more critical to Washington's success than outsiders give him credit for. Bates started 11 games last season, guaranteeing even more protection for his quarterbacks than they already had, combining masterful technique with plain brute force to surge into one of the most elite role-playing contributors on the depth chart.
John Bates be moving that furniture around pic.twitter.com/73lYissxgU
He won't miss more than a few more weeks, but he leaves behind a tight end rotation that, while talented and versatile, will feel his absence. Both regular starter Chig Okonkwo and patient prospect Ben Sinnott have a lot to gain from filling in for Bates, though one has much more to prove than the other.
While established as a jumbo pass-catching threat, Okonkwo already seems poised to enjoy his longest leash yet this fall.
He's already spent all offseason since jumping from the Tennessee Titans to the Commanders getting discussed as a valued receiver, and he'll have even more room to work with following the team's Stefon Diggs acquisition. The newly signed free agent, along with regular touchdown threat Terry McLaurin , will open up plenty of downfield space for the athletic Okonkwo to sit in.
The Commanders know who he is; he can run, catch the football, and block passably when he needs to. That same clarity can't be shared by younger understudy Sinnott, who's yet to carve out quite as distinctive a niche as Okonkwo, let alone Bates.
Despite being generally buried beneath Bates and the since-departed Zach Ertz , Sinnott remained a deep-cut regular since getting drafted to D.C. two seasons ago alongside star quarterback Jayden Daniels . He's managed 33 appearances as a pro, but the alleged jack-of-all-trades never seemed like a smooth fit within former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury' s static approach.
Sinnott struck eagle-eyed viewers as a strong blocker in space whenever he was granted the opportunities to shine, instinctively fitting in well during trick plays as an open-field disruptor. Any ability to fire off a spur-of-the-moment Bates impression, a real possibility under creative Kingsbury replacement David Blough , could buy him in-game opportunities to demonstrate any pass-catching potential he's yet to show off.
#Commanders TE Ben Sinnott to @JPFinlayNBCS on the new offense: “I love it. I think this one really fits my play style, the kind of player I am” #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/zVeFVbh39C
He's earned a mere five starts over both healthy campaigns, but the time to impress in- and out-of-house evaluators alike may await Sinnott at this week's end. He has the chance to not only clearly leap ahead of talented receiver Colson Yankoff on the positional depth chart, but also clarify to hungry Washington fans that he has the talent and direction to aid Daniels' contending odds with this roster as yet another scouting report-worthy weapon.

title: The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ Ninth Training Camp Practice
full_text:
The Washington Commanders were back at it Monday with pads after having Sunday off, as the team works toward Wednesday's joint practice with the Miami Dolphins. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed before practice that Laremy Tunsil’s triceps injury will require surgery, leaving Washington reeling about what to do on the left side of the line without him. Brandon Coleman will get the first opportunity at left tackle as the player who was at the position before the team added Tunsil. The day saw the bottom fall out of the kicking competition as both guys easily had their worst day at camp.
All eyes on Brandon Coleman. He will get the first opportunity to be the Commanders left tackle with the Tunsil injury pic.twitter.com/4Sty3yBsXM
After a franchise-altering injury at one of the most important positions in football, Brandon Coleman had a decent first day at left tackle . It is important to remember that while he is not Tunsil, Washington drafted Coleman to play tackle, and he started there for 12 games during his rookie season before eventually moving inside last year. Coleman's day was highlighted by holding his own on one rush against Odafe Oweh , carrying him out of the play rather than allowing him to turn the corner. No one is expecting Coleman to miraculously become Tunsil, but the team is desperate for him to be competent enough to secure the spot. Andrew Wylie also received work at left tackle, giving Washington another option behind Coleman, but it's important to remember that Wylie has only played a handful of snaps at the position in live game action. Jayden Daniels was back to his strong upward trend on Monday. On the first snap of a second-and-long drill, Daniels attacked the defense deep and connected with Dyami Brown for a touchdown in the front corner of the end zone. Plays like that highlight that Daniels is comfortable enough in David Blough’s new offense to attack downfield rather than merely producing efficient underneath work, which is still there for the taking. On another play, Daniels found Stefon Diggs near the sideline on a throw placed just beyond Leo Chenal. His workload and the difficulty of the throws involving him continue increasing as Washington gets Diggs caught up .
Stef Diggs getting ready for the day pic.twitter.com/osIf7go849
One name that is not going away on defense is Joshua Josephs , who was able to get his hands on Marcus Mariota for a sack during Monday's practice. Josephs has repeatedly shown up in padded practices and has me legitimately ready to watch him closely once preseason starts. Antonio Hamilton Sr. intercepted Mariota and returned it for a touchdown, giving Washington another takeaway from a defense that has been preaching about creating more turnovers all spring and summer long. Josephs and Hamilton's days were the exact types of performances Washington's staff is looking for out of players fighting for snaps and roster position heading into preseason.
Bill Croskey-Merritt vs. Leo Chenal The fellas getting after it today pic.twitter.com/PwytnkuaU3
The proverbial bottom fell out of the kicking competition Monday as Jake Moody went 2-for-6, missing four straight field goals from 44, 49, 51 and 55 yards, while Drew Stevens did not fare much better, going 3-for-6, missing from 39, 51 and 55. Moody has hit a really bad spot now with 11 misses over the last four practices, after starting camp matching Stevens, kick-for-kick . Moody was not alone in having a bad day, as Stevens also posted his worst day of camp, and it was a moment he was not able to capitalize on Moody's collapse. Moving forward, Stevens still has the advantage based on the larger body of work, but his first truly bad day keeps this from becoming a settled competition before the joint practice and preseason opener.
Drew Stevens had his worst kicking period as well. 3 for 6 with misses from 39, 51 and 55. https://t.co/qZwPLDJ6Z7
What was once viewed as just a sloppy day of practice on Saturday is now starting to look like a trend as Washington’s offense has now committed six pre-snap penalties over the last two practices, with the latest coming on third down during Monday’s two-minute drill. The reason something like this matters? A third-down penalty during a two-minute situation is exactly the type of procedural mistake that can sabotage an otherwise successful drive. This is something that needs to be watched and worked on over the next couple of sessions, including against Miami on Wednesday. That practice session will be a perfect way to finally have another defense creating communication and pre-snap variables instead of practicing solely against their own teammates. Monday gave Washington an encouraging first step toward finding Tunsil's replacement. While Coleman is far from perfect, he gives the team someone they already have trust in from inside the building. With Jayden Daniels trending in the right direction, the team needs to get the kicking competition back in line and get the pre-snap penalties taken care of.
